That inspection of the morgue took place as part of an investigation by the Public Prosecution Service. According to the newspaper Sud Ouest, this was because of the discovery, at the end of last month, of the remains of two newborn babies and two foetuses. These lay in a container with medical waste from the morgue. Lonely The Frenchman is described as a lonely man. He was divorced, had no children and died a natural death. One of his neighbours raised the alarm at the time, when the man had not been seen for some time. A search has nevertheless been started to find relatives of the man.

title: Eighteen Ajax supporters arrested in Croatia, 'they had weapons on them'
lead: In the Croatian city of Split, eighteen Ajax supporters were arrested yesterday, Croatian media report. Photos and videos of the arrests are circulating on social media. The Amsterdam club plays an away match against Hajduk Split in the Conference League tomorrow. Footage from news site Tportal, among others, shows the supporters being arrested on a terrace in the centre of Split, after which they are taken away in police vans. Bladed weapons were reportedly found on the fans. Stone blocks can be seen on the terrace tables. According to Croatian media, it was a preventive action and the aim was to prevent the Ajax supporters from clashing with supporters of the home club, NH Nieuws reports. Physically attacked: The Ajax supporters' association reports that fans were attacked by supporters of Hajduk Split. Ajax also writes that it has received multiple reports this morning of "Ajax supporters who have been intimidated or physically attacked in Split". Taxi drivers reportedly passed on to Hajduk's hardcore group that they were transporting Ajax supporters, after which they are waiting for them when they get out. "In some cases their luggage has been searched for club symbols", the club writes. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is said to be aware and to be present in greater numbers at the airport and in the city. "Please stay alert for your own safety", the club advises. Ajax had already warned its own fans in advance about safety risks. "Supporters of Hajduk Split are known for their fanatical following and may react to visible Ajax symbols or recognisable groups of Ajax supporters", the club said earlier. The match between Ajax and Hajduk Split will be played tomorrow at 18:45.

title: Tree of the year is red beech in Middelstum
lead: The red beech by the entrance of the Sint-Hippolytuskerk in Middelstum (<entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>) won the public vote for Tree of the Year. The tree, more than 150 years old, received nearly 3000 more votes than the number two, which stands in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>. The election is organised by the SBNL Natuurfonds. With the prize, the fund wants to draw attention to beautiful, special or monumental trees, or trees that are significant for their surroundings and community. Last year the mammoth tree in the Abraham Ledeboerpark in <entity id="org:gemeente-enschede">Enschede</entity> was named Tree of the Year. The beech was already chosen in a preliminary round as the most beautiful tree in the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>. In the national final, the tree received 6721 votes, RTV Noord reports. Hoping for offspring: member of the local church committee Mark van Dijken views the prize with mixed feelings: "Our red beech is having a pretty hard time. Just look at how many beechnuts are lying around. It is producing extra many, in the hope of offspring." According to Miriam van der Waart, green manager at Groninger Kerken, the beeches in the churchyard of Middelstum are suffering from prolonged drought and changing climate conditions. "That is exactly why this recognition is so special. It shows how much this tree means to Middelstum, but also how vulnerable our green heritage is", says Van der Waart.

title: Dolfinarium must work towards an end to dolphins in captivity
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> considers keeping dolphins in pools such as those at the Dolfinarium in Harderwijk untenable. But for now there is no decision to close the Dolfinarium. However, a formal breeding ban will come in two years, and dolphins may still be imported to a limited extent. That is stated in a letter from <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. An immediate ban on keeping dolphins in captivity is not desirable, says Erkens. It would mean that the 22 bottlenose dolphins in the Dolfinarium would have to be killed because they cannot survive in the wild. Erkens does not consider that an option. But in the long term, an end must come to this practice, he says. "Dolphins are intelligent animals that must be continually challenged and have a natural need to dive deep and swim long distances," says Erkens. "That cannot be offered in captivity. Living in chlorinated pools can also cause health problems." No new dolphins Erkens is working towards what he calls "phasing out the keeping of dolphins in captivity". This means that no new dolphins may be born in the Netherlands. Dolphins from outside the Netherlands may be imported, but this must not lead to "a population that rejuvenates itself permanently". The ultimate goal is that at some point no dolphins will be kept in captivity in the Netherlands. Erkens says this policy is not aimed against the Dolfinarium, but is related to the public debate about dolphins that must live in pools. The Dolfinarium disagrees with the cabinet decision and wants to talk with Erkens. "In practice, it means keeping males and females separate or giving animals long-term contraception," says a statement. "That may affect their social life and natural behaviour, and long-term contraception can carry health risks."

title: Again one-way traffic for shipping on the IJssel due to low water level
lead: Since this morning, shipping on the IJssel between IJsselkop and Zutphen may again only sail in one direction. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> has reinstated the measure due to the low water level. As a result, ships must again make a detour of around 300 kilometres. On Monday, the one-way traffic was still lifted, because the minimum measured depth on the Boven-IJssel had reached the required 1.45 metres. Because less rain has fallen than expected, the water level has dropped below that threshold again, reports Rijkswaterstaat. Inland shipping may now only sail upstream. Ships wanting to enter the IJssel from Germany therefore cannot sail towards Zutphen at Arnhem. They must make a detour via Amsterdam and the IJsselmeer. The one-way traffic also affects inland shipping towards the Twente Canal, writes RTV Oost. Skippers can no longer sail directly to the canal from either direction and must therefore make a detour. Water level continues to fall. Rijkswaterstaat expects the water level to fall further over the next five days. That depends, among other things, on the amount of water entering the Netherlands via the Rhine at Lobith. Rain in Germany and Switzerland may cause water levels to rise again. Water levels are therefore being closely monitored. If they change, the measures for shipping may also be adjusted.

title: Former mayor Schuiling convicted again for masturbating, gets fine
lead: Former <entity id="pos:burgemeester-groningen">burgemeester van Groningen</entity> Koen Schuiling must pay 250 euros for what is officially called schennispleging. The court of appeal in <entity id="org:gemeente-zwolle">Zwolle</entity> finds it proven that he masturbated in his car in March 2024. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had demanded a fine of 250 euros. That is the same amount Schuiling was ordered to pay by the district court last year. The former mayor has always maintained that he was not masturbating. That is why he appealed. Schuiling was mayor of Groningen between 2019 and 2024. He stepped down before the end of his term after what he called an "extremely intensive period". Dagblad van het Noorden wrote that minister Uitermark of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> put pressure on Schuiling because of the matter. If he did not announce his departure, the ministry would suspend him. The mayor would then have decided to stop. The ministry tells NOS that Schuiling did not leave under pressure. Driver's statement The case against Schuiling started after a statement from a lorry driver. He had stated that from his cab he could see the mayor masturbating in his car, while the interior light was on. The two vehicles, according to the lorry driver, were near each other for some time. The OM considered the driver's statement reliable, and so did the court. In this regard the court points out that the driver had a good view of Schuiling's car and that the man always gave a detailed and consistent statement. Also, according to the court, there is no reason to assume the driver wanted to set Schuiling up. Stomach pain 'not credible' Schuiling has always firmly denied that he was masturbating. He argued that since 2022 he has suffered from sudden, severe stomach pain and that he had it at that moment. For that reason he would have undone his belt and rubbed his stomach. The court does not believe that. According to the court, Schuiling has not always given the same statement. He initially stated that he had his trousers open because he needed to pee, later Schuiling said he had a lot of stomach pain. In principle the statement of one witness is not enough for a conviction, but the court finds so-called corroborating evidence in an audio recording of the lorry driver. On it can be heard that the driver angrily confronts Schuiling at the exit. Schuiling then responds that he had to pee. Furthermore, the court points out that the former mayor did state that he was in the car and that the interior light was on. Together that makes the evidence sufficient, the court holds.

title: Three more arrests for fatal shooting incident at the Four Days Marches festivities in Nijmegen
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has made three new arrests in the investigation into the fatal shooting incident during the Four Days Marches festivities in Nijmegen. They concern an 18-year-old man from Zwaag, a minor boy from Hoorn and a 19-year-old man from Avenhorn. On Monday the police announced that they had arrested a 19-year-old Amsterdammer and a 21-year-old man from Hoorn in connection with the shooting. The suspects remain in custody, Omroep Gelderland writes . On Tuesday 21 July, around 22.00 hours, an 18-year-old man from Rotterdam was shot dead on the Graafseweg. That happened not far from the Four Days Marches festivities, which were under way in the city at that time. That same evening an 18-year-old fellow townsperson was arrested. He was released again a day later and is no longer a suspect. The motive for the shooting is still being investigated. The police therefore no longer provide information about exactly what the suspects are suspected of.

title: Arrests and raid at Turkish opposition channel Halk TV: 'Black day for Turkey'
lead: Turkish authorities raided the headquarters of opposition broadcaster Halk TV in Istanbul this morning. This is one of the most popular channels among the opposition. Critics therefore say the raid is politically motivated. According to the channel, hundreds of police officers entered the building around 06:30 local time. Images circulating on social media show staff filming the officers. Access to the premises has been closed off and live broadcasts have been stopped. A repeat is being aired. Turkish authorities have appointed a trustee to run the channel. 'Unfounded' The Turkish Public Prosecutor's Office suspects the channel's chairman, Cafer Mahiroglu, of bribery, money laundering and fraud. Mahiroglu lives in the United Kingdom and has not been arrested. As part of the investigation into him, Turkish authorities have issued arrest warrants against seventeen other people. According to Mahiroglu, these include some of his family members. Eleven suspects have since been arrested. In a video message on X, Mahiroglu condemns the raid. He calls it politically motivated and speaks of a "black day for Turkey". Mahiroglu denies the accusations, which he calls "unfounded". According to him, the raid shows how the judiciary in Turkey is being misused for political gain. It is the fifth time in twenty months that Turkish police have raided a television channel and a new trustee has taken over the channel. This also happened to Flash TV, EKOTÜRK, Habertürk and Tele1. The reasons Turkish authorities gave for these differ. Press freedom organisations and critics have long feared that independent journalism in Turkey is coming under ever greater pressure. Turkish opposition leader Özgür Özel reacted sharply to the raid. The leader of the Yeni Parti (New Party) calls the authorities' actions "weak and cowardly" and says they go against democratic principles. The Turkish Journalists' Association (TGS) also strongly condemns the action. The association calls the decision "arbitrary" and states that journalists in Turkey must be able to do their work freely, without government censorship. Gezi protests Halk TV was founded in 2004. For a long time the channel was closely tied to the largest Turkish opposition party, CHP. Due to a split within the opposition, the channel is now associated with Özgür Özel's New Party. The channel gained nationwide fame during the Gezi Park protests in 2013. While many major Turkish channels, including CNN Türk, paid hardly any attention to the mass demonstrations, Halk TV kept reporting. As a result, the channel grew into an important platform and mouthpiece for the Turkish opposition. Since then Halk TV has regularly been fined by the Turkish media watchdog. The reasons included, among other things, critical remarks about the government made by guests on the channel. In Reporters Without Borders' annual World Press Freedom Index, Turkey dropped from 159th to 163rd place out of 180 countries this year. Turkey thus belongs to the countries with the worst scores for press freedom. Muzzling Opposition in Turkey has also been under enormous pressure for a year and a half. A large corruption investigation is underway into hundreds of people with ties to the opposition. Several mayors, officials and prominent members are in custody. The removed mayor of Istanbul, Ekrem Imamoglu, is also still in custody. Last July, several more CHP mayors were arrested. The government says the judiciary operates independently. The opposition sees things very differently. It believes the investigation and police actions are being used to silence them and eliminate political opponents.

title: Family of Ivana Smit receives no compensation, and no new investigation in Malaysia
lead: The authorities of Malaysia do not have to pay compensation after all to the parents of Ivana Smit, who died in 2017. Last year a court ruled that serious mistakes were made in the investigation into the death of the 18-year-old Dutch model. That ruling has now been overturned on appeal. The news has hit Smit's relatives hard. "There have been serious shortcomings established in the police investigation into her death, but the government nevertheless manages to escape liability," lawyer Sébas Diekstra says on behalf of the family in a statement. "For them this is once again a particularly painful blow in a struggle that has been going on far too long." Suspicious circumstances The ruling on appeal is the latest twist in the case, which has now been going on for almost nine years. The 18-year-old died under suspicious circumstances in the capital Kuala Lumpur after she went home with an American couple. Initially Smit's mysterious death was treated as an accident. Almost two years later the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> nevertheless opened a murder investigation , but it never led to a conviction. Dismissal The family filed a lawsuit against the authorities in 2020. Last year the victim's mother was ruled in the right. The judge ruled that damages of the equivalent of almost a quarter million euros had to be paid. At the same time the judge ordered the police to dismiss the officer in charge of the investigation into Smit's death and to reopen the investigation. But the Court of Appeal has now ruled that judgment unlawful. Supervision of police investigations is reserved for the executive branch and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>, the court said. "The court must respect the separation of powers." 'Corruption' Lawyer Diekstra calls this turn of events scandalous. "This is exactly the kind of ruling that a corrupt or incompetent government can make very good use of." According to him the ruling on appeal sends the message that the police can get away with serious mistakes. According to Diekstra the family does not yet intend to give up the legal fight. It is possible to challenge the court's ruling at the highest court in the country, but first permission must be requested from this Federal Court. This option is currently being considered.

title: Five years in prison for drunk man who ran over 4-year-old child in Maastricht
lead: A 30-year-old man from Maastricht has been sentenced to five years in prison for causing a fatal traffic accident in which a 4-year-old boy died. He drove more than 60 kilometres per hour over the limit within the built-up area and had more than 3.5 times the alcohol in his blood that is permitted. The sentence imposed by the <entity id="org:rechtbank-limburg">rechtbank Limburg</entity> is equal to the demand of the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM). The court rules that reckless driving is the cause of the fatal accident. On 27 March, the convicted man, the 30-year-old Janus K. from Maastricht, drove 112 kilometres per hour within the built-up area, where 50 kilometres per hour was permitted. Around 19:10 a mother and her 4-year-old son Djorginyo got out of a bus. The woman put her child in a pushchair and wanted to cross the Dorpstraat. Before they reached the other side, they were hit by K., who was driving with a passenger in a borrowed black Mazda. The boy died a day later from his injuries. The mother was seriously injured. She suffered, among other things, a concussion, a broken neck vertebra and multiple fractures in her pelvis and right lower leg. She has permanent injuries. Without reason: Before the ride, K. said he had drunk seven glasses of beer with a friend in a café. While drinking, K. and his friend decided without reason to "go for a drive". The court finds this very difficult to understand, the verdict states. "What is especially worrying is that he stated that he himself thought he was not driving too fast." Blood tests after the accident showed that K. had 1.8 per mille alcohol in his blood, while the legal limit is 0.5 per mille. That corresponds to roughly eight glasses of beer. The man previously struggled with alcohol problems. He was in treatment for that, but stopped a detox programme a few months before the accident. He had not previously come into contact with the justice system for this type of offence. Living with a lifelong emptiness: The moving victim statements during the hearing show how irreparable the grief of the next of kin is. "When I woke up from the coma, I heard that my child was dead," said the mother. "I have to live on with physical limitations because of the accident, but these visible consequences pale next to the scar on my heart and the loss of my child. Since that night I have to live with a lifelong emptiness." The father stated that he cannot comprehend that his little son will never come home again. "A part of me died with him. He was my best little friend. People say that life goes on, but not for me." According to forensic research, K. could have prevented the collision if he had kept to the maximum speed. He could then still have stopped in time. The court therefore fully attributes the accident to him.

title: House of Representatives wants to curb experiments with small schools
lead: The law that makes it easier to set up a new school will be tightened again within five years, because too many small schools are being added. An example is the Renaissanceschool in Almere, which started this year with only four pupils. The school is closely linked to the political party Forum voor Democratie (FVD). <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> had already written to the House of Representatives that she wants to do something about the growth. "It is no longer sustainable to keep so many small schools running", she said. In a debate today she promised to take another close look at the market research that new schools must carry out in advance to gauge parents' interest in the neighbourhood. The coalition parties (D66, VVD and CDA) and several opposition parties have serious doubts about that market research, which would actually be no more than an online survey. The people filling it in often would not know exactly what kind of school it is. In part this is how the so-called FVD school, which opened its doors in August, was able to get approval. Beforehand it was measured that around 350 people were positive about its arrival, and that number counted for a large part in the approval of the school. Tielen wants to "look at whether we should tighten that part of the law or remove it entirely". She admitted that she too was surprised when only four children turned up at the new school in Almere. Innovative educational ideas The More Room for New Schools Act, an initiative of the VVD, came into effect in 2021. The law is meant to make it easier to start a school with government subsidy based on innovative educational ideas or a life or religious conviction. FVD voted against the law at the time. Since its introduction, more schools are founded every year, a large part of them Islamic. Political parties may also set up a new school under this law, provided there is sufficient interest and the educational requirements are met. According to a large part of the House of Representatives, there is a lot to criticise about the Renaissanceschool on that last point. It assumes, for example, that boys and girls need a different form of education. "Why I am so angry about this", said D66 MP Rooderkerk, "is that we are talking about 4-year-old children who may be indoctrinated by the FVD. Our education is meant to teach children to read and write and arithmetic, and to learn to form their own opinions. It must not be an experiment by a political party." 'Future ruined' Pro, for example, is also angry about the number of schools that are added too easily. That leads to segregation, competition and poor quality, says MP Moorman. She said there is not so much a need for more schools as for good schools. She also believes that children must not be used for experiments "who are now attending schools that will completely ruin their future and school career". Tielen said she sympathises with the concerns in the House, but so far sees no reason to intervene at the Renaissanceschool. She pointed out that at the start of the fourth school year the school must have at least 139 pupils, and otherwise must close at the end of that school year. "That will be quite a challenge", according to her. During the debate, VVD MP Kisteman announced a further private member's bill to allow earlier intervention at schools that underperform. In his view, such schools should be able to be closed much sooner if they perform poorly. News programme Nieuwsuur made this report about the Renaissanceschool in Almere on the first school day:

title: Police and Public Prosecution Service invite Ahold to file a report about 'cybersecurity incident'
lead: The police and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> say they have invited parent company Ahold to file a report about the hacking attack, or attempted attack, at Albert Heijn. Such a call is not often made publicly. A police press release states that there is currently no criminal investigation into the attack on the supermarket chain. The police write that there has been contact with Ahold, but that did not lead to a report. The company, which itself still speaks of a "cybersecurity incident", says in a written response that it is "cooperating with all relevant authorities". No explanation is given for why a report has not been filed so far. Ahold says it cannot make any further statements at this time. As soon as possible The police and the Public Prosecution Service emphasise the importance of a report in the press release. "To be able to investigate and prosecute successfully, it is crucial to always receive information from victims as quickly as possible", the press release states. The National Unit for Investigation and Interventions of the police says it has nothing to add to the appeal at this time. The Public Prosecution Service says it is waiting to see what happens. Ahold did report the incident to the National Cyber Security Centre, as the law requires. A criminal investigation can also be started without a report, in which case it is 'ex officio'. That is how the police and the Public Prosecution Service began a criminal investigation after a data leak at a laboratory in Rijswijk without a report having been filed.

title: Serious sexual violence against women in internment camps after WWII
lead: Thousands of Dutch women who were interned in camps after the Second World War were raped, tortured and humiliated by their guards. This is shown by witness statements that ended up in a drawer and have only now been examined by the NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies. The images of Dutch girls and women who were shaved bald after the Second World War because they were supposed to have associated with Germans during the occupation, had a relationship with them or collaborated, are burned into the minds of many. They were called 'moffenmeiden' instead of collaborators. Interrogations from 1950 That thousands of them were locked up in camps after the war and faced serious sexual violence there hardly features in the standard works on the war. Studies have been made of the shaving of the women's heads, but only for about fifteen years have historians known the testimonies about the camps. That is remarkable, because the interrogation reports of women held in this kind of internment camp have existed since 1950. Some of them were interrogated that year by former police inspector Johanna van Schilfgaarde of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> as part of the parliamentary inquiry into Dutch government policy in the war years. Historian and journalist Ewoud Kieft carried out research for the NIOD into these witness reports. He came across the statements while working on a series of background articles on the special legal procedure, the special legal system in the Netherlands after the Second World War. In his article published today he describes how women were raped and humiliated on a large scale, among others by the camp guards. The prisoners were penetrated with objects and their vaginas were roughly examined without medical necessity. The historian also describes testimonies in which women state that guards made them false promises of acquittal, reduced sentences or food in exchange for sex. Because prisoners were suffering from malnutrition, this was quite a means of pressure. Those promises usually turned out to be worthless. Yet the chief investigator of this commission, Arnaud Marie baron van Tuyl van Serooskerken, did not mention these testimonies at all in his final report from 1950. He even made it seem as if no witnesses willing to speak had been found, because the women would have been too afraid. "There is no evidence that women were raped", he wrote in his report. "Nevertheless, it cannot be ruled out that it did happen, because victims may not wish to make a statement about it." Because the report says nothing about the testimonies, which do indeed exist, the Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> never accounted for them. Negligent "I have not yet been able to establish whether the chief investigator deliberately left out the testimonies", Kieft tells the NOS. "But he was very negligent. This was not simply careless, it was irresponsible. He did not do his job", the historian says. Police inspector Van Schilfgaarde then brought her remaining documents to The Hague, where they were stored in various depots of the Ministry of Justice. There they remained untouched until they were transferred to the <entity id="org:nationaal-archief">Nationaal Archief</entity>. Other journalists and historians consulted the documents now and then since then, but no structural attention was paid to the sexual abuses in the camps. Victims not safe Kieft writes in his article that shortly after the war the Netherlands did not have a well-functioning legal system. "The Dutch government had been absent during the war and the police had worked for the Nazi regime", the historian explains. "So few people remained who could enforce the law and administer justice. There was popular rage about what had happened during the war, and a group of people wanted to assert themselves after the liberation." Kieft speaks of "wild arrests", in which women were picked up after gossip that they had a relationship with a German soldier. "Those women must have felt so alone." Victims did not dare to raise the sexual violence done to them in court, for fear of not being believed, he says. "They ran a great risk, it was not safe." The testimonies he has examined so far are "the tip of the iceberg", he says. In total there were more than 200 such camps. Kieft therefore also wants to do further research to map out the violence against women in internment camps. Second World War newsletter Interested in the Second World War? title: After an SOS, donations pour in for the almost bankrupt Seal Centre
lead: In an attempt to save the almost bankrupt Wadden Sea World Heritage Centre (WEC) in Lauwersoog, donors have raised 700,000 euros since Monday. Despite all the support, bankruptcy is not yet ruled out. "That really takes more than this", says a WEC spokesperson. The centre opened its doors in April 2025. Seals are cared for in the building, and there is a permanent exhibition about the Wadden. However, the desired visitor numbers failed to materialise. At the same time, the construction of the building came to about 17.4 million euros more than budgeted; the debt rose to around 2.8 million euros. In addition to that debt, the WEC has a loan of 9 million euros from the Nederlandse Waterschapsbank to finance the construction costs incurred. According to RTV Noord, the municipality <entity id="org:gemeente-het-hogeland">Het Hogeland</entity> stands as guarantor for this multi-million euro loan. Within fourteen days The WEC had placed all its hopes on financial support from the municipality of Het Hogeland and the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>. They would reportedly have been willing to take on about half of the WEC's debt. However, only on condition that the creditors would waive half of their claims. At the end of last week, the municipality and the province announced that they would not provide money. They saw no way to co-finance because of strict rules on state aid and the exceeded construction costs. WEC director Bas Wemmenhoven therefore said on Monday that bankruptcy would likely be filed within fourteen days, unless a solution was found before then. About forty employees risk losing their jobs in the short term, and the care of the seals is also at risk. Donations from Japan Supporters of keeping the centre then took action. A fundraising campaign by Stichting Zeehondencentrum Pieterburen has so far raised about 335,000 euros. The other part of the donations comes from direct donations to the WEC, writes RTV Noord. The WEC is also receiving support from an unexpected quarter. For example, 40,000 euros have been donated from the crypto community, the spokesperson says. "That is also an unknown world for us." Furthermore, the centre has been receiving more visitors than usual in recent days. "We are being overwhelmed with support", says the spokesperson. "On the one hand, there are people who say: 'We'll come and have a look anyway, because soon you won't be here anymore'. That is painful. But there are also people who want to support us this way. They say: 'This must not be lost'." Even reactions from Japan are coming in under the livestream of the seal care facility, where the seals were previously a hit. "For a lot of Japanese fans we are a kind of beacon, and for them it would really be dramatic if this disappeared. People are taking action for us and asking how they can help. We can hardly keep up." Turning the tide Whether all the support is sufficient to save the centre is still an open question. Solutions are already being sought in case it comes to closure. For example, the nature education centre Ecomare on Texel wants to help with the care of seals. Still, the WEC holds on to hope. "All the support is truly heartwarming. On Monday we saw it all very black, now the tide is starting to turn a little. It could work, we think." A substantial amount is still needed, adds Marco Boshoven of WER. He leaves open how large the total debt is, but "we need the target amount of 2.8 million euros to save it".

title: Podcast De Monarchie: how to proceed after research into the Oranjes' colonial past?
lead: The king must work with <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> on restoring the disadvantages caused by the colonial past. That is stated in the plan of Zwart Manifest, a collaboration of organisations that campaign against racism, which was presented this week to <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>. "After recognition and apologies, it is now time to work on restoration", says Dagmar Oudshoorn, director of Amnesty International Netherlands and affiliated with Zwart Manifest. Extensive research showed a week and a half ago, among other things, that the Oranjes supported colonialism for centuries and earned half a billion euros from it. The king had himself commissioned an independent investigation into his family history. That resulted in five books totalling 2000 pages. Disadvantages "Because of this history, people have been placed in disadvantaged positions", says Oudshoorn in the NOS podcast De Monarchie . "You see that lasting effect in institutional racism, discrimination on the labour market, in education and in healthcare. Taking responsibility and acknowledging also means asking: how can you repair that?" According to Oudshoorn, restoration is the most complex step. "You cannot simply undo disadvantages built up over many years. That is why you have to invest structurally and sustainably", she says. "Broad restoration is about improving the positions that have arisen from the lasting effects of the colonial past." Healing and reconciliation According to her, Jetten acknowledged the need for a next step during their visit. The plan of Zwart Manifest contains concrete plans per ministry. According to the organisations involved, there is also an important task for the king in embracing the plan. "The king used his position to have this research carried out, which has been very important. It may not and cannot stop at the research alone, it must go further." During the presentation of the research earlier this month, the king said in his speech that he sees "the uncomfortable outcomes of the research" as an incentive to keep working for connection, healing and reconciliation. But what can he do within his role? Royal House correspondent Beau Heimensen: "The king falls under ministerial responsibility. That means the ministers are responsible for what he says and does. His speeches first go through the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-algemene-zaken">ministerie van Algemene Zaken</entity> before he delivers them. As for filling in his agenda, he has somewhat more freedom. Every Monday he talks with the prime minister and discusses with his staff the invitations that have come in. <entity id="person:willem-alexander">Willem-Alexander</entity>, Máxima and their personal advisers also discuss which topics they themselves consider important to give more attention to." Oudshoorn thinks the king has enough room within his role to steer towards restoration. "As head of state he does have influence, and his words carry great weight. All the steps he has taken so far, from recognition to apologies, mean a lot. I trust that in conversations and meetings in the coming period he can also work on restoration." The <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity> refers in a response to the words the king himself spoke on 2 October: "For me, your research with its uncomfortable outcomes is an extra incentive to continue giving my full strength to what I swore at my inauguration. Namely to protect the freedom and rights of all Dutch people and all residents. I continue, together with the Queen, to work for connection, healing and reconciliation." Listen? The new episode of NOS podcast De Monarchie can be listened to via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps .

title: UWV pulls the plug on ICT project that cost 55 million euros
lead: The benefits agency UWV is ending the development and implementation of a new digital system after five years. The Bemiddelingsservice (BMS) was meant to connect employers and job seekers better, but according to the UWV the system does not meet expectations. The project has cost around 55 million euros, according to the UWV. The benefits agency has tested BMS on a small scale and taken additional measures. Even so, the organisation does not have sufficient confidence that the system can be introduced "within an acceptable timeframe and at responsible cost". Public funds In February the ICT Assessment Advisory Committee (AcICT) already concluded in a damning report that the "approach does not fit the innovative nature of the project". The UWV also failed to get a grip on the quality, and according to AcICT the project ran over time and budget. The committee then advised the benefits agency to choose a different approach. "We are very sorry that we cannot continue with the Bemiddelingsservice", says René Steenvoorden, member of the executive board. "At the same time we must be realistic and handle public funds responsibly. That means we are stopping projects where we do not have sufficient confidence that they will deliver the desired result." 'Diesel in an F-16' Han Stoffels, co-founder of software supplier 8vance, is upset that the UWV has pulled the plug on the project. In the FD he calls it "extremely disappointing". The company won the tender three years ago to improve this service. Stoffels says in the FD that the UWV's data, which feeds the system, is the problem. "We built an F-16 and the UWV then puts diesel in it." <entity id="person:hans-vijlbrief">Minister Vijlbrief</entity> of Social Affairs informs <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> in a letter that a "thorough evaluation" will take place and that the consequences of stopping development of the project will be mapped out. He will inform the House in more detail at a later time.

title: State Secretary Eric van der Burg: 'First invest, then the government can save'
lead: You can say a lot about State Secretary Eric van der Burg (<entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-kr">Koninkrijksrelaties</entity> and Effective Government, VVD), but not that he often takes the easiest route. After the Spreidingswet, he is now working on an effective government, where effectiveness means doing more with fewer people, less outside hiring and less money. 'Just give me another task that nobody wants', he once said jokingly.

title: 4,5 years in prison for former church elder who raped babysitter for years
lead: A 63-year-old man from Woudenberg has been sentenced to 4,5 years in prison for raping the babysitter of his children over many years. The father and the then 16-year-old girl belonged to the same church, within which the man was also an elder. The rapes began at the end of 2019, RTV Utrecht reports. The man is forty years older than the victim. According to the judges, the man deliberately used his age, authority and position within the church. The verdict states that there was a dependency relationship which he "deliberately used, strengthened and maintained". The man from Woudenberg said he had had sex with the victim, but denied that he had forced her. According to the court, there was sufficient evidence that the girl never consented to the sexual contact. Same church The sexual abuse began from the moment the girl was 16. The man knew the victim through her father, who also had a role in the same church in Woudenberg, RTV Utrecht reported earlier. From the age of fifteen she babysat his children. The girl was not paid for this, but often ate with the family. When the children were in bed, the babysitter spent the evening with the couple. They would then watch a film together or play a board game. When the wife was on another floor, or out of the house, the man raped the babysitter. He also regularly insulted and threatened her. This continued until early 2024. The wife discovered the abuse and the church was brought in. After several conversations between the church and the babysitter, she was offered help and the man was removed from the church board. He was also no longer allowed to enter the church. Fear and sleeplessness Still, the victim was not rid of the man. His children attended the school where she had meanwhile become a teacher. He reportedly stood in her classroom several times or insulted her when she walked past. At the university of applied sciences where the victim studied, he reported that she had committed plagiarism. After an investigation by the school, it turned out there was no basis for this. It led to fear and sleeplessness for the victim, among other things. She checked every evening many times whether the door was properly locked. She also no longer dared to go into the centre of Woudenberg for fear of meeting him. Thanks to the strength of God, she was able to tell her story in court, she said. "The most important thing is that this must never happen again. What happens to you I leave to God and to this court." In addition to rape, the court also found stalking and defamation proven. The man was therefore also given a five-year restraining order.

title: Found aircraft wreck in Dronten turns out to be British WWII bomber
lead: After extensive research, the municipality of Dronten has established that the aircraft remains found in a wood are from a British bomber shot down during the Second World War. The remains of the old aircraft were discovered four years ago during trench works in the Van Veldhuizenbos in Dronten. Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity> reports that researchers have established that the remains found are part of an Avro Lancaster Mk III JB120 LQ-D that was shot down over the IJsselmeer on the night of 27 to 28 September 1943. The aircraft was part of the Canadian 405 Pathfinder Squadron, which was stationed at an airfield near the English city of Cambridge. Failure That night the Lancaster flew together with almost 700 other aircraft towards Germany to bomb the city of Hannover. "However, this attack was a failure", the municipality of Dronten writes. "The scouting Pathfinders had used incorrect wind calculations, so that most of the target markers had blown away. As a result the bombs did not land on Hannover, but in an open field a few kilometres further on and on surrounding villages." The Lancaster did not reach Hannover. At 22.10 hours the aircraft was shot down on the way there by a German night fighter and crashed into the IJsselmeer, at the spot where the Van Veldhuizenbos now lies. The seven-member crew consisted of four Canadians, an Australian, a Scot and a Briton. Their bodies were never found. In 1959, however, remains were found in the area. These were buried at the military cemetery Jonkerbos in <entity id="org:gemeente-nijmegen">Nijmegen</entity>. During the recovery of the Lancaster parts, human remains were again found. Whether these come from the seven crew members is still being investigated by the Bergings- en Identificatiedienst of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity>. Mayor <entity id="person:jean-paul-gebben">Jean Paul Gebben</entity> of Dronten calls the identification of the aircraft of great historical value. "Behind every aircraft wreck lies a human story", he says. According to him, the seven men who have been missing since 1943 thereby regain a place in the history of the municipality. Unique identification number To establish which aircraft it was, the wreck was recovered in November 2025. For four weeks specialists searched for parts. This had to be done with extreme care, because there was also ammunition lying there, which could explode. During the work large quantities of soil were excavated and various aircraft parts were found. Ultimately, unique identification numbers on two pieces of aluminium proved decisive. It turned out to be the same Lancaster from which a gun turret had previously been found in the area. 5500 aircraft lost Part of the recovered wreckage will be lent to museums and foundations, so that the story of the Lancaster and its crew can be retold. It is estimated that around 5500 aircraft were lost over the Netherlands during the Second World War. A maximum of three aircraft recoveries are carried out each year. The recovery in Dronten ultimately cost well over 960.000 euros. Most of the costs were paid by the national government. Newsletter Second World War Interested in the Second World War? title: Unrest in Amsterdam neighborhood Floradorp, three arrests
lead: In the Amsterdam neighborhood of Floradorp it was restless this evening. The mobile unit was deployed after residents set fires and turned against emergency workers. Three people have been arrested for vandalism, including two minors. The unrest reportedly followed a letter from <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity> rejecting an alternative plan for a bonfire. At the start of the evening, a fire was set in Sneeuwbalstraat in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>-Noord. People had piled up junk in this street and set it alight. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, it became restless when the fire brigade arrived to put out the fire. Officers supported firefighters in fighting the fire. "When residents turned against them, they had to leave for their own safety," says a police spokesperson. Stones and fireworks were thrown at emergency workers. The calm has now returned to the neighborhood. Alternative bonfire. Earlier in the day, residents of Floradorp received a letter from mayor Halsema in which their alternative plan for the traditional New Year's bonfire is rejected. The neighborhood wanted a smaller fire in an open container, but according to the fire brigade, an open fire in a residential area is too dangerous to allow. Halsema has adopted this advice. At the end of last year, it was also restless in Floradorp after mayor Halsema banned the traditional bonfire because of safety risks. Fires were set repeatedly at that time, and the ME also intervened several times.

title: Kandinsky looted by Nazis sold at auction for nearly 32 million euros
lead: The work Das bunte Leben by the famous Russian-French expressionist Wassily Kandinsky was sold at a Christie's auction in London for 27 million pounds (nearly 32 million euros). In 2023 the German public prosecutor's office classified the painting as looted art and returned it to the heirs of the Jewish couple Lewenstein. Emanuel and Hedwig Lewenstein lived in the last century in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> and had a sewing machine factory on the Dam. The family had a large art collection, including works by Jan Toorop, Jozef Israëls and Jean Metzinger. Kandinsky made the auctioned work Das bunte Leben (the colorful life) in 1907 in Paris, where he was living at the time with his lover Gabriele Münter, also an artist. Emanuel and Hedwig Lewenstein bought the colorful painting in 1927. German occupation. Shortly after the start of the German occupation of the Netherlands, the work was auctioned and came into the hands of the Jewish art collector Sal Slijper. His family sold the work to the Bayerische Landesbank, which transferred it on permanent loan to the Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus, a museum in Munich. The work was on display there for decades. Research shows that a museum employee had the work (130x 162 cm) brought to the auction house in 1940 by a courier on the orders of an unknown person, where it was then offered for sale. According to the researchers, there are numerous indications that the Nazis had seized the painting. After the war, the children of the Lewenstein couple did everything they could to trace their parents' looted collection. The German bank returned the Kandinsky work to the heirs in 2023. Just over 60 million euros: In 2023 the heirs of the sewing machine manufacturer had already sold Kandinsky's Bild mit Häusern for just over 60 million euros. That painting was returned after a long-running dispute with the municipality of Amsterdam. Until February 2022 the painting hung in the permanent exhibition space of the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam.

title: Wake-up call 15/10: Protest against Israeli football club • Scientists decide on the fate of the leap second
lead: Good morning! In <entity id="org:gemeente-alkmaar">Alkmaar</entity> there is a protest against the arrival of the Israeli football club Hapoel Be'er Sheva, and in Paris scientists are deciding on the fate of the leap second. First the weather: it will be calm autumn weather with highs between 18 and 20 degrees. Friday will also be mild for the time of year. During the day it will start raining from the west and it will cool down. The weekend will be slightly changeable with highs around 14 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? In the Amsterdam neighbourhood of Floradorp it was restless last night. The mobile unit was deployed after residents set fires and turned against emergency workers. Three people have been detained for vandalism, including two minors. The unrest is said to be the result of a letter from <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity> about rejecting an alternative plan for a bonfire. Other news from the night: And one more thing: Off the coast of Turkey, the remains of a ship about 4,500 years old have been found. The ship has sunk but the pots that remained on board are still intact. Archaeologists speak of the oldest shipwreck ever found in the world. Have a nice day!

title: Busy election year adds extra pressure to European budget negotiations
lead: The leaders of the EU countries are speaking today in Brussels about a new European budget, high energy prices and new financial support for Ukraine. The discussion is under pressure from upcoming elections in four of the five largest EU countries, which could significantly shake up the balance of power within the EU in the coming year. The Spaniards (2026), French, Poles and Italians (2027) will go to the polls between now and the end of 2027. Especially the French presidential elections in April could strongly influence the negotiations on the European budget for the next seven years. In addition, they may have consequences for financial support to Ukraine. Campaign in Brussels In the French polls, the radical-right party Rassemblement National of Marine Le Pen is in the lead. Le Pen argues that France should contribute billions less to the European Union. Moreover, she sees no room for financial support to Ukraine. Ukraine is expected to fall short by tens of billions of euros next year to cover military and social costs, but the money is first needed in France, Le Pen believes, because her country is struggling with an enormous national debt. She makes Ukraine and the negotiations on the European budget part of her election campaign. For that reason she appeared yesterday, on the eve of the summit with EU leaders, at a press conference in a hotel in central Brussels. Her message to European journalists: the EU could look very different in a year. With much more influence from parties that would most like to sharply restrict the power of the EU. Tough negotiation So Le Pen hopes that her Spanish ally, the radical-right Vox, will manage to gain a place in a new Spanish government. Vox is now third in the polls. Le Pen's party colleague, Jordan Bardella, visited Santiago Abascal, the parliamentary leader of Vox in Spain, this week to express his support. The French believe that a good result for Vox in November could set the tone for the rest of the election year. Besides the votes in Spain, France, Italy and Poland, there are also elections in Estonia, Finland and Greece, among others. With her visit to the Belgian capital, Le Pen literally brings the French elections to Brussels. Although as a presidential candidate she may not sit in on the summit of EU leaders, they will certainly feel her presence. Especially in the discussion about a new budget for 2028 through 2034. Early deadline The heads of government and state of the 27 EU countries hope to come somewhat closer to an agreement today on how much money they want to spend in the coming years and on what. That discussion is so far extremely difficult. That is not unusual. Every seven years, countries that pay more money to the EU than they receive, such as Germany and the Netherlands, mainly want to cut costs. Opposing them is a large group of countries that would like to see a larger European budget. This often leads to negotiations that continue until the very last moment, because all countries ultimately have to agree. But this year European Council president Antonio Costa, the man who must steer the talks between the European leaders in the right direction, aims for an agreement still in 2026, a year before the budget is due to take effect in 2028. Costa hopes in this way to prevent all elections next year, and especially the French one, from completely derailing the negotiations. 'Democratic scandal' That early deadline seems too ambitious. So far the countries are not getting closer to an agreement. Moreover, not everyone is in a hurry. "We will not sign an agreement that is not favourable, just to meet the deadline," Italian prime minister Meloni said yesterday. Meanwhile Le Pen is trying to increase pressure on the current French president Macron not to conclude an agreement before his departure. That would, in her view, be a 'democratic scandal', just before the elections. It puts Macron in a difficult position in his final months as president: try to reach an agreement with his 26 colleagues in the coming months, with the risk that such a compromise plays into the hands of political opponents. Or wait, with the possible result that his successor torpedoes the budget negotiations.

title: 57 people arrested in Croatia after clash between Ajax and Hajduk Split fans
lead: In the Croatian city of Split, 57 people were arrested overnight by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> after a clash between fans of football clubs Ajax and Hajduk Split. The clubs play each other tonight in the Conference League. The police had to intervene to prevent hundreds of troublemakers from coming to blows in the city centre, Croatian media report. It involved about 200 Ajax supporters and 300 Torcida Split (fanatical fans of Hajduk Split). About 100 officers were deployed, but reinforcements arrived quickly. It is not clear whether Dutch fans were also arrested. Calm was restored after fifteen minutes, the police say. No one was injured. Days of unrest. The city has been restless for days leading up to the match. In total, over 150 fans have been arrested in the past two nights. The night before last, eighteen Ajax supporters were picked up. They reportedly also had weapons with them, Croatian media write. There have been five incidents so far, says Srdarević, head of the local police. In four cases, it involved confrontations between supporters of the two clubs, and in two of those, Dutch nationals were slightly injured. A criminal investigation into the perpetrators is underway. "We were aware that this would be a major challenge," says the police chief, "given the large number of fans of both clubs, especially those who misbehave". Additional police deployment. The police have been prepared for incidents around the match since last Tuesday up to and including tomorrow evening. Tonight 600 officers are being deployed in the city, the stadium and the area around the stadium. Other police forces are assisting. The police may also detain people who misbehave for two hours today, which is normally not allowed but is permitted on match days. The city expects 1900 supporters from the Netherlands. Tickets for away supporters are sold out.

title: Major fire destroys warehouse in Berkel en Rodenrijs, fire possibly arson
lead: A car dealership was completely destroyed by a fire in Berkel en Rodenrijs. No one was injured. A warehouse where the company was located has burned out completely. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating whether there was arson. In the same building on Noordseindeweg there was also a fire two years ago. At that time a car containing the body of a 20-year-old man was found in the warehouse, along with items for producing drugs. According to the police, no "unusual circumstances" were found in the warehouse this time. The fire broke out last night around 03.00 hours. According to the police, the flames quickly spread and a lot of smoke was released. Around 05.30 hours the fire brigade declared the fire under control. "They had just rebuilt it all. But they can do that again now," says a spokesperson for the safety region about the farm to the regional broadcaster Rijnmond. Also explosions. Whether there is a link with the earlier fire is not yet clear, but that will be investigated as soon as possible. In the course of the day the police will carry out further research into how this fire could have started. "A fully blazing fire in the middle of the night raises questions," said the spokesperson of the safety region. According to the police, there were also several explosions in the region last night: two in Rotterdam, one in Dordrecht and a fourth in Berkel en Rodenrijs. That last explosion was at a business premises on Industrieweg, about five kilometres from the building where the fire raged. No one was injured, but the explosions did cause damage. The police say there are so far no indications that there is a link between last night's explosions and the large fire at the warehouse, "but this will also be looked into further in the investigation".

title: Police find 50 heavy explosives in basement storage unit under flat in Utrecht
lead: Police have found fifty heavy fireworks bombs in a basement storage unit in the Utrecht neighbourhood of Overvecht. The owner, a 55-year-old man, has been arrested. Officers found the explosives the day before yesterday during an inspection with the municipality in a flat on the Tigrisdreef. They are Cobra 20s, which the police describe as "extremely heavy" fireworks bombs. In total the explosives contained about 10 kilos of flash powder. The owner's home was also searched. A further explosive was found there. The Tigrisdreef is located in the middle of the neighbourhood, the police stress. "That created an enormous explosion hazard and a major risk for local residents." All explosives have been seized and safely removed, the police say. Investigation is ongoing. The municipality has closed the basement storage unit. Laughing gas: Nearly forty cylinders of laughing gas were found in a garage unit on the Muylenborchdreef, also in Overvecht. These have been seized and that unit has also been closed. No one has been arrested for that yet, RTV Utrecht reports. The municipality of Utrecht and police carry out checks in garage and basement units more often. "It regularly happens that these spaces are used for criminal activities, for example for storing fireworks, explosives, flammable substances or other tools for explosive raids," according to the police.

title: Two ships set on fire after possible drone attacks off the Romanian coast
lead: Two commercial cargo ships caught fire off the coast of Romania last evening and overnight after possible Russian drone attacks. The vessels are two tankers that were at anchor in the Black Sea. Search efforts are ongoing for seven crew members from one of the ships, while other crew members have been brought to safety. The Black Sea, which borders not only Romania but also Ukraine and Russia, has been unstable for some time. This week, two other ships in the sea were also attacked; so far, at least six ships have been attacked in October. At least twenty crew members have been killed or gone missing as a result. It is still unclear whether the two struck oil tankers were hit by Russian drones, and research into this is ongoing. It is known, however, that the attacks took place within Romania's territorial waters. Multiple drones also violated Romania's airspace on Wednesday, according to <entity id="pos:minister-van-defensie">minister van Defensie</entity> Miruta. Ukrainian grain "These drone attacks are a direct result of Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine," says Romanian President Dan. "They not only endanger shipping in our region, but also the vital supply of agricultural products to other continents." The attacked ships were a few kilometres from the Romanian Sulina Canal, which connects the Black Sea with the Danube river. The canal forms a crucial route for the export of Ukrainian grain. Ukraine exports a large amount of grain through the waters of neighbouring Romania, because export through Ukrainian ports is extremely risky due to Russian bombardments. The increased unrest in the Black Sea could endanger the global food supply. Both Russia and Ukraine supply a large part of the world with grain. Much of the harvested crops in both countries remain in the granary due to the war. NATO countries The earlier attacks this week took place off the Bulgarian coast. Romania and Bulgaria are both members of the NATO military alliance. Under the NATO treaty, if one of the countries is attacked, this also means an attack on other members of the alliance, such as the Netherlands. "We have agreed that Romania and Bulgaria will work closely together to press for stronger measures against drones within the EU and NATO," says the Romanian President after a conversation with his counterpart Radev of neighbouring Bulgaria. Both countries have reported multiple airspace violations by Russian drones in recent years.

title: Albert Heijn: supply to stores fully resumed, no home delivery yet
lead: Four days after Albert Heijn was hit by a (attempted) hacking attack, stores are being supplied again as before. "Regular deliveries of both shelf-stable products and fresh products to our stores have fully resumed across the country," the supermarket chain says in a brief update on the situation. Product availability may still differ from store to store, Albert Heijn says. Over the course of the day, there should be fewer and fewer empty shelves to see. No delivery and no saving Yet the situation is far from normal. Albert Heijn still does not deliver online orders. The AH website is also not yet back online. The savings programmes and personal bonus offers are also not yet working. Now that supply is running again, the chain says it is focusing on "carefully and safely restoring the full range of services". What exactly happened is still unclear. Albert Heijn says it took its IT systems offline itself because of a 'cybersecurity incident'. Conversations between NOS and people from the security world revealed that it was a hacking attack. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> urged Albert Heijn yesterday to file a report. At that point, at least, this had not yet happened.

title: Japanese companies to invest billions in American chip factories
lead: Japanese companies will invest up to 21 billion dollars in building two chip factories in the United States. These will be owned by the American government and Japanese investors. The plan is part of a larger deal between Japan and the <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of Trump. Japan is investing a total of 550 billion dollars in the US in the coming years, in return for President Trump's promise to lower import duties on Japanese goods. That last part already happened immediately after the agreement was made: the duty on Japanese cars, for example, went from 25 percent to 15 percent. The US has, however, made it a condition that Japan actually carries out the investments. Management of the chip factories will be in the hands of GlobalFoundries, a large manufacturer in the semiconductor market. A semiconductor is the material a microchip is made of. The company does not sell its own chips, but produces them for others. Construction of the first factory is due to start by the end of this year. Chip production is intended to get going in 2029. At the end of 2028 a decision will be made on whether a second factory will actually be built. Dependence on China: On paper it is not a bad idea for Japan to invest in the American factories. The US is the largest buyer for most Japanese goods, including in the semiconductor industry and for sales of chip machines. Lower import duties are therefore advantageous. In addition, Japan wants to decouple more from China, the country from which Japan currently imports cheap chips. But above all, Japan wants to keep ties with the United States warm. That is important, partly because Japan is heavily dependent on the US for its national security. NOS op 3 made a video about the tensions between China and Japan: Japan also hopes it can earn something from the investment. Ideally, manufacturers of chip machines in Japan can sell their machines to the chip factories. Production moved back home: The United States, for its part, wants to pull the chip industry back towards itself. In recent years it has already made an enormous catch-up effort, but by American standards it is not yet enough. The US fears that the global supply chain will end up in Chinese hands. Despite all the ambitions, it is an open question whether the first factory will be finished on time and whether it can start running quickly. In America, wages and factory costs are high. In a similar project by the Taiwanese company TSMC, the largest independent manufacturer of semiconductor chips, construction of a factory in Arizona was considerably delayed. The United States very much wants to move forward, but does not always have the manpower and knowledge in-house to set up and keep running such advanced factories. In recent years America outsourced this kind of work to countries such as South Korea, Taiwan, Japan and the Netherlands. Criticism: It remains to be seen whether the Japanese investments prove financially sustainable. That thought is also alive among Japanese citizens. They criticise the plans and already see their money disappearing to the US. Japanese people have difficulty with Trump's fickleness: they see that it is hard to make firm agreements with the American president. More than a quarter of Japanese see the US as the greatest threat to world peace. Japanese citizens also want to become less dependent on China, but a large part of the population fears that the dependence is now shifting from China to the US. Japanese would rather see the country invest in its own industry. How can Japan invest billions? Japan's budget in 2025 was roughly 770 billion dollars, which means the country could never finance the mega deal itself. That is why the Japanese government urges companies to invest. The government offers subsidies, support and guidance for a greater presence in the American market. The construction of the chip factories in the US is not the first project under the recent trade agreements between Japan and the United States. Earlier, Toyota promised to invest up to 10 billion dollars in its American production facilities. Japanese CEO Masayoshi Son of technology investment company Softbank made a huge commitment at the end of 2024: within four years the company wants to invest 100 billion dollars in the US. That should yield some 100,000 jobs, focused on artificial intelligence. The CEO is a billionaire and has in the past more often had coffee with President Trump.

title: Animal ambulance receives unexpected 50,000 euros from inheritance: 'Never expected'
lead: The Stichting Dierennoodhulp <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity> is delighted with a large inheritance. The foundation has received no less than 50,000 euros from a man who died last year. Chairwoman Irma Moes of the Stichting Dierennoodhulp Flevoland had not seen the amount coming. The foundation had organised a digital collection for donations because of Animal Day when Moes was called and told the surprising news by an executor. Initially Moes assumed a donation of 100 euros. "Then that woman said: it is a much larger amount." She therefore had to swallow when the amount of 50,000 euros was mentioned. "We never expected this", she tells Omroep Flevoland. Animal lover The money was bequeathed by Joop van der Vaart, founder and former owner of an ice cream parlour in <entity id="org:gemeente-lelystad">Lelystad</entity>. He died at the beginning of last year at the age of 71. Moes did not know him personally, but according to her he did have a connection with the foundation. "Joop regularly called the dispatch centre of the animal ambulance because, for example, there was something with a little bird that needed to be picked up." Moes thinks Van der Vaart saw that her foundation does good work and that is why he decided to leave money behind. Rising fuel prices The Stichting Dierennoodhulp Flevoland is responsible for the animal ambulance and shelter in various municipalities in the province. The foundation also runs an animal shelter in Lelystad. According to Moes, the large sum comes in very handy. For example, it helps enormously to absorb the rising fuel prices and allows the animal ambulance to remain supported over the long term. "We have jointly decided to spread the amount over five years." The money can also help more animals. Moes explains that animals from the wild, unlike stray animals, do not fall under the responsibility of a municipality. The foundation therefore pays most of the costs of helping these animals itself.

title: Fierce battle over the world's most influential climate report: 'Never experienced before'
lead: It is make-or-break for the world's most influential climate report. It must be published before a decisive international climate summit in 2028, but the debate over the timing of publication is turning into a fierce political battle. The authoritative UN climate panel IPCC, currently meeting in Ethiopia, is creaking and groaning as countries are at each other's throats. In the report, the seventh so-called assessment report of the IPCC, hundreds of climate scientists from all over the world bundle all insights into global warming. It is considered the basis of international climate policy. Moreover, these IPCC reports are among the few things in the polarised climate debate on which almost all countries broadly agree in substance. In the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa, the 195 member states are negotiating, among other things, about the time they take for this latest report. The Netherlands, together with European countries and small island states, for example, would like to see it appear in 2028 as planned. But countries with large fossil fuel interests, especially Saudi Arabia and India, are trying to prevent that at all costs. Because it is precisely at the 2028 climate summit that countries must assess how much progress has been made toward achieving the Paris climate goals. There it was agreed to limit global warming to 2 degrees, and preferably even 1.5 degrees. For that assessment, such a bundling of the latest insights is of great importance, because then everyone bases themselves on the same and latest knowledge. Always a lot of drama. It is always haggling and theatre, says climate expert Leo Meyer, who has been involved with the UN climate panel since 1995. Even now, "supposedly retired", he advises the Dutch IPCC delegation independently. "But I have never experienced anything as hard as what is being played out now in all my years." IPCC expert Kari De Pryck of the University of Lausanne says the same. "This is truly without precedent. There has always been a lot of drama at the IPCC, but not about this." For about three years countries have been debating with each other, and the struggle reaches boiling point this week. If agreement fails to materialise, she foresees problems for the 2028 summit. "They certainly need input from the IPCC." Thick reports To what extent countries deliberately delay this report to get in the way of the independent climate scientists is not always clear. There are also poorer countries that argue for delay because they do not have the people and resources to comment on the thick reports in time. That problem plays much less or not at all in richer countries. "Participation and inclusiveness have been an issue from the very beginning. There has been great inequality from the start", says De Pryck. Poor countries, where fewer scientists usually have to do the work with less money, have therefore often had less input and are now putting on the brakes because they do not want to rush their work. But Saudi Arabia, for example, which also sides with this camp, is known in the field for "obstruction, attempts to slow down the IPCC and an anti-scientific attitude", says De Pryck. "I can still imagine that there is something legitimate in it for countries like Kenya", Meyer adds. "But Saudi Arabia, India, Russia and by extension China clearly embrace it. They really have an interest in pulling the teeth out of the IPCC reports." Behind the scenes it is said that the Saudis and the Indians in particular use the discussion about participation and inclusiveness to defend their fossil fuel industry. Political pressure Still, both experts emphasise that the world is not groping in the dark without a timely report. "Of course it is not the case that countries would have absolutely no idea. Like: 'hey, is there a climate problem? Gosh, let's just wait for those IPCC reports'", Meyer jokes. "But in terms of political pressure, it of course has a lot of influence. That diminishes if you cannot quote from the latest IPCC report." Ideally, the countries hope to have settled the political struggle by tomorrow at the latest, so that the budgets can be determined and the independent scientists know when their work is expected. If that does not happen tomorrow and they have to continue into the weekend, the question is whether enough representatives will still be left in Ethiopia to be able to vote at all.

title: Netherlands and France talk for the first time about cooperation on nuclear weapons
lead: Delegations from the Netherlands and France have for the first time held talks about cooperation in the field of nuclear weapons. That is what the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">ministerie van Defensie</entity> reports. The discussion, yesterday in Paris, did not come out of nowhere: President Macron announced in March that he wanted to talk with several other European NATO countries, including the Netherlands. The Netherlands and France discussed ways to "strengthen European nuclear and conventional deterrence", the Ministry of Defence reports. The security relationship between the two countries in general was also discussed. According to defence minister Yesilgöz, an important step has been taken with the talks. "In this way we are taking responsibility for our own security", she wrote on social media. The talks between NATO countries could lead to French nuclear weapons being stationed in other European countries. That also happens with American nuclear weapons: those are located, for example, at the Dutch air base in Volkel. Dependence on the United States European NATO countries want to become less dependent on the United States in the field of defence. According to <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>, "the American nuclear umbrella remains the foundation". He does state that Europe must take more responsibility for its own defence. Besides the Netherlands and France, the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, Belgium, Greece, Sweden and Denmark take part in the French initiative. The only two countries in that cooperation who possess nuclear weapons are France and the UK. France is expanding its arsenal, the UK has a smaller number of warheads. French submarines France has four nuclear submarines. One of them is always on patrol. That is to ensure that a retaliatory nuclear strike can be launched at any moment if necessary. The French president is the only one who can order a nuclear strike, but is supposed to abide by the non-proliferation treaty, which states that the use of nuclear weapons is restricted. The four missile submarines have room for ballistic missiles and warheads. Each submarine carries sixteen ballistic missiles, each equipped with six to ten warheads. The nuclear weapons are many times more powerful than the atomic bomb the US dropped on Hiroshima in 1945 and can hit targets more than 6000 kilometres away.

title: JA21 and SGP reject compulsion in housing asylum seekers
lead: JA21 and SGP want "in writing" a commitment from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> that municipalities will not be forced to take in asylum seekers, which they must do under the dispersal act. That is what JA21 <entity id="person:bernard-johannes-eerdmans">leider Eerdmans</entity> said after his meeting with minister Van den Brink of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>. Furthermore, they want tens of thousands of Syrians with a temporary residence status to be reassessed quickly, because parts of the country can be assessed as safe in their case and they may have to return. The cabinet must also quickly organise that asylum procedures take place outside the Netherlands and that in general the influx of asylum seekers goes down quickly.
