These demands come on top of the demand that the burdens on citizens in the Tax Plan must go down. For the two parties this is one of the conditions for supporting the Tax Plan and the budgets of the ministries before the end of the year. Lower burdens on citizens. The two parties together with the coalition parties have a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. In <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> they can also help the cabinet to a majority with other parties, but that is a lot more complicated. That majority is needed to approve the budgets. Without it the cabinet in principle may not spend money or levy taxes. Eerdmans does not yet want to say whether his party is already that far: "It is connected. We vote on the Tax Plan on 12 November. When we know the whole package, we will know whether we can vote for it." The talk with Van den Brink will be continued. What it means for the minority cabinet to go 'over left' or 'over right' has become somewhat clearer again. But how it will end is still uncertain. According to asylum minister Van den Brink these are not insurmountable demands in themselves. "I think I am able to keep working with JA21 on asylum and migration," he said after his visit to Eerdmans. Compulsion perhaps not needed. According to Van den Brink he is already working on most of the 'asylum demands' but is "only just started" as minister. About the dispersal act he says it simply has to be implemented. But he expects to "manage" with the municipalities. In other words: compulsion will in his view not be necessary. Asked whether his demands are not too high for the minority cabinet, Eerdmans answered: "The left asks six billion euros. We ask for asylum measures and those will rather bring in money. So I don't think at all that we are overasking." The left-wing opposition party Pro has demanded in negotiations with the cabinet that the cut on social security, such as the WIA and the WW, be taken off the table, in exchange for support for the budget of the ministry of Social Affairs. For the rest of the finances Pro has not yet guaranteed support.

title: Deceased wrong-way driver on A2 near Breukelen had become unwell
lead: The person who died last Saturday in a collision on the A2 near Breukelen had become unwell while driving. Research has shown this, according to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The motorist was driving in the direction of Utrecht and at some point lost control of the steering wheel. The car shot through the central reservation and ended up on the road towards Amsterdam. There the car collided with two other cars. The wrong-way driver did not survive, and one of the two other drivers was injured. The police are not disclosing the age and home town of the deceased driver. No guardrail On the relevant stretch of the A2 between Breukelen and Vinkeveen there is no guardrail, writes RTV Utrecht. The carriageways are separated for several kilometres by a grass strip. Every few hundred metres there is a short piece of guardrail. In 2019 a similar accident happened on the same stretch of the A2. Three people died then: the wrong-way driver himself and a couple who were in another car. New research A spokesperson for <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> told RTV Utrecht yesterday that it is simply not possible to place a guardrail everywhere. Rijkswaterstaat manages a total of over 3000 kilometres of motorway. "Installing and maintaining a guardrail costs money. And if an accident happens, that also requires extra maintenance." Rijkswaterstaat's policy is that no guardrail needs to be placed on a verge wider than 20 metres. Following Saturday's accident, Rijkswaterstaat is again researching traffic safety at the location in question. Whether a guardrail will come is not yet clear for the time being. "Ultimately we always ask: how can we arrange it cost-effectively while at the same time ensuring everyone can drive safely."

title: Dutch knowledge platform Raam placed on blacklist in Russia
lead: The Dutch knowledge platform Raam, which shares information about Russia and Eastern Europe, has been designated an undesirable organisation in Russia. It is the first time a Dutch-language medium has been placed on this list. As a result, Russian and Belarusian authors who write for Raam may face extra risks. According to the platform, those journalists risk a fine or criminal prosecution. A foreign organisation is designated as undesirable by Russia if its activities "pose a threat to the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation, the defence capability of the country, or the security of the state", Raam quotes from a Russian law article. There are now more than 420 undesirable organisations on the list. At the end of last month it was decided to place Raam's activities on the list, and yesterday this was made public by the Russian Ministry of Justice. The platform has existed for ten years. It is unclear why this decision was taken now. Russia does not give a reason, and organisations are not informed when they are placed on the list. Burden for Russian staff: Hubert Smeets, one of the founders of the platform, found out through a report by the independent Russian news site Mediazona. Smeets says he is astonished. "We are not that incredibly important. We are also not active in Russia itself. It shows that we are being used by the Russian authorities to escalate relations with the Netherlands." The Russian embassy in The Hague has had the Dutch <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> and Raam in its sights for some time, says Smeets. "Apparently they now want to make clear that there are also legal consequences to our activities." For the Dutch driving forces behind Raam there are hardly any consequences, apart from not being able to travel to Russia, says Smeets. "But it is really annoying for our authors in Russia and Belarus. They could suffer from this, they are vulnerable journalists. I very much hope that the Dutch embassy in Moscow, for example, keeps a close eye on this." Ultimately harmful: Smeets says that for years care has been taken when deploying these authors. "But some of our staff insist that they are named on our site in full. They say that if they have to work in secret and anonymously, they are no longer Russians. By their own account, they then resign themselves to the police state Russia has become." Even so, Smeets says Raam will become more careful. "We will ask even more explicitly what the Russian staff themselves want. We will have to rely even more on their own assessments of the dangers they face." For now, Smeets expects nothing to change in Raam's content despite the Russian measure. "Not in the short term, but I do not rule out that authors will start working in other ways. If we have to work with anonymous sources, that will come at the expense of reliability. That is annoying, because we try to work with open visor. Ultimately, it is indeed harmful."

title: No support yet for health care budget due to uncertainty about compensation for chronically ill
lead: In the debate on the health care budget, it remains unclear whether there is enough support for the plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Minister Hermans</entity> of Health received many questions about how chronically ill people will be compensated for the abolition of the health care tax deduction in 2028. Parties in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> want clarity on this before they decide whether to support next year's budget. Money has already been set aside to compensate chronically ill people who risk getting into trouble due to a build-up of measures, including the abolition of the health care tax deduction. However, there is still no plan for exactly how that money will be used. Concern among patients is great. Opposition parties are therefore not yet willing to support the health care budget. That support is needed, because the minority cabinet has no majority. Minister Hermans said she will come with new proposals next month, in the hope that these can win the approval of the opposition. The House will discuss the tax plan in early November. Clarity must be provided before then. Own risk In the cabinet's original plans there are two measures that threaten to affect chronically ill people. The own risk rises by 15 euros per year, and it is already being set that the health care tax deduction will be abolished in 2028. That would mean chronically ill people may no longer deduct costs not covered by health insurance from their taxes. Especially that last measure could cost people with high care costs thousands of euros per year. Hermans said she realises that many people are able to participate in society and work thanks to the health care tax deduction. "That group is very much kept in mind by us", said the minister. Still, the cabinet wants to abolish the tax benefit, because many people with higher incomes also use it without really needing it. That makes the arrangement unnecessarily expensive. In addition, the arrangement is prone to fraud and complicated. Many mistakes are made with it, so people can face reclaims from the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>. Alternative According to Minister Hermans, it is "no easy puzzle" to meet the House halfway. The House wants research into whether an alternative deduction is possible, one more targeted at people who really need it. The cabinet fears the arrangement would only become more complex and is therefore also looking at other ways to arrange the compensation. Parties such as Pro, JA21 and ChristenUnie want to know how the abolition turns out for chronically ill people. They want to know this before the House further discusses the tax plan and also the health care budget. PVV and SP are outright negative. Member of parliament Bushoff of Pro stressed that the minority cabinet must look with his party for a total deal "in which ordinary people get ahead". Without such a deal, the cabinet is, in his view, "heading straight for a wall".

title: Complaint filed against SGP member over Israeli wine from illegal settlements
lead: The pro-Palestinian organisation BDS Nederland has filed a complaint against former SGP House member Roelof Bisschop. The reason is his violation of the trade ban on goods from illegal settlements in Israeli-occupied territories. Two weeks ago Bisschop said in a programme on the Christian TV channel Family7 that he had deliberately bought two Israeli bottles of wine. The purchase was according to him a "statement" in protest against the import ban that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> had announced. Bisschop said he fundamentally disagrees with that decision. Family7 posted the interview on YouTube under the headline "Roelof Bisschop kocht bewust wijn uit Israëlische nederzetting na ingaan handelsverbod". Two days earlier Bisschop had already posted on X a photo of two bottles of wine, with the text "Toch nog maar even aangeschaft. Ze zijn er nog, de Israëlische wijnen!". Omzeiling Since 22 September a ban applies in the Netherlands on imports of goods from illegal settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories and on the Syrian Golan Heights. Besides an import ban there is also a sales ban, a ban on intermediary trade, a ban on circumventing the rules, and a purchase ban. What is BDS Nederland? BDS Nederland stands for Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions. The organisation is the Dutch branch of the international BDS movement, which calls on Israel to respect international law. The activists said after Bisschop's statements that they would report to the Fiscal Intelligence and Investigation Service (FIOD). That service can act if there are signals that rules are being broken. In the complaint BDS Nederland says that Bisschop knowingly acted in violation of the sanctions policy, and that he has promoted this on various platforms and at various times. "By doing so he has indirectly urged others to keep buying the Israeli wines, or other goods." "Anyone who as a former House member publicly announces they will deliberately test the law must be able to expect that the OM will look at whether that is punishable," BDS continues. The OM says it is aware of the complaint. It will study whether there are enough leads to start an investigation. 'Provocative' The Israeli winery in question, Teperberg, has vineyards in the occupied West Bank and is therefore on a United Nations list of companies active in settlements. But the winery states on its website that these specific wines are made just outside, in the Israeli Shfelat Yehuda. Satellite imagery confirms that vineyards are indeed located there. When asked, Bisschop said he did not know exactly where his wine bottles come from. It is therefore not yet certain that the two bottles Bisschop bought actually come from occupied areas and thus fall under the trade ban.

title: Albert Heijn hack problems persist: no deliveries for the rest of the week
lead: Albert Heijn cannot deliver groceries at home at least through Sunday. This is related to the hack attack or attempt at one, which led the supermarket chain to take its systems offline early this week as a precaution. This afternoon Albert Heijn reported that stores nationwide are being supplied as usual again. However, product availability may differ per store. Not everything is back online yet. For now, customers also cannot place new online orders, and the app is not yet fully available either. Customers who have already paid for their ordered groceries will be compensated, according to AH, when the systems work again. The chain says the checkout systems are working normally and that the prices on the digital shelf labels are correct. That was not the case earlier this week. Personal discounts and loyalty campaigns are not yet available. Albert Heijn has not yet communicated exactly what went wrong last Sunday and only speaks of a "cybersecurity incident". The NOS spoke with people from the security world who concluded that it was a hack attack. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> called on the supermarket chain yesterday to file a report. As far as is known, that has not happened yet. To report or not? Why the supermarket chain has not filed a report so far, and whether parent company Ahold plans to do so in the future, is not clear. Companies are often not waiting for a police investigation, cyber experts say. "When you bring the police in, it is quite a process. You are busy saving as much as you can and getting operational again yourself. The police have a different interest: catching the criminals." At the same time, a quick report is important, says former police officer and cybersecurity expert Pim Takkenberg. "The longer you wait, the more potential warm traces can disappear." Read more here about why a company would or would not want to report a cyberattack.

title: To report or not after a cyberattack? 'The golden hour applies to hacks too'
lead: After days of empty shelves and disruption at Albert Heijn, no police investigation into the hacking attack has started yet. Justice did invite parent company Ahold to file a report yesterday. Why is such a report important or not important for a company? The NOS reported earlier this week that there is a hack or a serious attempt at one. Albert Heijn speaks of a "cybersecurity incident". The company is cooperating with "all relevant authorities", according to a written statement. Why the supermarket chain has not filed a report so far, and whether Ahold plans to do so in the future, is not clear. The company is currently investigating what happened and does not want to say anything more about it. 'Golden hour' That Ahold is not currently working with the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is not so strange, says cybersecurity adviser Eric Schouten. External companies are often hired for such an investigation, he says. "Ahold may first want to find everything out itself. For the company, the most important thing is that the organisation is up and running again. That people can simply do their shopping again." Getting the company running again is Ahold's primary goal. "I can imagine that filing a report is not the highest priority for the company right now", says former police officer and cybersecurity expert Pim Takkenberg. At the same time, Takkenberg does not really understand why you would not file a report. "The longer you wait, the more potential warm traces may disappear." The police also find it important that those traces are secured as quickly as possible. "Just as in liquidation investigations, the 'golden hour' applies to a hack. The longer it takes for the police to arrive on the scene, the more traces are lost", says Stan Duijf, responsible for the approach to cybercrime at the police. But cyber experts notice that companies are often not waiting for such a police investigation. For example, cyber security expert Inge Bryan regularly advises companies that have to deal with a cyberattack. "If you bring the police in, that is quite a process. You yourself are busy saving as much as possible and making things operational again. The police have a different interest there: catching the criminals." Connecting the dots Out of fear that the police investigation will delay getting your business going again, experts see that a report is regularly skipped at the start. Although, according to the police, that need not be so. "If an attacker is still in the system, you want to start a criminal investigation as quickly as possible", says Stan Duijf of the police. According to him, the police never simply pull the plug or shut everything down. "The police follow the attacker's path in reverse", says Takkenberg. "If as an organisation you know, for example, the IP address of an intruder, that is the same as a licence plate. You know which car it is, but not who was inside it." Something the police might be able to find out through special investigative powers. "By, for example, hacking, seizing or searching, we can see what is running on an IP address and what is behind it", says Duijf. New cyber law Since August there has been a new law to increase digital resilience and cybersecurity. An important part of this new law is the stricter reporting obligation for companies facing a major cyber incident. They must report this to the <entity id="org:nationaal-cyber-security-centrum">Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum</entity> (NCSC). Ahold has done so. "But that is not a substitute for a report to the police", says Duijf. The fact that the company is not filing a report does not mean that no criminal investigation will follow, however. The police and the public prosecution service can decide to start one themselves. It is not yet known whether they plan to do so in Ahold's case. The situation at Ahold is also a wake-up call for other companies, says cybersecurity expert Bryan. "They must realise that this is where we are heading: that you must at all times be ready to take systems offline as quickly as possible."

title: Drug suspect Jan G. from Overasselt extradited by Germany
lead: The man whose home in Overasselt was shot at last month, Jan G., has been extradited to the Netherlands by Germany. The 28-year-old was arrested there in mid-September at the request of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Jan G. is in restricted custody, which means he may only have contact with his lawyer. G. allegedly tried to import nearly 4000 kilograms of cocaine, the public prosecution service says about his suspicion. That shipment was found at the beginning of last month in containers in the French town of Dunkirk. For the same offence another suspect was arrested in Dordrecht on 4 September. Explosion of violence On 1 September there was an explosion of violence in the Gelderland village of Overasselt. Dozens of heavily armed men walked through the streets. At G.'s home, shots were fired at the security guard who was guarding the house. The 51-year-old man was murdered in his car. Two officers were also shot, one of whom was seriously injured with life-threatening wounds. At that moment G. was still in Overasselt. He had fled to family elsewhere in the village, according to a reconstruction by NOS and Omroep Gelderland. Meanwhile 42 suspects have been arrested, who come from the Netherlands, Belgium, France and Ukraine, among others. Read our reconstructions of the explosion of violence here:

title: Up to 2 years in prison demanded for assault and humiliation of 17-year-old from Haarlem in Beverwijk
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is demanding prison sentences of one and a half to two years against three men from <entity id="org:gemeente-heemskerk">Heemskerk</entity> and Beverwijk. They are suspected of attempted manslaughter and assault on a 17-year-old teenager from <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity>. The violence reportedly arose from a quarrel between two rival youth groups from Heemskerk and Beverwijk, and Haarlem. The severe assault on the 17-year-old boy took place on 6 September last year. Two days later a 22-year-old from Heemskerk was severely assaulted, probably a retaliation. Footage of both assaults circulated on various social media. This led to much unrest in the region. Out of fear of further escalation, five secondary schools in Beverwijk and Heemskerk closed their doors for a day. Lessons also fell out in Haarlem. The mayors took emergency measures and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was allowed to conduct preventive searches in certain places. Many rumours turned out to be unfounded or could not be confirmed. Machetes and baseball bats The three suspects appeared in court today for their role in the first violent incident, in Beverwijk. The victim had eaten with friends in Beverwijk on the day in question, writes regional broadcaster NH. When he left the restaurant, a group of boys approached him and asked him where he came from. As soon as it became clear that he came from Haarlem, he was surrounded, according to the victim's statement, by about twenty boys with machetes and baseball bats. He tried to run away. The boys took him to a nearby park where they severely assaulted him. Footage shown in court shows that the victim was seriously injured. He was undressed, hit and kicked several times in the head, including when he was unconscious. The violence was filmed and posted online with provocative texts such as: "3-0 for Beverwijk, you Haarlemmers are snot-noses" and "Look what I did to a Haarlemmer". The consequences are great for the young man from Haarlem. Images of him, partly naked, with his name attached, are circulating online. "He does not know who has seen these images or when they will suddenly resurface," the public prosecutor said. A statement from the victim was read aloud in court today by his father. The boy did not dare to come to the hearing. "I was 17, I had done nothing and yet I was attacked." He thinks back to that night every day. "There are days when I can't take it anymore." Heavy prison sentence According to the OM, it has been proven that the three suspects are guilty. One of the three, a 24-year-old man from Heemskerk, was the only one to admit that he was present at the violence, but said he no longer knew exactly what he had done. Whether he dealt blows, he says he cannot remember. "It was total chaos." The other two suspects, two men aged 22 and 25 from Beverwijk, according to the OM gave little or no clarity about their role. The public prosecutor holds them heavily responsible for this. "In this case, according to the OM, only a heavy prison sentence can be appropriate," the prosecutor said. The OM demands 24 months in prison, of which 12 months suspended, against the 24-year-old suspect. A 24-month unconditional prison sentence is demanded against the 22-year-old man and 18 months unconditional against the 25-year-old suspect. The OM also demands that all three be given a ban on entering Haarlem and a ban on contact with each other and the victim. Second violent incident When the second violent incident will be dealt with on the merits is not yet known. That took place a few days later in Haarlem and was probably a revenge action for the first incident. A 22-year-old from Heemskerk was abducted from Beverwijk that day. During the car ride to Haarlem he was tied up and a pistol was pushed into his mouth. He too was severely assaulted. Two adult men from IJmuiden and Vijfhuizen have been arrested for this. One of them is in custody, the other may await the trial in freedom but remains a suspect. A third suspect is on the run and is being sought.

title: Biography with 'camp lies' Willem Wilbrink (99) removed from sale
lead: The biography of 99-year-old Willem Wilbrink has been removed from sale. He ran into controversy last week over untruths about his wartime past and his time in the Dachau concentration camp. After a publication by Historisch Nieuwsblad, his story turned out to be highly unlikely. A spokesperson for Bol.com tells the NOS that the book titled Getekend voor het leven in Dachau en Indië by Laurens van Aggelen has been taken offline at the request of the publisher. That publisher, White Elephant Media from Arnhem, cannot be reached for comment this evening. Boekblad, the trade magazine for the book industry, says Bruna and Amazon have also blocked or removed the title. Wilbrink was a regular presence at commemorations of the Second World War. For example, last year he was at the National Commemoration of the 1945 Capitulations in Wageningen, where he sat next to <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity>. He also told stories about his past at schools. No evidence for claims He said that at 15 he was arrested for resistance work and deployed as a corpse carrier in the concentration camp near Munich. There, he claims, he saved forty people from death. He alleged that he took people who were due to be put in the crematorium but were still alive to the infirmary. Researchers examined his story and concluded there is no evidence for his statements. For example, he had no camp number, while in Dachau everything was recorded precisely. Wilbrink also wears decorations whose origin is unclear, such as a Polish 'hero title'. Other Dachau survivors had no memory of the stories Wilbrink had told. The Netherlands Dachau Committee had known about the untruths since 2024. The organisation had tried to prevent him from spreading them further. However, it was not actively communicated, because "we know better than anyone what a war trauma can do with the stories in your head", said chair Jaeger on Friday. He is convinced that Wilbrink believes he experienced his period in Dachau. The NIOD Institute for War, Holocaust and Genocide Studies said after the revelation that stories like Wilbrink's harm the truth about the Second World War. Ill-intentioned people can thereby sow doubt about what happened in the Holocaust, according to NIOD.

title: Another incident at a hairdresser's in Vlaardingen, possibly linked to 'hairdressers' war'
lead: In Vlaardingen there has been another incident at a hairdresser's. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, shots were fired at a shop on the Liesveld around 01.00 hours. No one was injured, and no one has been arrested yet. In Vlaardingen there have been several incidents at hairdressers. For example, last Sunday night a shop window was blown out by an explosive. The regional broadcaster Rijnmond reported last summer on a 'hairdressers' war' in the South Holland municipality. The reason for the attacks is unclear, but it is speculated that it may be related to unfair competition. The hairdressers targeted are said to be charging haircut prices that are below the usual rates, the AD wrote earlier this year.

title: More reports of labour exploitation and too few perpetrators punished, says rapporteur
lead: The number of reports of labour exploitation increased last year, says the <entity id="org:zbo-nationaal-rapporteur-mensenhandel-en-seksueel-geweld-tegen-kinderen">Nationaal Rapporteur Mensenhandel en Seksueel Geweld tegen Kinderen</entity> in its annual report . It mainly concerns exploitation of staff in hospitality and agriculture. "The number of victims of labour exploitation who came to light rose by 13 percent compared with the year before," says National Rapporteur <entity id="person:conny-rijken">Conny Rijken</entity>. "In hospitality, reports have doubled, and in agriculture and fisheries they have nearly tripled." Inhumane conditions There is labour exploitation when someone has to work under inhumane conditions and force, threat, violence, extortion, fraud or deception plays a role. Rijken: "Often it also involves substandard conditions, long working days and staff who are paid too little." The National Rapporteur sees the increase in reports in labour-intensive sectors. "In hospitality, people are easily kept out of sight, for example in the back of the kitchen or in the rooms, and there are few inspections during the night hours. In agriculture you see that staff often work in remote locations. We ask the whole of society to keep their eyes and ears open, but in places like that this is quite difficult." From various countries The victims of labour exploitation in the hospitality sector come from various countries, mainly Bangladesh, Turkey and Syria. In reports of labour exploitation in agriculture, forestry and fisheries, the number of victims with Romanian nationality is highest. Polish victims are the next most common. What does the National Rapporteur do? National Rapporteur Conny Rijken reports to <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> on the nature and scale of human trafficking and sexual violence against children in the Netherlands. The Rapporteur monitors the effects of policy in these areas and makes recommendations to improve the approach to human trafficking and sexual violence against children. Labour exploitation is a criminal offence in the Netherlands. According to the rapporteur, the approach to perpetrators is lagging behind. "Although there is increasing attention for the vulnerable position of people on the labour market and the risks of exploitation, in practice it still proves difficult to trace perpetrators and tackle them under criminal law," says Rijken. "In 2025 the Labour Inspectorate started 57 investigations. Only ten cases were handed over to the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>." Criticism from the Openbaar Ministerie The OM is critical of these statements by the National Rapporteur. "We bring many cases before the court and work hard on them," says a spokesperson. "Investigating labour exploitation is complex, time-consuming and must be done carefully." This week, two cases of labour exploitation came before the court. In Arnhem, a trial was held on Wednesday against a man and a woman suspected of exploiting staff at an Indian restaurant. In Amsterdam, the OM yesterday demanded years-long prison sentences against two women who allegedly exploited and abused another woman. "In addition, during an investigation it may turn out that there are insufficient leads to speak of labour exploitation," says the OM. The Openbaar Ministerie therefore points to administrative law instruments that the Labour Inspectorate has. "They regularly use administrative law and impose fines on employers, but that is then not included in this report." Fines instead of criminal law The Labour Inspectorate agrees. "The burden of proof is high, the cases are often complex and the work is very intensive. If we cannot pursue labour exploitation, we try other options in criminal law, such as fraud or money laundering. Then we can also tackle the abuses. But those actions are then not included in the rapporteur's figures. That does not do justice to our full work," says a spokesperson. The Labour Inspectorate and the OM work together. "We have a broad approach and we consider it successful. Through administrative law, we imposed fines on the gym in Amsterdam this year, for example." Fines are not enough For the National Rapporteur, this does not go far enough. "Fines are often imposed for unpaid wages, and then the victims are not classed as victims of human trafficking," says Conny Rijken. "Then they also do not receive the protection they need. We know that some companies factor those fines in, so you are not really stopping them that way."

title: Wake-up call 16/10: Cabinet announces infrastructure projects • Second day of EU summit
lead: Good morning! Today the cabinet will announce which infrastructure projects will receive funding in the coming years and which will not. And in Brussels the EU summit enters its second day. Among other things, support for Ukraine will be discussed there. First the weather: this morning it is dry with cloud patches and some sun. This afternoon it becomes cloudy from the west and will occasionally rain. It will be 18 to 20 degrees with a moderate to fairly strong wind turning to the northwest. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? The number of reports of labour exploitation increased last year, says the <entity id="org:zbo-nationaal-rapporteur-mensenhandel-en-seksueel-geweld-tegen-kinderen">Nationaal Rapporteur Mensenhandel en Seksueel Geweld tegen Kinderen</entity>. It mainly concerns exploitation of staff in hospitality and agriculture. There is labour exploitation when someone has to work under inhumane conditions and coercion, threat, violence, extortion, fraud or deception plays a role. The victims in hospitality mainly come from Bangladesh, Turkey and Syria. The reports in agriculture often concern Romanians. Other news from the night: And finally this: In Paris the General Conference on Weights and Measures decided that the leap second will disappear. In 1972 the leap second was introduced to make atomic clocks run precisely in sync with the rotation of the Earth. But computer systems suffer a lot from it, so it is now being abolished . Have a nice day!

title: Fight over new European budget is stuck
lead: An agreement on a new European budget is still a long way off. The leaders of the 27 EU countries tried at the European summit in Brussels last night to move closer together, but so far have not succeeded. "We face very difficult negotiations," said the German Chancellor Merz ahead of the talks. Once every seven years, all EU countries must reach an agreement on a new budget. Currently they are negotiating the EU budget for the period from 2028 up to and including 2034. The negotiations leading up to such a deal are always fierce. Richer countries such as the Netherlands, Germany and Sweden contribute more money than they receive back from the EU in subsidies and funds. These countries, the net payers, therefore want the budget not to become too bulky, because then costs rise. Germany leads this group. Cut or invest? Opposed to them is a group of seventeen countries that would like a more generous budget, because there would then be more money available for, among other things, their farmers and for developing disadvantaged regions. This group is led by Italy and Romania. Various proposals for a new budget have already been on the table. The European Commission kicked off the discussion in July with a proposal for a budget of just under 2,000 billion euros for a period of seven years. The countries are now discussing, after fierce opposition from the net payers, a variant that is about 150 billion euros lower. But that is still too much, thinks <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>. "The current proposal is not good enough to reach an agreement. The budget must be smaller and more modern to be ready for the future." Negotiating under high pressure: the discussion is under more time pressure than usual. Several countries hope to reach a political agreement this year. The chair of the European Council, Antonio Costa, has also expressed that wish. As chair, Costa has the role of steering the talks between the European leaders in the right direction. The time pressure is the result of a year full of elections that Europe faces. Between now and the end of 2027, Europeans in four of the five largest EU countries may go to the polls (Spain, France, Italy and Poland). The French presidential election in particular could make the negotiations even more difficult than they already are. Marine Le Pen, who leads the French polls, is campaigning for a much lower financial contribution from France to the EU. To give that message more weight, she earlier this week held a press conference in Brussels especially for this purpose. Tech or agriculture? The countries are not only squabbling over the size of the budget, but also over how they want to spend money. The group of Germany and the Netherlands advocates a 'modern budget', as they themselves call it. In it, more money should go to innovation, defence, tech and the energy transition, and less to agriculture and poorer regions. The proposal now on the table is admittedly less extensive than the original plan of the European Commission. But that reduction is partly concentrated in the themes that the Netherlands considers important, such as research and innovation. "We are still very far apart two and a half months before the end of the year," says Merz. "But that does not mean we cannot come up with solutions in the coming months." Negotiating marathon: the German is pushing for an agreement at the European summit on 17 December. If the leaders really want to reach agreement then, that summit could last several days and nights. "I will pack a few extra shirts for that summit," said the German Chancellor. French President Macron is also putting pressure on the negotiations. France wants a deal before the end of the year, because negotiating over EU billions during the French presidential election would be too sensitive. But not all leaders feel the need to hurry. "We will not sign an agreement that is not favourable, just to meet the deadline," said Italian Prime Minister Meloni earlier this week. Ultimately, all countries must agree on the new budget. On 13 November the EU leaders will meet again, this time in Dublin.

title: How supermarkets are preparing for new emergencies
lead: Power outage, internet disruption or hack: not only citizens are urged to prepare for an emergency with an emergency kit; <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will also have its contingency plans for food security ready in the coming year, 'just in case'. "We are moving as fast as we can on this," says <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">staatssecretaris Erkens</entity>. According to him, the finishing touches are being put on the National Crisis Plan for Food Security. Supermarkets and distribution centres also play a role in this. They are essential and vulnerable facilities, as became clear this week when Albert Heijn was hacked. Although food security was not at stake, the situation exposes the vulnerabilities of a system that in the Netherlands is set up as efficiently as possible, with as few stocks as possible. Emergency stocks: at present, supermarkets and distribution centres are not required to keep an emergency stock. But according to the cabinet's plans, those stocks should ultimately come. The question is how supermarkets see their role in this. State Secretary Erkens says he is in talks with supermarkets to see whether "we will also build emergency stocks of certain critical goods together, so that you can always fall back on that emergency stock in disruptive situations". Warehouses to buy: According to Marc Janssen, director of the Central Bureau for Food Retail (CBL), this will be difficult with existing buildings. "At least in the short term, because of storage capacity. If you want more of that, it means renovations." An alternative, according to him, is for the government to buy or build warehouses and fill them with the right products. "And that we make agreements in close consultation about logistics and distribution, via shops or, for example, neighbourhood centres." Erkens thinks existing distribution centres could also house emergency stocks. That would mean giving up some maximum efficiency. "But then you do have goods for two or three days in there to always absorb a first risk." That leaves the question: suppose you have such an emergency stock in a distribution centre, what do you do if a digital system fails or has to be shut down? The director of the CBL says the situation at Albert Heijn this week is a learning experience. "From an incident like this you can also learn that you need a plan B for more analogue food distribution, so that you are not solely dependent on digital systems." The range in such an emergency stock will always be more limited than what shops offer in normal times. According to Erkens, it is currently being mapped out which products are essential. "It is not a major national disaster if kiwis cannot be delivered, because you still have other kinds of fruit," says Erkens. "But if truly essential product categories drop out, then you do need to build up a stock of those together." Insufficient: earlier this month, researchers from the Clingendael Institute and Erasmus University warned that the Netherlands is insufficiently prepared for a disaster involving food security. One of their recommendations is to have supermarkets keep a dynamic emergency stock. That works as a buffer that moves along with normal sales and does not spoil. Ultimately, the best way to prepare is not at the supermarket but at home, says researcher Pieter Zwaan. His advice is therefore to have food at home for not three but eight days, advice the cabinet does not yet want to adopt officially. Zwaan acknowledges that this is not an option for everyone because of space or cost. "Then supermarkets can play a role, for example if it really is a crisis. They can then hand out products in a coordinated way."

title: Large fire in underground car park in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, 26-year-old man arrested
lead: A large fire broke out in an underground car park on Theodoor van Hoytemastraat in Amsterdam Nieuw-West at around 02.45 hours. At least 55 homes above the car park had to be evacuated, the Amsterdam-Amstelland Safety Region reports. The fire may have been set deliberately. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports that a 26-year-old man from Amsterdam has been arrested on suspicion of arson. The investigation team is looking into whether there was a conflict in a personal relationship. Around 05.15 hours the fire brigade had the fire under control. A lot of smoke was released: the residents have been taken in by a hotel nearby. It is unclear when they can return; first it must be determined how great the damage is exactly. A lot of smoke was released during the fire. The fire brigade deployed a lot of equipment and also used a firefighting robot to extinguish the blaze. The safety region reports that several people were checked on the spot by ambulance staff, but no one was taken to hospital. Grid operator Liander has cut off power to the building for safety reasons. As a result, some surrounding homes and businesses currently have no electricity either.

title: Belgian dentist arrested on sex offence charges, allegedly groped 71-year-old woman in the crotch
lead: A 46-year-old dentist from Kasterlee in Belgium is accused of sexually transgressive behaviour. In total there are complaints from seven patients, at least one of whom says she was touched in her genital area. Yesterday the man was arrested during a house search. He has since been released pending judicial investigation. He was released under strict conditions, and the dentist was also imposed a ban on practising. The police opened an investigation into the dentist after a 71-year-old woman filed a complaint last summer. According to her, the man sat against her crotch during a treatment. Three more complaints followed in September from women aged 28, 32 and 33. This week a 57-year-old woman also filed a complaint. Sensual rubbing The Belgian newspaper HLN spoke in early September with two women who filed complaints. Because of the ongoing police investigation, they had not yet been able to share their stories. "It was the seventh or eighth time I came to this dentist", says the 28-year-old woman. "Previously he also made bizarre remarks. He called me a pretty girl and said I have beautiful eyes. He actually looked at my eyes more than at my teeth." She never reported this. Until the dentist allegedly stroked her hair during a new check-up. "I didn't know what was happening. I felt myself tensing up completely and could no longer open my mouth properly. He then stopped removing tartar and started again, stroking my hair and my neck. He also rubbed my lips sensually, and even when he was working on my teeth again, he kept rubbing my cheeks with one little finger." The woman tells the newspaper that the man also pushed her head towards his genitals. "It was the worst half hour of my life." 'He groped my crotch' After the 28-year-old victim told her story, the 71-year-old woman did the same, because she had experienced similar things. She tells HLN that the dentist had always been very "friendly and touchy". During an appointment to fill a cavity, the woman was afraid of the anaesthetic, she says. "He kept rubbing my cheek to say I shouldn't be scared. Right after that he leaned over me and grabbed me from below. He groped me in my crotch." The 71-year-old tells the Belgian newspaper that after the shock she asked, "out of politeness", whether she had to pay. "He put his finger to his mouth and gestured that I could leave without paying. He clearly realised he had gone too far." No medical necessity "It appears that the dentist crossed boundaries during dental treatments and touched women in places that are not part of any treatment, so without any medical necessity", says Kristof Aerts of the Antwerp public prosecutor's office, part of the Public Prosecution Service. In the investigation, officers came across two complaints of sex offences against the same man several years ago. Nothing could be done with those complaints at the time due to a lack of evidence. Now that new possible victims have come forward, those incidents are also being reviewed. Belgian media report that the man is accused of violating sexual integrity, with the aggravating circumstance that as a dentist he had a relationship of authority or trust with his victims. The man is not accused of rape. The police do not rule out that more victims will come forward.

title: Donors to Trump's ballroom revealed: tech giants and the US ambassador to the Netherlands
lead: The US ambassador to the Netherlands, Joe Popolo, is contributing to the construction of the ballroom at the White House. Tech companies such as Nvidia and Apple have also opened their wallets, writes the newspaper The Washington Post, which has an overview of the main donors to the project. According to the newspaper, the leaked list of donors raises questions about conflicts of interest: half of all donations come from companies or prominent figures who have interests with the national government. Transparency about this is lacking. According to the newspaper, Ambassador Popolo and his wife transferred 1 million dollars at the end of last year. The donation came two months after the businessman was appointed ambassador to the Netherlands, at the end of October. He does not want to elaborate on this further to the newspaper. The list, with the status as of the end of September., includes the 67 contributions of 10.000 dollars (8900 euros) or more. Chipmaker Nvidia and Apple account for 25 million dollars, Google has pledged 22 million, and Microsoft and arms maker Lockheed Martin have committed 10 million. Amazon, like The Washington Post owned by Jeff Bezos, has set aside 5 million for the project. In addition, 25 million dollars came from a fund of the late business magnate Sheldon Adelson and his wife, which supports Israel and the Jewish people. He often donates generously to Republicans. Trump stated last year that he would also make a contribution to the prestige project. "It is being paid for 100 percent by me and a few of my friends", said the president, but according to the newspaper, there is nothing in the list to show a contribution from his side. Anonymity In total, 333 million dollars has been pledged for the ballroom, of which 77 million dollars comes from donors who indicated they wish to remain anonymous. Democratic politicians had previously tried in vain to obtain a list of donors and the circumstances of the donations. The money is managed by a fund, which has made agreements with the national government to keep the financiers secret. Political donations in the US are bound by rules, but non-profit organisations are generally not obliged to disclose their donors. It was already known that Nvidia had donated, but the company did not want to make the amount public. Now the chipmaker says it is proud of the donation. "As an American company, our support for the United States comes first, separate from business interests", a spokesperson said. It is one of the few donors who provides an explanation in the newspaper. Critics say the way funds are raised raises questions about the transparency of the donations and the influence of the financiers. The White House rejects the criticism. "The same critics who think there is a conflict of interest would also complain if the taxpayer had to pay for the much-needed renovations", a spokesperson said. For several donors, major interests were at stake in their relationship with Trump. For example, an investigation into the company of telecom director Charles Ergen (25 million) was dropped, and <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>-Trump had to judge whether Nvidia could export to China. The father of the Venezuelan-Italian Isabela Herrera (2,5 million) received a pardon from Trump in a bribery scandal. Incidentally, The Washington Post reported earlier this year that half of the construction costs are being paid with taxpayers' money. The total costs are said to have risen to 600 million dollars, whereas 400 million had previously been expected. Shelters Last year Trump ordered the eastern wing of the White House to be demolished. It housed, among other things, the residence's cinema and the offices of the first lady. Instead, a ballroom is to be built which, according to the president, will accommodate almost a thousand guests. He pointed out that the existing reception spaces do not meet requirements. A military bunker is to be built beneath the banquet venue, with, among other things, shelters and installations to withstand drone and missile attacks. For that part of the plan, Trump unsuccessfully tried to extract one billion dollars from Congress this year. According to the president, the bunker is important for national security. Besides a new ballroom at the White House, Trump has further construction plans in Washington. Watch more about this in this video:

title: Limburg named 'smartest region' in the world
lead: Limburg has been named the smartest region in the world by the Intelligent Community Forum (ICF). The international think tank presented the prize to Brightlands, four campuses in the province where research is carried out into, among other things, health, AI, more sustainable chemistry and food. The ICF is a worldwide federation of 200 cities and regions that support each other in the field of innovation. Each year the think tank publishes a ranking of smart communities based on factors such as economy and social development. The ICF therefore gave the honour this year to the Brightlands campuses. The jury praises Limburg for the cooperation between government, entrepreneurs and knowledge institutions through the Brightlands campuses. There is also praise for the transition Limburg underwent after the closure of the mines, half a century ago. "After the discovery of natural gas in 1959, the region lost not only jobs, but also economic security and hope", said ICF founder Robert Bell. The Brightlands in Limburg came into being in 2014 as an initiative of the <entity id="org:provincie-limburg">provincie Limburg</entity>, educational institutions and the regional business sector, writes L1 Nieuws. The campuses in <entity id="org:gemeente-maastricht">Maastricht</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-sittard-geleen">Sittard-Geleen</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-heerlen">Heerlen</entity> and Venlo each have their own specialisation in the fields of food, chemistry, health and digitalisation. Maastricht received a campus focused on health, linked to the academic hospital. Heerlen focused on data, with the offices of pension fund ABP and the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity>. Earlier this year it was renamed Data en AI. In Sittard-Geleen the materials campus was located on the Chemelot site. In Venlo the Brightlands campus focused on food security, making use of the infrastructure of the Floriade from 2012. <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity> Limburg had, with Brightlands, reached the last seven finalists. The other regions were Assai (Brazil), Bursa (Turkey), Hilliard (United States), Kingston (Canada), Las Rozas de Madrid (Spain) and Yunlin County (Taiwan). Last year the Canadian region of Durham was given the honour of most innovative region. In 2011 the Brainport region in Eindhoven won the title.

title: Man must lose eye after shooting in Roosendaal, suspect arrested
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested a man from Roosendaal suspected of shooting another man in the eye. The 44-year-old man was arrested last night by the Dienst Speciale Interventies, which is deployed against suspects who are dangerous with firearms. The victim was found on Wednesday evening in a home on Hoogstraat in Roosendaal. He had been shot in the face, presumably with a gas-powered weapon. The man also had wounds on his chest. He is expected to lose an eye and is still in hospital. According to witnesses, the two men had argued. According to the police, they quickly knew who the presumed shooter was and arrested him at home last night. He is suspected of attempted manslaughter. The weapon has not yet been found. A gas-powered weapon could be, for example, an air rifle or a CO2 pistol. Some gas-powered weapons are legal, but that does not apply to, for example, gas-powered weapons that closely resemble real firearms.

title: Rotterdam neighbourhood area ban extended to prevent unrest from returning
lead: Mayor Schouten of <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> has extended the area ban for part of the De Esch neighbourhood by three months. "I am doing this to further reduce the attraction of the area", the mayor writes in a letter to the council. She also wants to prevent the nuisance from immediately returning after 23 October, when the area ban would initially expire. The new area ban does not apply the whole week, but from Thursday through Sunday from 23.00 to 05.00 hours. On the other days the area is kept closely monitored by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and boa's. "Should the situation nevertheless deteriorate, I will take additional measures where necessary", Schouten writes. The new area ban is in force until 23 January 2027. Concrete blocks Over the past years, residents of the Rotterdam neighbourhood, where just over 4000 people live, have had to deal with nuisance. Especially at night there were street races, drug use and prostitution. People who do not live in De Esch came to the neighbourhood, according to police research. The municipality had earlier already placed concrete blocks, tightened supervision and spoken with those causing nuisance. Those measures did not help enough. Eventually, in July, a unique measure was deployed: an area ban for a large part of the neighbourhood. For three months, between 23.00 and 05.00 hours, only people with a good reason were allowed to stay in the neighbourhood. Those are mainly residents and people who work there. 'Situation in De Esch considerably improved' According to the mayor, the measure has helped to reduce the nuisance. The number of nuisance reports to both police and municipality has fallen sharply. Residents and the neighbourhood council also indicate they hardly experience any nuisance at night anymore. "Over the past three months the situation has been continuously monitored, and the police further tightened supervision in the designated area", Schouten writes. "This has led to the situation in De Esch being considerably improved." When the area ban had just come into effect, people who had no business in the area still regularly came to it. In total, 140 people received an official report, 23 of them on the first evening. The municipality suspects this was because the area ban was not yet known to everyone, according to regional broadcaster Rijnmond. Different solution Mayor Schouten says she realises that an area ban is a far-reaching measure that cannot be extended indefinitely. That is why the municipality wants to work together with local residents to investigate whether a more sustainable solution can be devised. "In the recent period, thought has been given to sustainable alternative measures that could be deployed. In the period up to 23 January 2027, this process will be continued, and the neighbourhood council and residents will also be involved to consider how a sustainable solution can be reached."

title: Families and businesses near Lelystad Airport must leave due to defence expansion
lead: Four farms and six businesses must disappear, because the Ministry of Defence needs more space around Lelystad Airport. The families and businesses concerned were told this today. "I understand very well that this is a worthless message," says <entity id="person:derk-boswijk">staatssecretaris Boswijk</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity>), who will also visit these people later today. Defence says it will help them through "careful contact and personal guidance". This could involve, for example, a move to another location or compensation. According to Boswijk, Defence needs the space because the F-35 fighter jets will have to fly more often. "That means you also have to train and do maintenance more," says the state secretary. "Those support units need physical space." Lelystad Airport is becoming even larger than expected due to defence goals. At first it was 150 hectares, which has now become 240 hectares. 40 hectares of that is needed to make the runway longer. The airport does not yet have a nature permit, which is needed to be able to use the airport. That application is still being prepared. "We cannot wait for that and only then do this," says Boswijk. "That would take too long." Boswijk does not expect that more homes and businesses that have to disappear due to defence expansions will follow soon. "But I cannot rule it out either, because the situation in the world is unpredictable."

title: TU Delft may not reserve study places for women
lead: <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">Minister Letschert</entity> of Education does not allow TU Delft to reserve a minimum number of places for female students for the Aerospace Engineering programme. The <entity id="org:zbo-college-voor-de-rechten-van-de-mens">College voor de Rechten van de Mens</entity> had advised that it should do so, but the ministry will not go along with this. That is a setback for the university. It wanted to introduce a quota to increase the structurally low intake of women on the programme. Last June, the College voor de Rechten van de Mens approved plans for this preferential policy, partly because according to the college it had only limited consequences for male students and served a legitimate aim. A last resort Minister Letschert says she supports the university's goal, but sees a quota as a last resort. The minister also describes introducing a quota for women at the university as time-consuming: because in current practice it is only possible to set requirements based on quality and not on sex, the Higher Education Act must be amended. Furthermore, an amendment of the law could open a debate about all sorts of other forms of preferential treatment, according to the ministry. Dominated by men The minister says she wants to achieve the university's goal in other ways within the current legislation. Among other things, by rolling out programmes to encourage women to take up jobs and courses in technology. A parliamentary motion was also adopted this month calling on <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> to investigate how women can be attracted to and retained in male-dominated sectors. Henri Werij, Dean of Aerospace Engineering at TU Delft, says he is disappointed by the minister's decision. "Ever since I took up the position of dean almost ten years ago, we have been working hard to get more women into the programme. Despite all the measures we have taken so far, it is only happening slowly. For real change, this quota is simply necessary."

title: Fireworks show at Erasmusbrug Rotterdam this New Year's Eve after all
lead: There will be a major fireworks show at the Erasmus Bridge in Rotterdam after all this New Year's Eve. The new Rotterdam city council had originally wanted a show with drones and lasers, but there is too little time to organise that. Moreover, it was not feasible within the set budget. Pro, D66, VVD, CDA and Volt agreed in their coalition agreement that from now on every New Year's Eve there will be a drone and laser show at the Erasmus Bridge. No more traditional and spectacular fireworks, as at the National Fireworks Show. A drone show is more environmentally friendly, the parties believe. The city council wants to set aside half a million euros per year for it. Too little time and money. Even so, a major fireworks show will be organised for the coming end-of-year celebration. Alderman Nunnely concludes after talks with experts that there is now too little time to organise an alternative show, the regional broadcaster Rijnmond reports. Moreover, a drone and laser show is not possible within the reserved budget, she writes in a letter to the municipal council. "Given the introduction of the national fireworks ban from 2026, it is desirable to offer a good alternative for consumer fireworks this year at least." To make the fireworks show possible, Rotterdam will spend roughly the same as last year, according to the alderman: that was then exactly 816,194 euros. That is therefore well over 300,000 euros more than the budget. Nunnely can cover the extra costs because the municipality is probably spending less this year than expected. From next year the executive board wants a more sustainable show. "The national fireworks show has grown into a widely attended and traditional event for many Rotterdammers and visitors," the executive board writes.

title: Billions for aging bridges and locks, at the expense of several large projects
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is allocating 18 billion euros for maintenance and renewal of aging bridges, roads, locks and other infrastructure. A large part of that amount is being taken from planned projects for which money had already been reserved. Those projects will therefore be postponed indefinitely. One of the prominent projects receiving a lot of money is the Haringvliet bridge, which connects the Hoeksche Waard with Goeree-Overflakkee. That bridge, which 66,000 people drive over every day, is in poor condition and must largely be renewed. Dry feet A considerable sum (2.3 billion euros) also goes to the pumping station in IJmuiden, which is very outdated. Renewal is important because that pumping station, according to the cabinet, keeps "dry feet" for four million people. In total, 175 roads, locks, bridges, viaducts and tunnels will be renewed or maintained. Most of them were built in the 1950s, 60s and 70s, and at many locations the steel and concrete, for example, have had their best days. These are some of the projects for which money has been set aside: "We face the biggest renewal task ever, it is time for a new reconstruction of our infrastructure", says <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> of Infrastructure. According to him, it is essential to ensure that the Netherlands remains protected against water and at the same time "accessible and economically strong". The selection mainly considered preservation of existing infrastructure and safety. The cabinet is also allocating money for improvements to the rail network. A number of viaducts that the high-speed line crosses between Leiden and Hoofddorp will be tackled, so that trains can run faster there: 300 kilometres per hour instead of the current 120 km/h. Furthermore, the money for the Nedersaksenlijn remains in place, more money goes to rail expansion in Meppel, and there is also a large amount for the "rollout of the European train safety system" to make the railway safer. The cabinet gives priority to renovation, but also opens its wallet for making new housing development areas accessible. Extra money is coming for four large new projects in Alkmaar, Apeldoorn, Helmond and Hengelo/Enschede. Pain But as mentioned, some projects are also being postponed to finance the above. "That of course hurts", the cabinet acknowledges in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. "But this is the only way to carry out the major maintenance task." Money is being taken, among other things, from the RandstadRail between The Hague, Rotterdam and Zoetermeer and from the Rotterdam metro network. That money was meant to expand capacity. Furthermore, the widening of the lock at Kornwerderzand in Friesland will not go ahead after all. That also yields hundreds of millions. The bridges there, at the end of the Afsluitdijk, will still be replaced. The cabinet is withdrawing money from the following places, among others: In Amsterdam, part of the long-running Zuidasdok project is postponed. The project includes, among other things, the partial tunnelling of the A10 motorway at the Zuidas. For the northern section of the project there is, for now, no money. Regarding road projects, the cabinet is also taking money from the A27 between Zeewolde and Eemnes. That will not be widened for the time being. The A28 between Hoogeveen and Amersfoort, the N33 between Eemshaven and Appingedam, and the ring road around Utrecht will also not be improved for now. And Ameland is also out of luck. Because of the continually silting shipping channel to the mainland, people have been talking for ten years about a better optimal shipping connection. The minister also needs that reserved 250 million euros elsewhere. Water quality and drought control Furthermore, the cabinet is taking hundreds of millions away from improving water quality and from a programme to prevent drought. That is striking because water quality in the Netherlands is under pressure and drought is becoming an ever greater problem. For all projects that are not being carried out now, the cabinet emphasises that they are "not off the radar". Whether the House of Representatives accepts this will become clear within a few weeks. After the autumn recess the House will debate the plans. No doubt some parties have a different selection in mind than the cabinet, but whether they will get a majority for it is still the question. Moreover, says minister Karremans, the House must then also explain how it should be paid for. "If they want it differently, they must say so. But then they must also ensure they get it financed."

title: After years of discussion, financial arrangement for KNIL widows after all
lead: The widows and widowers of civil servants and military personnel who served in the Netherlands Indies government during the Second World War will nevertheless receive a financial compensation. <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has decided this after years of political discussion. The arrangement supplements the 2015 arrangement for the KNIL soldiers and civil servants themselves. It concerns compensation for lost salary. The arrangement is only for the widows and widowers, not for their heirs. Those concerned must submit an application themselves. This can be done from 1 February 2027. After the application, individual archival research will be conducted to see whether the applicant qualifies for the arrangement. There are no files or archives in which this information is centrally stored. "I fully realize that full restitution can never be offered to these widows and widowers", says <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">minister Sterk</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">VWS</entity>. "What happened to them during and after the Second World War can never be reversed or undone." Japanese occupation Civil servants, teachers and military personnel in the Dutch East Indies received no salary during the Japanese occupation. The discussion about this began directly after the war. But the Dutch government was not legally obliged to pay the back salaries and held out. It took until 2015 before KNIL soldiers received compensation of 25,000 euros from the government for their back salary. At that time, the then cabinet reached an agreement with Indisch Platform 2.0, which supported Indian and Moluccan soldiers. Around 600 people registered for this arrangement.

title: Podcast De Stemming: Dolphins, a pincushion and an asylum operetta
lead: Minister Van den Brink of Asylum went again to <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> to defend his asylum plans. This time it went a bit better than a few months ago. But Van den Brink immediately got another problem, because JA21 suddenly sets tough demands on asylum. Meanwhile, VVD leader Yesilgöz is not entirely comfortable with her own base, and the US once again came under fire over the International Criminal Court. De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister. You can also find all previous episodes there. Just like on all other well-known podcast channels. About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings (EenVandaag, AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) go through the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Want to respond? Email destemming@nos.nl.

title: US sanctions against the ICC already putting ABN Amro in a tight spot
lead: For six months, the Netherlands and the European Union tried to persuade the United States through diplomacy to call off the planned sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). But although the sanctions are only due to take effect in April, time is already running short in practice. Companies that provide services to the ICC fear the long arm of US justice if they still do business with the court in half a year. ABN Amro is in a difficult position because of the situation, RTL Z already reported yesterday. The ICC has a bank account at ABN Amro to receive donations, for example, as stated on the website of the court, which is based in The Hague. When asked, ABN Amro says it never comments on individual clients. But the bank adds that it always abides by applicable laws and regulations. Major consequences If the bank, still 20 percent state-owned, listens to <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and does not drop the ICC as a client, the consequences could be enormous. In the US, ABN Amro still holds a US banking license, for a division that processes transactions on the financial markets for large traders. This so-called clearing bank accounted for 20 percent of ABN Amro's annual profit last year. Through that US banking license, ABN Amro is in the grip of US justice. ING experienced this, for example, when the division in Caribbean Netherlands transferred money to Cuba and Iran. That led to a huge US fine for the Dutch bank. Earlier incidents at Dutch banks due to US sanctions: Prime Minister Jetten had initially used firm language at the United Nations General Assembly in New York to make clear that the US must keep its hands off the ICC. After the sanctions were nevertheless announced shortly afterwards, he hoped that in the meantime "a suitable solution" for the ICC could be found with the US. Patience Yesterday the American ambassador in the Netherlands made clear that there is little to talk about. "Our patience with the court was met with escalation instead of reform, and dawdling instead of decisiveness. President Donald Trump has said: 'Not anymore", wrote Ambassador Joe Popolo in a letter to the editor in the FD. Popolo states that the sanctions against the ICC will only be lifted if "every threat to American citizens is neutralized". In other words: if the court officially records that it will not pursue Americans. The officials in The Hague are meanwhile keeping quiet about the ICC. Behind the scenes, it is clear that they are mainly looking for a way for the court to keep functioning if the US sanctions are nevertheless imposed. How the ICC should work without cloud services, email and bank accounts is for now a black diplomatic gap. The US has been targeting the ICC for years:

title: Community service for rapper Appa after 'doxing' of Jewish woman and journalist
lead: Rapper Appa has been found guilty of intimidating a Jewish woman and a journalist from NOS. He did so by 'doxing' them, in other words by publicly sharing their personal information. The 43-year-old rapper receives forty hours of community service, half of which is suspended with a probation period of two years. Earlier, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had requested sixty hours of community service. The judge arrived at a lighter sentence because he had never before been prosecuted for such an action. The police judge in Utrecht speaks of serious offences, from which the two victims suffered greatly. "Both were approached in unpleasant ways by people who were stirred up by the posts." The rapper was acquitted of a third case. According to the judge, rapper Appa, with his posts on social media, infringed on the privacy of the victims and caused feelings of insecurity. Actions of this kind can lead followers or others to break the law and commit acts. The judge holds this against him, according to the ruling. What is doxing? Doxing is the public sharing of sensitive personal data in order to intimidate. Since 1 January 2024 this has been prohibited and punishable by law. According to the government, publicly disclosing personal data is very common and often has serious consequences for the victims. Doxing is often aimed at journalists, politicians, judges or care workers. In March 2024, the personal details of relatives of Israeli soldiers in the Netherlands were spread online. They subsequently faced hatred and threats. One of the instigators was rapper and activist Appa, who on his Instagram account shared photos and personal details of at least one Israeli-Dutch woman subject to conscription in Israel and of this woman's mother. In doing so, he posted hateful texts and the call 'fight!'. NOS journalist A NOS journalist who wrote two articles on this matter then also became a victim of doxing by the rapper. He posted a photo of her with text including "and that is why you, just like that terrorist, will be exposed. (..) see what you do." The police judge rejected the defendant's defence in both cases. He argued that he only wanted to gather information about the Jewish woman for a possible lawsuit against her. In the case of the NOS journalist, he wanted to correct reporting that he considered incorrect. Fear and nuisance But the judge concludes that the 43-year-old artist must have realised that his conduct would lead to fear and nuisance for the victims. In the case of the journalist, he moreover points out how doxing "seriously hinders" the practice of the profession and her fear is fuelled. "We are very satisfied with the ruling," responds Wilma Haan, deputy editor-in-chief of NOS Nieuws. "We are glad that the judge, in addition to the personal burden the victims, including our colleague, have suffered from this, has also paid attention to the chilling effect on journalism. It must never become normal for journalists to be personally intimidated because of their work." It is not yet known whether the convicted man will appeal; he has two weeks to decide.

title: Fewer trains around Utrecht due to farewell drinks for train traffic controllers
lead: Since 14.30 hours, fewer trains have been running around Utrecht due to a shortage of train traffic controllers. The shortage is partly due to a farewell drinks event for "two highly valued colleagues" at ProRail. That is what a spokesperson for the rail infrastructure manager told NOS after reports by RTL Nieuws. Because of the farewell drinks, ProRail did not manage to get enough staff on duty. As a result, until about halfway through the evening, fewer trains run on the routes Amersfoort - Den Haag, Rotterdam - Utrecht and Bodegraven - Utrecht. The autumn holiday also contributes to the failure to make the work roster work: many colleagues are on holiday and there is a lot of sickness. ProRail says it has "done everything" this week to get the planning sorted. The spokesperson says it finds this "incredibly annoying" for passengers. The spokesperson does not know whether an attempt was made to postpone the drinks. ProRail has been struggling with a shortage of train traffic controllers for some time. The company has difficulty finding new staff and moreover cannot easily train traffic controllers itself, according to the latest annual report. Train traffic controllers monitor train traffic 24 hours a day and intervene in the event of an emergency. Without them, no trains can run.

title: Dutch cloud sector demands clarity over server seizure at US request
lead: The Dutch trade association for the cloud and internet sector, Dutch Cloud Community (DCC), has serious concerns about a server that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> seized this week in Amsterdam-Oost. That seizure was at the request of American authorities. It concerns a server of the Italian anti-capitalist and anti-fascist internet service provider Autistici/Inventati (A/I), which was located at the Amsterdam Science Park. According to DCC, the course of events seems to create a blank cheque for the US to request data, without it being clear whether an independent Dutch legal review preceded it. The trade association says it has sent a brandbrief to the police to get clarity on the legal basis for the seizure and the course of events. "Without a clear Dutch review, the Netherlands is losing the trust of the organisations and companies that store their data here", the organisation says.
