Due to the strong wind not all runways are available and fewer aircraft can take off and land, says a spokesperson for Schiphol. Passengers should therefore take cancellations and delays into account. Until 17.00 this afternoon it concerns nearly eighty cancelled flights, according to data on the Schiphol website. It mainly concerns European flights, for example to Paris, Manchester, Hamburg and Stockholm. Flights to Schiphol have also been cancelled, although a number is missing. On the website of the Stockholm airport, for example, it can be read that a KLM flight to Amsterdam has been cancelled. Nuisance and damage Last evening and overnight the strong wind, caused by the low-pressure system Boelo, led to nuisance and damage in several places, including fallen trees. For example, a tree fell onto the railway between Lochem (Gelderland) and Goor (Overijssel). No trains are running there this morning. In central Amsterdam a tree fell onto a moving car. The driver remained unharmed. Boelo Boelo is the second storm of this season after Austen. It is one of seven names that the weather institute <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> provided, selected from the names that were submitted. The East Groningen name Boelo was submitted by a Groninger "in whose family this name has existed for generations", the KNMI reports.

title: Will Brazilians choose Lula after all, or will the Bolsonaros expand their power further?
lead: The second and decisive round of the election in Brazil today is a tense contest between sitting leftist president Lula da Silva (80) and radical right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (45), son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro. But whoever becomes Brazil's new president after today, the power of the Bolsonaro family has already grown considerably. After the first round of the election three weeks ago, not only Bolsonaro's radical right Partido Liberal ( PL) gained considerably in the National Congress, several family members also personally won seats. The wife of former president Bolsonaro, Michelle, gained a seat in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Bolsonaro's son Carlos also won a seat there. The former president's youngest son, Jair Renan, won in the Chamber of Deputies. And Jair Bolsonaro's younger brother, Renato, also won a seat there. What does this mean when so much power lies with one family? Military dictatorship Former journalist Ricardo Moraes (74) experienced up close the repression that prevailed during the military dictatorship in Brazil, which lasted from 1964 to 1985. "There was no freedom back then. During my student days the military had all the power and they had surrounded our university. They wanted to arrest the students because we were demonstrating. We wanted free elections and a return to democracy. I then fled and went into hiding for a while," he recounts. With the prospect of a possible victory for Flávio Bolsonaro and the strong political power of his family, he is worried about democracy in his country. Bolsonaro has announced that he will pardon his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, if he wins. He also wants to amend the constitution and carry out reforms within the Supreme Court. "That is why Lula must win, because it is dangerous if this family becomes so powerful, they could ruin everything in Brazil," says Vinicius Portella, the 25-year-old son of Ricardo Moraes. Electric shocks He grew up with his father's stories and photos from the dictatorship era. After his studies Ricardo Moraes became a journalist and worked for Brazilian newspapers. Press censorship prevailed and he was eventually arrested by the army and tortured for ten days. "I still remember how I was forcibly brought into one of the military's torture centres. I was put on a chair, the so-called dragon chair. A wooden chair, but the seat was covered with metal plates. I received electric shocks. An unbearable pain through my whole body," Moraes says. It is his father's experiences that made son Vinicius aware from an early age of the value of democracy. That was put at stake again in Brazil four years ago, after the 2022 elections. Storming of government buildings Bolsonaro then narrowly lost to the current president Lula da Silva, but refused to accept his defeat. Together with a number of senior officers he planned a coup, which was eventually called off at the last moment, as the Federal <entity id="org:politie">Politie</entity> discovered in an in-depth investigation. Supporters of Bolsonaro then stormed government buildings in the capital Brasilia and caused damage at, among other places, the Supreme Court. They received heavy sentences for this. Bolsonaro himself was eventually sentenced to 27 years in prison, which he is serving under house arrest for health reasons. A lot at stake That president Lula da Silva lost the first round was a shock for Vinicius. In all the polls Lula was actually ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro. "But we have now been woken up, because a lot is at stake. Young people are campaigning en masse. We talk in groups of five or six people with people on the street who are still undecided about who to vote for. Hopefully we can get them to vote for Lula," he says. Whether that will succeed is still an open question. Although Lula rose in the polls in recent days, Bolsonaro still appears to be the favourite of many Brazilians. They have placed their hopes precisely on the Bolsonaros and want to be rid of Lula and the Workers' Party. The result of the Brazilian election is likely to be known around 23.00 (Dutch time).

title: Groups of minors were deliberately out to cause unrest and violence, says Walibi
lead: The disturbances at the Walibi amusement park during the Fright Nights were, according to Walibi, caused by young people who had the deliberate aim of creating unrest. Last night groups of young people came to blows with each other and vandalism was committed. Footage circulating on social media shows groups fighting with each other and throwing things. The mobile unit (ME) was deployed to restore calm. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> says when asked that no one has been arrested. People involved in the disturbances were, according to Walibi, taken outside with the help of the police. Calm then returned, the amusement park in Biddinghuizen reports. Walibi had specifically taken new safety measures this year to prevent disturbances like last year. Fights also broke out then. In the past, costumed actors have also had to deal with violence and boundary-crossing behaviour from visitors. Minors The disturbances of last night are, according to Walibi, mostly the work of "minors who deliberately come to provoke in places where many people gather, as we unfortunately also see happening in other parts of the Netherlands and Europe". The Fright Nights is an annual Halloween event that draws thousands of visitors. There are haunted houses and Scare Zones where costumed actors try to frighten visitors. Last night 20,000 visitors attended the sold-out event. Scare Zones closed The mood turned last night one hour before closing time, at 22.00 hours. The incidents began at the main stage by the Ferris wheel and moved toward the Hall of Fame at the entrance. Because of the fights, the Scare Zones were closed. "The emergency lighting came on and the actors were taken to the back," says the spokesperson. Walibi's Fright Nights continue today and next weekend. The spokesperson says when asked that the event is going ahead as normal today. When asked whether actors have withdrawn and visitors have asked for their money back, the spokesperson cannot give an answer. What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? title: Sinkholes in Rotterdam Crooswijk caused by underground leak
lead: Sinkholes have formed in pavements and streets at several locations in the Rotterdam neighbourhood of Crooswijk due to a water leak underground. According to the safety region, the leak has also flooded the crawl spaces of homes. The problems are occurring on the Crooswijksestraat and the Hendrikstraat. Due to the leak, sand is washing away, which has created the holes in the streets and pavements. The streets have been cordoned off. Drinking water shut off. Water has been cut off at several homes on the Crooswijksestraat so that water company Evides can repair the leak. The water in the crawl spaces must first be pumped out before the leak can be repaired, the safety region reports. Once that has happened, the homes will be supplied with drinking water again. Evides cannot yet estimate how long this shutoff will last. The work is expected to be finished this evening, writes regional broadcaster Rijnmond. The safety region advises residents to turn off all their taps. "This prevents possible leaks when you have water again."

title: Voters queue for hours at embassy in The Hague: 'Want a new future for Serbia'
lead: Lines are long at the Serbian embassy in The Hague due to the parliamentary elections in Serbia. Eligible voters can vote at the embassy and thereby help determine whether autocratic leader Aleksandar Vucic must step down after more than ten years in power. The long queue in The Hague does not bother voters. "I waited three hours and it was worth it," says a woman. "If it were necessary, I would do it again." A mother and daughter from Nootdorp think some people may have to wait four or five hours. "But nobody considers that a problem," says the woman who is voting for family and friends in Serbia "who are still fighting hard for freedom of expression and more". Until ten years ago she lived in the Serbian capital Belgrade. "I hope that everyone I love in Serbia no longer has to be afraid or uncertain about his or her future." Although a man from Rotterdam finds every election important, this one is especially special for him. "I am so looking forward to these elections. This is now our only chance for a new future for Serbia." Voters from all over the Netherlands The voters have come to The Hague from all over the Netherlands. A woman from Groningen is also in line. "I travelled for three hours and am now standing in line for three hours." She wants change in her homeland. "Serbia is so corrupt now." A woman from Apeldoorn who sat on the train for an hour and a half agrees. "Young people eventually see no future in Serbia because of the corruption and cronyism." As a result they leave, she says. "Then a country empties out, and that is good for no one." Besides in the Netherlands, lines also form in, for example, Switzerland and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Early elections The 56-year-old Vucic held several ministerial posts on behalf of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) before he became prime minister in 2014. In 2017 he became president of Serbia. Last June he announced his resignation. A tactical step, because next year Vucic's second and final term as president would end. Vucic hopes that with early parliamentary elections he can become prime minister again, and thus stay in power after all. Long queues in The Hague: Opponents of Vucic have been calling for his resignation for more than a year and a half. The protests started after part of the roof of the station in the Serbian city of Novi Sad collapsed. Sixteen people died as a result. Demonstrators blame the accident on corruption within the government. Opponents also say that Vucic intimidates political opponents and restricts press freedom. Under Vucic's rule, Serbia has made hardly any progress toward joining the European Union. Student list Today's parliamentary elections are, according to polls, a neck-and-neck race between Vucic's SNS and the Student List, a party that emerged from the protests against the current <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. Turnout is so far higher than at the previous elections in 2023. At 14.00 hours, 46.4 percent of eligible voters had cast their vote, reports the Serbian public broadcaster <entity id="org:zbo-registratiecommissie-tandheelkundige-specialismen">RTS</entity> . In 2023 turnout at the same time was 32.2 percent. Long queues at polling stations in Serbia: What do you think of the NOS app and website? What are we doing well? What could be better? We are curious about your opinion. Fill in the survey via this link .

title: Woman seriously injured after assault at party in Amsterdam
lead: In Amsterdam, a woman was seriously assaulted during an argument early yesterday morning. That is reported by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The woman suffered serious injuries and has been taken to hospital. The argument broke out around 05.40 hours between two women at a party on Rhôneweg in Amsterdam. A man then struck one of the women on the head with an object. The police arrived on the scene because of the unrest that then arose. The suspect was able to flee at that time. The police are still searching for him. He is a tall man of about 30 years old with a dark skin tone. He was wearing a white T-shirt and dark denim jeans, according to the police. A police spokesperson tells NOS that it was not a party of the Amsterdam Dance Event. What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? title: Cyclist dies in Amsterdam after a tree falls on him
lead: In Amsterdam a cyclist died today after a tree fell on him. The investigation into the identity of the victim is still ongoing, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> told NOS. The man died on the Sloterweg in the Nieuw-West district. It is not yet clear what time the accident happened. Emergency services received a report at the end of the afternoon from someone who had seen the man lying under a fallen tree. On arrival, the police found a dead man. Storm Earlier this weekend, two trees also fell onto moving cars in the capital due to stormy weather that moved over Amsterdam. A motorist was injured in the process, the other had no injuries. The Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE) also suffered from the strong wind. The festival Into the Woods at the NDSM wharf, for example, was stopped early because of the wind.

title: Woman found dead in apartment in Eindhoven, man arrested
lead: In an apartment in Eindhoven a woman was found dead this afternoon under suspicious circumstances. A man suspected of involvement in her death has been arrested. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> rules out that the woman died a natural death, says the spokesperson for the Oost-Brabant unit. The suspect was arrested "near the apartment". A detective team and forensic investigators are at the home this evening to carry out an investigation. The police received a report around 16.30 hours. The deceased woman was subsequently found in the apartment on Van Kinsbergenstraat in the north of Eindhoven. Whether the suspect and the victim knew each other, the police cannot say in the interest of the investigation. The police may have more information tomorrow.

title: Search for watersports enthusiast near Scheveningen halted due to darkness
lead: Around Scheveningen and Kijkduin there was a large search for a missing watersports enthusiast. It is presumably a surfer or kiter. The search was stopped at the beginning of the evening. Just after 14.00 hours an alarm was raised with the emergency services control room about the missing watersports enthusiast. Since then, searches have been carried out on land, at sea and in the air, in the area between Kijkduin and the pier at Scheveningen. "Despite the enormous effort of the emergency services, the missing person has unfortunately not yet been found," the Haaglanden Veilig safety region reports. "The conditions make it too dangerous for the rescuers to continue searching. The strong wind and high waves make the search difficult. Now that it is dark, it is impossible to continue a safe search." The search will resume tomorrow morning. A spokesperson for the Coastguard tells Omroep West that the missing person was part of a group and went out of sight. The weather was particularly stormy in the search area, with gusts up to 80 kilometres per hour.

title: Former president Vucic admits defeat: student movement wins Serbian elections
lead: The Studentenlijst in Serbia has won the most votes in the parliamentary elections. That is what former president Vucic says based on an exit poll. He thereby acknowledges his defeat. "We do not have final results yet, but based on a sample it is clear that we have lost these elections. The Studentenlijst has won. They will get between 135 and 140 seats, while we will win 105", said Vucic. These are the most exciting elections in Serbia in a long time, in which a large-scale student protest movement, the Studentenlijst, is taking on the autocratic leader Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). In Belgrade people are celebrating: cars drive through the streets honking and people are shouting "victory" and "he's finished". The spokesperson for the Studentenlijst said that "the voice of the people has been heard". "Tonight we celebrate the victory, tomorrow we build the future", he added. Correspondent Thijs Kettenis is in Belgrade and is barely audible right after Vucic admitted his defeat: The voters have turned out in record numbers. Turnout stood at 67.6 percent at 19.00 hours, according to polling agencies and observer organisations CeSID and Ipsos. That is the highest turnout since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992. There were long queues at polling stations across Serbia and at embassies abroad today. According to news agency Reuters, Vucic also had to wait almost two hours to be able to vote. He stepped down in September after nine years as president and wanted to become prime minister now in order to stay in power. The student movement had called on people to vote early today, because the party feared that Vucic would try to stay in power with the help of fraud. Early in the evening, reports circulated of violent incidents at a number of polling stations. The European ambassador to Serbia expressed his concern on X. "We call on all parties to remain calm, act responsibly and refrain from violence and provocations. We also call on the competent authorities to guarantee the safety of everyone involved in the electoral process", he wrote. Images also circulated on social media of groups of men dressed in black marching through the capital Belgrade. The riot police have been deployed at various locations in the centre. Mass protests The Studentenlijst grew out of two years of mass protests against Vucic. These began when part of the station in the city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing sixteen people. The renovation of the station was reportedly poorly carried out by companies with close ties to the SNS, according to the criticism. In recent weeks, reports have emerged that civil servants, their friends and their families have been pressured to prove that they vote for Vuvic and his SNS.

title: Polling stations in Brazil open two hours longer after intervention by Supreme Court
lead: Polling stations in Brazil will remain open two hours longer today for the decisive round of the presidential election, the Supreme Court has decided. The reason is problems voters are experiencing with transport to polling stations. Originally, polling stations would close at 17.00 Brazilian time (21.00 Dutch time). Voting has now been extended on the order of the Supreme Court until 19.00 Brazilian time (23.00 Dutch time). In view of the ruling, the highest Brazilian electoral court (TSE) decided to temporarily halt the processing and publication of the interim results. Brazil votes electronically. This is at stake in these elections: The decision of the Supreme Court was taken by judge Cristiano Zanin and came after requests from the two presidential candidates Lula da Silva (80) and Flávio Bolsonaro (45). The team of the current left-wing president Lula said that voters in nine states were hindered by problems with buses from casting their vote in time. His opponent, the far-right Flávio Bolsonaro, submitted a similar request to the Supreme Court due to heavy rainfall in southern Brazil, where flooding made transport to polling stations difficult. According to the judge, extending voting by two hours was justified "given the seriousness of the reported facts". Neck-and-neck race Candidate Lula is trying to become president for the fourth time and is locked in a neck-and-neck race with his ideological counterpart Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro surprisingly won the first round of the presidential election, while Lula led in the polls. Because Bolsonaro did not obtain an absolute majority, a second round was needed to determine a winner. The result determines whether Brazil, with more than 200 million inhabitants, continues on its left-wing course or turns to the right. The elections are seen as important for the political balance in South America. Earlier this year, Trump-friendly right-wing candidates won the presidential elections in Peru and Colombia . In Chile that happened at the end of last year . A win for Lula would mean that Brazil, like Mexico, retains a left-wing <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>.

title: Lula Wins Election in Brazil, Bolsonaro Does Not Accept Defeat
lead: The election in Brazil has been won by incumbent president Lula. He received about 52 percent of the votes, the electoral council has announced. The election was a close race between radical-right Flávio Bolsonaro (45) and left-wing Lula da Silva (80). The first round was won by Bolsonaro, although Lula had led in the polls. Because neither had an absolute majority, a second round had to follow. In this new round, the difference was ultimately about 4 million votes in favour of Lula. Lula also led Brazil between 2003 and 2011 and took office again as president in 2023. Now he begins his fourth term, which makes him history. Left-Wing Course With Lula's victory, the country is again choosing a left-wing course. He campaigned with a progressive and social agenda, including special family allowances for the poor. Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is instead in favour of a free market with little government interference. He also wants the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> to act harshly against crime. Lula was welcomed with loud music at a gathering in Sao Paulo after the result. In a victory speech he thanked his voters. "We managed to convince people that voting was extremely important to keep democracy in Brazil safe." After losing the first round, Lula's supporters, many of them young people, began to mobilise. In groups they took to the streets to win over undecided voters. The fierce struggle between the two candidates shows how divided the country is. Part of the Brazilian population is celebrating and relieved that the presidency remains in Lula's hands. Another part of the population feels defeated and disappointed. Lula promised that he will be a president for all 215 million Brazilians. "There is no electoral opponent anymore." Bolsonaro Does Not Accept Result Bolsonaro refuses to accept the defeat. In a speech he said he wants the result declared invalid. In this he points to the decision of the Supreme Court to keep the polling stations open two hours longer. Bolsonaro calls that "unacceptable", which is striking, since he himself had asked for a longer voting period. Originally the polls would close at 17.00 Brazilian time (21.00 Dutch time). But on the orders of the Supreme Court they closed at 19.00 Brazilian time (23.00 Dutch time). Bolsonaro asked for an extension because voters in the south of the country had difficulty reaching polling stations due to heavy rainfall. Lula also wanted the polling stations kept open longer because voters in nine states could not otherwise cast their votes in time due to bus problems. Bolsonaro's refusal to recognise the election result could increase tension in an already polarised Brazil. The situation resembles 2022, when his father, former president Bolsonaro, also refused to accept his defeat. Angry and incited supporters stormed government buildings. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro and others planned a coup, which was eventually called off because there was too little support from the military. Last year Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for this. Governing Will Not Be Easy Governing will not be easy for Lula. In the National Congress he faces a powerful right-wing bloc, so it is unclear how much support he will get for his plans. In addition, the power of the Bolsonaro family has grown considerably. Members of the family are represented in both the Chamber of Deputies and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Lula will also have to take seriously the concerns of a large part of the population that did not vote for him. These Brazilians are drawn to the so-called bolsonarismo, the conservative radical-right movement around former president Bolsonaro. For them, issues such as crime and the economy were important election themes. For the Amazon and Indigenous Brazilians, Lula's victory is good news. Under his presidency deforestation decreased in recent years. Under Bolsonaro senior, more logging took place and large landowners got more room for production in the Amazon. The fear was that this policy would be continued under Bolsonaro junior. Left in a Right-Leaning Region Under Lula, Brazil is one of the few remaining left-wing countries in Latin America. The region has moved steadily further to the right over the past year and a half. US President Trump is trying to exert his influence in the region as much as possible. He prefers to do business with right-wing governments that are ideologically close to him.

lead: Good morning! Today the House of Representatives debates <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> on the Tax Plan, and tonight it will be announced who will be named the best footballer of the year. The maxima are between 12 and 14 degrees with a fairly strong south wind. In the coming days it is often dry, with Wednesday and Thursday in particular offering room for sun. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss: The elections in Brazil have been won by incumbent president Lula. He received about 52 percent of the votes, the electoral council has announced. The elections were a neck-and-neck race between far-right Flávio Bolsonaro (45) and leftist Lula da Silva (80). The difference ultimately amounted to 4 million votes. In a victory speech Lula thanked his voters. Bolsonaro refuses to accept the defeat. He said in a speech that he wants the result declared invalid. Other news from the night: And then this: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela. She was warmly welcomed at the Santa Rosa church in Barquisimeto. The opposition leader stayed abroad for almost a year after secretly travelling to Norway to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. Recently she was in Panama. Have a nice day!

title: Two dead in UK after trees blown over during Storm Boelo
lead: In the United Kingdom two people died yesterday because of Storm Boelo. In London a man in his twenties died after a fallen tree landed on the car he was driving. In the southwest of Scotland a fallen tree struck a 60-year-old man. Both men died at the scene. In Scotland two women were also taken to hospital after being hit by falling trees. Strong gusts Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 135 kilometres per hour. Streets flooded during the storm, rail, air and water traffic was hindered, and over the weekend around 800,000 households in total were without power because trees and branches fell onto electricity cables. According to the trade organisation of grid operators, Energy Networks Association, repair work was hampered by the weather, although by Sunday evening the vast majority of households were reconnected to the grid. Around 90,000 households were still without power then. Shortly before Boelo, Storm Austen had already caused disruption. Meteorologists expect more bad weather in the coming days. Disruption in the Netherlands The Netherlands also had a restless and stormy weekend due to Storms Austen and Boelo. In Amsterdam a cyclist died yesterday after a tree fell on him. Two cars in the capital were also hit by falling trees. One motorist was injured, the other escaped with a fright. In Volkel on Friday a falling tree made a large hole in the roof of a farmhouse. On Saturday evening a house was also damaged in Rijnsburg, near Leiden. In Culemborg a tree fell on a parked car. In many places the fire brigade was busy over the weekend removing trees and branches from roads. The N207 near Alphen aan den Rijn was blocked for some time. On Sunday evening Oudeschild on Texel experienced water nuisance due to Storm Boelo. Hotels and restaurants were no longer accessible. In an attempt to keep the water out, sandbags and water pumps were deployed. Water also stood high in Harlingen.

title: Search for missing kitesurfer called off again: 'Not safe enough'
lead: The rescue services that have been searching since this morning off the Scheveningen coast for the water sports enthusiast who went missing yesterday afternoon have stopped again. Conditions at sea today are not safe enough to continue, says a spokesperson for the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Yesterday afternoon at around 14.00 the man was reported missing. Rescue services began a search that was halted around 19.00 . It was getting too dark and therefore too dangerous. This morning rescue services resumed the search, but around midday it was suspended again. "There is still a jeep driving along the coastline and a helicopter flying overhead," said the spokesperson. Land, sea, air. Yesterday the kitesurfer was searched for all afternoon from land, sea and the air between Kijkduin and Noordwijk. Eventually the search area was limited to the coast of Scheveningen, because the water sports enthusiast was last seen there. The strong wind and high waves made searching difficult, a spokesperson said. The weather was particularly stormy in the search area, with gusts up to 80 kilometres per hour. Divers later today too. Boats from the Royal Dutch Sea Rescue Society (KNRM), among others, were deployed for the search. The safety region initially hoped that divers could also get to work later today to help.

title: Staff fed up with problems with Frisian taxis: 'People are waiting for hours'
lead: Staff members of the taxi company Dorenbos have difficulty with the way they have to do their work. Elderly people sometimes wait for hours to be picked up, and minibuses sometimes suffer long-lasting technical problems. That is what drivers working for the company say to Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity> . Dorenbos is based in Norg in Drenthe and over the past two years took over four Frisian taxi companies. The company is responsible for pupil transport and Wmo transport. The latter type of transport is intended for people who can no longer travel themselves, for example because they are older or have an illness. The most recent takeovers took place last summer, in the municipalities of <entity id="org:gemeente-smallingerland">Smallingerland</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-sudwest-fryslan">Súdwest-Fryslân</entity>. In two months, those municipalities received a total of just over 300 complaints about the way taxi transport has been arranged. Two hours of waiting after chemotherapy A former driver who wishes to remain anonymous tells the broadcaster that the problems at Dorenbos were already occurring before the summer. "In the morning I get the schedule, and then I can already see that I will arrive three hours late," he says. He no longer works for Dorenbos. The last straw for him was when he collected a woman after chemotherapy more than two hours after the agreed time at the hospital. "That lady doesn't get a message, but the schedule knows the taxi is hours late," the former employee says. "That woman was very emotional. You feel responsible for that. It is inhumane." But 70 kilometres per hour The regional broadcaster has also viewed WhatsApp conversations between drivers. In them, they discussed defects and technical problems with taxi minibuses. The former driver says that one day he did not want to make a trip because the wheelchair locking system in his bus was not working. "But the next day the schedule sent another colleague out with that same bus." He also tells of another colleague who was sent out in a car that could not go faster than 70 kilometres per hour. "Dorenbos had said there was no other car and that she had to drive through side roads to destinations." 'Start-up problems' According to deputy director Rijk van Dijk of Dorenbos, the complaints from Smallingerland are due to start-up problems. Dorenbos had two weeks to set up the transport after the former taxi company there went bankrupt. According to him, the municipality was aware that the transport would not immediately meet all standards. Moreover, according to Van Dijk, Dorenbos could take over fewer drivers and minibuses from the former providers. He acknowledges that passengers in Smallingerland and in Súdwest-Fryslân may have been picked up one to two hours later since the summer. He offers his apologies for that. "I think we had to row with the oars we had, and that we stuck our necks out." Utrecht pupil transport Pupil transport is not always in order in other places in the Netherlands either. In <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>, the company Willemsen de Koning is responsible for the hundreds of pupils who attend special education. Parents, schools and politicians regularly voice criticism of the way this is done. The complaints concern late buses, changing drivers and poor communication, writes RTV Utrecht . Nevertheless, the company may continue to carry out pupil transport from 2027, when the tender expires. Three other parties were interested, but according to the municipality Willemsen de Koning had "the best offer on both quality and price". The municipality has, however, tightened the quality requirements.

title: Cabinet wants 25,000 fewer civil servants, police and defence excluded
lead: The central government must also be able to manage with some 25,000 fewer civil servants. That is in the plans of State Secretary Van der Burg for Effective Government (Slagvaardige Overheid). By 2035, some 16 percent of the approximately 160,000 (full-time) civil servants must be cut. That this cabinet is aiming to shrink the civil service was already known. But Van der Burg is now making, for the first time, an estimate of the number of jobs that this will cost. He says nothing yet about which departments must cut how many jobs. What is clear is that police and defence are staying out of it. Implementing bodies such as the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>, <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> and the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>, which are already under pressure, are not automatically exempt. Exception to exception Van der Burg states that such bodies can also manage with fewer people, provided work is done on simplifying or scrapping rules. That is a key priority of the cabinet . "With fewer exceptions to exceptions, the work becomes simpler." The past few years there were, incidentally, more cabinets that wanted to trim the number of civil servants, but in the meantime there have only become more . When asked, Van der Burg says that this cabinet will do it, because everyone sees "that it must be different". To manage with fewer people, among other things facilities services at ministries will be scaled back, ICT systems will be standardised and the cabinet is looking at other efficiency measures, including the use of AI. Cutting advisory bodies But Van der Burg acknowledges that working more efficiently alone is not enough. "Choices are needed regarding what the government will do differently, less or no longer do." Those choices have not yet been made, but are still being "further elaborated". The cabinet is also looking at scrapping advisory colleges (of which there are now 28) and advisory committees (some 150), which issue advice in various areas. "Cutting there saves a lot of civil service capacity," says Van der Burg. He will announce later exactly which advisory bodies will be cut. The cabinet is also looking at reforming the Open Government Act. Journalists and other citizens can invoke this law if they want government information made public. "The request for information is often so broad that it is no longer clear which information must be provided," Van der Burg writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. And that costs civil servants a lot of time. Within half a year, the state secretary hopes to have finished many of the plans to make central government "simpler, smarter and smaller". Ultimately, all of this should lead to an annual saving of 3.5 billion euros in 2035.

title: Eleventh of the Eleventh in doubt in Tilburg: municipality and hospitality sector clash over teenagers
lead: Are minors always welcome during the Elfde van de Elfde, the traditional opening of the carnival season? The municipality of Tilburg and the local hospitality businesses clash over that question. As a result, the celebration is hanging by a thread. Tomorrow the municipality and hospitality sector will sit down to talk. "Carnival is a party for everyone," says the municipality of Tilburg. "Minors must also be able to party, just like adults." But the hospitality sector wants to be able to refuse people at busy moments. "For example a 14-year-old who has never been in a crowd, but also someone who is in poor health on their legs," says entrepreneur Alex Boonmann on behalf of the Tilburg hospitality board. "It concerns their safety." According to him, the fact that teenagers often drink beforehand and are even less used to it plays a role with them. "They then arrive drunk and in such a crowd they pose a danger to themselves and their surroundings." Elfde van de Elfde 11 November is the traditional start of the carnival season, and it is celebrated on a grand scale mainly in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> and Limburg. At exactly 11:11 the season is rung in and the countdown to carnival can begin. Carnival itself starts next year on Sunday 7 February. The Tilburg hospitality sector refuses to sign a contract from the municipality stating that everyone is welcome on the festival squares. If the hospitality operators do not admit teenagers to the site, they can expect a fine of 2500 euros per case. A supervisor for every young person What the municipality of Tilburg is now proposing is "unworkable," Boonmann believes. If he is only allowed to intervene on the site when things go wrong, "I would have to put a supervisor on every young person." He also finds the risk too great. He points out that the hospitality operators are responsible for supervising the alcohol rules and safety on the festival site. "If a 14-year-old gets trampled somewhere, it is my responsibility." Other cities are also struggling with how to deal with minors during carnival. In many cafes age is checked and they are not welcome at all. As a result, teenagers can often only be outside, where checking alcohol is very difficult. Anyone under 18 who has alcohol with them is punishable and can receive a fine or community service. "Keeping watch is difficult," says Sjef de Graauw of the Oeteldonksche Club, the carnival association in Den Bosch. Mark van den Heuvel of the Sfeerbeheer Groep agrees, which oversees safety during the Elfde van de Elfde in Breda and <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity>. "If you drink from a can on a square with a thousand people, it doesn't get noticed easily." A bottle of drink on the way Moreover, the risk of incidents is greater because of the way teenagers drink today, says Boonmann. "They drink at home as if their last hour has come, because they know they won't get alcohol in a professional setting. Once they are on our site, the alcohol hits." Van den Heuvel of the Sfeerbeheer Groep sees it the same way. "They drink at home, on the way another bottle of lukewarm drink, and when they've been in town for a quarter of an hour, the lights go out." Regularly he and his colleagues have to call parents to come and pick up their children. "Then I say: 'I'm standing here with your daughter and she mistakes the earth for a currant bun. Maybe it's a good idea for you to come.'" Alcohol use among 12 to 16-year-olds has fallen over the past twenty years. But in recent years they have increasingly 'binge drunk', the Trimbos Institute observes. That means they drink a lot of alcohol in a short time. Drunk teenagers put great pressure on the first aid posts during the Elfde van de Elfde and carnival. "They keep us very busy," says hospitality operator Boonmann about the situation in Tilburg. In Breda too, the pressure on the first aid post was very high last year during carnival, the organization said earlier to BN De Stem. At the post, 88 people were treated at that time for heavy alcohol use, including minors. The youngest was 14 years old. At the Bossche first aid post they mainly see that alcohol poisonings among teenagers are more severe than before. "Earlier they came to us after too much beer, now it is often strong liquor," says Peter Aarsel. "The injuries are therefore greater." 'Preventing things from going wrong' In Tilburg the hospitality sector and municipality hope that the Elfde van Elfde will still go ahead. "We also very much want to organize festivals for minors," says Boonmann. "But I want to prevent things from going wrong." He hopes that the talks with the municipality tomorrow will offer a solution.

title: Storm Boelo causes flooded quays from Texel to Breskens
lead: Storm Boelo caused flooded quays in several places across the country yesterday. The harbour of Oudeschild on Texel was badly flooded in particular. The water rose as high as the facades of restaurants, shops and hotels. To keep water out of the doors, wooden boards and sandbags have been put in place. "We fasten those boards and then we fill the cracks with sawdust," says the owner of a restaurant in the harbour to regional broadcaster NH. "That swells in water." The owner also has water pumps ready. "In case water comes into the conservatory and the outbuilding. We keep an eye on that the whole time." Ferry operator TESO, responsible for the crossings between Den Helder and Texel, took into account that sailings might be cancelled this morning due to the high water level, but that turned out not to be the case. Storm surge barrier The Hollandsche IJssel barrier near Krimpen aan den IJssel closed yesterday evening for the first time this storm season. It is one of the thirteen Delta Works that are meant to protect the Netherlands from high water from the sea. The storm surge barrier closes on average about three times a year, according to <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity>. Because the Hollandsche IJssel barrier closed, the water rose in Vlaardingen instead. At Koningin Wilhelminahaven the water stood about 40 centimetres high in some places, regional broadcaster Rijnmond reports. The quay was closed to traffic until 07.00. Car under water Harlingen also felt the effects of the high water levels. There too, several quays were flooded yesterday evening and almost 3 metres above NAP was measured. One quay had to be closed off, Omrop Fryslân reports. The harbour of Breskens in Zeeland also flooded overnight. Several cars were partly under water, Omroep Zeeland reports.

title: Suspended prison sentence for Chris Brown over assault in British nightclub
lead: The American artist Chris Brown has been sentenced to a suspended prison sentence of eight months for a serious assault in a London nightclub in 2023. A court in the British capital has decided this. Brown was present in court. He was met at the entrance by fans. He had covered his face with a face mask and wore a cap and sunglasses. The 37-year-old singer had pleaded guilty in July to public violence in the nightclub. The artist and his vocal coach attacked a music producer with a tequila bottle. The victim, a former friend, was hit twice on the head with the bottle. British prosecutors had agreed to drop more serious charges, such as causing bodily harm, if Brown and his vocal coach pleaded guilty to public violence. Cameras Many people in the club saw the attack happen. It was also captured on camera. The footage was shown during the hearing. It shows that Brown had to be pulled away from the victim after he had hit him twice on the head with the bottle. According to the prosecutor, the music producer had to go to hospital for head and knee injuries. The court said that repeatedly striking with the glass bottle could have caused more serious injury to the victim. Despite the seriousness of the case, Brown will not receive an unconditional prison sentence because, among other things, he pleaded guilty. During today's hearing the singer apologised for the attack. "This is an unpleasant and disagreeable event", said Brown's lawyer in court. "It is something that has undoubtedly caused suffering to those present, and for which Mr Brown offers his sincere apologies." Outside the court, the R&B singer was met by cheering fans, who came from Italy and the Netherlands, among other places. Brown gave a kiss on the hand to a fan while walking towards a waiting car. Brown was arrested last year at his hotel in Manchester for the fight in February 2023. This happened after the British tabloid The Sun contacted the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> with questions about his possible arrest. After paying the bail of 5 million pounds he was released and able to begin his world tour.

title: Rare poisonous mushroom 'Angel of Death' found in Soest
lead: It looks like a harmless mushroom: 9 to 12 centimetres tall, with a conical cap and snow-white. But appearances are deceiving with this sticky kleverige knolamaniet: it is one of the most notorious mushrooms in Europe, nicknamed 'the Angel of Death'. Besides being notorious, the species is also threatened - it was even considered extinct on the Utrecht Heuvelrug - but now it has nonetheless been found there. "I jumped for joy", says mycologist (mushroom expert) Rob Chrispijn to RTV Utrecht. He found the kleverige knolamaniet on the De Paltz estate in Soest, while he was leading an excursion there. Chrispijn found the species in two different places. The kleverige knolamaniet is listed as threatened on the Dutch Red List. The species has been declining sharply for years and is vulnerable to eutrophication and acidification of the soil. "Nitrogen plays a role in that", said Chrispijn. The mushroom looks a bit like a champignon, and that is exactly why things can go badly wrong. Eating the kleverige knolamaniet can be life-threatening without medical treatment. At first you will notice nothing after eating it, says Chrispijn. But later you may become nauseous and get severe gastrointestinal complaints. "After two days the liver and kidneys are affected, and the consequences can be permanent." The Angel of Death is not easy to find, because the mushroom only stands above ground for a few days. Of the two specimens found, one will be examined further. The other is still on the estate. Chrispijn does not expect anyone to take it. "The Dutch are a bit scared of mushrooms."

title: Bus carrying churchgoers collides head-on with truck in Kenya, 24 dead
lead: Yesterday, at least 24 people died in a head-on collision between a bus and a truck in the south of Kenya. It happened on the highway connecting the coastal town of Mombasa with the capital, Nairobi. Local media report that the bus driver had 45 churchgoers on board. The bus was on its way back to Mombasa after attending the funeral of a pastor. Near the village of Mtito Andei, the driver tried to pass several vehicles during a long overtaking manoeuvre. This went wrong when a truck suddenly appeared. The bus driver still swerved to the right, but could no longer prevent a collision. 24 people were also injured, most of whom were taken to the hospital in Mtito Andei. This is not the first accident on this highway. Three weeks ago, seventeen people died in an accident on the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway. The route between Nairobi and Mombasa is considered one of the most dangerous in the country. President Ruto now wants all vehicles in the country to be checked for road safety. A national day of mourning for all road accident victims must also be introduced.

title: Art historian Rudi Fuchs (84), former director of the Stedelijk Museum, has died
lead: Art historian Rudi Fuchs has died. His family announced this to Het Parool . He was considered one of the most influential art critics and museum directors in the Netherlands. The former director of the Stedelijk Museum died last night in his home city <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>. He was 84 years old. Fuchs was director of the Stedelijk Museum from 1993 to 2003. "He devoted his entire working life to the visual arts at home and abroad", his family said. <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, Amsterdam Fuchs was born in 1942 in Eindhoven and studied art history in <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>. In 1975 he became director of the Van Abbemuseum, the museum for modern and contemporary art in his birth city. He gained international fame in 1982 when he was chief curator of Documenta, the five-yearly international exhibition of visual art in Kassel, Germany. From 1987 to 1992 Fuchs was director of the Gemeentemuseum Den Haag, which is now called Kunstmuseum Den Haag. In 1993 he swapped Den Haag for Amsterdam and took charge of the Stedelijk Museum. New building and financial problems At that time he campaigned for the expansion of the museum, but according to Het Parool his Amsterdam years were also marked by financial problems and conflicts with the municipality over the new building. In 2002 he resigned from his post. Rein Wolfs, the current director of the Stedelijk Museum, calls Fuchs, according to news agency ANP, "without doubt internationally one of the most influential museum directors of the last fifty years". "As artistic director of Documenta in 1982 he presented himself as a champion of the new painting, as director of the Haags Gemeentemuseum he changed the view on Mondrian, and as director of the Stedelijk he surprised with unexpected comparisons and new presentation models", Wolfs states. A dislike of explanatory labels The late director sometimes went "radically" to work when setting up museums, director of the Kunstmuseum Den Haag Margriet Schavemaker tells news agency ANP. "He sometimes exhibited works from very different collections together: so musical instruments, contemporary art and classic works side by side, if he had a good reason for it according to him." Fuchs taught people to look more closely at art, Trouw writes. He didn't think much of explanatory labels next to artworks, as he once said himself about exhibitions in the Stedelijk Museum. Those only lead to tunnel vision. "Most people read those first and then go look at the work to see if it matches. And then you're done thinking." After his time at the Stedelijk, Fuchs remained active as a writer, columnist and exhibition maker.

title: Serbs celebrate election victory of Student List, but question about concrete plans remains
lead: "Serbia is free" and "finally we are becoming a normal and free country". With slogans like these, Serbs last night celebrated the election victory of the Student List and the end of the rule of autocratic leader Aleksandar Vucic. The party, which sprang from massive protests against <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>, obtains a majority in the Serbian parliament. After a night full of celebration over the election victory, the question arises of how the party wants to govern and which people should then be part of the government. Vucic, who had been in power for just over twelve years until his resignation at the end of September, acknowledged his defeat last night. The student movement holds him responsible for corruption and cronyism within the government. According to the students, he is also guilty of the decline of the rule of law and press freedom in the country. Novi Sad The main focus of the Student List was therefore tackling corruption. The most tangible example of this, and the direct cause of the student protests, was the collapse of the new Novi Sad station building, in which sixteen people died. According to opponents of Vucic, this was the result of poorly executed work by construction companies that had won the job thanks to corruption. With the promise to nip this kind of corruption within the government in the bud and clean house, the Student List ran its campaign. But how these ideas should concretely become policy is not yet clear. The party is, for example, a collective organisation, within which all decisions are taken by internal referendum. This is not an efficient way of decision-making, so people must be appointed to make decisions. With a majority of about 138 of the 250 seats, the party can moreover form a government, but it is unclear who would join it. According to the students, the campaign revolved around the ideas of the movement and not around the candidates on the electoral list. That list was led by a cardiologist, and otherwise relatively unknown academics and experts are on the list. This admittedly fits the Student List's wish to form a kind of technocratic cabinet of experts, but political experience is lacking. Now that the elections have been won, the question is who will join the ministerial team. Frequently mentioned for an important post is Dejan Soskic, the former president of the central bank of Serbia. Because he is one of the few with international experience, he could possibly become prime minister or <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity>. The party promised before the elections to scrutinise all government institutions and government contracts and to eradicate corruption. It is certain that the Student List will want to tackle corruption. The party is expected to start with managers within the government. The state security service, which has acted increasingly repressively in recent years, is also being scrutinised. In addition, the party has ideas on how education can be improved. But long-term plans on, for example, the economy are lacking. Plans of this kind will therefore have to be made in the coming period. That it is not yet certain what policy will look like and who is to implement it also leads to skepticism about the election victory of the Student List. A 60-year-old social worker tells news agency Reuters that she does not like "that the country has to be changed so quickly all of a sudden". "I don't even know who those people are behind it or who is going to lead the country." Inexperienced The question remains how the party will concretely govern. When the euphoria over the victory has faded, the Student List will have to address these kinds of issues. The party is closely watched in the meantime by former president Vucic, who is expected not to sit idly by. Although he acknowledged his defeat yesterday, he repeatedly said before the elections that he expects the Student List to collapse like a house of cards. And if that happens, according to him, there is no alternative except himself and his party. Still, the movement, despite its inexperience and lack of concrete plans, can count on broad support from the population. The party has namely achieved what the old political opposition failed to do: with a lack of resources, against the odds of state propaganda, bringing Vucic to his knees.

title: Haga Lyceum must improve according to state secretary, or financial penalty threatens
lead: The board of the Cornelius Haga Lyceum in Amsterdam must immediately make improvements, according to state secretary <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> (Secondary Education). If that does not happen, she threatens to cut off the flow of funds to the Islamic secondary school. "It is unacceptable that these pupils receive education every day that falls short," says Tielen. "School should be a place where you can develop and move forward. School boards have the responsibility to ensure that." Mismanagement The Inspectorate of Education previously concluded that the Stichting Islamitisch Onderwijs (SIO), as the school's board is officially called, is guilty of mismanagement. For example, the quality of education is insufficient and examination results and pass rates are lagging. The school board also does not function well according to the Inspectorate. The board was instructed several times to fix these problems. But according to the Inspectorate, this has not been done sufficiently. That is why the state secretary is now intervening through a so-called 'aanwijzing'. That is the most serious legal measure she can take. The board of the Cornelius Haga Lyceum must, according to Tielen, appoint two additional board members and draw up a plan to make improvements. The Ministry of Education must also hear every four weeks how things are progressing. Lesson cancellations are high The lawyer for the Haga Lyceum, Wouter Pors, acknowledges that the quality of education must improve in some areas and that the examination results have been disappointing. "But the problems in education also originate with the government. It is difficult for all schools to find qualified teachers, and for the Haga Lyceum this proves to be especially difficult in practice. Applicants for second-degree positions regularly withdraw, so lesson cancellations are sometimes too high." Furthermore, the press release speaks of two new board members, but according to Pors it does not mention that their appointment must be approved by the state secretary. "That is in conflict with the freedom of education, as laid down in article 23 of the constitution." At the same time, the Haga Lyceum says it will continue to look for members to strengthen the board and thereby improve the quality of education.

title: Rotterdam man suspected of identity fraud after football ticket scam
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> arrested a 31-year-old man from Rotterdam last week on suspicion of hacking the accounts of nearly fifty season ticket holders of fifteen Eredivisie clubs. The police got onto the man's trail when at the end of May sc Heerenveen discovered that the account of an employee had been hacked, and that football tickets were being sold on Marktplaats under that person's name. A police investigation later showed that Marktplaats users thought they were in contact with a genuine season ticket holder. Buyers were therefore unaware of any wrongdoing when they bought the login details and used them to purchase football tickets. When the fraud became known at the Frisian football club, sc Heerenveen invalidated the tickets in question as a precaution. Buyers only found out at the stadium. Identity fraud Further police investigation led to the 31-year-old Rotterdammer, who was arrested last week Monday at his home in Pernis. The police seized data carriers, such as a phone or laptop, for investigation. The man is suspected of identity fraud. The police have asked football clubs where season ticket holders were hacked to file reports.

title: Companies campaign to keep staff discount scheme for employees
lead: An employee of a clothing store who can buy clothes from the own shop at a discount. Or someone who works at a travel organisation and gets a discount on a city trip. They are nice perks, but it seems they have had their best days. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants the special scheme for this kind of staff discount to end on 1 January. 25 industry organisations are now calling on politicians to keep it anyway. "Employees and employers experience the value of the staff discount scheme every day," the organisations say. "Keep this scheme, which receives broad appreciation." Maximum 500 euros Trade union FNV is also against scrapping the scheme. "On the high street we see that wage increases have been lagging for years. The FNV therefore believes that wages must above all rise. But it is of course bitter that precisely the people whose wages are lagging also threaten to lose this extra." Employers cannot simply give their employees everything for free or at a discount. Because that is then seen as a form of wages, on which the employer must pay tax. But there is still a special scheme for tax-free staff discounts. Companies may sell their own products or services to their own staff at up to 20 percent discount. And that discount may total no more than 500 euros per employee per year. 'No social purpose' A research bureau examined the scheme on behalf of the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">ministerie van Financiën</entity> and concluded last year that it serves no social purpose and can therefore be abolished. That would also help make the tax system less complicated, with fewer exceptions. The cabinet then came this year with a package of measures to compensate for high energy prices for citizens and businesses. But this also had to be paid for somehow. A majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> then voted for abolishing the staff discount scheme, as one of the ways to free up money. The abolition should yield about 123 million euros per year. Scrapping the Christmas package? If the scheme disappears, companies can still give their staff tax-free discounts. Because employers may in any case give their employees something without having to pay tax on it. Only that will then, unlike now, come at the expense of their so-called free space. In practice this often concerns the Christmas package, a gift voucher or a sports subscription. The amounts they may spend on these have a maximum, namely 2 percent of the first 400,000 euros they spend on wages in total and 1,18 percent of the wage amount above those 400,000. 'Too little free space' If the staff discount also has to come from that free space, companies fear they will no longer be able to do everything and will have to choose between, for example, a Christmas package or a staff discount. "Placing it within the free space is not a realistic solution," the industry organisations say. "Employers already use that space for other facilities for employees, such as a staff outing, birthday gift or Christmas gift." If employers exceed that free space with gifts and discounts, they must pay as much as 80 percent tax on that amount. Tax plan The Second Chamber debates today the Tax Plan that contains this abolition. Later this year the Second and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> will vote on it. The industry organisations hope the plan will still be amended.

title: Police employee on leave after possible leak of secret information
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> has launched a criminal investigation into an employee of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> Oost-Brabant who may have leaked secret information. The man has been temporarily placed on leave. The police employee is suspected of breaching his official secrecy, whereby he may have misused the police systems and shared information with people outside the police. It has not been made public which function the man holds. It is also unclear what kind of confidential information is involved and with whom it may have been shared. Two investigations The OM has launched two separate investigations. Alongside the investigation by the justice authorities, a disciplinary investigation will also take place. That latter investigation will examine whether the employee has failed to do his work well, honestly and reliably. The employee may not work for now, but has not been arrested. The public prosecutor will decide later whether the man will be prosecuted, reports Omroep Brabant. It is not known when there will be clarity about this. Until then the OM does not want to say anything more about the case.

title: Cabinet resumes talks with opposition, but agreement not yet in sight
lead: The cabinet is again in talks with opposition parties, seeking support for next year's tax plan. After a first day of talks, support does not yet appear to be in sight. After a break in which D66, CDA and VVD consulted among themselves about commitments to the opposition, they spoke with JA21 and BBB. Afterwards, there was certainly no breakthrough. JA21-<entity id="person:bernard-johannes-eerdmans">leider Eerdmans</entity> wants firm commitments, in return for support, that municipalities will not be forced under the dispersal act to take in asylum seekers. Asylum minister <entity id="person:bart-van-den-brink">Bart van den Brink</entity> said earlier that he aims for this, but could not make firm commitments. Today, those did not come either. According to Eerdmans, the cabinet does not want to "budge" on this. If that remains the case, according to Eerdmans it will be over, and in his view "they must" "go over to the left". The cabinet, by contrast, says it keeps aiming for broad support from both left-wing and right-wing parties. Other parties too, including BBB and SGP, are linking their support for the tax plan to other demands. What <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> thinks of this he made clear when he today called on parties to let the negotiations on the tax plan "really be about that plan". According to Jetten, the cabinet has many plans that "are better for people and businesses", and hopes the opposition will mainly want to look at those. This weekend it became known that the cabinet has agreed internally on how it wants to meet the opposition halfway. It announced it would again sit down at the table with seven parties: Pro, JA21, BBB, SGP, ChristenUnie, 50Plus and Volt: BBB earlier repeated that, without "significant adjustments" to the nitrogen plans, the party cannot give support to the tax plan. According to BBB-<entity id="person:hendrik-vermeer">fractievoorzitter Vermeer</entity>, small adjustments are not sufficient. "Making a bad plan a little less bad" is not something you can agree to, says Vermeer. BBB and JA21 both feel the cabinet still is not making clear choices. Vermeer calls the amount of 350 million that the cabinet now wants to set aside to soften the planned tax increases a "drop in the ocean". Time is pressing. The tax plan is important for the cabinet, because it sets out how taxes will be arranged in the coming years. This year, for example, the cabinet plans to extend the reduction of the excise duty on petrol and diesel by 1 year, to the end of 2027. It also wants to implement a reduction of the starter's deduction for entrepreneurs. Time is pressing. Because the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> needs time to implement these measures, the tax plan cannot be postponed for too long. The aim is for it to be voted on on 12 November. Tomorrow, talks with, among others, 50Plus, BBB and PRO and Volt are on the agenda. The cabinet also warned today that if the Tax Plan is voted down, matters such as the excise cut on petrol will also be off the table. Box 3. There is also still no solution for the wealth tax (box 3). The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> majority agrees with the plan that <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> has for this, but it remains unclear how it is to be paid for. A plan to have 'smaller' savers and investors pay for it was withdrawn by the cabinet after criticism. D66, VVD and CDA are reportedly in agreement on new funding, but a majority in both the Eerste and Tweede Kamer still needs to be found for that too.

title: Romania: sabotage network directed by Russian secret service uncovered
lead: Romania's intelligence service says it has uncovered a sabotage network coordinated by Russia. According to the service, the group set a fire in September close to a Romanian state-owned company that produces weapons. The Romanian news site Digi24 writes that the intelligence services believe the network was directly controlled by the Russian secret service. That service had given the group a list of targets. These included state-owned and private companies producing weapons, and other targets "of military and industrial importance", according to the intelligence service. Those targets were not only in Romania but also in other EU countries. Which EU countries has not been disclosed. A Ukrainian and two Belarusians are linked to the network and are being prosecuted for attempted sabotage. Two of them were arrested in Germany, where, according to the Romanian public prosecutor, they were engaged in similar actions. The third was arrested in Poland. The Romanian authorities will request the transfer of the suspects. Hybrid actions Last month the security services of Estonia announced that, in their view, Russia was behind an arson attack at a defence company in the capital Tallinn. That company supplies weapons to Ukraine. Intelligence services across Europe, including the Netherlands, have been warning for some time that the threat of Russian hybrid activities has increased. For example, the services suspect that Russia is responsible for, among other things, arson, disrupting air traffic with drones and damaging undersea cables. In hybrid warfare a country tries to weaken an opponent without starting a war. The aim is to cause unrest, undermine trust in governments and thus sow division. Russia consistently denies accusations of sabotage in Europe.

title: After persistent protests, France announces measures for better education
lead: The French government is announcing measures to improve education. For example, 5 billion euros is being set aside for the renovation of school buildings and universities, say education ministers Geffray and Baptiste. The measures follow persistent mass protests. Pupils are taking action against problems in education, such as dilapidated school buildings, overcrowded classes, a shortage of teachers and high workloads. Earlier today President Macron said that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> would meet the 'legitimate demands' of the demonstrators. The money for renovating school buildings will be made available to local governments. It mainly concerns loans. Furthermore, ministers Geffray and Baptiste promise to make 15,000 extra places available in higher education. This should give more pupils the chance to study. The French Parcoursup system for admission to higher education is also being adjusted. Students criticise unclear selection criteria and unequal opportunities. They say that as a result they cannot follow their desired studies. The education ministers promise that the system will become more transparent and will be replaced in 2028. For secondary schools, a maximum of 28 pupils per class in la Seconde will be introduced. That is the first year of the upper school of secondary education, which corresponds to the fourth year in the Netherlands. In cities, more than 35 pupils often sit in a class in la Seconde now. To make smaller classes possible, 500 extra teachers will be hired. Pupils continue to demonstrate. Geffray and Baptiste met this afternoon with Prime Minister Lecornu and representatives of secondary schools and universities. Pupils' trade unions then announced that they are pleased with the announced measures, but feel they are not enough. "Not everything has been solved yet." They therefore call on pupils to demonstrate again this coming Saturday. Protests have been going on in France for weeks. The persistent actions by pupils for improvements in education have grown into a broader protest with trade unions, farmers and the opposition movement of the yellow vests. Last weekend hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across the country. The protests often start peacefully, but troublemakers and looters change the atmosphere. On 17 October, demonstrations in several cities escalated into riots, looting and arson. Hundreds of millions of euros in damage was caused. More than 2300 people were arrested. To prevent new violence, last week the right to demonstrate was considerably restricted. For example, a curfew applies in various places in the country. Also, 70,000 officers were deployed at this weekend's protests. According to Minister Nuñez of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, new looting has been prevented by police action. 'Saturday will be a risky day' Earlier today President Macron warned that Saturday will again be a 'risky day', just like 5 November. On that day the trade unions have planned a nationwide action. Macron says demonstrators should again not come into city centres then. It cannot be ruled out that a state of emergency will be declared, Macron says. If that happens, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> can carry out preventive searches and demonstrators can be ordered to stay at home. The education ministers hope that the announced measures will calm things down and stress that the plans will actually be carried out. "They are not empty promises."

title: Court of Audit: Rent in Rotterdam remains too high despite municipality's efforts
lead: Many private landlords in Rotterdam still ask far too high rent, despite the municipality's efforts to do something about it. That is the conclusion of the Rotterdam Court of Audit, which examined the municipality's approach since the introduction of the Affordable Rent Act. To protect people from excessive rent, the Affordable Rent Act has existed since July 2024. A points system now determines how much the homeowner may ask for a house or room. As a result, the rent is in many cases lower than what the landlord wants to charge. With the introduction of the law, the municipality has gained more options to tackle excessive rent prices. The municipality can give a landlord who asks too much a warning and ultimately also fine them. But before the municipality can intervene, tenants must first report to the municipality that they are paying too much. Few reports from tenants. In Rotterdam there are about 213,000 rental homes. Nearly 7 in 10 of these are owned by housing associations. The rest belong to private owners. The municipality tried to persuade tenants through a campaign and home visits to report if they pay too much rent. The Court of Audit's research shows that only a few tenants have done so. Until March this year, only 212 reports came in. Of those reports, few have led to rent reductions: in total, the rent of only 34 homes has been lowered. Disappointing results. The Court of Audit finds the results disappointing. Relative to the results, the approach is labour-intensive and expensive, according to the Court of Audit: "Every euro of rent reduction costs the municipality 95 euros." A majority of tenants still cannot find the municipality's reporting point. The Court of Audit's survey shows that only 30 percent of tenants have some idea where to go if they pay too much rent. There is also another reason why few reports are made. "The worse the behaviour of the landlord, the lower the willingness of tenants to report. These are precisely the tenants who must be protected by the law," says director Sjoerd Keulen. "We see that reports fail to come in, often because of fear of the consequences, little trust in the government, or intimidation by the landlord." 'Cautious approach' As long as no report is made, a landlord who does not comply with the law remains out of reach, the Court of Audit says. "While the municipality informally knows which landlords systematically break the law." For example, Rotterdam suspects that in the Carnisse district, where many migrant workers live, at least 60 percent of tenants pay too much rent or live in terrible conditions. If a violation is found, the municipality chooses a cautious approach, according to the Court of Audit. While the research was ongoing, the municipality did not take over any homes from landlords. No fines have been imposed either. "Because of this approach, it pays for a landlord not to comply with the Affordable Rent Act." Court of Audit wants a stricter approach. The Court of Audit recommends actively tackling systematic offenders. Moreover, heavier measures should be applied more quickly in the case of violations. Attention should also be paid to tenants who get into trouble after making a report, the Court of Audit advises. The city administration almost fully adopts the recommendations. For example, enforcement was tightened just before the summer, the responsible alderman Kockelkoren told regional broadcaster Rijnmond. "Everyone in Rotterdam deserves a safe and affordable place to live," she says. "Yet there are still tenants who pay too much or face discrimination and intimidation. That is unacceptable."

title: Flávio Bolsonaro says he may not leave Brazil: 'It is an attempt at intimidation'
lead: Brazilian senator and former presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro says the federal police have ordered him to hand in his passports. The son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro speaks of an 'atrocity' intended to intimidate him. Bolsonaro junior says he was approached by the police after visiting his father, who is under house arrest. "I was ordered to hand in my passports. I was also forbidden to leave the country," Bolsonaro says in a video on social media. This reportedly happened on the orders of a judge of the Supreme Federal Court following statements by Flávio's brother. Eduardo Bolsonaro said last week that Flávio could do better to leave the country if he lost the presidential election, but Flávio says he will not do that. "I have never considered leaving the country. I will hand in my passports and defend myself against this atrocity." Refuses to accept defeat. On Sunday it became known that the far-right Bolsonaro had lost the presidential election. The victory went to the left-wing incumbent president Lula, who received almost 52 percent of the votes. Bolsonaro refuses to accept his defeat and wants the result declared invalid. In a short speech after the result was announced, Bolsonaro pointed to the decision of the Supreme Federal Court to keep the polling stations open for two hours longer. Bolsonaro calls that "unacceptable", which is remarkable. He had himself asked for a longer voting period because some voters had difficulty reaching the polling station due to heavy rain. On Monday Bolsonaro again criticised keeping the polling stations open longer. "What happened in those two hours must be clarified. Nobody knows exactly what the consequences are," he said. Brazilian media report that around 34,000 votes were cast in those two hours. That seems to have made little difference to the result. Lula received over 4 million more votes than Bolsonaro.
