The three parties want to pay for their plans through cuts in other areas. Asked by the NOS, the parties say that they are reserving the details "for the negotiating table with the cabinet". According to SGP <entity id="person:christiaan-stoffer">leider Stoffer</entity>, everything is "covered down to the last euro" and the focus should mainly be on "cutting government spending". Left or right. Because of the cooperation and the content of the package, the coalition, which is already divided internally, will come under even more pressure. D66 and CDA prefer the left, while the VVD prefers cooperation with right-wing parties. The cabinet says it always wants broad support in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> with a hundred seats. Opposition parties say that this is not possible and that the cabinet must choose. Besides putting this right-wing alliance on edge with the minority coalition, it also becomes clearer that broad support is becoming increasingly difficult: the package contains demands that Pro and Volt will not support. On Monday Prime Minister Jetten still urged parties to judge the tax plan mainly on its content and not to link other matters to it. With this letter SGP, JA21 and BBB are doing exactly that: they emphasise their concerns about the cabinet's plans. Besides adjustments on nitrogen, asylum and medical ethics, they also want major changes to the tax increases. "The Netherlands runs on people who work, run businesses and care for their families", they write, and people deserve "a government that ensures that working and entrepreneurship pay off and that taking responsibility is not punished". Proposed tax reductions by SGP, BBB and JA21 - Scrapping the 'freedom contribution'. - Tackling the tax gap between single-earner and dual-earner households. - Raising the SME profit exemption to relieve entrepreneurs. - Scrapping the VAT increase on ornamental horticulture. Scrapping the tax increase for defence spending is particularly sensitive for CDA. The SGP demands on abortion and surrogacy will be especially hard to swallow for D66, the largest governing party. On the demand that municipalities not be forced to take in asylum seekers, asylum minister Van den Brink (CDA) has said several times that he cannot promise this on paper because it conflicts with the Dispersal Act. The major adjustments to the nitrogen package will also meet resistance. The proposal conflicts with agreements that the cabinet said earlier were necessary to get permits moving again. And if the plans are changed substantially, Pro will withdraw its support. The right-wing opposition parties themselves speak of a "constructive offer", with which the cabinet sees its plans assured of sufficient support in the House and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. An offer that will mainly appeal to the VVD will make the pressure on the already divided minority cabinet even greater than it was.

title: Struggling seal centre gets no extra money from municipality
lead: Zeehondencentrum Pieterburen cannot count on extra money from the municipality to stay afloat. The centre has been struggling with financial problems for some time and previously reported that its survival was at stake if the municipality and province did not step in. In the municipal council of <entity id="org:gemeente-het-hogeland">Het Hogeland</entity>, where the centre is based, a majority voted against extra financial support last night. Last year, the Zeehondencentrum Pieterburen merged into the new Werelderfgoedcentrum Waddenzee (WEC) in Lauwersoog. The new centre was meant to give the outdated seal care a "sustainable future", including by offering more space for education and experience. Building the WEC cost 43,7 million euros, 17,4 million more than budgeted. The doors opened in April 2025, but visitor numbers then fell short. As a result, the WEC's debt rose to around 2,8 million euros, an amount the centre cannot simply pay itself. Revenue from entrance fees and other sources is roughly equal to the costs incurred. Valuable: The future of the centre is therefore uncertain. Last night the municipal council of Het Hogeland discussed the matter publicly for the first time. D66 submitted a motion rejecting extra financial support for the centre. Only Pro voted against, a party that wants the executive to "make maximum efforts to keep the WEC". For that, the centre would have to come up with a new course and a sound plan, and cooperate better with entrepreneurs in the port. Still, that financial support is not coming after all. Most parties are convinced that the seal care is of great value to the region, RTV Noord reported, but believe the WEC should save itself financially. A majority of the council also sees no way to co-finance because of strict rules on state aid and the exceeded construction costs. Het Hogeland does still support the WEC in other ways. The municipality stands as guarantor for a loan of 9 million euros that the WEC has taken out with <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity>. The municipality also spent a total of around 340.000 euros on advisory costs for the centre's financial and legal matters. This concerns, for example, state aid analyses, financial advice and a marketing strategy. Donors: About ten WEC employees attended the council meeting. They handed the petition 'Red het Zeehondencentrum WEC' to mayor <entity id="person:hans-broekhuizen">Hans Broekhuizen</entity>. It had been signed more than one hundred thousand times. That there is broad support for keeping the seal centre was also shown by a fundraising campaign. According to the organisation, more than 1,25 million euros in donations have already come in to save the almost bankrupt WEC. These range from amounts starting at 5 euros to, for example, a gift of 40.000 euros. Bankruptcy application: This gave the centre's supervisory board reason to postpone the bankruptcy application by one week last week. The financial support gave new opportunities to keep the centre open after all. That week ends tomorrow: by then WEC will decide at the latest whether to apply for bankruptcy.

title: War in Middle East again leads to billions in profit at Shell
lead: Shell's profit rose sharply again last quarter. The oil and gas company made 12.1 billion dollars in profit at the bottom line. Shell itself adjusts for higher oil prices and keeps 10.8 billion in net profit. In the same period last year it was 5.4 billion. The company posted revenue of nearly 93 billion dollars. The good results are mainly due to the ongoing war in the Middle East. Several refineries there have been attacked, which process crude oil into petrol and diesel, among other things. These now produce less, and because fewer products are coming onto the market, purchasing becomes more expensive. Companies like Shell, which sell products such as oil, benefit from this. Revenue from liquefied gas has also increased, the quarterly figures show. The European gas price has now passed 100 euros per megawatt hour, the level of the crisis in 2022. That was when Russia invaded Ukraine. More dividend for shareholders. Prices are also rising because the Strait of Hormuz was completely blocked for a long time. Dozens of tankers are passing through again each day, but not yet as many as before the war in the Middle East. Shareholders of the company are benefiting from the high profits. Shell is going to pay out more money per share, the so-called dividend. Appeal: Do you have a dynamic energy contract or have you recently signed a fixed energy contract? And would you like to take part in a TV and radio report? Then we would be glad to get in touch with you. Send an email to economie@nos.nl and we will contact you. From politics, there was an earlier attempt to tax the high profits of oil and gas companies extra. In spring a majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> agreed to a motion on this from Pro and D66. But partly because Shell is no longer a Dutch company, imposing such an extra tax is very difficult. It is still being examined at European level whether there are possibilities.

title: Hackers put data on 41,000 employees of the US Department of Homeland Security online
lead: Activist hackers have put online the data of over 41,000 employees of the American Department of Homeland Security. It concerns names, phone numbers, email addresses and other data of the staff of services such as <entity id="org:douane">douane</entity> and the immigration police ICE, including employees in sensitive positions. "They have our data, so it is only fair that we have theirs", reasons a spokesperson for the activist website Distributed Denial of Secrets, which published the data in a searchable database. The aim is to "replace anonymity with accountability", says co-founder Emma Best of the site. She thinks that a great many official requests for the disclosure of documents can be made with the data. Because the data also includes job descriptions and email groups, the hacker group says it is possible to trace the internal structure of departments within the ministry. "This makes clear who the architects and driving forces behind the policy and its implementation are", Best said. For security reasons, the government provides little information about this. Under fire The Department of Homeland Security was set up in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks to combat the fragmentation of national security. Various security services, for example for immigration, aviation security and internet security, fall under it. Under President Trump, mainly the immigration police ICE made the news, because of a very active deportation policy and violence when arresting immigrants and protesters. The service was criticised because agents are not in uniform, do not wear identification and are sometimes masked, which according to human rights organisations makes it difficult to hold them accountable. Distributed Denial of Secrets says that by leaking the data it aims to make more oversight and transparency possible. Critics fear that employees will be put at risk as a result: criminals also have access to the data. Agents and their families have been threatened more often in the past. Not informed It is not entirely clear how the hackers obtained the staff data. They themselves say they found a leak in the login system of the Department of Homeland Security. The company behind it denies that security is not in order. A spokesperson for the ministry itself says it is aware of the reports about the hack and says that an investigation is under way. Meanwhile, according to the spokesperson, the department is doing everything it can to guarantee the safety of employees. In connection with the leak, Distributed Denial of Secrets did stress that the data may be incomplete and partly incorrect. Even so, American media were able to contact various employees using data from the database. Some turned out not yet to have been aware that their personal details had been leaked. Third major leak in a short time This is the third time in a short period that the American government has faced a major data leak. In September, the hacker group ShinyHunters reported having an enormous amount of files on FBI employees. That was a retaliation for the FBI's call never to pay extortionists. Shortly afterwards, a suspect was arrested in the Netherlands. Later that month it emerged that someone had had access to the personnel records of the Pentagon for months. Millions of data records of American military personnel were taken in the process.

title: Flevoland invests millions in new harbour near Urk, 'up to 750 jobs added'
lead: Twelve years after the first plans were put on the table, the decision has now been made: a service harbour is to be built outside the dike near Urk. The project is meant to considerably strengthen shipbuilding and the maritime sector in Urk and the <entity id="org:gemeente-noordoostpolder">Noordoostpolder</entity> in the coming decades. The province of Flevoland will invest tens of millions of euros in it. A majority of the Provincial States has agreed to that college proposal. According to the college, existing maritime companies can keep growing thanks to the project, and there will be more room for new economic activities. The harbour is to create 550 to 750 jobs. To realise the harbour, the province will have to borrow quite a lot of money. The exact amount has been declared secret. What is known: the project will be profitable after 45 years and all loans and investments will be repaid after 73 years, Omroep Flevoland reports. This happens thanks to entrepreneurs from Urk and the Noordoostpolder who commit to the project for the long term. They are willing to pay the province annual ground lease fees over the coming decades, with which the loans will ultimately be repaid. Risk versus nerve. A too-large financial risk, opponents said, including Pro, the Party for the Animals and also coalition party VVD. They argue that it takes far too long before the investment is earned back. "We have always been in favour of developing the harbour and we still are," said VVD parliamentary group leader Francho Achtien. But the current proposal, in his view, saddles the province with too heavy burdens. "Paying back the loans takes a lifetime." Moreover, the province cannot spend the borrowed money that is tied up for the harbour in those years on anything else. "We have a big problem with bus transport," says Kjell van de Wijlandt of the Party for the Animals. "With this money we can pay for that." BBB parliamentary group leader Andrea van Veen instead pointed to the nerve this project shows. "You are not only voting for the harbour, but also on whether you have a vision for Flevoland. The harbour will contribute to the growth of the province." According to the ChristenUnie, the maritime sector is "booming," said parliamentary group leader Ria Visser-Kapitein. "We need to provide room for this. We urgently need the employment and entrepreneurship." Ground lease. Entrepreneurs from Urk and the Noordoostpolder seem to have confidence in it, at least. According to entrepreneur and harbour initiator Henk Kapitein, eleven companies want to take part and fifteen more are on the waiting list. The proposed investment credit for the harbour was already raised several times due to higher costs for energy, building materials and personnel. Several factions asked whether that amount will not rise even further in the coming time than foreseen. The college will therefore inform the States every six months about the harbour's progress, it was decided last night. Ready in 5 years. Soon the province will start a European tendering procedure to find a contractor. According to executive member Sjaak Simonse, that procedure takes about nine months. Construction of the harbour must start in 2028 and be finished in 2031. The service harbour is intended, among other things, for shipbuilding, ship maintenance, maritime services and sustainability.

title: Nature targets for peat areas not met, 'environment too fragmented'
lead: The hundreds of millions invested in peat areas have not yet led to the nature targets being met there. That is the conclusion of the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Rekenkamer</entity> in the report Nature policy for peat: a bog? The researchers looked at the 173 peat areas spread across the Netherlands, wet nature areas with a soil type made up of plant remains. Not only do many animals and plants that occur nowhere else live there, the peat also helps hold tons of CO2 in the soil. Because of this importance, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has released two billion euros between 2021 and 2030 to strengthen the areas. According to the Rekenkamer, this currently succeeds sufficiently in only 18 of the 173 cases. The Netherlands Court of Audit examines whether government spending is lawful and effective. 'Administrative bog' Peat areas are threatened by drying out, nitrogen, invasive exotic species and deteriorating water quality. To counter all of that, improvements in the areas themselves are not enough on their own; buffer zones must also be built around them. That is where it goes wrong, according to the Rekenkamer. In the peat areas the provinces have the say, but in the buffer zones a web of authorities holds control, from municipalities and water boards to the national government and private parties. The direction there is often unclear, and dependence on others leads to long, sluggish processes, "a bog of administrative decision-making". Conflicting interests are often at play around the peat, the Rekenkamer observes. For example, farmers want to be able to use pesticides and keep the water level low, while that is bad for the peat. Recreation, new housing and road building also put pressure on and fragment the areas. The Rekenkamer believes that <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity> of Nature (D66) "plays only a limited role". He can push policy through, but according to the report he does too little of it. "If the minister does not do this, the targets for peat areas but also for other nature areas are in danger," the Rekenkamer warns. 'Delay is decline' The ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> states in a response that the monitoring and steering of nature policy is organised decentrally and lies primarily with the provinces. It also sees the need to gain more direction on the file. It is discussing this with the provinces, among others. "The findings show that we cannot wait with nature restoration. Delay is decline, and we must move forward."

title: 2 years in prison for severe assault on Haarlemmer (17) in Beverwijk
lead: Two men from <entity id="org:gemeente-heemskerk">Heemskerk</entity> and Beverwijk have been convicted of the severe assault of a 17-year-old boy from <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity>. They were sentenced to two years in prison. A third suspect was acquitted. The three suspects, aged 22, 24 and 25, stood trial for attempted manslaughter and robbery with violence. The court found the first charge proven for two of them. Fouad B. (24) and Adam E. B. (22) were each sentenced to two years in prison, six months of which are suspended. They must also pay damages of over 41,000 euros and are subject to a no-contact order with the victim. Inadmissible The third suspect, the 25-year-old Mourad L., denied using violence during the assault. Nevertheless, he can be seen in footage of the incident, together with a fourth suspect. That suspect is said to have filmed the incident and pulled down the victim's trousers. But this suspect was not prosecuted. Therefore the court declares the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) inadmissible for the third suspect. A judge can decide this if the OM has not met formal requirements, or if the investigation and prosecution were not carried out properly, writes NH . The trio was not present at the verdict. Social media The assault took place on 6 September last year. The violence probably arose from a quarrel between two rival groups of youths from Heemskerk and Beverwijk, and Haarlem. On that day the victim had eaten with friends in Beverwijk, and when he left the restaurant he was asked by a group of boys where he was from. As soon as it became clear the answer was Haarlem, he was surrounded by about twenty boys with machetes and baseball bats, according to the victim statement. Footage shown in court shows the victim being stripped, beaten and kicked several times in the head, including when he was unconscious. He broke his hand, got bumps on his head and temple, and had to abandon his studies. The assault was filmed and the footage spread on social media. It caused great unrest in the region. Several secondary schools in Beverwijk and Heemskerk closed their doors for a day, and sports clubs stayed closed. Mayors took emergency measures, and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was allowed to carry out preventive searches in certain places.

title: No AI for children in primary school, says House of Representatives
lead: The use of generative AI in the classroom should be banned for children in primary school. A majority in the House of Representatives supports a proposal on this from Volt and the CDA. "We must not make the same mistake as when social media were embraced uncritically", says <entity id="person:laurens-antonius-josephus-maria-dassen">Kamerlid Dassen</entity> of Volt. CDA MP Armut: "As far as we are concerned, generative AI adds nothing for primary school pupils." Generative AI is artificial intelligence that, based on instructions, is itself capable of generating text, audio, video or images, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot. According to the parties, young pupils in primary education develop to a large extent "their critical thinking, creativity and imagination". The use of generative AI poses a risk to this, they think. Critical thinking Children must first learn well to read, write and think critically, including about AI, before they start working with AI themselves, Dassen believes. "I believe in the opportunities AI offers us, but at the same time generative AI increases learning gaps. We need to act on that now." As far as the CDA is concerned, learning from books remains the foundation. For children, digital literacy is also important, says MP Armut, but AI must then be used purely to support learning. The parties that want a ban are Volt, CDA, Pro, D66, PvdD, Denk, SP, 50plus, ChristenUnie and JA21. Together they hold 88 of the 150 seats. <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> understands the concerns of the House of Representatives, but she is not in favour of banning AI for primary school pupils right now. She is working on a plan on digitalisation in education and says she wants to be careful. "I simply need a bit more time for that." Too little learning about AI The PO-raad, the sector association for primary education, welcomes the proposal. "Initial research shows that learning yield declines when pupils make frequent use of generative AI, so we understand the concerns politicians have about the use of generative AI in education. Above all, it is extremely important that pupils learn how to analyse a source and that they can think critically themselves." "At the same time, a possible total ban for primary education comes out of the blue. We are open to making good agreements about this with the ministry and experts, because it is clear that something needs to be done", the PO-raad adds. Educationalist and group 8 teacher Barend Last understands the concerns among politicians. "I can follow the reasoning that children should not have unrestricted access to generative AI systems." Even so, he fears that such a ban would cause children to learn too little about AI and then miss valuable lessons about preparing for society. "The core objectives state that pupils must learn to use AI responsibly. So you should not ban all use of generative AI", he says. According to him, there are plenty of examples of it being used in an educational way. Barend Last fears that the House of Representatives will formulate a statutory ban too broadly. "Educational chatbots can for example be instructed not to give the answers but, for instance, to think along with the pupil according to didactic principles. Educational publishers are also experimenting with AI chatbots."

title: Polls: coalition loses dozens of seats, a year after elections
lead: Exactly one year after the last elections for <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, the coalition parties are facing sharp losses in voter favour. In the most recent Peilingwijzer, D66 of <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, which won the most votes at the elections a year ago, now stands at 13 to 17 seats in the House of Representatives. That is 11 fewer than it currently holds in the House. The VVD keeps 14 to 18 seats in this weighted average of the polls by Ipsos I&O and Verian/EenVandaag, a loss of 6. Meanwhile the CDA also falls by 4, to 12 to 16. As a result the minority coalition is around 45 seats, less than a third of the seats in the House. By far the largest party in the Peilingwijzer remains opposition party PRO, at 25 to 31 seats. The party of Jesse Klaver still reaps, according to research by Ipsos I&O and Verian/EenVandaag, the fruits of the discontent of many progressive voters over the 'right-wing' government policy that D66 signed up for. Lowest rating for Yesilgöz: Mirror image, the VVD is reproached by its voters from last year for having moved too far to the left. According to Verian/EenVandaag there is an important difference between the situation at D66 and at the VVD: whereas confidence in Jetten among his base is still fairly high, only 28 percent of VVD voters think leader Dilan Yesilgöz should again be lead candidate at the next elections. Ipsos I&O sees the same. Yesilgöz, who recently said he wanted to remain leader through the next elections, receives the lowest rating from voters of the main political leaders. Expressed as a grade, it is a 3.7. No more than 8 percent of VVD voters say they vote VVD because of the leader. PVV also loses: Notably, it is not the PVV that benefits from the further diminished appeal of the VVD. The party of <entity id="person:geert-wilders">Geert Wilders</entity> is also down, at 18 to 23 seats. Switchers from VVD and PVV mainly cause JA21 (15-19) and Forum voor Democratie (10-14) to grow. Ipsos I&O sees in the underlying research great volatility among voters. On the one hand, the coalition parties are held against them for failing to achieve enough, and many people are therefore looking elsewhere at the moment. On the other hand, about three quarters of opposition voters think their party must hold firmly to its own principles, "even if <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> fails to get the budget done". Those budget talks with the opposition are being held these days. BBB nearly disappears: Among the smaller parties, three stand at 4 to 6 seats in the Peilingwijzer: 50Plus, the Partij voor de Dieren and the SP. Roughly the same size is the ChristenUnie, with 3 to 5, followed by the SGP and Volt with 2 to 4 and Denk with 1 to 3. Of BBB little remains in the current Peilingwijzer, at 0 to 2. Maurice de Hond. Political scientist Tom Louwerse, the maker of the Peilingwijzer, stresses that seat polls outside election time have little predictive value for the next result, according to available research. "On the other hand, parties do respond to them. You saw that recently, for example, when the poll by Maurice de Hond, which is not included in the Peilingwijzer, came out at 12 seats for the VVD. That led to many newspaper pieces and critical questions at party meetings." "Another effect," said Louwerse, "is that it puts more pressure on these parties to bring concrete matters into negotiations in which their own profile stands out well. Compromises then become even harder. That makes budget negotiations like those currently being held not easy." About the Peilingwijzer: De NOS regularly publishes the Peilingwijzer, which combines seat polls by Ipsos I&O and Verian/EenVandaag. More about the method behind it can be found on the website of its maker, political scientist Tom Louwerse of Leiden University.

title: Public Prosecution Service drops case against trainee officer over fatal 2023 arrest
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is dropping the case against an officer over a fatal arrest in 2023 in Rotterdam. On 9 June of that year a 32-year-old Rotterdam man died when officers were holding him under control. Research reportedly showed that the officers involved violated the use-of-force instructions applicable to them, which caused the suspect to die . The OM now reports that an eighth officer, who had previously been named as one of the suspects, was still in training. He followed instructions from colleagues with a higher rank. After investigation by the national investigation service, the OM concludes that he did not take action on his own initiative that contributed to the man's death. The case against the other seven officers will be heard in January and February 2027 in a special court in Utrecht. That court handles cases against investigating officers. Never before in the Netherlands have so many officers had to appear before the judge at the same time. Traffic incident In February 2024 the Public Prosecution Service announced that it would prosecute eight officers for their involvement in the death of the arrestee. On 9 June 2023 two officers responded to a report about a traffic incident. The arrestee reportedly had collided with a car on his bicycle and kept going. The man was chased by the officers, first in a police van and later on foot, the Public Prosecution Service writes. The suspect did not follow the officers' instructions, after which he was tasered. More officers arrived to assist. Because the man kept resisting, several officers held him face down. The man became unwell and was resuscitated. He eventually died in hospital. A few months later suspicion arose that the way the man had been restrained may have played a role in his death. Alfredo Goeloe The case of the 32-year-old victim recalls the arrest of 51-year-old Rotterdam resident Alfredo Goeloe . He was checked by officers last 12 September after a report about a stolen fatbike. When Goeloe could not show proof of identity, he ran away. Afterwards it turned out he had drugs on him. After a chase, officers finally detained him. While officers held him down on the ground, he lost consciousness. Footage of the arrest captures Goeloe calling for help and saying he had diabetes. Resuscitation was unsuccessful and he died. Editor's note An earlier version of this article framed the story as the OM prosecuting the seven officers. That had been known for some time and is therefore not the news. The article has been rewritten.

title: Thousands of THC candies seized, destined for the Netherlands
lead: French customs intercepted thousands of packages of THC candies intended for the Dutch market. THC is the main active substance in marijuana. According to the European anti-fraud office OLAF, the candies and packaging closely resembled products of a well-known European brand. This infringed trademark rights, but OLAF also warns that children could easily confuse the THC candies with ordinary sweets. And that can be dangerous. The anti-fraud office also warns that such food products do not comply with European rules. Due to the packaging, users get the impression that it is a normal and safe product. In total, 3560 packages were seized and destroyed. They had been sent from the United States and were to be forwarded to the Netherlands. Children ill The office also has websites and shops on its radar that sell such candy. Incidentally, all of them are in France. According to OLAF, the authorities there are taking appropriate measures. There are regular incidents with THC candies. This summer, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in Utrecht already warned about unsafe candies that had made children ill. They had found the candy in a schoolyard. Last year, Haribo candies were recalled by the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">NVWA</entity> after THC was found in them. Several people had become unwell. One child had even fallen into a coma. But it later turned out that the recalled candy did not contain any THC after all, the <entity id="org:nederlands-forensisch-instituut">Nederlands Forensisch Instituut</entity> concluded after investigation.

title: Cabinet to talk with various opposition combinations tomorrow
lead: The cabinet will continue talks tomorrow with various combinations of opposition parties. That is the outcome of consultations between the cabinet's leadership. The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is still looking for support for the tax plan and other budgets. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (both <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) will first talk with the ChristenUnie and 50Plus tomorrow, then with JA21, BBB and SGP, and finally with Pro and Volt. Most of these parties also already held talks earlier this week. Three routes The three talk groupings stand for three routes the cabinet has to find a majority for its plans. CU and 50Plus, together with the seats of Groep Markuszower, can secure a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. Markuszower, who spoke with Heinen this week, said earlier that he makes few demands. For him, it is mainly important that Pro does not come to power, said the former PVV member of the House of Representatives. Freedom contribution JA21, BBB and SGP together form 'the route on the right'. The three opposition parties announced this morning that they will now work together in negotiations with the minority cabinet. Jetten, deputy prime ministers Van den Brink (CDA) and Yesilgöz (VVD) and minister Heinen held talks this afternoon about the package of demands. The three right-wing parties offer their support for the tax plan and other budgets in exchange for adjustments to the coalition's plans. JA21, SGP and BBB want the tax increase to meet the NATO norm, called the freedom contribution by CDA, taken off the table, and a substantial reduction in the tax burden. The trio also wants adjustments to the nitrogen plans that BBB requested earlier, and more asylum measures, which JA21 consistently advocates. The SGP's demands on surrogacy and abortion policy have also become joint demands. Broad support The cabinet has so far consistently said it wants to pursue broad support in the Tweede Kamer with a hundred seats. Opposition parties consistently say that is not possible and that the cabinet must choose. The package from the right-wing alliance underlines this again, because it contains demands that Pro and Volt, who together form 'the option on the left', will not support. Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> stressed in recent days that he is willing to compromise. Due to the cooperation on the right and the content of the package, the coalition, which is already internally divided, will come under even more pressure. D66 and CDA prefer the left, the VVD prefers cooperation with right-wing parties. Incidentally, the cabinet's leadership will meet again this evening at Jetten's ministry to discuss how to proceed.

title: World summit on combating racism and discrimination kicks off in The Hague
lead: About 1500 people from more than 80 countries are visiting The Hague today and tomorrow for the Unesco Global Forum against Racism and Discrimination summit. Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> gave the opening speech at the World Forum today, and <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> was also present. "Millions of people face discrimination and racism in their daily lives", Jetten writes on Instagram. "A harsh climate prevails for everyone who stands up for equal rights, and institutions set up to protect all of us are under great pressure." The king spoke with several guests from different countries about the specific challenges in combating racism and discrimination worldwide. The forum is the only international summit focused specifically on the global approach to racism and discrimination. "Worldwide, tensions are rising. Discrimination, racism and incitement to hatred are increasingly visible in societies", writes Unesco. The UN agency for education, science and culture has been fighting racism since its founding in 1945. In 1978 it adopted the Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice. In it, it is reaffirmed that "all human beings belong to a single species and are descended from a common origin. They are born equal in dignity and rights and all form an integral part of humanity." Change and taking responsibility are central at the summit this year. "Treaties have been concluded on racism and discrimination, declarations drawn up, action programmes developed and promises made. That has been important. But what have all those agreements actually delivered?", according to Unesco. In The Hague, among other things, strategy and policy on combating racism and discrimination will be discussed. The Hague: The event is being held in The Hague because it is worldwide the international city of peace and justice. For example, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Criminal Court (ICC) are seated in the city. The latter is under heavy pressure from the United States. "Combating racism and discrimination is at its core a fight for human rights and human dignity", says National Coordinator against Discrimination and Racism Rabin Baldewsingh. "There is therefore no better place imaginable to bring the world together precisely on this issue." "For the Netherlands this is a unique opportunity to take international responsibility", according to Baldewsingh. He emphasises that he does not think the Netherlands has a monopoly on wisdom, but "because we are convinced that countries can learn a lot from each other". 'Change possible' Baldewsingh calls it an honour that the Netherlands was chosen by Unesco to co-organise the summit. "The Netherlands has taken important steps in recent years, including by establishing an independent National Coordinator, strengthening the national approach to discrimination and racism, and the social dialogue about our colonial and slavery past. We are bringing those experiences to this Forum." Earlier editions took place in France, Mexico, Brazil and Spain.

title: Commotion around Tax Plan could lead to chaos in tax assessments
lead: If <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> rejects the Tax Plan 2027 of the minority cabinet at the end of this year, chaos could arise for millions of taxpayers. That is connected to the deadline that applies to the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>. On 20 November at 12.00 noon, all changes to income tax must truly be in, because after that the provisional assessments are made, which are sent from December onwards. If the Eerste Kamer rejects the Tax Plan after 20 November or forces changes through a novelle, the provisional assessments will no longer be correct. This must then be corrected later, in the final assessment one and a half years later. That means back-claims or refunds. The phrase "that will become a second Childcare Benefits Scandal but even bigger" is already being used in the corridors. Not far-fetched. ChristenUnie MP Grinwis raised the topic last Monday in the House debate on the Tax Plan. He asked the <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-financien">staatssecretaris van Financiën</entity> Eerenberg: "What if <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> says yes by majority to the Tax Plan, but the Eerste Kamer does not?" That option is certainly not far-fetched. The minority cabinet is still engaged in difficult negotiations with the opposition over support for the Tax Plan. Whether that will succeed with parties that can provide a majority in both the Tweede and Eerste Kamer is uncertain. Eerenberg therefore said in the debate in answer to Grinwis that this is "the scenario we really should not want with each other or make appealing, because it is not". How does the provisional assessment work? Anyone can request a provisional assessment from the Belastingdienst for the following year from early December. You do that, for example, if you want to receive the mortgage interest deduction monthly, instead of in one lump sum at the end of the tax year. The Belastingdienst determines the following year what the final assessment is. Then it becomes clear to what extent the provisional assessment was correct, and thus whether you must pay an additional amount or get money back. To set the provisional assessment, the Belastingdienst assumes the tax rules that apply then. If the Eerste Kamer changes those at the last moment, the final assessment is likely to turn out differently. The enormous implementation problem that looms will change the discussion for senators of the opposition parties. Their possible vote against could cause uncertainty about income tax and thus the disposable income of millions of Dutch people. That is why the minority cabinet may ultimately settle for only a majority for the Tax Plan in the Tweede Kamer. Opposition parties in the Eerste Kamer will then probably never dare to vote it down. Gamble. So far <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> keeps saying this route is certainly not desirable. But the minority cabinet is still undecided, due to internal disagreements, whether it wants to do business 'from the left' with Pro and Volt or 'from the right' with JA21, SGP and BBB. If this process goes completely wrong, they can take a gamble: rely on CU, 50Plus and Groep Markuszower in the Tweede Kamer, and count on nobody in the Eerste Kamer wanting to be responsible for chaos with income tax. ChristenUnie MP Grinwis responds that there is a "great responsibility" resting on the House and cabinet to get out of this regarding the Tax Plan. "It would surely be irresponsible if we gamble with the tax assessments and benefits of millions of Dutch people by presenting them with the bill afterwards."

title: Herman Brood included in state art collection: 'Like winning gold at the Olympic Games'
lead: An untitled painting by singer and artist Herman Brood, who died in 2001, has been included in the state art collection. The curators of the <entity id="org:rijksdienst-voor-het-cultureel-erfgoed">Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed</entity> (RCE) say they reached this decision because "we believe Herman Brood, as an icon of the twentieth century, deserves more recognition as an artist". This is the first time an artwork by Brood has been included in the Rijkscollectie, an enormous collection of more than 120,000 artworks and historical objects owned by the Dutch state. Brood, who scored big hits as a singer with songs such as Never Be Clever and Saturday Night , thus joins a list that includes 17th-century masters such as Rembrandt van Rijn and his pupils Govert Flinck and Ferdinand Bol, but also modernists such as Piet Mondriaan, Karel Appel and Armando. On the wall at the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> The acrylic work, which shows two men holding a pistol, until recently hung on the wall at the headquarters of the Belastingdienst in The Hague. Because many fake works and forged certificates of Brood are in circulation, the RCE says it has spent a lot of time in recent months establishing the authenticity of the work. To do so, it worked with the Stichting Valsbrood, a team of three old friends of Brood who specialise in recognising forgeries. The Rijksdienst writes that after research it was established that the work is authentic and dates from the early 1990s. 'A junkie who painted' One of the friends is 76-year-old Rob Dupre. He says Brood would "come to life spontaneously" if he heard this news. "During his lifetime he was seen as a rock 'n roll singer who earned extra money as an artist. Others called him a junkie who painted. As if anyone could do what he did. This news is like winning gold at the Olympic Games." Dupre says he is certain the painting is genuine. "Brood himself said he could not paint, but that his art was his handwriting. If you have looked over his shoulder for so long, you know when something is real or not." The two friends got to know each other in 1990 when Brood walked into Dupre's discotheque in the centre of Amsterdam. "Every Tuesday he performed for us. In return he asked us to help him sell his paintings." About eight months ago, the auction house Sotheby's approached Stichting Valsbrood with the question of whether they could take a look at Brood's untitled work on behalf of the RCE. According to Dupre, the team often sees immediately whether something is a forgery or not. "Herman's work is not as detailed as that of Rembrandt. We therefore have to look at the use of colour, because Herman was colour blind. We check whether the colour combinations fit and what kind of paint has been used. And whether the linen the paint is on is old enough. We of course examined this work extra carefully. We could not allow a forgery into the Rijkscollectie." A deal over tax debt Dupre estimates the value of the work at 15,000 euros. It is unclear whether Brood himself ever received money for the painting. Dupre does not rule out that it ended up with the Belastingdienst through a deal over a possible tax debt of Brood's. "He did not do receipts and that kind of bourgeois stuff. He painted five paintings and then spent them on drink, drugs and women. He was not businesslike at all." That a painting by Brood has been included in the state art collection, Dupre sees as the ultimate recognition of his craftsmanship. "People often said: 'My little daughter can do that too.' But what he did was incredibly difficult. If he took longer than 30 minutes over an artwork, we worried. Almost nobody can work that fast." The curators of the RCE acknowledge his distinctive style. "Especially his early work is creative and original, because he experimented with all kinds of techniques, but in which the hand of the artist is clearly recognisable", says a statement. The use of primary colours is mentioned, as is the fact that he often used syringes to apply paint to the artworks. "It was his own version of action painting. Or perhaps we can better speak of 'rock 'n roll' on canvas."

title: After earlier acquittal, 11-year prison sentence for man who killed girlfriend in 2016
lead: A 48-year-old man from Harderwijk has been sentenced on appeal to eleven years in prison for killing his girlfriend in 2016. The district court had earlier acquitted the man due to lack of evidence. According to the court of appeal, it can only be that Robert L. killed his partner, the court said. Despite "highly incriminating circumstances", he has left important questions unanswered, according to the court. L. reported the woman missing at the start of 2016. She was said to have left their home in Amsterdam-West in the night of 7 to 8 January 2016, in a drunken state, after an argument. On 29 March of that year, a hiker found her body in the Zandenbos near Nunspeet. After investigation it became clear that she had died by strangulation. Her boyfriend was quickly named as a suspect. Out of the house The woman wanted Robert L. to move out of the house. Their relationship was therefore very bad, but the man never said exactly where he was on the day of her disappearance. The court assumes that in those hours he drove from Amsterdam to Nunspeet. He was well acquainted with the place where her body was found. The court speaks of "a place that is not easy for others to find". He has always denied that he did anything to his girlfriend and remained silent during the trial. According to the court, it was L. who last saw the 51-year-old woman alive. A few weeks after his girlfriend went missing, L. lived in the home with another woman. The court holds L. heavily responsible for having killed the woman "in a very gross manner", reported her missing and refusing to answer questions about what happened, writes Omroep Gelderland. For example, he has told nothing about what the argument they supposedly had was about. Last year L. was acquitted in the district court in Amsterdam, after prosecutors had demanded fourteen years in prison. The judge ruled at that time that there were indications pointing to Robert L., but that hard evidence was lacking. The public prosecution service appealed.

title: Fixed, variable or dynamic? Households search for the right energy contract
lead: For months, prices for oil and gas have been rising because of the war in the Middle East. Large energy companies are not suffering from this, today's figures show. While companies are making high profits, energy tariffs for consumers keep climbing. And that raises the question: is it best to take out a fixed, variable or still dynamic contract? Several energy companies announced the sky-high profits they made over the past three months. Shell and Vattenfall, for example, saw their profits double due to high oil and gas prices. Meanwhile, the gas price for a megawatt hour rose above 100 euros yesterday for the first time since autumn 2022. The rising gas bill is raising questions at the Consumentenbond. "A lot of questions from people about what they should do. It is really alive." says Joyce Donat of the Consumentenbond. Consumer collective United Consumers also sees that customers are looking for answers and certainty. Still, there is no ready-made answer. Fixed contract "Until recently it paid to take out a fixed contract just before summer. Normally prices are lower then. But that was not the case this year because of the war in Iran," says Donat. The Consumentenbond advises people to mainly look at what feels most comfortable. A fixed contract for three years now means a lower price, but it can also mean that you pay a higher amount for a longer period if the gas price falls again. Some households the NOS spoke to choose certainty instead by taking out a fixed contract, even though it may cost more. Freerk Twijnstra is one of them. "We are moving this week, so we had to take out a new contract. It's just like investing: you don't really know how things will go. So we locked it in for three years." Anyone with a fixed contract that expires automatically gets a variable contract, whose prices are adjusted several times a year. For some people a fixed contract is not an option. For example, a fixed contract for the detached house of Harm in De Meern is so expensive that he chose a dynamic contract. With that contract type the price changes every day or sometimes every hour. Harm now pays just over 300 euros per month for energy. "I'm now above 2 euros per cubic metre. A year ago it was something like 1.10 euros." Even with a dynamic contract there is still an option to limit excessive costs. For example, when taking out his contract, Ibrahim Faydali from Enschede chose a cap on the gas tariff. "I pay a few euros extra per month for that. I'm very glad I did." A household's energy bill consists of the costs of gas and electricity themselves, but also of grid operator charges and an energy tax from the government. Minister Stientje van Veldhoven of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-kgg">Klimaat en Groene Groei</entity> says in a response to the NOS that she can well understand that households are worried about the rising gas price. "The cabinet is choosing measures to support precisely the households that need the most help." She is referring to the Noodfonds Energie and various subsidies for insulation. Not only gas. The high gas price is not only felt by people who use gas to heat their homes, because the electricity price is also linked to the gas price. Although much electricity is generated using wind and solar energy, still just over a third of electricity is generated in gas power plants. Marian Stevens runs a pottery workshop in Venray. Over the past years she has made it sustainable and she is fully off gas. Recently she had to take out a new energy contract. "I was quite shocked by what I saw: I have to pay a lot more. Given the investments we made to get off gas, I had thought we would not be spending so much on energy costs." The unrest in the Middle East persists for now. That also means that in the coming months the energy companies will probably continue to make large profits. In a response, Shell says: "We acknowledge that high energy prices can be problematic for vulnerable citizens and businesses, and that governments are also facing difficult choices." Voices in politics are being raised about imposing extra taxes on profits at companies like Shell. The company itself says it already bears a considerable tax burden worldwide. At this DIY store in Den Hoorn, they notice that mainly stoves and draught excluders are selling very well:

title: With a fat cat, French AI company Mistral says: take a look at us too
lead: With a reference to a fat cat, the French AI company is launching its newest AI model on the market: le chonk . The nickname refers to an internet joke about the weight of cats. The fatter the cat, the more 'chonk' the little beast is. The new AI model is officially called Large 4 and, according to Mistral, is the biggest and most powerful AI model the company has released so far: chonk, then. Mistral is seen as the only serious European answer to the American and Chinese AI companies, says Eric Postma. He is professor of artificial intelligence at Tilburg University. "The company is trying to compete with the American models, with the idea that you are not dependent on the United States for AI technology." It is difficult to compare different AI models well with each other, but experts see that the AI companies Anthropic and OpenAI remain the providers of the most powerful AI models. "Mistral is trying to develop the same type of product as these companies", says Jelle Zuidema, lecturer in artificial intelligence at the University of Amsterdam. "But they are always a few months ahead and it is just a little bit less." Much more investment in America But we should not let ourselves be too distracted by this 'race', Zuidema thinks. "The Americans are very much busy with that: who has the very best AI model? That is partly also to make a great impression." "They partly do that to raise money from investors", says Postma of Tilburg University. "That is deeply embedded in the culture of the United States: it is a ruthless struggle to raise as much money as possible. As a result, the American AI companies have a great deal of money at their disposal." Since its founding in 2023, Mistral has raised more than 6.6 billion euros, according to data from market analyst Crunchbase. By comparison: roughly 181 billion euros have been invested in OpenAI and 153 billion euros in Anthropic. "Because investors put such incredibly large amounts of money into Anthropic and OpenAI, these companies can offer their AI services far below cost", says Zuidema. "You can take out a subscription for 200 euros, but use thousands of euros' worth of AI computing power. The strategy: get people used to AI technology now, and raise prices later." Because Mistral cannot compete with that, the company has to look for something else that sets it apart from the competition, says Paul Verhagen. He is an AI and geopolitics analyst at The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies (HCSS). He thinks Mistral can benefit by emphatically presenting itself as a European company. "Mistral is not necessarily better than the AI models developed in the United States or China. And competing on price is difficult." Independent of the United States "But in Europe there can be another reason to still choose Mistral: you are then not dependent on other countries. We have seen in recent months that the American government is willing to block access to American technology. If that really happens, you do have a problem." "You do not want another country to be able to decide whether you have access to this technology", says Postma. Because AI is used in so many places, that could bring our entire economy to a standstill, says Zuidema. "We cannot assume that a good relationship with the US will always persist. If things go further in the wrong direction, Europe still wants to have access to good AI technology." Verhagen thinks European governments and important organisations should look seriously at Mistral from that perspective. "Think of Defence, but also the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> and energy such as gas and electricity. That is important for our security. It is good to use AI models from Europe there." "Mistral needs that support to become a successful company, he thinks. "The government does not necessarily have to look at the cheapest option, but can choose to consider independence more important. With the money Mistral earns that way, the company can keep developing its AI models and also help other companies with its knowledge. Mistral does not necessarily have to make the very best AI models, but it does have to be good enough to keep up."

title: CDA and D66 not happy with JA21, BBB and SGP's list of demands: 'Doesn't make it any easier'
lead: Coalition parties D66 and CDA are not happy with the list of demands that JA21, BBB and SGP presented this morning. "This has not made it any easier", says CDA-<entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">leider Bontenbal</entity> this evening. "Is this really what you want?", asks D66-<entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">fractievoorzitter Paternotte</entity>, addressing the three. The three right-wing opposition parties announced this morning that from now on they will work together in the negotiations with the minority cabinet. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is still looking for support for the tax plan and other budgets. The three are offering their support in exchange for adjustments to the plans of D66, VVD and CDA. JA21, SGP and BBB want the tax increase to meet the NATO norm, called the freedom contribution by CDA, scrapped, and a substantial tax cut. Medical ethics as bargaining chip. In addition, the trio want adjustments to the nitrogen plans, which BBB has long asked for, and more measures on asylum, which JA21 consistently advocates. The SGP demands on surrogacy and abortion policy have also become joint demands. Especially the latter irks Paternotte. "We are not going to trade fundamental rights of women for a budget," he says. "Medical ethics as a bargaining chip, that is crazy." Bontenbal does not go into the substance of the package from JA21, SGP and BBB, but does say that it has become more complicated to get out of it. "Because they have taken over each other's demands together." He does think the cabinet should keep talking with them. "Also to hear how firm the demands are." Showing colours. This evening the top of the cabinet is meeting together at the ministry of <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> to discuss how to proceed. Earlier today the premier, the deputy prime ministers and the <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> already discussed this here as well. Tomorrow morning the cabinet will speak with different combinations of opposition parties: first with the ChristenUnie and 50Plus, then with JA21, BBB and SGP, and finally with Pro and Volt. After that it is time for the cabinet to show its colours, says Bontenbal. "My patience is starting to run out." The three discussion combinations of tomorrow stand for three routes the cabinet has to find a majority for its plans. CU and 50Plus can together with the seats of Groep Markuszower secure a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. JA21, BBB and SGP together form 'the route on the right'. Pro and Volt also hold on to each other and are 'the option on the left'. Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> stressed in recent days that he is willing to compromise.

title: Cabinet wants smoking banned in places where many children are
lead: Smoking in places where many children are will be banned, if the cabinet has its way. People would no longer be allowed to light a cigarette at farms with animals for children or, for example, on the outdoor grounds of childcare centers. A proposal to ban this is expected to be discussed tomorrow in <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, sources told the NOS. Through the legislative change, managers of such places would be obliged to introduce a smoking ban. In principle, they would then also have to enforce that no smoking takes place. Many of those places, such as squares at after-school care and supervised playgrounds, have already been declared smoke-free by their managers. They want visitors not to smoke there. Yet at a small part of the places this is not yet the case. For those last places, the cabinet therefore wants a mandatory smoking ban after all. The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> has also asked for this, although parliament actually went further. Broad support: The Tweede Kamer initially also considered a smoking ban at other places where many children come, such as zoos and amusement parks. But the cabinet is first focusing on places that are entirely aimed at children, such as supervised playgrounds and childcare, because that would be easier to arrange given the broad support for it. Later, unsupervised playgrounds and places such as outdoor swimming pools could be considered. Smoke-free generation in 2040: The cabinet is aiming for a smoke-free generation by 2040, and this plan is part of that. Other measures have already been taken for this, such as a display ban, neutral packaging and fewer points of sale. The Adviescollege toetsing regeldruk (ATR) was already critical when the cabinet submitted this plan for advice, and the college also noted that earlier plans to have a smoke-free generation by 2040 did not appear to be effective.

title: Agent tasers parcel delivery driver after illegal parking in Amsterdam, bystanders outraged
lead: A parcel delivery driver in Amsterdam was tasered during his arrest yesterday afternoon. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the driver blocked the road while loading and unloading and the situation escalated. Bystanders filmed the incident. The incident happened around 3:30 p.m. in the Runstraat in the city centre. Footage in the hands of city broadcaster AT5 shows the driver has several parcels on the ground behind a white van. Behind that is a motorcycle. Watch the footage here, which a bystander filmed: The clip starts a few seconds before the man is tasered. A motorcycle officer and the driver are in discussion and the driver asks: "Why am I being arrested?", while stretching his hands out to the side. The driver is then tasered from close range. The driver falls to the ground. The footage makes clear that several bystanders express their outrage. For example, a woman shouts: "You can't just taser someone. Have you gone completely mad?" Situation escalated. A police spokesperson tells AT5 that the man had parked his van in a place where that was not allowed. The officer then spoke to him about it. The officer reportedly then asked the man to move the van so traffic could pass. The driver reportedly refused. A police spokesperson stresses to NOS that the footage is only a fraction of the bigger picture and that the officer was forced to use the taser. According to the police, the officer wanted to arrest the man but the man did not cooperate. He then used his electroshock weapon because the situation had reportedly escalated. The police spokesperson says the escalation may have taken place before the start of the video. Incident under investigation. The spokesperson stresses that officers must always report when they use force. Every use of force incident is investigated. "That should show whether this was proportionate," said the spokesperson. After his arrest the man was taken to the police station. He received several fines there. He has since been released.

title: Heavy fighting in Yemen, Houthis accused of causing famine
lead: Heavy fighting and bombardments are taking place in various places in Yemen. In the besieged city of Taiz alone, thirteen deaths are reported, mainly women and children. The local authorities accuse the Houthis, who have surrounded the city, of causing a famine in the city. "The city is not on the edge of a famine, but in a famine", says governor Nabil Shamsan. The southwestern city has been cut off from the supply of water, food, medicine and fuel. Since the start of the heavy offensive earlier this month, almost 300 people reportedly have been killed in fighting. Possible war crime There is a deliberately caused humanitarian crisis in Taiz, says Human Rights Watch in a statement. According to the human rights organization, the Houthis may even be guilty of a war crime. People in Taiz recently told the NOS that there is systemic starvation . In the city, nine civilians have been killed by Houthi fighters in two days, a local human rights organization states. Eleven civilians reportedly have been kidnapped. According to the Houthis' ministry of Public Health, thirteen people were killed today by a Saudi bombardment. These were reportedly mainly civilian casualties. Denial Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi claimed today in a televised speech that humanitarian aid is indeed being allowed into Taiz. He stated that only weapons deliveries to pro-Saudi militias are being blocked. The Houthis have occupied large parts of Yemen for years and are fighting against the Saudi Arabia-backed <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. The Yemeni armed forces claim that in 24 hours they have killed or wounded more than 300 Houthi fighters. Hundreds of attacks reportedly were carried out within one day. Positions of Houthi fighters in the west of Taiz in particular have been fired upon, according to the army leadership. Missile attack on Saudi Arabia The Houthis have claimed a series of air attacks on Saudi Arabia. Among the targets were two international airports and several oil refineries. According to the Saudi authorities, several missiles were intercepted. A Saudi citizen in the capital Riyadh was injured by falling debris. A house was also damaged.

title: Convicted Australian mushroom murderer loses appeal, will never be released
lead: The woman sentenced in Australia to life imprisonment for the murder of three people by poisoning with mushrooms has lost her appeal in the case. That means Erin Patterson has no chance of early release. Patterson (52) was sentenced at the end of last year to three life terms, with the possibility of early release after 33 years. The Office of Public Prosecutions appealed against that ruling. Justice found that, because of the seriousness of the criminal offences committed, the woman was not entitled to early release. The Court of Appeal of the state of Victoria agrees. "This offence was extraordinarily cold and calculating and deserves the most severe sentence possible", said one of the judges. The three judges of the court also rejected Patterson's appeal against her convictions. Poisonous mushrooms Patterson maintains that during a family lunch in July 2023 in Leongatha she accidentally added death caps, highly poisonous mushrooms, to the meal. The parents and aunt of her ex-husband died from the effects of the poisoning. The uncle of her ex survived the lunch but lay in a coma for weeks. Her ex-husband had also been invited to the lunch but cancelled at the last minute. Patterson can still challenge the Court of Appeal's ruling before the Australian High Court. That is her last opportunity to appeal her conviction. The case caused great upheaval in Australia and received much (inter)national media attention. A prison sentence with no prospect of early release is very rare in Australia.

title: Crypto platform Binance hacked, possibly billions stolen
lead: Binance, the world's largest crypto platform, has become the victim of a hack. According to the company, an estimated 6.3 billion dollars in crypto assets was affected by the attack, roughly more than 5.6 billion euros. The company says that about 3 billion dollars in assets has been recovered and frozen, so they cannot fall into the wrong hands. What has happened to the remaining more than 3 billion, Binance does not say. The company does note that "all user funds are safe". Co-founder Yi He says the company "will compensate all losses from hacks". According to its own account, the platform has a bitcoin fund to cover users' balances in case of a hack. Binance tells financial news agency Bloomberg that an investigation has started. In an initial statement the company says hackers may have entered the systems via a developer's laptop. It hopes users can access their balances within 48 hours, once the necessary security scans have been done. In a newer statement the company speaks of a complex attack and multiple points where security was breached. Because Binance does not have a license from the Dutch regulator <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">DNB</entity>, it has not been active on the Dutch market since 2023. It also received a fine of over 3 million euros because it was still active in the Netherlands without that license. Prices fell. The news about the security problems immediately led to sharp drops in cryptocurrency prices. Bitcoin fell to around 77,500 dollars, its lowest point in six weeks, and ether dropped below 2,200 dollars, its lowest point in months. The providers of crypto tokens Tether and Circle said that in response to the incident they have frozen balances. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino reported that his company has frozen more than 1.5 billion dollars in assets. Jeremy Allaire, co-founder and CEO of Circle, said that his company, "in coordination with investigative services", has frozen more than 800 million dollars in balances. Both companies issue so-called stablecoins, digital coins whose value is pegged to the US dollar. Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao. He stepped down as CEO in 2023 as part of a settlement with the US Department of Justice after he failed to prevent money laundering on the platform. In 2024 he was sentenced to a prison term, but in 2025 President Trump granted him a pardon.

title: Mega operation in Vught: monumental station building is lifted and moved
lead: This is no ordinary move: the monumental station building in Vught is being lifted in its entirety today and moved 13.6 meters. Weighing 720 tons, the building from 1868, including its historic basement, will be moved east over the course of seven hours. Watch a time-lapse of the first hour here: The operation began this morning at around 08:00. By mid-afternoon, the building, 28 meters long and 9.5 meters wide, must be standing in its new place. Livestream The move of the station building can be followed live at NOS. The station building has to make way for a fourth track. From 2030 onward, more trains must run between Meteren and Boxtel. That fourth track will be laid in a trench between Den Bosch and Vught, exactly where the station building now stands. That is why the building must be moved. Leaving the building in place and building around it, or demolishing and rebuilding it, were not options. The station building is a national monument, and by moving the building in its entirety, including the basement, its monumental value is preserved. The move is part of the High-Frequency Rail Transport Programme, an initiative of the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> that has been running since 2010. The goal is to run more trains on busy routes. On some routes, this must result in a "metro-like" frequency of six trains per hour. Currently, most routes have only two to four per hour. Concrete structure as a tray To move the national monument, it is first lifted. A concrete structure will then be placed beneath the building to serve as a kind of tray. A sliding track will be installed under that structure, with which the building will be slid to its new location in steps of 40 centimeters. In total, 34 steps are needed; exactly 13.6 meters. The building will ultimately sit 32 centimeters lower than it does now. Taco Bresser, director of the company responsible for the move, told the Brabant regional broadcaster DTV Nieuws that the chance of something going wrong is small. The building is in good condition and the distance is relatively short. The building will nevertheless be continuously monitored with measuring equipment during the operation. If anything deviates or weather conditions are unfavorable, the move can be postponed. Place with a wartime past The fact that the station building is a national monument is related to the major role it played in the Second World War. The station was at that time a place for the transports of thousands of Jews and other prisoners to and from Camp Vught. Het Brabants Dagblad writes how station master Willem Jooren, who lived above the station, helped prisoners who were deported via Vught. He provided them with food, tobacco, warm clothing, and helped some escape. The station's basement played an important role in this. Jooren hid people there and thus helped them stay out of the hands of the Germans. Granddaughters Ageeth, Gerdie and Marianne looked into their grandfather's story and are glad that the station building, including the basement, will be preserved. In 1984, Jooren was posthumously awarded the Verzetsherdenkingskruis, a decoration for resistance fighters from the Second World War.

title: 'Unworkable' and 'unfeasible', experts say of demands from right-wing parties
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> still cannot choose between left and right, so the opposition is putting pressure on the cabinet. JA21, SGP and BBB are putting demands on the table in exchange for support for the cabinet's tax plan. The most important demands concern migration, nitrogen and taxes. What exactly does the new alliance want, and are the demands feasible? Migration Unlike the previous cabinet, the Jetten cabinet wants to maintain the dispersal act, which distributes asylum seekers more evenly across municipalities. JA21, SGP and BBB believe that act should not be enforced: municipalities should be able to refuse an asylum seeker centre (azc) or reception facility. The parties also want the temporary status of Syrian refugees to be reassessed sooner, so that they can be sent back. And they want to see "concrete steps" in the short term on housing asylum seekers outside Europe, so that they can await the procedure there. "Many of the things written here seem practically unworkable," says associate professor of migration law Mark Klaassen (University of <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>) about the parties' proposal. "The <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> is already buried under a large mountain of applications and is currently not at all able to actively reassess Syrians. Then they would have to redo the entire procedure for these people." Not enforcing the dispersal act is in principle possible, says Klaassen. "But that will undermine municipalities' willingness to carry out the dispersal act. The minister does not have to apply administrative enforcement, but having no means of doing so at all will make municipalities less willing to comply with the obligation." Focusing on waiting for the asylum procedure abroad is already cabinet policy, Klaassen adds. "Whether that plan succeeds depends on the cooperation of countries outside Europe." Nitrogen The cabinet wants the agricultural sector to emit 42 to 46 percent less nitrogen in 2035 compared with 2019. This means, among other things, that dairy farmers may keep no more than 2.6 cows per hectare. JA21, SGP and BBB want to scrap this measure. The parties also want to raise the arithmetic lower limit, which concerns how much nitrogen may end up in nature, to 1 mol. That is 200 times higher than the current lower limit. "I assume these parties endorse the nitrogen targets, so that the country can get out of the lock," says Jan-Willem Erisman, professor of environment and sustainability (Leiden University). "But they are taking elements out of the plan without coming up with an alternative. With these proposals we will not get out of the nitrogen crisis." Taxes The parties want to get rid of the "freedom contribution", the extra tax on citizens to pay for investments in defence. In addition, they want tax relief for small and medium-sized enterprises in the Netherlands (MKB), and they want to address the tax gap between single-earner and dual-earner households. The parties do not explain where the money should come from. "What is in this letter is not concrete enough," says Bas Jacobs, professor of economics and public finance (Vrije Universiteit). "Correcting the tax burden for single-earner and dual-earner households involves many billions. The freedom contribution could also amount to an X number of billions. Tax relief for entrepreneurs in SMEs: hundreds of millions, if not billions as well." In general terms, the professor states that the parties are only concerned with serving their own constituencies. "Nobody feels responsible for the collective, for the treasury. That is becoming a problem, and the only way to solve it is to dare to take on pain too, and not just keep asking."

title: Incriminating material possibly shredded in Serbia as anti-corruption hunt begins
lead: It was already clear that Serbia's incoming leaders will have a tough time prosecuting their predecessors for corruption. But it may become even harder now that there are indications that government bodies are sending documents through the shredder. The country's highest prosecutor orders that the destruction must stop. In a statement she calls on prosecutors across the country to ensure that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> intervenes and reports such practices. The destruction is punishable and she calls for any attempt to do so to be recorded. Her instruction is "urgent", she writes in capital letters. Evidently there is a rush: the prosecutor points to "findings and information" that documents are going through the shredder at state institutions, banks, security services and other important institutions. Party mood In recent days photos have surfaced of bags full of paper shreds, taken by employees of public services. It is not certain whether these really are remnants of sensitive documents. The claim that large sums of money are disappearing at a state bank has also not been proven. But concerns that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of former president Vucic is trying to clean up its act as much as possible while it still can are not coming out of nowhere. It is precisely the fight against corruption and cronyism, and the promise to prosecute those who have been guilty of it, that gave the Student List a resounding victory in Serbia's parliamentary elections on Sunday. Serbia is still in a mood of relief and celebration, but the students are not yet in power, and that will take a while. First of all, the elections in 53 polling stations spread across the country must be rerun because of irregularities. Voters can cast their votes again there on Sunday. The final result will be determined on that basis. After that, the president has thirty days to convene the new parliament. That president is Ana Brnabic, a loyal follower of Vucic who is temporarily holding the post after he resigned in September to be able to run in the parliamentary elections.
