She can drag things out by taking the full thirty days. After that a government must be in place within ninety days. Brnabic must also call presidential elections, which by law must take place before the end of the year. Editors-in-chief dismissed Meanwhile the old government remains in office, albeit in a caretaker capacity. The civil servants at the ministries are also still in their posts, as are the municipal authorities, which without exception are in the hands of Vucic's party. The country is thus in a kind of power vacuum, where it is clear which direction it is heading in, but not exactly when. Footage is circulating of citizens removing portraits of Vucic from government buildings and throwing them into rubbish containers. Some officials are choosing to get ahead of events. The director of public broadcaster <entity id="org:zbo-registratiecommissie-tandheelkundige-specialismen">RTS</entity> resigned, after first sacking the editors-in-chief and heads of various programmes. RTS had under Vucic turned into a state broadcaster. Yesterday, the main TV news bulletin paid no attention to Vucic for the first time in a long time. Today the presenter, on behalf of the broadcaster, apologised on air. "Dear viewers, these are the first steps towards, we hope, the recovery of RTS. This is the first apology for everything we have failed to do in recent times. We still have to work on the content of the programme. We want to restore your trust." Misconduct The students want the regulator to take steps against commercial broadcasters close to Vucic. They are said to have systematically broken the law. Presenters of news programmes there have suddenly disappeared without a trace. As a result, gaps are appearing in the programming. The students also call on media, government and state-owned company employees to report misconduct via a special email address. As whistleblowers they will enjoy legal protection, the students promise. There is good news for festival-goers: the Exit Festival, also popular among Dutch people, is returning to Serbia. This year it has for the first time moved to various locations abroad. The organisers were under political pressure because they openly supported the student protests in the country. In July it will take place again as it used to in the city of Novi Sad.

title: US tech companies seek money in Europe, risk for European companies
lead: Quarterly figures from American tech companies this week show that they need even more money to develop artificial intelligence (AI). They increasingly raise that money by issuing loans, first in dollars but now also in euros. That also brings a risk for European companies. Building data centres in particular costs a lot of money. Previously these hyperscalers, as the large American tech companies are also called, mainly used their own profits, but that is no longer sufficient. That is why they issue many bonds. These are loans with interest and an end date on which the total amount lent is repaid. And these technology companies are doing this increasingly in euros instead of dollars. This allows them to reach a new group of investors. Alphabet, the parent company of Google, was the first hyperscaler last year and issued two loans that together amounted to more than 13 billion euros, and another 9 billion euros this year. And this year Amazon also followed with the largest corporate bond ever issued in euros: 14.5 billion euros. That was reason for the European Central Bank to keep a close eye on this development. Crowding out. Companies react differently to this development than before, says Oana Furtuna, financial markets analyst at the European Central Bank. "For example, there are European companies that postpone issuing a loan when an American tech company does so, in order to avoid direct competition." In addition, it may be that investors buy these new bonds and can buy fewer from other lenders. That could lead to crowding out of European corporate bonds, ECB economists including Furtuna write. Companies would then have to offer a higher interest rate on a loan, and it becomes more expensive for them to raise money. Economist Tyrone Gunther of <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity> also sees this risk. "When a lot of debt suddenly comes to the market, you see investors asking for more interest when they lend money. So it becomes more expensive for companies to borrow." Both economists do stress that this is not yet an issue in Europe. But in the US it is a different story. Chair of the American central bank Kevin Warsh recently expressed concerns about tech companies issuing loans. According to him, the rapid increase is one of the factors behind higher interest rates in the US. Debt mountain. Still, Furtuna thinks the arrival of these euro bonds may also bring advantages. In the European Union there are still only few technology companies issuing bonds on this scale. And these are often loans with a very long term. The choice for investors thus becomes greater. "In general, investors are certainly pleased with that", says chief strategist at Achmea Investment Management, Thomas van Galen. The arrival of these euro bonds also has another advantage, according to him. Many large European investors use bonds issued in euros to reduce certain interest rate risks. "The pond of bonds that investors fish in is thus better stocked", says Van Galen. The wave of debt that hyperscalers are now issuing comes at a time when governments face high financing costs. Interest rates on government bonds of the US, but also France, Germany and the United Kingdom, are rising to levels not seen in 25 years. That also affects investors' choices. "If you have the choice between a French government bond or a bond from a hyperscaler, then it is no longer a given that the government loan is the safer investment", says Van Galen. Now that AI companies increasingly issue long-term loans, the question arises whether investors will swap their government bonds for bonds from tech companies. Then it would become more expensive for governments to borrow. Although some analysts on Wall Street claim this, there is as yet no clear evidence for it.

title: Number of first asylum applications falls in third quarter
lead: The number of first asylum applications in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 13 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. That is what the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS) reports, based on provisional figures from the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst</entity> (IND). In the third quarter, which runs from 1 July through 30 September, almost 5900 people applied for asylum for the first time. That is 850 fewer than in 2025. Mainly Eritreans and Syrians made fewer applications. They accounted for 480 applications from Eritreans and 470 from Syrians, about half as many as a year earlier. Even so, the number of first asylum applications in the first nine months of 2026 is still 8 percent higher than in the same period of 2025. European Asylum and Migration Pact Since 12 June the European Asylum and Migration Pact applies, with as its main aim to reduce the number of migrants who enter the EU illegally and to gain more control over the asylum influx. The third quarter is therefore the first full quarter since the pact was introduced. The IND has also changed the way it works. Staff must now process asylum applications within six months, whereas that procedure often took about two years before. To make this possible, the procedure has been simplified. Vluchtelingenwerk Nederland and asylum lawyers warned that the procedure is indeed faster, but that this comes at the expense of care and quality . Especially vulnerable asylum seekers run risks as a result. Fewer family reunification migrants According to the CBS figures, in the third quarter 3200 family members of status holders came to the Netherlands. That is considerably fewer than in the third quarter of 2025, when 4700 family reunification migrants came to the Netherlands. About 70 percent of them came from Syria. The number of family reunification migrants over the whole of 2026 is almost equal to last year. Separately from the European Asylum and Migration Pact, the two-status system was also introduced on 12 June of this year, which aims to relieve the Dutch asylum chain and reduce the inflow of asylum seekers and family reunification migrants. A and B status That system distinguishes between refugees with an A status and people with a B status, for example people who fled war. Asylum seekers without a fixed refugee status (who have B status) may now only bring their family over after two years. Under the new rules they also must first have housing, have enough money to support their family, and family reunification is limited to the core family. Whether the decline in the number of asylum applications is related to the introduction of the new rules is unclear. Neither the CBS nor the IND can confirm that link, news agency ANP reports.

title: Two cats abandoned in neighbourhood cupboard: 'I'm sorry I did it this way'
lead: In a neighbourhood cupboard in Leusden, no food or hygiene products were left, but two cats. A handwritten note from the former owner was enclosed. In it, the person states that they do not have the money to pay the medical costs and see no other way out. It concerns two animals from the same litter. "I hope they can stay together. I'm sorry I did it this way." The cats are called Mikasa and Ashoka, the owner further writes, and they are not microchipped or neutered. That is why the animals could not go to the shelter, the former owner thought. "Out of desperation I see no other solution." The animals have been taken in by the Dierenbescherming in Amersfoort. They did not have to stay long in the neighbourhood cupboard before someone found them, the organisation reports. "We can imagine that people sometimes end up in a desperate situation and no longer know how to care for their animals. That is sad, for people and animals alike." Still, abandoning animals has consequences, the animal shelter emphasises. "The care, shelter and any medical costs come to us." The cats would not have needed to be microchipped to get a place in the Amersfoort shelter, it says. "Always call first, to prevent misunderstandings." 'Ring the bell' The Dierenbescherming is nevertheless glad that the cats were at least left with some information. For example, the note says the animals are sisters and were born in April 2023. "We are also grateful that they were left in a place where they could be found." The organisation calls on owners to ring the bell if there are financial problems or other factors that make it no longer possible to care for a pet, reports RTV Utrecht . "Sometimes just talking about your situation helps, and we can look along with you for a suitable solution."

title: Jetten speaks to the opposition: 'We can do business today'
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> thinks that results can be achieved today in the negotiations with some of the opposition parties on the Tax Plan and the budgets. "Everyone feels that you will have to make compromises somewhere. As far as I am concerned, business can be done today," Jetten said at the start of the talks. He says that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will make concrete proposals today based on the earlier talks. Jetten is speaking in turn with the three combinations of ChristenUnie and 50Plus, JA21, BBB and SGP, and last with Pro and Volt. The weekly <entity id="org:ministerraad">ministerraad</entity> has therefore been postponed to the afternoon. JA21, BBB and SGP presented themselves yesterday as an alliance with which a majority can also be secured in the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. But they do ask something in return, as is clear from the list of demands. These range from the nitrogen file to surrogate motherhood. Doubts Jetten already has doubts about this beforehand. "We also have a number of questions for them," he says. "Do you really want to link very heavy medical-ethical themes with what people have to pay at the petrol pump? I would not link them that way. Tying too many topics together leads to standstill." Coalition parties D66 and CDA already said last night that they were not so happy with the demands package of the new right-wing alliance. Jetten still says that the cabinet is not aiming for a choice 'between left or right'. He hopes that the cabinet can win over different opposition parties with different proposals.

title: Dutch economy continues to grow despite unrest in the world
lead: The Dutch economy continues to perform well. Over the past three months the economy grew by 0.6 percent. That is somewhat less than the previous quarter, according to calculations by the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS). Compared with a year earlier, the economy grew by 2.1 percent. "That the economy has been growing faster than 0.5 percent for two quarters now means the Dutch economy is in pretty good shape," says CBS chief economist Peter Hein van Mulligen. This was partly thanks in recent months to Dutch industry, which accounted for more than half of the growth. This mainly concerns the machine industry, which includes ASML, for example. "Dutch machines find their way to the whole world, we earn good money from that and this gives the Netherlands a competitive advantage," says Van Mulligen. More civil servants In addition, spending by consumers and the government increased. Consumers mainly bought more food and clothing and went on holiday more often. The government spent more on care and civil servant salaries. According to Van Mulligen, around 5,000 civil service jobs were added, mainly at the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and at defence. That is striking, because <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> wants to reduce the number of civil servants by 25,000 in the coming years. Expectations Despite all the political and economic unrest in the world, the economy continues to perform surprisingly well, according to Van Mulligen. "The expectations were that the economy would not grow strongly, but we are now beating all those forecasts." This was the reason the International Monetary Fund (IMF) adjusted its growth forecasts for the Netherlands a few weeks ago. According to the IMF, the Dutch economy has managed to keep the effects of the Iran war on oil and gas supplies limited. The Netherlands also appears to benefit from the fact that the German economy is doing better again.

title: Independent Russian newspaper Novaja Gazeta shuts down under pressure from authorities
lead: The independent Russian newspaper Novaja Gazeta is shutting down, editor-in-chief Sergej Sokolov announced in a statement on YouTube . The newspaper has existed since 1993 and is considered one of the last independent news media to have been critical of the Kremlin and President Putin. According to Sokolov, the decision was taken under pressure from the Russian authorities and secret services. The newspaper writes that from 9 November "the lights go out in our house where we have lived for thirty years". Last week Sokolov was already arrested and his home was searched. The organisation Reporters Without Borders, which campaigns for press freedom, called on Russia to "put an end to the legal intimidation" of Novaja Gazeta journalists. Silenced The newspaper made its name with solid investigative journalism and for years appeared several times a week in print and online. After the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, it was silenced after receiving warnings from the Russian media regulator for violating strict censorship laws by calling the war a war or an invasion. Since then, pressure on independent media has increased further. Novaja Gazeta lost its media licence in early September 2022, when a court in Moscow revoked the newspaper's licence. Part of the editorial staff continued from abroad under the name Novaja Gazeta Europe . Investigative journalism Last month the medium was placed on the list of 'foreign agents' by the Russian Ministry of Justice. Internationally this is seen as a means of repression to silence critics of the regime. Receiving donations has become even more difficult as a result. In the short term they must also leave their office in Moscow. Founder and former editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021. He dedicated that prize to six colleagues who were murdered, including investigative journalist Anna Politkovskaya.

title: JA21, SGP and BBB come up empty-handed with the cabinet, but Pro and Volt also see no movement either
lead: The three parties JA21, SGP and BBB, which together form 'the route over the right', did not reach agreement in their talks with the top of the cabinet. Pro and Volt, which work together as 'option on the left', still saw no movement from the cabinet on their part. "It was a tough, complicated conversation", said JA21 leader <entity id="person:bernard-johannes-eerdmans">leider Eerdmans</entity> after his talk. He spoke on behalf of the right-wing trio. "It is not yet where we would want it to be." Party leaders Eerdmans, Stoffer (SGP) and Vermeer (BBB) did not want to say anything about the content of their talks about the Tax Plan and the budgets. They also did not know whether they would talk further with the cabinet. "Everyone is going to let this sink in for a while", said Eerdmans. The three did say that their "little alliance" is still intact. Petrol station <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> said this morning that he already had doubts about the trio's package, mainly because of the demands on surrogacy and abortion. "Do you really want to connect very heavy medical-ethical themes with what people have to pay at the petrol station?" Coalition parties D66 and CDA also said last night that they were not so happy with the package of demands . After the three right-wing opposition parties, Pro leader <entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> and Volt leader <entity id="person:laurens-antonius-josephus-maria-dassen">leider Dassen</entity> were up next. They saw "not a single movement" from the cabinet on their most important demand. The two want the burdens for the wealthy to rise and those for workers to fall. "The gap is very large", said Pro leader Klaver. "We will have to talk about that further." Klaver expects that to happen this weekend, but a follow-up conversation is not scheduled. Back in the little car, ChristenUnie and 50Plus were the first to arrive this morning. When they came out, they were positive about what the cabinet had presented to them. "But we still need to see it on paper first", said CU leader <entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">leider Bikker</entity>. Both Bikker and Struijs of 50Plus issued a warning at the same time. If the cabinet makes major changes to accommodate other parties, their support could be in jeopardy. "Then we'll jump back in the little car and come back to talk here again", said Struijs. ChristenUnie and 50Plus, together with the Groep Markuszower, can secure a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. Markuszower, who spoke this week with <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>, said earlier that he makes few demands. For him it is mainly important that Pro does not come to power. How things go in the coming days, and with whom the cabinet will continue talking, is not yet known.

title: Police: tasered courier did not want to show papers and grabbed officer by the wrist
lead: The officer who tasered a parcel courier in the centre of <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> yesterday afternoon, according to the police, saw no other way at that moment to bring the situation under control. The courier had refused to move his van and also did not cooperate with his arrest, the police say. In a press release, the police state that the motorcycle officer asked the courier to move his van so that traffic could pass. In the busy shopping area of the Negen Straatjes, where this happened, a no-stopping rule applies between 12.00 and 18.00 hours. Traffic signs indicate this too. The no-stopping rule also applies to brief stops, for example to load or unload, the municipality says. The no-stopping rule was introduced for traffic safety reasons. 'Officer grabbed by the wrist' The police report that the courier did not want to move his van, whereupon the officer asked him several times for his driving licence and identity document. The man refused again, after which the officer wanted to arrest him and lead him to a wall. According to the police, the man grabbed the officer by his wrist, but the officer tore himself free and then used his taser. Footage of the incident, made by bystanders : Parcel delivery company GLS says it is distressed by the incident. The courier works for a transport partner that delivers parcels on behalf of GLS. "We are in close contact with the transport partner about the welfare of the parcel courier. We trust that the police will carry out a thorough investigation into the facts," said GLS. 'Judging too quickly' The police state that a short fragment "never shows the complete picture." "We ask everyone not to pass judgement immediately on the basis of only part of the information." Maarten Brink of the Dutch Police Union says that the police more often suffer from videos spread online. "We say, you need to have the whole picture. Often the videos are cut or edited. People quickly form a judgement through the media." Brink also points out that every time the police use force, it is reviewed: "This happens in all incidents." Officers must weigh at each situation which means of force to use. The use of the taser has been reported to a judicial officer, who will review it. The courier was taken to the police station yesterday afternoon. There he received three fines and was then sent home.

title: Zeeland provincial council member in trouble again, allegedly secretly entered commissioner's room
lead: The Zeeland member of Provinciale Staten Martin Bos is in trouble again. According to the King's Commissioner in <entity id="org:provincie-zeeland">Zeeland</entity>, <entity id="person:hugo-de-jonge">Hugo de Jonge</entity>, Bos has repeatedly misbehaved, he writes in a letter to Bos. The letter states that Bos insults officials, speaks intimidatingly and secretly entered <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de kamer</entity> of the commissioner. Bos says he was not there and cannot agree with the other accusations. The letter was sent to Bos by De Jonge two weeks ago. Bos came into Provinciale Staten as a one-man faction on behalf of Forum voor Democratie. At present he is no longer a member of Forum, as that party expelled him a year ago. Did not show up for appointment: The contents of the letter came out via Omroep Zeeland. The commissioner notes that he and Bos had agreed to hold a conversation, but that Bos did not come to that appointment. "That is why I set out below which topics we would have wanted to discuss with you," said De Jonge. In the letter De Jonge writes, among other things, that Bos sent staff of the clerk's office pressuring emails outside working hours, did not abide by house rules at his workplace, and submitted excessive expense claims. Bos denies that he was in the working room of Hugo de Jonge. He also says his tone in emails is always correct. "I do not recognise myself at all in this letter." Bos spent a lot of money on meals: This year it became known that for two years Bos spent conspicuously much on meeting costs compared with other factions. In 2024 alone he spent 10,000 euros on it, while another one-man faction (JA21) spent 100 euros in that respect. The receipts showed that Bos spent 88.5 percent of those meeting costs on meals. Strictly speaking that is not punishable, but Hugo de Jonge said at the time: "It is certainly irresponsible. You should not handle taxpayers' money like that." De Jonge asked Bos to repay part of the costs reimbursed in 2024 to Provinciale Staten. Bos has no intention of doing so: "Everything went according to the rules and everything was done correctly." 'Shameful and disrespectful' Colleagues in the Zeeland Provinciale Staten are also not happy with Bos's behaviour. "The whole affair is reprehensible and shameful," says Patrick van der Hoeff (PVV). "It does not do politics in general any good." Bos's actions reflect on everyone, says Gert Heijkoop (JA21). "I find it disrespectful towards your colleagues." Bos denies all accusations, but it is hard to explain, says Lizo Koppejan (ChristenUnie). "I am curious about the story. It is too bizarre for words." Wouter Versluijs (D66) does not believe him. "What on earth possessed him?" Forum not happy either: If the Staten members wanted to take measures, that is actually not possible. A Staten member is elected, and a representative cannot simply be dismissed. "The only one who can really say anything about it is the voter themselves," says political scientist John Bijl. "And they get a vote again in March 2027." That is when the Provinciale Statenverkiezingen take place. If Bos then campaigns, the question is for which party, now that FVD has expelled him. Forum is not happy, because the only one who can change the faction name is Bos himself, says a spokesperson for the party office. "For us there seems to be nothing else to do but to explicitly make clear ourselves that our name is being unlawfully used by Bos. We bear no responsibility for his behaviour and statements."

title: A week after Nairobi building collapse, search for victims continues
lead: Rescue services in Kenya are still searching for victims of the building collapse that took place in Nairobi last week . An eighteen-storey building under construction collapsed then. This morning the first fatal victim was pulled from the rubble. The woman was severely mutilated when she was crushed by heavy concrete that came down on Friday. This week rescue workers have used heat cameras to search for survivors. According to Kenyan authorities two people were detected under the rubble with those infrared cameras. It is not known how they are. Many people have now given up hope of finding more survivors. Relatives of possible victims have been waiting anxiously for days for news about their loved ones. Sixteen people are still missing. One day after the collapse four people were rescued. No permit The governor of Nairobi says the building was being worked on without the proper permits. He also says the ground-floor spaces should never have been rented out. There was an electronics shop, butcher and greengrocer there. According to news agency AP, buildings under construction collapse more often in the capital. There is said to be insufficient supervision of compliance with building regulations. Kenyan authorities say most of the rubble has now been cleared.

title: Russian with thousands of photos arrested in Poland on suspicion of espionage
lead: A 55-year-old Russian man has been arrested in Poland on suspicion of espionage. He reportedly took thousands of photos of transport facilities. A court has ruled that he will remain in pre-trial detention for three months. "The man is suspected of having carried out activities for a foreign intelligence service", the police said. "Everything indicates that the photos he took could have been used against state security." While securing a football match in the southwestern Polish city of Swidnica, officers saw a man taking photos of passing trains and the infrastructure at an unguarded railway crossing. According to the police, the Russian was sitting in a car and drove away quickly when he saw the officers. Later the police encountered him again. The man reportedly behaved nervously. Hundreds of thousands of files According to the police, professional camera equipment and data carriers with hundreds of thousands of files were found on him, including photos of important infrastructure and transport facilities, also outside Poland. The police suspect the man of taking the photos with the intention of passing them on to a foreign intelligence service. If convicted, he faces a minimum of five years in prison. "The fact that it has been possible to arrest a Russian citizen is quite rare", said Tomasz Siemoniak, spokesperson for the Polish intelligence service. According to him, Russian intelligence services previously avoided deploying their own citizens and preferred to recruit "disposable agents" from other countries for such tasks. Rising tensions Tensions between Russia and Poland have further escalated in recent months. Poland accuses Russia of espionage and sabotage on its territory. In September a Russian helicopter violated Polish airspace for 42 seconds, after which Polish fighter jets took to the air. Ground troops were also placed on high alert. At the end of September Nieuwsuur made this video:

title: Measures in cities after calls for demonstrations, police are alert
lead: Measures are being taken in several cities due to social media posts calling for demonstrations. These are aimed at <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity>, but the posts also call for riots and looting of shops. For example, a demonstration may take place tomorrow at the Malieveld in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, and there are also calls to riot in cities such as <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-maastricht">Maastricht</entity>. <entity id="person:pieter-heerma">Minister Heerma</entity> of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> says that "signals of worrying reports about demonstrations" have reached him. "The local triangles of various cities are working on it," he says. "They will take measures if there is cause to. They are on top of it." 'Demonstrating normally' It is difficult for the police to judge how seriously the calls should be taken. It is unclear to what extent they will be heeded. The police say they are in any case monitoring the online posts closely, are alert to possible disturbances, and are "visibly and invisibly" present at places named as protest locations. The police also call on everyone to demonstrate in a normal way and to report any demonstrations to the municipality. Minister Heerma agrees with this message. To people who want to take part in the demonstrations, he says that demonstrating is a right, "but think it over, behave yourself, and don't let yourself be dragged into situations where you think afterwards: how did I end up here?" Warning for parents Because many of the widely shared posts speak of a 'Gen-Z protest', schools and parents are also on alert. Schools in Maastricht, among others, have urged parents to be alert. The school umbrella organisation Stichting Limburgs Voorgezet Onderwijs (LVO) has sent a message to parents of all affiliated schools. It asks them to be alert to any plans their child may have. "We do not know whether the calls will actually lead to action or unrest," the schools said. "However, young people may decide out of curiosity or group pressure to go and look, without properly considering where they could end up. We would appreciate it if you discussed this at home." The police in Limburg support this request: "We also want to ask parents to keep an eye on their children's social media use," a spokesperson says. Also in Limburg, the police make no statement about escalation or deployment. A spokesperson does say the situation is being monitored. The <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity> Huygens Lyceum has also alerted parents by letter to the posts circulating. Shop windows in The Hague boarded up The police in Den Haag also say they are aware of the posts circulating. The municipality of Den Haag says that no demonstration has been registered, but according to a spokesperson it is "alert and prepared". Several shops in Den Haag are taking precautionary measures for fear of riots tomorrow. At a number of shop premises in the Hague city centre, windows have been boarded up. In recent weeks, massive protests in France got badly out of hand. Among the demonstrators were many pupils and students protesting against the poor state of French education. The demonstrations and riots then spread to Belgium. Protests are also expected again in France this weekend.

title: Woman dies after accident at Duiven Christmas show, police investigating
lead: A visitor died after an accident with an escalator at a Christmas department of a large garden centre in Duiven. That happened yesterday afternoon. The victim is a woman of 78. The woman is said to have fallen from the escalator at the garden centre's new Christmas show. The garden centre is known for its extensive range of Christmas items at the end of every year. Emergency services received a report of the accident yesterday around 4 p.m. The victim was resuscitated on the spot, writes Omroep Gelderland. She was then rushed to hospital, but help came too late. Possible medical incident It is unclear exactly what happened in the store. The police are investigating and are looking, among other things, at whether this was more than a medical incident. The store was temporarily closed yesterday after the accident, but is open as usual today.

title: What Do We Learn From the Biggest Crypto Heist Ever? 'Keep Quiet About What You Own'
lead: A few transactions totalling some 18,000 bitcoin, from the world's largest crypto platform, Binance, to an anonymous digital wallet that had only just been created. At roughly the same time, billions of dollars in other cryptocurrencies also disappear. More than that is not currently visible of what is the biggest crypto heist ever. If it really concerns an amount of some 6 billion dollars, it is by far the biggest heist ever. Bart Mol, of the podcast Satoshi Radio about bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, saw the first reports appear late last night. He quickly realised that something was seriously wrong. Crypto exchanges such as Binance hold money and cryptocurrencies of their customers, which are then traded with one another on the company's trading platform. Anyone can look up on the internet the digital wallets in which Binance keeps customer holdings. It is also possible to see how much crypto is in these so-called wallets. "People are keeping an eye on that," says Mol. "When large transactions are made, that immediately stands out." Part of the fairly unknown crypto coins was quickly converted into other cryptocurrencies via unregulated platforms. This is how the internet criminals are trying to cover their tracks, confirms Frank van Weert of Whale Alert, a company specialised in tracking large crypto transactions. "A red flag," says Mol about this. Binance issued its first statement soon after. Since then the company has been providing regular updates. A first investigation reportedly showed that the thieves got in through a developer's laptop. In the meantime, the company speaks of a complex attack and several points where security was breached. Binance repeatedly emphasises that everyone will be repaid. Can the company make good on that? "In absolute terms it is a huge amount, but compared to Binance's assets it is peanuts," says crypto expert Jacob Boersma. Around 140 billion dollars in cryptocurrency is parked at Binance. "I have every confidence that they can compensate customers," says Boersma. Crypto traders seem to be relying on that for now. The price of bitcoin, still by far the largest cryptocurrency, is only a few percent lower today. But Van Weert of Whale Alert is less convinced. "That 140 billion is not only Binance's. A large part belongs to the customers. You cannot fill one hole with another. It is going to hurt a lot, and you can wonder whether customers will still trust Binance after this." The company says it has meanwhile set aside the necessary money, without giving details about where it comes from. Experts whom NOS spoke to do not expect many Dutch people to trade on Binance's platform. In 2023 Binance withdrew from the Dutch market because it did not receive a licence from supervisor <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">DNB</entity>. Still, there is also a lesson here for Dutch holders of cryptocurrencies, believes Peter Slagter. Besides Mol, he is also a presenter of the podcast Satoshi Radio. "For years I have been saying: treat crypto exchanges like a public toilet," says Slagter. "You don't linger there either." There is a long list of crypto exchanges that did not survive incidents like this, with large losses for their customers as a result. A discussion that has been going on for as long as crypto has existed is therefore: where do you keep them? For European crypto exchanges, according to Slagter, the answer is now more nuanced because of stricter rules on security. "For an average crypto holder, I think that is now safer than keeping them yourself. There are also companies now that specialise in this." Your own vault But for those who are somewhat technical and install updates properly, keeping them yourself is still the best option, according to Slagter. "Keep in mind: then you are your own vault and your own security company. That also brings risks." "Make sure that a single incident cannot make you lose everything," Mol adds. "Keep part at home under your own control, part on one exchange, and yet another part somewhere else." "Keep quiet about it," says Van Weert. It is just like with cash money, he says. "As soon as they know you have it, they come after you."

title: Podcast De Stemming: Heartburn, a right-wing boy band and a shake-out
lead: Suddenly, on Thursday morning, things came to a head when the newly formed right-wing bloc of BBB, SGP and JA21 presented its demands to <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> in exchange for support for the tax plan. The coalition parties were so shocked by this knife to the throat that they almost immediately went into talks about how to proceed with their search for broad support. The right-wing and left-wing blocs were then allowed to come over on Friday morning to talk with the top of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, but that did not yet produce much result. De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister There you can also find all previous episodes . Just like all other well-known podcast channels . About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings ( EenVandaag , AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) take you through the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Want to respond? Email destemming@nos.nl.

title: Ouwehands says farewell to panda Lang Yue: 'Forever a little bit ours'
lead: Farewell was bid this morning to 2-year-old panda Lang Yue at Ouwehands Dierenpark in <entity id="org:gemeente-rhenen">Rhenen</entity>. The animal leaves for China today. "But she was born here, so she will always have Rhenen in her passport," says a slightly sad, but also proud mayor. Lang Yue was born in Rhenen in 2024. According to an agreement with the China Wildlife Conservation Association, she is moving to China now for her fourth year. Her parents originally come from China. After more than two years Lang Yue no longer needs her mother and can therefore live independently in China. Pandas are by nature animals that live alone a lot. 'Very well into the crate' "It is a mixed feeling," says keeper Brenda van Ekeren to RTV <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> . "You're glad everything has gone well, so far, but of course we're also going to miss her very much." This is how Ouwehands Dierenpark said farewell to Lang Yue: According to Van Ekeren, all keepers took leave of the panda together this morning. That happened when Lang Yue walked into the transport crate. Van Ekeren: "With a whole lot of training beforehand we managed that. She walked very well into the crate and had complete trust in us." The most important moment for the keepers came when the gate of the crate closed. "Then it's really final. Then you think: this is it." Waved off by children Also present at the farewell were dozens of primary school children from Rhenen. They stood ready with orange caps with panda ears to wave Lang Yue off. Because the panda was already in the transport crate, they did not see the animal themselves. "I've been here very often," the 10-year-old Julia told RTV Utrecht. "I just thought she was a really cute panda. So it is a shame. She was the cutest panda." After a traditional Chinese dragon and lion dance, the truck with the panda drove out of the park under police escort towards Schiphol. The keepers walked along to the exit and mayor <entity id="person:geran-kaai">Géran Kaai</entity> of Rhenen was also there. He finds Lang Yue's departure "a little sad". But, he also says: "She will always remain a little bit ours and we will always keep following her." Breeding programme in China In China, Lang Yue will take part in a breeding programme that maintains the population of giant pandas. She is the second panda cub born at Ouwehands since the park received two panda bears on loan from China in 2015. The parents, Wu Wen and Xing Ya, remain in Rhenen. They came to the Netherlands in 2017 under great public interest as part of the cooperation with China to protect the giant panda. Ouwehands is the only zoo in the Netherlands with giant pandas.

title: France recalls millions of condoms due to manufacturing defects
lead: France is once again recalling unsafe condoms. According to the French agency for consumer protection and fraud prevention, manufacturing defects have been found in fifteen different brands. The thickness and quality of the condoms are substandard, making them more likely to tear or break. In total it concerns seven million condoms, all produced by the Malaysian manufacturer Richter Rubber Technology. The condoms are also sold in other EU countries, possibly also in the Netherlands. It concerns the ultra-thin latex condoms for men of the brands Releaf, Einhorn, My Lubie, Primeros, You & Me, Amor, R&S and ON. These are sold both online and in shops. All recalled condoms are listed on an official website of the French authorities. The Netherlands is studying the signal. The Dutch <entity id="org:inspectie-gezondheidszorg-en-jeugd">Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd</entity> (IGJ) received a report from the French authorities this morning. France has taken precautionary measures to protect public health, the inspectorate tells the NOS. "We are studying this signal and will take any necessary action in the Netherlands. We are in contact with our colleagues in France and other European countries." Because condoms are legally medical devices within the EU, they fall under the supervision of the IGJ. Part of the seven million recalled condoms is sold only in France, writes the ministry of Economic Affairs. France urges users to get an STI test or, in case of a missed period, a pregnancy test. The country also advises consumers to contact the point of sale. In addition, France is suspending imports of the unsafe condoms for one year as a precaution. That measure can be extended if necessary, according to the French ministry of Economy. Second recall In August, France also recalled condoms. That concerned about 300.000 copies . The IGJ received no warning at the time. The inspectorate did see reports in the media and checked whether consumer reports had come in. "In general the IGJ occasionally receives reports about condoms. We have not been able to link these to the problems now being discussed in France", the inspectorate reports.

title: Man runs at king during working visit in Ursem, security staff step in
lead: During a working visit to the North Holland village of Ursem, <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> was approached this afternoon by a possibly confused man. That happened when the king had visited a fire station. Footage shows the man coming close to the king, but being stopped by security staff. A reporter for the regional broadcaster NH Nieuws was standing next to the king when it happened. "Security staff stopped him in time and the king spoke very briefly with him. The man said he needed help, because he is being destroyed by radar radiation." The regional broadcaster also writes that the man said he came from the village of Hoogwoud. Handing over a letter. The man then wanted to give a letter to the king, but the king referred him to his security staff. Eventually the man was taken away by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The king then continued his visit to the West Frisian village. He was there to visit various resident initiatives. The <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity> stresses that there was no attack. According to a spokesperson, the man "explicitly wanted to convey his message". A police spokesperson says the man was not arrested because he did nothing criminal. After he had walked along with the officers, he was allowed to continue on his way.

title: DNA match leads to arrest of 57-year-old man for 1994 sex crime case
lead: A 57-year-old man from <entity id="org:gemeente-helmond">Helmond</entity> has been arrested on suspicion of raping a 15-year-old girl in 1994. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> tracked the man down after more than 30 years through a DNA match, the Oost-Brabant police report. The deaf and visually impaired victim was waiting with a number of other children at a riding stable in the <entity id="org:gemeente-sint-michielsgestel">gemeente Sint-Michielsgestel</entity> on the evening of 30 May 1994, for transport to the institute for the deaf where she was staying. The man then allegedly pulled her into a car. He then allegedly raped her in a nearby forest. Afterwards he dropped the girl out of the car near her home, writes Omroep Brabant . During the police investigation, evidence was sent to the Forensic Laboratory, now known as the <entity id="org:nederlands-forensisch-instituut">Nederlands Forensisch Instituut</entity> (NFI), but despite extensive investigation it never led to an arrest at the time. The evidence was however kept for possible follow-up investigation. DNA profile in database. The case file was recently reviewed by the police cold case team. The detectives decided to ask the NFI to re-examine the secured evidence. "This investigation produced a DNA match with the suspect," says the police. According to the police, the DNA profile of the man from Helmond was in the national database because of another criminal offence. What kind of offence that was, the police do not want to say now. The man is in custody and was brought before the investigating judge today. The judge has decided that he will remain in custody for fourteen days longer.

title: Lawyer for Overasselt drug criminal Jan G. quits
lead: The lawyer for Jan G. from Overasselt laid down the defence today. He confirmed this to the NOS. He does not want to say why. Jan G. was arrested in Germany last month, because he is said to have been involved in smuggling almost 3900 kilos of cocaine via a transport company in Dordrecht. He is now in a Dutch cell. His pre-trial detention was extended by a month this week. On 1 September, G.'s house was attacked by more than thirty armed men, presumably over a drugs conflict. They shot dead a security guard that G. had hired outside the door. Officers who arrived at the scene were also shot and seriously injured. Drug lab The 3900 kilos of coke were intercepted in the French city of Dunkirk shortly after the attack on Jan G.'s house. This is not the only case he is currently involved in, writes Omroep Gelderland. Numerous other proceedings are ongoing. For example, the appeal in the case about a drug lab in Angeren, which G. ran together with several co-suspects in 2021, is to be heard in February. He was sentenced to four years in prison for this, but denies being involved. One of the other suspects lived a few houses away in Overasselt. He acknowledges the evidence in the case and has since made procedural agreements with the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>. With procedural agreements, the suspect waives an extensive trial in exchange for a lower sentence. Meanwhile, the public prosecution service also wants to seize the criminal profits G. allegedly made with the drug lab. A separate case is running on this. Brabant case Jan G.'s name also recently surfaced in a major Brabant drugs case. One of the suspects in this case told the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> that he was involved in ketamine trading with Jan G. in 2023. G. is not a suspect in this case himself, but may have to appear as a witness. The court of appeal still has to decide on this. Omroep Gelderland also mentions a separate investigation into Jan G. and his parents for money laundering. During a house search in 2023, officers found counterfeit money and firearms, among other things. According to the public prosecution service, however, this case is currently on hold. Threatening video Besides the intercepted consignment of 3900 kilos of cocaine, Jan G. may also have been involved in another drug shipment. Shortly after the attack on his house, a threatening video appeared in which he was held responsible for a missing consignment of 1283 kilos of cocaine. In the clip, masked men stated that Jan G. had to compensate for the loss. The conflict may have directly triggered the wave of violence that hit Overasselt in early September. The public prosecution service cannot yet say whether the content of the threatening video will lead to another criminal case against Jan G. over drug trafficking.

title: Prime Minister Jetten wants to resume talks on tax plan, but not on nitrogen
lead: A tough week awaits <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>, now that the nitrogen bill has been postponed and support for the tax plan is still uncertain. Still, Prime Minister Jetten remains optimistic. "I still see real opportunities" and "we will keep talking in the coming days," he says during his weekly press conference. At the same time, he announces he is not willing to "take steps back" on nitrogen and abortion. That raises the question of whether he will still get JA21, SGP and BBB to the table. They have made adjustments to the nitrogen plans and abortion policy a hard condition for support of the minority cabinet. Presentation of nitrogen plans cancelled. Remarkably, the presentation of the nitrogen plans by <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity> (Agriculture) was cancelled today at the very last moment. He wanted more time to process the comments from agricultural organisations LTO and NAJK. The timing of the budget talks with JA21, SGP and BBB may also have played a role. "Everything is connected to everything in politics, let's be honest about that," says Van Essen. What is the tax plan? The tax plan is the foundation of the cabinet's policy, because it sets out which taxes residents will have to pay in the coming years. With that money, the cabinet must then finance its own plans. This cabinet wants to raise income tax. At the same time, the tax plan this year also includes measures to improve purchasing power. Furthermore, it includes, for example, an increase in the drinking water tax and, on the other hand, a lower excise duty on petrol. The minority cabinet has to find support for this package. Tomorrow the cabinet will talk further about it with Pro and Volt and with ChristenUnie and 50plus at the Catshuis. The top of the cabinet will hold video calls with JA21, BBB and SGP. Pro and Volt, the 'left' option, saw no movement from the cabinet this morning. The two parties want lower income tax and more tax on wealth, but they have not yet brought the cabinet along. 50plus and ChristenUnie were more positive about their talks with the coalition. Together with Groep Markuszower, a party with which no official negotiations have taken place so far, they could help the cabinet reach a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The cabinet could, via that 'third' route, gamble that <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> would then not want to cause chaos with the tax assessments. But that is not the cabinet's intention, Jetten insists during the press conference. "We are really looking at how we can organise a majority in the Tweede and the Eerste Kamer, so that we can get some peace." Jetten meanwhile is increasingly putting the ball in the court of the opposition parties by pointing to the tax plans that will bring money to the Dutch. Without a majority, those will not go ahead either. "Good luck explaining that excise duties at the pump will then not go down," Jetten warns the opposition. Deadline getting closer. The deadline for the tax plan is thus getting closer. Normally a decision is made in August, but now at the end of October it is still not clear what the plan actually is. By Tuesday at the latest the cabinet wants to send it to the House of Representatives. The week after, the House must vote on it. The presentation by agriculture minister Van Essen of his nitrogen bill is now also scheduled for next week. The question is how agricultural organisations LTO and NJAK will respond. They sat at the ministry until late last night, but for now are keeping their support in their back pocket and say they have not yet seen the latest version.

title: Lawyer of tasered courier: man is injured and files a complaint against officer
lead: The parcel courier who was tasered yesterday afternoon will file a complaint against the officer involved. That is what the courier's lawyer, Gerald Roethof, says. According to the lawyer, tasering in this situation was in violation of the use-of-force rules of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Roethof also says his client was injured. "He was hit just above his private parts and a second time in his stomach." The courier, who works as a self-employed person, has been to a doctor. "In addition, my client fell because of the electric shocks. As a result he sustained an injury. His arm and wrist are bruised and he cannot move his fingers properly." A taser may only be used if someone, for example, has a weapon on them or intends to inflict serious bodily harm, says Roethof. According to the lawyer, none of that was the case. "So that use of force is far beyond all proportion." The police say the stun weapon may be used "in cases of directly threatening danger". Refusing to cooperate with an arrest can be such a situation, states the official instruction for the police. The officer saw no other way to get the situation under control, the police said today. The courier did not want to move his van and, according to the police, did not cooperate with his arrest. 'Investigation needed' When asked why the courier did not move his van, Roethof responds that it concerns a "man who wants to earn his bread honestly through hard work". He was indeed in a narrow street to deliver his parcels, says the lawyer. "Before he got the chance to do what was asked, the officer already wanted to arrest him." For example, the officer asked the man to identify himself. His driving licence was not in his pocket but in the car, says Roethof. His client would not have been given the chance to cooperate. Roethof claims his client's account differs from the police's. "The investigation must show whether the officer's claim is correct." Witnesses found tasering unnecessary. City broadcaster AT5 spoke with witnesses. One of them is Iris. She works in a shop where the courier had to be and witnessed the whole incident. "I think the way the police acted is unjust," she tells AT5. "The tasering was also very unnecessary." Another employee of the same shop says there are "always vans parked everywhere" in that place. According to her, that is nothing new. "I understand that you have to address someone, but to then arrest and taser someone, I don't understand that at all." The parcel courier had his hands up, another shopkeeper says. "I don't think the courier escalated it, I think the police did that." Images of the incident, made by bystanders: According to the police, the courier did not want to move his van, whereupon the officer repeatedly asked him for his driving licence and identity document. The officer then wanted to arrest him and lead him to a wall. According to the police, the man grabbed the officer by the wrist, but the officer pulled free and the man used the taser. The incident took place in the busy shopping area of the Negen Straatjes. The police stress that a short video fragment "never shows the complete picture". "We ask everyone not to pass judgement immediately based on only part of the information." The Dutch Police Union pointed out that police conduct is assessed every time the police use force. "That happens with all incidents."

title: Seal centre postpones bankruptcy for now after 'overwhelming support'
lead: The former Pieterburen Seal Centre is not for now filing for bankruptcy. The centre's board has announced this. Thanks to "overwhelming support from society", the seal centre can for now suspend a planned bankruptcy application. The Wadden Sea World Heritage Centre (WEC) has received 1.3 million euros in donations in three weeks. More than 100,000 people also signed a petition to save the centre. Thanks to all the support, the seal centre can keep operating for now and room has been created to look for a solution for the future. Last year the former Pieterburen Seal Centre was absorbed into the new WEC in Lauwersoog. The new centre was meant to give the outdated seal care facility a "sustainable future", partly by offering more space for education and experience. A bankruptcy is not yet fully off the table, says the WEC, which stresses that financial support will still be badly needed in the coming period. "Every donation helps to keep the work going and to build a sustainable future. The support also gives the centre the duty to do everything to continue to exist." Talks about the future Last week the centre also postponed the bankruptcy application by a week. Since then, talks have been held with various parties to close the financial shortfall of 2.8 million euros. There have also been talks with creditors and, according to the board, there is a prospect of an agreement. More clarity on this is likely within two weeks. "An agreement is a condition for being able to continue working on the future," the WEC said. The construction of the WEC cost 43.7 million euros at the time, 17.4 million more than budgeted. The doors opened in April 2025, but visitor numbers subsequently disappointed. As a result, the WEC's debt rose to around 2.8 million euros, an amount the centre cannot simply scrape together itself. The income from, among other things, entrance fees is roughly equal to the costs incurred. Great support from society The seal centre announced on 12 October that its survival was at stake and that it risked going bankrupt within two weeks. The WEC had placed all its hopes on financial support from the municipality of <entity id="org:gemeente-het-hogeland">Het Hogeland</entity> and the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>, but they let it be known they would not give money. Since the cry for help, supporters of keeping the centre are taking action. Donations are pouring in and there are many fundraising and sponsorship campaigns. Partners of the centre also want it to stay open, writes RTV Noord. Among others, WWF-NL, Visit Wadden, the University of Groningen and seal wardens sent letters of support to the municipality and province. The WEC says today that it is "deeply moved" by the support it has received so far, and says it will put "all its time and energy" into finding a solution.

title: Ten years on, more darkness in the Wadden area, but the battle is not yet won
lead: It is ten years this week since dozens of organisations agreed to better protect the darkness in the Wadden area. In that time a lot of steps have been taken, experts say, but there is still much to be gained. In October 2016, 43 parties, ranging from the central government and <entity id="org:zbo-staatsbosbeheer">Staatsbosbeheer</entity> to all kinds of nature organisations, signed a letter of intent called Dark Sky Werelderfgoed Waddengebied. Since then the partnership has worked to combat light pollution in the Wadden area and to preserve the darkness. This concerns 'excess' artificial light: outdoor lighting, advertising, illuminated logos and light in offices. According to ecologists, light pollution can disrupt the biorhythm of animals and plants. In addition, excess light makes the stars and planets less visible. Steps taken An de Wrede of the Friese Milieu Federatie, an umbrella organisation working for Frisian nature, sees that along various parts of the coast lighting is being used more consciously. "I'm thinking for example of the harbour in <entity id="org:gemeente-harlingen">Harlingen</entity>, or of the islands where green lampposts stand," she tells Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity>. But according to De Wrede, it could be much better. One of the biggest problems is the growing number of business parks, she explains. New buildings, car parks, advertising and outdoor lighting also mean new light sources. Room for improvement That there is still room for improvement is also the view of Jorian Moree, a cultural geographer specialising in climate adaptation. He has been involved in projects aimed at reducing light pollution in recent years. According to Moree, habit and convenience play an important role. It is easier to switch on all the lights at once than to investigate for each building or site how many lamps are really needed. "There is still much to be gained there." One of the places in the Wadden area where a lot of excess light was found at night was the harbour in Lauwersoog. Researchers looked at how many lampposts, floodlights and illuminated buildings there actually were in the harbour area. That produced striking examples. Quays where no ship was moored at night were fully lit. In restaurants or buildings by the fish auction that had been closed for hours, all the lights were still on. In 2023 the entrepreneurs decided to do something about the light pollution in the harbour. With the so-called Donkerte masterplan, they want to cut light emissions by 50 percent within three years. A dark harbour would also have positive effects for the Lauwersmeer National Park right nearby. Lighting was adjusted or made dimmable. In other places, motion sensors were installed, so lamps only come on when someone is actually present. Milky Way visible During the Nacht van de Nacht, a yearly campaign in 2024 in which municipalities, businesses and households switch off their lights at night to draw attention to light pollution, it became clear how much effect the changes in Lauwersoog had. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> and shipping company Wagenborg were asked to switch off as much lighting in the harbour as possible for one hour. "When the cloud cover cleared, the Milky Way became visible above Lauwersoog," says project leader Klaas Laansma of the Donkerte plan. "Measurements by researchers at the University of <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> show that there is now less light."

title: The Hague braces itself: shopkeepers board up their shops out of fear of riots
lead: Out of fear of what tomorrow may bring, a considerable number of Hague shopkeepers began boarding up their shop fronts today. They are playing it safe and do not seem willing to wait and see whether the disturbing reports circulating on social media become reality. Via platforms such as Snapchat, Telegram and Instagram, calls have been made to take to the streets in various Dutch cities to protest. There are fears this will escalate into riots and looting, although it is unclear who or which organisation is behind the calls. It is also difficult to estimate how many people will turn out. Apple store already empty That no protest has been registered with the municipality of The Hague does not seem to concern the entrepreneurs there. In France, Belgium and Italy, demonstrations recently escalated into large-scale riots, in which many shops were vandalised and looted. The fear after all the reports on social media is that The Hague is next. Anyone walking through the city centre immediately sees all the precautionary measures taken. Among others, the Tommy Hilfiger shop, the Lego store, a branch of fashion brand Guess, a Kruidvat outlet, a jeweller and the local kitchenware shop have been barricaded. Some shopkeepers have even announced they will stay closed so their staff can stay home. The Hague Apple store has chosen to clear out the premises in advance. Images show there is no phone or laptop left anywhere in the store. A group of carpenters is busy with the preparations. That The Hague shopkeepers are choosing to board up their premises seems to earn understanding from the shopping public who were in the centre today. "It is something you don't expect in the Netherlands. It is un-Dutch," says a woman to Omroep West. "If I were a shopkeeper here, I would rather spend a few thousand euros on preparation than later face tens of thousands in damage and have my shop looted," her husband adds. The chairman of the shopkeepers' association says several entrepreneurs have been threatened by phone. "They were told their shop would be cleaned out tomorrow." 'It can happen quickly' A carpenter who is boarding up a perfumery explains how he goes about building the barricade. The skirting boards in front of the shop fronts have been removed, wooden posts have been placed, and then plenty of wood has been screwed against the shop front. Whether this keeps potential rioters out? "They get through everywhere, but we're trying to stop them." Meanwhile there is still hope that all the precautionary measures will turn out to have been unnecessary after all. One shopkeeper says: "Hopefully nothing at all will happen tomorrow, but with social media it can happen very quickly."

title: Group photo at G20 summit cancelled, countries do not want to be photographed with Russia
lead: The traditional group photo at the G20 summit in the United States did not go ahead because of the presence of Russian minister Lavrov of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. The American government decided to drop the photo moment because other attendees threatened a boycott. Delegations from a number of countries that support Ukraine, including Canada and Australia, did not want to be in the 'family photo' with Sergei Lavrov in Atlanta, the photo with all participants of a summit. A number of delegations even threatened to walk away, writes the American news channel CNN. European officials still thought that two separate photos might be made, one with Lavrov and one without him. When that proved not to be the case, the American Secretary of State decided to forego it, because he did not want the summit to be overshadowed by a photo row, say involved American diplomats to news agency AP. Chance to talk Lavrov responded calmly to the controversy. "If it is mainly important to you how you stand in the photo and who you stand next to, then that says enough." He repeated the Russian position that it is mainly European hostility towards Russia that stands in the way of peace negotiations. German minister Wadephul acknowledged that Lavrov's visit to the summit was controversial, but also called it an opportunity to keep pressing for peace in Ukraine. "It is really time to end hostilities and discuss how this conflict can be resolved." Whether agreement will be reached on that is still an open question: analysts fear that, because of mutual disagreement on important issues, not even agreement on a joint closing statement will be reached. Besides Ukraine, the agenda also included, among other things, the American war with Iran and China's influence in Asia. Putin invitation Minister Lavrov warned that the recent rapprochement between the US and his country does not mean the air has cleared. Trump may have scrapped diesel sanctions because of high fuel prices, but other sanctions are still in force. "The underlying questions have not been resolved", Lavrov believes. "No real steps have been taken in the relationship with the US. Don't harbour any illusions about the diesel deal.' The G20 consists of the nineteen countries with the largest economies, the European Union and the African Union. This summit was a preparation for a meeting of heads of government next month in Florida. President Trump has also invited his Russian counterpart Putin to that, but it is not yet clear whether he will come. Lavrov said afterwards that he had had a pleasant conversation with American minister Rubio. Only briefly, "because as host he also had other commitments", the Russian said.

title: Podcast De Dag: tons of subsidy for a film that never reached the big screen
lead: A star cast with Oscar winners Dustin Hoffman and Helen Hunt, beautiful footage in palazzos in the Italian town of Lucca, and all of it under the direction of the respected and well-known director Peter Greenaway; the film Lucca Mortis has it all. The <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-nederlands-fonds-voor-de-film">Nederlands Filmfonds</entity> puts in more than five tons in subsidy, to help Dutch makers involved in the film. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps . Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. But a few years after filming, the film has ended in a tragedy. Nieuwsuur reporter Fleur Damen looked into it and made a reconstruction together with NRC. Shooting days did not go ahead because the actors and crew were not paid, post-production is on hold because invoices were not transferred, and director Greenaway is no longer involved in the film. The Filmfonds says it knows nothing about this and maintains confidence that Lucca Mortis will appear on the big screen. What does that say about making these kinds of films with subsidies? Reactions: email to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial: Marco Geijtenbeek & Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Wake-up call 31/10: Anti-government protests in several countries • Five Eredivisie matches, including Ajax-AZ
lead: Good morning! In several countries people are demonstrating again today against the policy of the national <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. People have also been called to protest in the Netherlands on social media. Football is also being played today: five matches are on the programme in the Eredivisie. Leaders Feyenoord play Fortuna Sittard, and number 2 Ajax host number 5 AZ. First the weather: cloudy and somewhat misty. In the south there will be sun now and then this afternoon. It will be around 12 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss: An evacuation convoy from the Ukrainian city of Olejsky has safely reached the Crimea, which is occupied by Russia. Residents of the besieged front-line city were brought to safety by buses and ambulances. Most residents there had already fled earlier, but an estimated 2000 were still left behind. The residents were living in dire conditions, with almost no supplies and a constant threat from drones, mines and snipers. Russia and Ukraine had agreed a ceasefire to make the evacuation possible, after mediation by Pope Leo and the American first lady Melania Trump. According to Ukraine, several hundred people made use of it. Other news from the night: And finally this: In the Zeeland capital Middelburg as many as 42,000 little lights are hanging on a house for Halloween. The light spectacle by Bob Rijnaard is a great success. It started out as a bit of fun, but it has now grown into a real happening with lights, lasers and sound effects. The whole neighbourhood helps, and children in particular are wildly enthusiastic. Have a great day!

title: Cabinet continues talks with opposition as deadline approaches fast
lead: The cabinet is continuing talks today at the Catshuis with the opposition about the tax plan. So far it has not succeeded in securing sufficient support for it, while the deadline is fast approaching. This morning there was an internal meeting between <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, the deputy prime ministers Yesilgöz and Van den Brink and <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. Afterwards the party leaders Bikker (ChristenUnie) and Struijs (50Plus) will drop by. Together with the Groep Markuszower, with which no official negotiations have yet taken place, they could help the minority cabinet in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> reach a majority. Digital conversation Afterwards there is a digital conversation with party leaders Eerdmans (JA21), Vermeer (BBB) and Stoffer (SGP). This 'little alliance' of right-wing parties is not visiting The Hague, at its own request. The three gave a lukewarm response yesterday regarding their offer to support the tax plan, provided a number of conditions are met. These concern, among other things, asylum, nitrogen and abortion and surrogacy. The coalition parties D66 and CDA have great difficulty with that. This afternoon Pro and Volt will come to the Catshuis. They are also working together. These parties could together secure a majority in the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>, but the VVD in particular sees little in a cooperation 'over the left'. Deadline approaching The deadline for the tax plan is getting closer. Normally it is settled by August, but now, on the last day of October, nothing is clear yet. By Tuesday at the latest the cabinet wants to send the bill to the Tweede Kamer, which will vote on it a week later. Afterwards it will still go to the Eerste Kamer. Most measures in the tax plan must take effect on 1 January.

title: Police clear centre of Zoetermeer, ten people arrested
lead: Police intervened last night in fights in the centre of Zoetermeer. The ME cleared the area. Ten people have been arrested. According to Omroep West, unrest arose during or after a Halloween party in the Stadshart. There were several fights between groups of young people. When the police wanted to intervene, fireworks were thrown at officers. Subsequently dozens of young people fled. Some of them ran into car parks. Others fled along the shops. Pursuit While dozens of police officers launched the pursuit, the mobile unit cordoned off the centre. Everyone still walking around there was sent away. A number of arrestees are still in custody. It has not been announced what they are suspected of.

title: Intellectually disabled man abducted and abused after date arranged on dating app
lead: A group of people in their twenties is suspected of abusing and humiliating at least two people they approached via a dating app. One of the victims was also abducted. The abducted victim is a 61-year-old man from Schiedam. Last month he was taken from his home and held overnight in Amsterdam. He was also abused there. His hair and eyebrows were partly shaved off. His nephew speaks on behalf of the victim and says he is a very vulnerable man. "My uncle has a mild intellectual disability," says nephew Jerry. "He often ends up in situations where people take advantage of his good nature, but this surpasses everything." Date In the night of Saturday 19 to Sunday 20 September, the man from Schiedam thought he had a date with another man. They had made contact via a dating app. The victim's family suspects he was lured into a trap. The man agreed to meet at home in Schiedam and was then taken against his will by two men to Amsterdam-West. There he was abused and a video was made of him. A third man is said to have been involved as well. Images on Snapchat Footage of the victim was subsequently posted on Snapchat. The video also shows a young man who says with a laugh: "Listen, today I cut someone's hair for the first time in my life." "My stomach turned when I saw that," says Jerry. "What was done here is degrading." The video also shows the victim looking dazed, receiving slaps to the head and having fingers poked into his eye. "Treating vulnerable people like that, I have no words for it." Jerry thinks his uncle was drugged and is a victim of homophobia. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating the motive. Two arrests In the case, two men from Amsterdam aged 21 and 23 have meanwhile been arrested. The police also suspect them of a similar incident in Hilversum. There, someone was abused in June, also after a date arranged via a dating app. A third suspect, a 21-year-old man from Haarlem, is in custody for that incident. All three are suspected of coercion and assault. The third suspect who was involved in the abuse of the man from Schiedam has not yet been identified. The intellectually disabled victim from Schiedam was eventually released the next morning. The men took him outside and left him alone. The man rang the doorbell of a house nearby and the residents alerted the police. Officers searched the house where the victim had been held that same morning, but no one was home at the time. The suspects were arrested later, the second one last week. In intensive care The man from Schiedam, according to his family, spent a few days in the hospital's intensive care unit after the abduction. "He had several kinds of drugs in his blood," says Jerry. He thinks the drugs were administered to him. The police are investigating this. In the meantime his uncle is doing better. He lives in a different place. "He doesn't dare be at home anymore, because that's where it all started," says Jerry. The victim's family hopes that attention to this case can help prevent similar incidents. According to the police, dates arranged via dating apps more often end in a crime. "Think of people who are robbed or fall victim to sexual violence," says a spokesperson. Out of shame or fear, victims do not always dare to go to the police. The police emphasise that such an incident is never the victim's fault and that they are always taken seriously by the police.

title: Rain forecast for part of Gelderland uncertain because there are (possibly) bats
lead: Quickly checking the app to see whether it will rain is of little use for now in parts of Gelderland.
