"Both countries should work together and provide clarity. You are simply dealing with people who follow their hearts, who want to play football for Suriname, but who now do not know where they stand. They are being mercilessly punished in this way. I find that truly incomprehensible." Several Surinamese players decided not to play for 'de Natio' during the last international break because of the uncertainty, Fraser admits. Players such as Danilho Doekhi (Lazio), Milan van Ewijk (Coventry City) and Jayden Oosterwolde (Fenerbahçe) have also put the choice for Suriname on hold. Voluntarily giving up nationality Jean-Paul Boëtius was also not involved in September. But the clubless winger was simply not called up, he says by telephone. However, he too has automatically lost his Dutch nationality, after he first played for Suriname in 2025, and thereby, without knowing it, voluntarily gave up his Dutch nationality. Boëtius is by no means the only one. Among others, Tjaronn Chery (NEC) and Virgil Misidjan (RKC <entity id="org:gemeente-waalwijk">Waalwijk</entity>) are in the process of trying to regain their Dutch nationality. That could take a year, Chery said at the start of this season in conversation with the NOS. Recently Boëtius received a letter from the Rotterdam municipality. "It stated that within the next two weeks I must hand in my Dutch passport. Under the so-called huppelepup law, you have lost your Dutch nationality. Yet just before all this began I had renewed my Dutch passport. It is still valid until 2036." "I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport, which gives me a residence permit to live in the Netherlands. But yes, that is also only for a year. Yes, this is a very annoying situation. I simply want to become Dutch again. I was born and raised here." "The Dutch passport is also simply stronger than the Surinamese one", Boëtius continues. "If I want to fly somewhere, east, west, north, south, wherever... With a Dutch passport that always works. But with a Surinamese passport you often have to apply for a visa." "You know, I am super proud that I was allowed to play, and still am allowed to play, for Suriname. But it is a pity that it has turned out this way. I and other players feel rather misled, by people who, incidentally, no longer work for the Surinamese federation." Boëtius: "I just want to say that I am now receiving very good support from the federation, there are lawyers who are working out every detail for us. But their predecessors came up with the so-called sports passport. Only... that did not exist at all."

title: Dead and injured after two helicopters collide on Mount Everest
lead: Two helicopters collided and crashed on Mount Everest. One person died and two people were injured. Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and China and is the highest mountain in the world. There are no roads on the mountain, so helicopters are the only way to bring sick or exhausted hikers down. The helicopters crashed in the village of Pheriche, which lies at about 4,200 metres altitude. Rainy season over. A 47-year-old tourist from India died in the accident, news agency AP reports. A traveller from New Zealand and one of the helicopter pilots were also injured. It is not clear how many people were in the helicopters. Autumn is a popular season to climb Mount Everest, because the rainy season is over and it is less cold than in the winter months. But the trek is also very popular with hikers in the rest of the year. So popular that the Nepalese government has in the past taken measures to curb the number of climbers, but without a clear effect.

title: Prime Minister Jetten asks opposition: take responsibility
lead: Prime Minister Jetten calls on the opposition in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> to take their responsibility and give sufficient support to the tax plan. He points out that extra investments are being made in purchasing power and safety. According to him, there are now very nice elements "for left and right" in it. Jetten said this after an extra <entity id="org:ministerraad">ministerraad</entity>, in which new adjustments to the tax plan and Box 3 were formally adopted. The plan now goes to the Tweede Kamer, which will debate it tomorrow. Once the letter has been sent, more will become known about the content. At the last minute: <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>'s top agreed last night on changes to the tax plan. According to Jetten, this is now the third time the cabinet has made concessions to the opposition. The minority cabinet does not want to choose the bloc on the right (JA21, SGP and BBB) or the bloc on the left (Pro and Volt), and is therefore not assured of a majority in advance. Still, Jetten is optimistic. He said there have been many "constructive talks" and that he also feels the need, together with the opposition, to enter 2027 with a good tax plan. Ahead of this morning's consultation, Jetten said he has every confidence that it will turn out well. "I am convinced we can bring the Chamber over the line to support these plans." Jetten pointed out that a number of opposition parties are positive about the adjustments. This concerns in any case the small centre parties ChristenUnie and 50Plus. Those two cannot together help the cabinet to a majority, but with the support of the Groep Markuszower, which split off from the PVV, it does add up sufficiently. According to Jetten, it should also succeed in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. "Together here in The Hague we bear the responsibility to do good things. And a good tax plan with many improvements for citizens and businesses is part of that." 'Tough process' <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> called making a tax plan with a minority cabinet that has insufficient support in the Tweede and Eerste Kamer "a tough process". He said he will keep puzzling until the last vote. "I keep presenting proposals. We cannot let this slip from our hands." He too expects the plan to be adopted in the Tweede Kamer in any case. About the Eerste Kamer he says: "We are doing it step by step, and this whole route is full of risks, but I keep puzzling, and every time we come one step closer."

title: Tax plan 2027: purchasing power up slightly, VAT increase on ornamental horticulture postponed
lead: The higher VAT on flowers has been postponed by a few months and the freedom contribution, a tax on labour, will not go ahead next year. That is apparent from the revised tax plan, which was approved this morning by <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. The document has just been sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. New in the plan is that the higher VAT on ornamental horticulture will only be introduced in the course of 2028, instead of at the start of that year. It was a major wish of BBB to change this plan. Furthermore, it becomes clear that the freedom contribution, a plan of the CDA to levy extra tax on labour and spend that money on defence, is off the table for next year. That concerns 347 million euros. The tax would place too much on the plate of 'ordinary, hard-working people', several opposition parties felt. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to cover that by scrapping tax benefits for companies and individuals, but still wants to consult the Tweede Kamer on which benefits these should be. Purchasing power improvement <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> said this morning in an explanation that there will be 1.5 billion in purchasing power improvement compared with Prinsjesdag. Several commitments have been made since then, including not raising the excise duty on fuel. The deduction for specific care costs remains, but will be more targeted at people who really need it. That was a major wish of ChristenUnie and 50Plus. In addition, a total of 95 million will become available for security in the coming years, among others the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> will benefit from that. That was mainly at the request of Groep Markuszower, which together with ChristenUnie and 50Plus can secure a majority in the Tweede Kamer. How exactly this amount will be spent will be made clear later. The new wealth tax in box 3 will, after criticism from the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>, be postponed by one year from 2028 to 2029. Only "if that is feasible" can the cabinet possibly still let the plans take effect in 2028. The change is partly 'covered' by temporarily further lowering the low rate for entrepreneurs in box 2. The hope is that they will use this benefit to withdraw more capital from the business, which would then ultimately yield tax money for the state coffers. This coverage therefore for now exists only on paper. Furthermore, 3.1 billion comes from a pot that was ready to compensate wealthy people who have paid too much tax in recent years. CO2 storage The plans also state that the cabinet saves almost 170 million euros by postponing money for 'Aramis' to 2032. Aramis is a project to store CO2, originating from industry, in an empty gas field under the North Sea. What this postponement means for the climate goals is not clear. The Tweede Kamer debates the package of tax measures tomorrow. Premier Jetten called on the opposition in the Tweede Kamer today to take responsibility and give sufficient support. In the letter, the cabinet already responds positively to an amendment (a proposal for a change in legislation) from ChristenUnie and 50Plus to lower income tax for the two lowest income groups. To pay for that, the increase in the labour tax credit that the cabinet had proposed would be scrapped. That means the tax reduction will apply to a larger group of citizens than only employees. ChristenUnie wanted people with a disability benefit to benefit from it too.

title: Americans to the ballot box, here is where the difference is made
lead: In America it is Election Day , and the results of the Congressional elections will trickle in tonight. In these midterm elections, the Republican majorities in Congress are at stake. All seats in the House of Representatives are being elected again, and in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> it concerns 35 of the 100 seats. The elections are important for President Trump and his Republican party to firmly keep power in Washington. The Democrats see an opportunity to curb Trump's extensive power. Although Trump remains unpredictable, Congress at least has influence over budgets. That can also be important, for example, for American support for Ukraine or the introduction of sanctions packages. Both the House and the Senate are currently in Republican hands. According to Cook Political Report , an independent American polling website, the Democratic party is on course to win a majority in the House of Representatives. In the Senate, the task is harder. That is because Democrats must take several seats from the Republicans, in states that were won by more than 10 percentage points two years ago. Still, a shift is not unthinkable. How exciting is the Senate election? Of some of the 35 seats in the Senate being decided today, it is already virtually certain who will win them. In fifteen states, according to Cook Political Report, the race is not yet over; in six states, it could really still go either way. In North Carolina, one of the fifteen states mentioned, the Democrats hope to take a seat from the Republicans fairly easily. That would be an early boost for the party in the evening. It is important, though, that the Republicans do not take a seat from the Democrats in New Hampshire, Minnesota or Michigan . In that last state, a hard campaign was fought and it could go either way, but Cook now considers the chance greater that the Democrats will keep their seat there. Nieuwsblad The Economist is more cautious than American polls when it comes to the Democrats' chances. The chance that they gain control of the Senate is, according to them, 53 percent. How exciting is the House of Representatives election? That the Democrats could win the House of Representatives is therefore not unthinkable. For that they need 218 seats. Cook Political Report considers the chance already present that the Democrats could take fifteen seats from the Republicans. That could already be more than enough for a majority. Eighteen elections could still go either way. In swing states such as Michigan and Pennsylvania, red could easily turn blue again. If the Democrats manage to gain a majority, the speaker of the House of Representatives will be a Democrat. For now, that is still the Republican Mike Johnson, an important figure in American politics. Election night at the NOS The NOS will broadcast the results live tonight in a livestream . From 03.00 hours, Arjen van der Horst will provide commentary on all developments. At 07.00 hours he will hand over to Mark Visser, who will connect with studio guests and our correspondents and reporters in the United States. From 09.00 to 09.30 hours we will address viewer questions. Want to know something? Email vraag@nos.nl . When will we know the result? It is likely that we will know the day after the elections who gets the majority in the House of Representatives. The Senate may take longer. Four years ago, it was only clear on Sunday who got the Senate. Each state has its own counting system, so in some states it takes longer. The political sensitivity surrounding the counting of votes may also cause certain results to take longer to become known. The Trump administration openly questions the system. Donald Trump is already pursuing several lawsuits to steer results that he does not like in his favour. So it could still be a turbulent night. Want to know more about the elections? In the video, our correspondent explains what is at stake:

title: Woman in Tilburg home died as a result of a crime
lead: The woman found dead last Sunday in her home in Tilburg died as a result of a crime. That is what the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. The body of the 54-year-old woman was discovered Sunday morning in the home on Berkenrodelaan. What exactly happened has not been made public. A day later, the police still reported that there were suspicions of a crime but that multiple scenarios were being taken into account. According to Omroep Brabant, a great deal is still unclear. Who is responsible for the woman's death is not yet known. No suspect has been arrested yet. After the body was found, the police conducted an investigation in the home, among other things. A team spoke with neighbours. Screaming According to the Brabants Dagblad, the woman lived alone and neighbours heard screaming on Sunday. Her body was then reportedly discovered by family members.

title: Fireworks dealers can apply for compensation, entrepreneurs dissatisfied
lead: Shopkeepers who sell fireworks can register from today for a compensation scheme, because they are missing out on income at the coming New Year's Eve. This New Year's Eve there is a fireworks ban, and private individuals may not set off fireworks. There are a number of conditions fireworks dealers must meet to claim the compensation. For example, shopkeepers must show that around New Year's Eve from 2025 to 2026 they sold fireworks intended for New Year's. Dealers must also have sold fireworks in December in at least one previous year. This concerns 2022, 2023 or 2024. If entrepreneurs are entitled to the compensation, they will be reimbursed for the lost profit. This is based on the quantity of fireworks they purchased earlier. The lost profit is a set average profit percentage on that purchase value, and the entrepreneur may choose a reference New Year's period: 2022-2023, 2023-2024 or 2024-2025. The amount shopkeepers receive is corrected for inflation. On top of that, entrepreneurs receive a one-off surcharge of 15 percent for one-off costs, and an additional 3500 euros per sales location is paid out, up to a maximum of five sales locations per dealer. Shopkeepers can register until 18 January at 17.00 hours with <entity id="org:rijksdienst-voor-ondernemend-nederland">Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland</entity> (RVO) for compensation. The RVO plans to pay out 80 percent of approved applications by 1 March 2027. Dissatisfaction Dealers are dissatisfied with the compensation. The vast majority of the fireworks retail trade is affiliated with the foundation Vuurwerkcheck, of which Frans Köhler is chairman. The foundation campaigns for the preservation of consumer fireworks and advocates safe fireworks use. Köhler calls the compensation scheme a "compensation for shopkeepers that is as limited as possible". Köhler thinks businesses that depend mainly on fireworks sales in the winter period are heading for bankruptcy. He knows that some shopkeepers have to adapt their premises for new activities. "They only get one year for that, and the costs of those adjustments will probably be much higher than the compensation." The chairman says the fireworks ban will encourage the illegal fireworks market. "Illegal fireworks have already been imported on a large scale by criminals. They are far more dangerous and there is no quality control on the products. You also don't know where they are stored," he says. "Illegal fireworks are sold 365 days a year, and a criminal doesn't stick to three sales days." Some young people still want to set off fireworks. In April 2025 a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> voted for a private member's bill regulating a total ban on consumer fireworks. In earlier years this was discussed more often, and in 2020 some firework varieties were already banned. In July 2025 <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> also voted for the law, which took effect last August. Speaking to NOS Stories, about three thousand young people said they still plan to set off fireworks, even though it is prohibited. Young people who want to set off fireworks say in a questionnaire that they mostly plan to buy them abroad. Germany, Belgium and Poland are especially popular. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> says it will carry out extra checks on this. Municipalities barely grant exemptions. Neighbourhood clubs and associations can apply to the municipality for an exemption so they can still set off fireworks. Regardless of the scheme, most Dutch municipalities say they will not grant exemptions for the coming New Year's Eve, Trouw newspaper found in its survey. Municipalities say they have had too little preparation time. There are also not enough enforcement officers to supervise, and it remains unclear who is liable in case of damage or injury. Interested associations must comply with strict rules, such as the delivery of fireworks on New Year's Eve, drawing up a safety plan, keeping sufficient distance from the public, and having no more than eight adults set off fireworks.

title: Fishermen help thousands of eels cross safely at Maurik hydroelectric plant
lead: Professional fishermen have over the past two months safely transferred more than 9,000 kilos of adult eel at the hydroelectric plant in the village of Maurik (Gelderland). According to the fishermen, that is a record, writes Omroep Gelderland. The adult European eel is also called silver eel. The silver eel migrates every year from the Dutch inland waters towards the Sargasso Sea, some 5,000 kilometres further in the Atlantic Ocean. There, near the Mexican coast, the silver eels reproduce. Dangerous obstacles Along the way they encounter all kinds of obstacles such as pumping stations, weirs and the hydroelectric plant in Maurik. Some of the eels do not survive that, for example because they are ground up by the turbine blades. To prevent the population from being seriously disrupted, professional fishermen catch the silver eels upstream of the hydroelectric plant and release them on the other side. This has been done since 2011 within the Paling Over de Dijk project. "For this project we use fifteen large fyke nets. We catch the silver eel that is on its way to the sea but is held back by the locks in the weir and the power plant. The aim is to catch the species before the animals reach the plant, so the eel is not damaged," explains fisherman Frans Komen to the regional broadcaster. Not correct The autumn migration of the eel lasts for the rest of the month. Komen expects the number of rescued eels to rise to about 10,000 kilos. Last year around 7,000 kilos of eel were moved from one side of the power plant to the other. That difference is easy to explain, the fisherman says. "This is because there has been no raised water level this year. When the water level is raised, the weir is opened and the eel has a free passage to the sea." The fishermen give the eel a hand because they consider it "not correct on ethical grounds" for the eel to be damaged by a plant, Komen says. But there is also a commercial interest for the fishermen. "I also have an interest in a good eel stock, so that the silver eel can be released undamaged and take part in reproduction." All other fish species caught in the operation are returned to the water.

title: Chinese web giant JD.com may buy MediaMarkt's parent company under conditions
lead: Ceconomy, the German parent company of MediaMarkt, MediaWorld and Saturn, may nevertheless be taken over by the Chinese web giant JD.com. The European Commission investigated the takeover because JD.com would receive financial support from the Chinese government. There were fears that MediaMarkt, MediaWorld and Saturn could engage in price wars after the takeover. JD.com is statutorily based in the Cayman Islands and is listed on the stock exchange in Hong Kong. The Commission's investigation showed that JD.com indeed benefits from, among other things, tax advantages it receives in China. As owner of Ceconomy, the stores in Europe could also use this support to introduce "aggressive prices", leaving competitors behind. The Commission concluded that the EU internal market would thereby be unfairly distorted. To prevent the takeover from being prohibited, JD.com offered that all services and transactions with Ceconomy will take place on "market-conform conditions". Supervision In practice this means that, in short, no unclear discounts would be given for, for example, purchasing and logistics. That also applies to the storage of goods and technology services. The agreement applies for ten years. For the European Commission, the main concerns about the takeover have thus been resolved. An independent party will supervise compliance with the agreements. A notification must also be made if Ceconomy or one of its subsidiaries in the EU achieves an annual turnover of 500 million euros or more, or receives more than 50 million euros from abroad.

title: Woudenberg couple sentenced to 20 and 12 years in prison with TBS for years of abusing childminding children
lead: The 57-year-old Richard van den B. from Woudenberg and his ex-wife Evertje van E. must serve 20 and 12 years in prison respectively for abusing their childminding children. Both will also be subject to TBS with compulsory care. The couple sexually abused five young children aged between 0 and 10 over many years. There is not enough evidence for the abuse of a sixth child. It concerns children from two different families whom the couple regularly babysat. The parents of one of the families were friends with the couple. The other family is that of Van E.'s brother. Some of the children were drugged with GHB during the abuse. A cautious calculation by the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) showed that the children were abused more than 700 times in total. This afternoon the judge spoke of "an abuse case of the outer category". According to the judge, the suspects raped children "who had been entrusted to their care and vigilance" by means of coercion. "Children were seen as objects for use", quotes RTV Utrecht . The two were arrested at the beginning of last year after two children told at home about the abuse. The man had been asked for a 30-year prison sentence, the woman for 20. Fear Van den B. has denied most of the abuse. He admitted that he had a sex addiction, but said that he abused the children "not deliberately". His ex-wife initially denied it but later admitted that she cooperated out of fear of her then partner. Zo admitted that she had administered GHB to the victims and said that she held children while her partner abused them. TBS Richard van den B. was difficult to examine, experts found in court. He never "showed the back of his tongue". In his case, the experts could not reach an advice on TBS. Nevertheless, the judge imposes TBS with compulsory care on him. The court finds that he cannot return to society without treatment. His ex-wife did receive a TBS advice and the judge follows it. Several disorders have been identified in her, including PTSS as a result of years of sexual abuse by her father. Her father has been convicted for this. She receives a shorter prison sentence, partly because she is not fully criminally responsible. The two have also been given a contact ban with the victims.

title: Month in prison for pro-Palestinian demonstrator who hit others with a plank
lead: A man who abused two people during a pro-Palestinian protest in 2024 will receive a one-month prison sentence. The court in Amsterdam has decided this. The 37-year-old man, Samer A. protested on 6 May 2024 at Roeterseiland , on the campus of the University of Amsterdam. The demonstrators had set up tents there and erected barricades. At some point the protest was disrupted by masked men, who broke through the barricades. The man then attacked two people who had nothing to do with the disruption, the court writes. He hit them with a wooden plank, as a result of which they suffered head injuries. The man has already spent 36 days in pre-trial detention. He therefore no longer has to go to prison. A. still has to pay compensation to the victims: 1385 and 750 euros. Physical complaints The two victims, according to the court, still suffer from the abuse. "They both experience physical complaints, such as tension headaches, fatigue and restlessness, and psychological complaints, such as feelings of fear, stress and feelings of insecurity." They also both could not work, or only to a limited extent, temporarily. A. is according to the court guilty of an attempt at serious assault. He argued that there was a case of necessary defence or a state of emergency, but the court does not go along with that. He was also suspected of public violence, but he was acquitted of that. The Public Prosecution Service (OM) had requested a prison sentence of 100 days, 64 of which conditional. The OM had also requested a community service order of 180 hours.

title: Fewer women invited for breast cancer screening due to staff shortage
lead: Fewer women took part in the population screening for breast cancer last year. That is shown by a new monitor on population screening for breast cancer by the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">RIVM</entity>. Due to staff shortages, including too few screening laboratory technicians, fewer women were invited for the screening last year than normally. Because fewer invitations were sent, fewer women therefore also took part. Without screening, cancer may be discovered later in some people, while early detection of breast cancer is important. It can mean a less severe treatment and the chance of recovery is greater. There have been backlogs for years. As a result, dozens of women a year additionally die in the longer term from the consequences of breast cancer. <entity id="person:sophie-hermans">Minister Hermans</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-volksgezondheid-welzijn-en-sport">Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport</entity> wrote today in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> about the important developments around population screenings. It states that for the time being there is no prospect of improvement. Screening laboratory technicians: There is a shortage of screening laboratory technicians who take the breast X-rays for the population screenings. A delay arose when the breast cancer screening was halted for some time in 2020 due to the corona pandemic. The delay has not yet been made up. In 2025, almost 1.2 million women received an invitation for the population screening for breast cancer. Of them, almost 820,000 women took part in the screening. In 2024, 6 percent more invitations were sent. Participation was comparable in both years. The number of women screened therefore decreased, because fewer women were invited. Solving the shortage: In an attempt to curb the staff shortages, Bevolkingsonderzoek Nederland, which carries out the screenings, launched a recruitment campaign for training candidates. The candidates could follow the training to become a mammography technician and then start working in breast cancer screening. The RIVM writes on its website that the campaign was successful and that all available training places have been filled. The RIVM has also looked into options for having mammograms made by hospital staff. The public health institute writes that various hospitals have made an offer for this. But despite the measures that the RIVM and Bevolkingsonderzoek Nederland have taken, there is still no prospect of improvement. Three types of population cancer screening: Every year, hundreds of thousands of women take part in the population screening for breast cancer. Women under 55 and over 70 take part least often. In 2025, just over 2.7 million people took part in population screenings for three types of cancer. Besides breast cancer, there was also a population screening for bowel cancer and cervical cancer. Through the three screenings, about 27,000 tumours or precursors of them were detected, according to monitors by the RIVM. More cancer diagnoses: The expectation is that the number of new cancer diagnoses in the Netherlands will rise from just over 136,000 last year to almost 170,000 in 2045. That was reported by Integraal Kankercentrum Nederland (IKNL) at the beginning of October. Population growth and ageing are the main causes. The number of people dying of cancer is also rising: from just over 46,000 in 2024 to just over 57,000 in 2045. Yet according to IKNL, the average risk of getting a cancer diagnosis will remain roughly the same over the coming twenty years, due to population growth and ageing.

title: Indian navy rescues 20 crew members from Iranian fishing boat hijacked by pirates
lead: The Indian navy has rescued twenty crew members from the Iranian fishing vessel Azini. The ship was hijacked by pirates northeast of Somalia last week, the Indian Ministry of Defence reports. The 48-hour rescue operation took place in the Arabian Sea, more than 3,000 kilometres from Mumbai. There were 21 Iranians and two Somali security guards on board. It is unclear what has become of the remaining crew. According to India, a warship, a maritime surveillance aircraft and marine commandos were deployed in the operation. To free the hijacked ship, commandos were also dropped by parachute over the sea from a C-17 transport aircraft. According to an official of the maritime police of the Puntland region, twelve suspected pirates were disarmed and released. The regional authorities were reportedly only informed after the operation had ended. Minor injuries The suspects and the two Somali security guards came ashore at the coastal town of Bandar Bayla, in northeastern Somalia, according to the official. Three of them had minor injuries. The Iranian embassy in New Delhi thanked the Indian government on X for rescuing the twenty Iranian crew members. According to the embassy, the rescue operation reflects the "friendship, solidarity and cooperation" between Iran and India. The hijacking took place between the coastal towns of Bandar Bayla and Hafun. The Indian forces followed the ship by sea and air before intervening. The hijacking took place on a busy shipping route between Asia, the Middle East and Europe. According to the Indian navy, the hijacked fishing boat was at risk of being used for new pirate attacks on strategic trade routes in the Indian Ocean. Five months in the hands of hijackers The hijacking took place against the backdrop of a resurgence of Somali piracy in the Gulf of Aden and the western part of the Indian Ocean. Between April and August, pirates hijacked six commercial ships, some of them far from the Somali coast. One of these was the oil tanker Sibu 1, hijacked about 252 kilometres east of al-Mukalla in Yemen. In September, the Puntland authorities reported that pirates had killed five crew members of the tanker MT Honour 25 before security forces retook the ship. The ship in question had by then already been in the hands of the hijackers for more than five months. According to the authorities, sixteen suspected pirates have since been arrested. Thanks to international naval patrols and improved security at sea, Somali piracy had declined sharply over the past decade. The recent hijackings have, however, reignited concerns about a return of the phenomenon.

title: Cabinet presents nitrogen law, more room for tailored measures
lead: Provinces will get more room to fill in nitrogen policy around sensitive nature. That is set out in the detailed nitrogen plans of the cabinet. The cabinet also wants to speed up raising the so-called arithmetic lower limit. Before the summer, the cabinet had already announced the nitrogen plans in outline. The nitrogen package must ensure that emissions in 2035 are drastically reduced compared with 2019. The nitrogen law presented today states that provinces have until September 2028 to come up with plans for zones around nature areas. This may mean that the zones around nature areas where restrictions apply become smaller, but the policy becomes stricter. 9 miljard euro uitgetrokken: the cabinet has allocated 9 billion euros. Before the summer, the cabinet aimed for a zone of 500 metres around nitrogen-sensitive nature, and around fifteen areas the zone would even be 1000 metres wide. In recent times Minister of Agriculture Van Essen has been in talks about this with farmers' organisation LTO and NAJK, which represents young farmers. Within a few months it must become clear which nature areas will get zones. Farm businesses in those places must comply with stricter nitrogen emission rules than their colleagues outside them. If provinces do not manage, strict national rules will apply in the zones. To support farmers in the zones, the cabinet has allocated 9 billion euros. Furthermore, the cabinet wants to bring forward the raising of the arithmetic lower limit. That lower limit is currently 0,005 mol (roughly zero), which in practice means that a nature permit must be applied for everywhere, also for very small (construction) projects. With raising the lower limit, it becomes easier to build. A condition for the raising is that the nitrogen targets and measures proposed by the cabinet are fixed. The fear is that otherwise raising the arithmetic lower limit would not be legally tenable. The arithmetic lower limit can, incidentally, only be used for permit granting once nature on the spot is in order. With the nitrogen law presented today, a large part of the plans is filled in. "In June we chose the direction. Today we lay down the route", says <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity> of Agriculture about it. Later, more specific measures will incidentally follow. The target of 42 to 46 percent less emissions in agriculture and 50 percent in mobility and industry is being enshrined in this law. This makes room for large (construction) projects, which often cannot get a nitrogen permit now. The targets apply to 2035, and 2028 is the first checkpoint. "If we are not on course then, we will intervene", says the cabinet. Generic cut: in case this does not work, the cabinet had a stick behind the door in mind, namely a generic cut. In other words: nationwide shrinking of the livestock population, so that all businesses would have to shrink. This measure drew criticism, including from the <entity id="org:planbureau-voor-de-leefomgeving">Planbureau voor de Leefomgeving</entity>, because it would also affect farms that have already taken big steps. The cabinet says today that tailored measures will also become possible here. Opposition party Pro has so far supported the nitrogen plans of the minority cabinet, which means a majority in both chambers is in sight. The party is positive about what has been presented today. MP Bromet says she considers it "good work" by the minister. "After years of talking, finally action." Van Essen says in any case that today's plans are "no watering down". The minister also hopes that farmers' organisations LTO and NAJK can live with it. He does not expect them to "lead a polonaise", but in his view they can see "that talking pays off".

title: Podcast De Dag: Wikipedians in the age of AI
lead: Around 10,000 Wikipedia pages are read every second. The online encyclopedia is 25 years old and attracts enormous numbers of people, but due to the rise of AI that is declining. Want to listen? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. Wikipedia is maintained by volunteers. In this podcast, two of them, Hay Kranen and Stella van Ginkel, describe how a Wikipedian works in 2026. How do you make the encyclopedia as complete as possible? How do you inspire others to start writing and how do you guide them in that? And how does it feel when the articles you have poured your heart and soul into are slurped up by AI bots and served up in their own programmes? Presentation and editing: Dieuwke Teertstra Editorial team: Max Smedes and IJsbrand Terpstra Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Discharging PFAS? That could now cost companies millions of euros in fines
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> and environmental enforcers are getting more options to act against environmental crime. For example, penalties for environmental violations will be higher. More acts will also become punishable. Furthermore, it will become harder for companies that have caused serious pollution to escape prosecution. This is the result of rules adopted by <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. They implement a European directive, which all EU member states must transpose into legislation. Environmental crime includes, among other things, drug dumping, illegal discharges by companies and manure fraud. The OM is "very positive" about the new rules. "The approach to environmental crime is very complicated and technical. These rules offer a number of options to make the approach more effective," says Joost de Weijer of the OM. Prosecuting directors. The OM wants to demand higher sentences. "In practice you see that sentences imposed for environmental cases are relatively low. This directive gives the OM the chance to demand higher sentences." De Weijer mentions higher fines as an option. From now on, fines of up to 40 million euros can be imposed. Until now, in environmental cases, usually no more than a few hundred thousand euros were demanded. Furthermore, more emphasis will be placed on prosecuting directors of companies that commit serious violations. Halting business operations also comes more prominently into view as an option, according to De Weijer. PFAS scandals. Sjoerd Lopik, jurist and environmental law researcher at Leiden University, calls the directive an important step in tackling environmental crime. He also notes that penalties for offenders were very low in the past. "They often were not in proportion to the profits companies make." He expects the higher penalties to have a deterrent effect. He points out that companies with an outdated permit now have a greater chance of prosecution. "Under the previous situation, companies could simply keep discharging as long as they had a permit, even if it was clear that what they were doing caused serious pollution." That will become harder under the new rules. Examples of outdated permits leading to pollution are the PFAS scandals involving Chemours in Dordrecht and Sabic in Bergen op Zoom. These companies turned out to have discharged large amounts of PFAS for years. Their defence was that they simply had a permit for discharges, so any damage could not be attributed to them. Many companies still work with outdated permits today. Last year, former minister Tieman of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> acknowledged that the central government is lagging behind in renewing permits. More serious. Under the new rules, danger to the environment becomes an independent reason to prosecute people or companies. "Criminal prosecution often only took place when there were human victims. With the new rules, seriously polluting the living environment is also punishable in itself," says environmental criminologist Marieke Kluin of Leiden University. According to Kluin, the directive fits a trend in which environmental crime is being taken more seriously. "The Netherlands has had a number of major scandals. The discharge of benzene and PFAS by large companies, and cases involving major manure fraudsters; because of these, more people have woken up." Kluin points out that more is needed to tackle environmental crime effectively. Earlier research she conducted showed that environmental criminals still very often escape their sentence. This is partly due to capacity shortages at government bodies and the huge fragmentation across services that deal with environmental pollution. For those shortages, the minister has admittedly made 3 million euros extra available structurally, but that money has to be divided across various services.

title: CU and 50Plus positive, other parties want to keep talking about tax plan
lead: The ChristenUnie and 50Plus are positive about the adjustments to the tax plan that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has come up with. There are also factions that say they cannot vote for it in this form. Those may be needed for a majority in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. CDA-<entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">fractieleider Bontenbal</entity> wants to sit down with them again. "As far as the tax plan is concerned, we are certainly positive about it", responds ChristenUnie-<entity id="person:mirjam-hannah-bikker">leider Bikker</entity>. She is glad that the cabinet is freeing up 347 million euros by dropping the freedom contribution next year. She is also pleased that the deduction for specific care costs remains in place. The cabinet made those adjustments in the hope of persuading the two parties to vote for the tax plan, and they appreciate that. "It is good news that chronically ill people, ordinary people and working Netherlands will pay less", Bikker believes. 50Plus-<entity id="person:jan-albert-struijs">leider Struijs</entity> is also "reasonably satisfied" with what is now on the table, although he still has many questions about, among other things, the funding of the plans. According to him there are still some "catches". But about the chances of success in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> he says: "We are not the problem, but the Eerste Kamer is a major risk." 'Voting against is childish' ChristenUnie and 50Plus cannot together help the cabinet reach a majority, but if the Groep Markuszower votes for the tax plan, there is a majority. <entity id="person:gideon-markuszower">Fractievoorzitter Markuszower</entity> lets it be known on request that "it would by now be childish to vote against". "So much sour has been dished out, there is so much sweet in it." JA21, BBB and the SGP, which since last week form a 'bondje', still want to strike a deal with the minority cabinet. They do not want to support the tax plan now on the table, although "cautiously some steps" are being taken in their direction. They still want to negotiate their conditions on asylum, nitrogen, abortion and surrogacy. So far the coalition does not want to make agreements on topics unrelated to the tax plan. But JA21-<entity id="person:bernard-johannes-eerdmans">leider Eerdmans</entity> still says: "I think a deal on that is certainly possible." Stoffer of the SGP also sees some glimmers of hope. "It is still a long way off from 12 November", he says. That is when the Tweede Kamer will vote on the tax plan. "I think that, also with a view to the governability of the country, we should try to get out of this." 'Very disappointing' Pro and Volt, which form a left-wing 'bondje', do not want to support the tax plan in its current form. That is no surprise. Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> already said over the weekend that too little is moving in their direction and that he encountered "political unwillingness". That there is now a proposal for which there is not yet a certain majority, he considers "an irresponsible risk". Incidentally, the two parties have not yet given up hope. Tomorrow, in the debate in the Tweede Kamer, they want to try to achieve that less is taken from "the very richest". "I will keep doing my utmost until the very last moment", says Klaver. CDA-fractieleider Bontenbal finds it very disappointing that the cabinet has not succeeded in closing a deal with the opposition that leads to a majority in both chambers. He calls that "casino politics" and calls it "gambling" with the taxes of millions of taxpayers. Bontenbal has cleared his agenda to sit down with a number of fellow faction leaders over the coming week after all. "My assignment now is to seek majorities."

title: Employees insufficiently prepared for losing their job, more training needed
lead: For years the biggest challenge in reducing shortages on the labour market was: how do we get more people to work? But by now that is no longer the most important question, concludes the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>. "We will not solve the shortages only by getting more people into work, but also by making the people who already work more adaptable," says UWV board member Judith Duveen. Labour participation in the Netherlands is historically high, according to the annual labour market report that the benefits agency publishes today. Nearly three quarters of the people who can work do so. Still, there are shortages. For half of the open vacancies, it is difficult to find staff. At the same time, the share of higher-educated people receiving a WW unemployment benefit is rising. "That group has traditionally had little difficulty finding a new job," says Duveen. "But that is changing." Mismatch Notably, according to Duveen, more and more people from the ICT sector are unemployed, while there are large shortages in that sector. Unemployment is also rising for some technical occupations. "So there is evidently a mismatch between what people can do and what companies are looking for," says Duveen. That more and more highly educated people are receiving WW benefits is partly because there are more highly educated people in the Netherlands than before. AI, or artificial intelligence, also plays a role. "In various sectors, tasks are being taken over by computers," says Duveen. "But new tasks are also emerging. Only, people looking for a job are not always trained for them." In other sectors an enormous exodus is coming, says Duveen. "Not because of AI or unrest in the world, but because of ageing. In logistics and transport, for example, a great many older employees work. They will retire in the coming years, so employers will have to look for new staff. But they often don't find them, because the people looking for work do not have the right skills." Retraining Diploma and job requirements are, according to the UWV, a barrier for many job seekers in finding a new job. That is why, according to the benefits agency, it would be good if, when looking for new staff, more attention were paid to skills. To what people can do, apart from their education. In addition, employees, employers and the government should put more effort into retraining and further training, the UWV believes. "We have been making that call for a few years, but this time we are doing so with extra emphasis," says Duveen. "We see that the labour market is changing even faster than before. It is really necessary for workers to keep developing, even if they currently have a job. Nowadays you simply don't know what your current job will look like in five years." For the employers' association AWVN, this does not sound new. "Lifelong learning, learning and development, development budgets: it has been in collective agreements for decades," says spokesperson Jannes van der Velde. "But it keeps failing to really get off the ground." Sometimes, according to AWVN, this is because employers don't know quite how to organise it. And when training is offered, employees don't always make use of it. "If you are satisfied with your job and you earn well, why would you think about what your job will look like in ten years," says Van der Velde. "Whereas that is exactly what you should be doing." Move to another sector To make that training truly effective, employers should, according to the UWV, also train their staff for other sectors. Occasionally this already happens, for example in the financial sector. "Many jobs have disappeared there in recent years," says Van der Velde. "Those people had to start doing something else. Money was then made available for retraining." That can also turn out favourably for the employer. "When it became clear that reorganisations were coming in the financial sector, many employees left voluntarily because they had found another job. Sometimes, thanks to that retraining, in a different sector."

title: Prospective buyer of Seyss-Inquart bunker rightly excluded from bidding process
lead: One of the bidders for the bunker of Seyss-Inquart, a former Nazi command bunker in Wassenaar, has rightly been excluded from the sales process. That is the ruling of the judge in The Hague. Heritage organisation Boei, which showed interest in the building, did not follow the rules and may no longer submit a bid for the bunker. Boei shared its vision for the building with third parties, against the rules, and reportedly tried to make contact with the other bidder. One of the conditions in the bid book is that interested parties may not share their plans and other information with third parties during the sales procedure. Boei reportedly wanted to talk with the other bidder, a Hague property entrepreneur, about possible cooperation and financing. The director also reportedly gave an informal presentation about his plans for the command post. The property entrepreneur reported this to the seller, the <entity id="org:rijksvastgoedbedrijf">Rijksvastgoedbedrijf</entity>. The State then had an integrity investigation carried out, on the basis of which the State excluded Boei from the bidding process. The heritage organisation filed a summary proceeding to have that decision reversed, but the judge did not rule in its favour. The Seyss-Inquart bunker The bunker, camouflaged as a farmhouse, dates from the Second World War and was built on the orders of the Reich Commissioner for the Netherlands. Arthur Seyss-Inquart was one of the leaders of the Nazi regime and responsible for the deportation of more than one hundred thousand Jews to concentration and extermination camps. He lived for a while on the Clingendael estate on the border of Wassenaar and The Hague, where he had the command bunker built. It housed, among other things, his office. The Rijksvastgoedbedrijf can now sell the bunker to the property entrepreneur so the building can be given a new purpose. The Rijksvastgoedbedrijf wants to be rid of it because defence has not used the building since 2013. Interested parties could present their vision for the redevelopment of the bunker during the preselection. In doing so, the cultural-historical value of the complex had to be respected. A selection committee would then choose from the two remaining bidders. Appeal Boei says in a response that it will file a complaint and take further legal steps. The heritage organisation says that the sale to the property entrepreneur is exactly what was not intended, namely "parties becoming owners of nationally important monuments without having the right knowledge or experience". "The general heritage interest must weigh more heavily than a quick sale or limited proceeds," says director Arno Boon of Boei. He also says there was no contact between property dealer De Wilde and Boei, and that the judge therefore went too far in his ruling. He points to a meeting of the standing House committee for <entity id="org:ministerie-van-onderwijs-cultuur-en-wetenschap">Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap</entity> on 5 and 9 November and wants <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Kamer</entity> to have the chance to express its view before the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf "takes an irreversible step".

title: Tarwekamp recovers after explosion, but legal case brings tension: 'Going in with trembling knees'
lead: The court in The Hague will begin hearing the case over the explosion in an apartment block in the Mariahoeve district of The Hague from tomorrow. Six residents lost their lives in it. The neighbourhood is slowly getting back on its feet, but with the legal case approaching there is also tension. The wine shop of Ingo Wewer on Tarwekamp has been open again for almost a year. He is doing well, he says, but that is not true for everyone on the street. "If you have lost people or your house, then that is far more serious than having some damage to your shop and being able to carry on again after ten months." His shop functions as an informal 'contact centre' for the neighbourhood. Fellow entrepreneurs and local residents regularly come there to unburden themselves. "If I have to make a rough estimate, I would say that 60 percent have picked up the thread again," says Wewer. "But 40 percent are still in deep trouble." Gaping hole The explosion on 7 December 2024 literally blew a hole in the neighbourhood. After an attack on a bridal fashion shop at the bottom of the apartment block, part of the building collapsed. A gaping hole in the block of houses still serves as a reminder of the incident. In these images from 7 December 2024 you can see how great the devastation was: Some of the residents have since returned. Their homes could be repaired, but not everyone feels at home. Wewer estimates that at least ten people are living elsewhere. Their home was wiped out or they do not want to return. Double housing costs "People have literally been blown out of their beds or have lost neighbours," says Bart Visser, spokesperson for Namens de Familie. The organisation supports various next of kin and victims of the explosion on Tarwekamp. "There are people who still hear that bang at night. They simply do not want to live here anymore." Not only emotionally, but also financially, the consequences of the explosion are great, Visser notes. Affected residents have double housing costs: the mortgage on the destroyed home (often an owner-occupied house) and the rent for temporary housing. Selling their apartment on Tarwekamp is not possible, because it is uninhabitable or because the value of the property has collapsed. "They are financially trapped in this situation, and that is very distressing." Wine merchant Wewer also hears the stories about financial stress, disputes with insurers and an uncertain future. In recent times he has tried to offer a helping hand by giving the hairdresser from around the corner a place in his shop. "Her own shop was still too damaged to work in." The hairdresser, Far Garhib, reopened the doors of her own salon last Saturday. Together with her husband she has rebuilt the business from scratch. "We have worked very hard, sometimes until 02.00 at night. For months. But now we are happily open again." Garhib describes the past two years as crushing. "Mentally and physically we are all broken. Six people have died. We knew these people. We said hello to each other and waved at each other. Now they are no longer here." Regret Tomorrow the substantive hearing of the case begins against the four people held responsible for the explosion. Alongside the alleged client Moshtag B. there is an intermediary and two suspects who are said to have set off 200 litres of petrol. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) is convinced that B. wanted revenge on his ex-girlfriend, the owner of the bridal fashion shop. The relationship had ended shortly before the explosion. Moshtag B. is also suspected of stalking, threatening and abusing his then girlfriend. He says the explosion was not his idea, but that of one of the others. "I deeply regret it," B. said during an earlier preparatory hearing, at which the case was not yet heard on its merits. "It was never the intention. It completely got out of hand." Trembling knees The legal case is causing great tension in the neighbourhood. "Some people are indeed a little afraid of reliving what happened two years ago," notes Ingo Wewer. Cees Jenezon, who ran a company dealing in, among other things, awnings on Tarwekamp, is dreading the legal case. "I am actually going there with trembling knees. It stirs up a lot of resistance in me. What those people have done is terrible." Over thirty victims and next of kin will make use of the right to speak next week. They want to tell what injustice has been done to them and how great the suffering still is. "An enormous crater has also been torn in the lives of many people," says Bart Visser of Namens de Familie. In the coming days the case file will be discussed with the four suspects. A prosecution demand is expected at the end of the month. Some residents fervently hope that the OM will ask for life imprisonment. Heavy weeks Ingo Wewer is letting the legal case pass him by. He says he has confidence that justice will take its course. He is glad that there is some liveliness in the neighbourhood again. In September there was a neighbourhood party, which Wewer called "a party with a small p." Residents together made an artwork in memory of the disaster on 7 December 2024. At the same time, the more than one hundred attendees tried, "with appropriate cheerfulness and openness," to look ahead and make something pleasant of it. "I think that is also a bit of our role now," says Wewer. "That we listen and try to bring some positivity to the neighbourhood." But he fully realises that the situation is very different for people who have lost their home or loved ones. "These are heavy weeks for everyone here." Life is carefully going on again on Tarwekamp, sees Bart Visser of Namens de Familie as well. "But a legal case like this brings all the bad memories back to the surface. The trauma comes right up again."

title: Bomb threats on seven flights in Europe, no explosives found
lead: Bomb threats were made on at least seven passenger flights in Europe today. Aircraft in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy were searched as a result. As far as is known, no explosives were found. One of the most striking incidents concerned a LOT Polish Airlines flight from London to Warsaw. The aircraft diverted to Warsaw-Modlin airport, where air traffic was temporarily halted while authorities investigated. Besides the flight from London, other aircraft also faced bomb threats. In Poland a second aircraft, an SAS flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw, was checked after landing. Warsaw-Chopin airport remained open. No explosives have been found on the aircraft examined, as far as is known. In Spain, Italy and Bulgaria authorities explicitly reported this. In Poland the warnings were withdrawn, but not all details about the investigation into explosives have been made public. The places where the bomb threats were : Spain A Ryanair flight from Manchester to Murcia made a precautionary landing. According to the government representative in the Murcia region, no explosives were found after inspection and regular air traffic has resumed. The landing led to a large security operation at the airport. The 114 passengers and seven crew members had to leave the aircraft, while police, emergency services and explosives experts examined the plane. Images published by Spanish media show that sniffer dogs were also deployed during the inspection. Bulgaria In Bulgaria, according to transport minister Georgi Peev, two flights to Sofia were affected by bomb threats: a Wizz Air flight from Bergamo in Italy and a Ryanair flight from Dublin. No explosives were found during checks. News agency BTA earlier reported that an aircraft coming from Israel had received a bomb threat, but according to the authorities this later turned out not to be correct. The Bulgarian authorities say the bomb threats were part of a broader series. Bomb threats had also been sent against various institutions, a senior official of the Bulgarian Ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> told news agency BTA . Which institutions these were was not stated. Italy Also in Italy, two Ryanair flights to Rome Fiumicino airport were checked after anonymous threats. They were flights from Dublin and Lisbon. According to the BBC, no suspicious objects were found during inspections. The flight from Dublin was escorted by the Italian air force during landing. The warnings were withdrawn after the investigation concluded. Wizz Air yesterday The reports follow a similar incident yesterday. A Wizz Air flight from London Luton to Budapest then made an emergency landing due to a reported bomb threat. The aircraft was escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet on arrival. The flight was also bound for Sofia. After checks of the aircraft and passengers, the airline reported that nothing suspicious had been found. The authorities have not disclosed whether there is any connection between yesterday's report and today's threats. 'Possibly deliberate action' An aviation security expert, speaking to the BBC, calls the series of reports unusual. Bomb reports about aircraft on passenger flights are, according to him, not common. That several airlines faced similar reports on the same day points, according to the expert, to deliberate action. "It seems they were made in a credible way," he says. "That makes me suspect it was a very deliberate action by a single perpetrator, rather than a series of coincidental, malicious phone calls." According to the expert, crews and authorities follow extensive procedures to assess the credibility of a report. If a threat is considered serious enough, an aircraft can be diverted to another airport, as happened in Warsaw.

title: Public Prosecution Service demands 100 hours of community service for officer who used a baton at a wedding party
lead: If it were up to the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM), the officer who used his baton against party guests in August 2024 should receive a community service sentence of 100 hours. According to the OM, that violence was not necessary. The officer came with a colleague and two boa's to the grounds of the Perenhoeve in Ruinerwold on 23 August 2024. There, the owners, Nico and Ginette Westenbrink, were holding a party at that time to celebrate their 40th wedding anniversary. The four came to check whether the party was being held according to the rules. According to the OM, that conversation began "somewhat friendly" but turned when one of the residents made a remark about the many enforcers on the grounds. Subsequently, violence was used by the officers. Counting out loud The officer who appeared in court today is a 55-year-old man. That evening in August he allegedly struck the owners' daughter five times with his baton. He counted out loud for the first four blows, the OM reports. The woman was hit on her head and broke her forearm. Three family members were also struck by the officer. Later, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> offered apologies for this and said the situation should have been resolved differently. According to the public prosecutor, the officer even struck people who were trying to protect themselves or were doing nothing. The officer does not agree: he believes he acted correctly. According to his lawyer, no violence instruction was violated, "but we do regret that it ended this way". Nico Westenbrink accepts the demand, he tells RTV Drenthe. "If that is the sentence, then so be it. We are all losers in this case." He finds it a pity that the officer is not remorseful, he adds. Rules Officers in the Netherlands may use force if they see no other solution. There are, however, rules attached to the use of force. When officers do so, they must report it to an assistant public prosecutor. Afterwards, the situation is investigated and assessed. The judge will rule in one month.

title: Suspects of people smuggling by rubber boat off Cadzand remain in custody longer
lead: The two Sudanese men arrested last Saturday on suspicion of people smuggling will remain in custody for two more weeks. The investigating judge has decided so. They will also remain under full restrictions and may only have contact with their lawyer. The men are suspected of transporting 36 Afghan migrants on the North Sea, including six minors. The rubber boat had no motor and had become adrift. The boat was towed to a marina in Cadzand. The adults have not applied for asylum and are being housed. The minors have been transferred to the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity> reception centre in Ter Apel. Incident It appears that the Netherlands was not the intended final destination of the migrants. From France, rubber boats with migrants on board regularly sail towards the United Kingdom, sometimes also from Belgium. It is possible that such a boat drifted off course on the North Sea and ended up off the Zeeland coast. The Marechaussee says it will not additionally check the coastline and considers this rescue an incident.

title: Night work often unnecessary and workers insufficiently protected, warns Labour Inspectorate
lead: Employers pay too little attention to the health risks of night work. Moreover, night work is often unnecessary. That is what research by the Labour Inspectorate shows. Although the <entity id="org:gezondheidsraad">Gezondheidsraad</entity> already advised in 2017 to limit night work, the number of night workers is not decreasing. The inspectorate examined employers in, among others, the (food) industry, transport, care, hospitality and distribution. These are sectors where a lot of work is done at night. Nearly two thirds of the 92 inspected employers were fined or given warnings by the Labour Inspectorate, because these employers did not comply with the rules for healthy and safe work and working hours. The Labour Inspectorate further concludes that concrete measures to prevent the risks are lacking at nearly 70 percent of the inspected employers. Workers also do not always receive sufficient information. In the Netherlands, about 15 percent of all workers sometimes or regularly work at night. Night work applies when more than one hour is worked between 00.00 and 06.00 hours. Health risks "We do not sufficiently realise what it does to a person to work at night", says Jane Tijssen, programme manager at the Labour Inspectorate. Various studies show that night work disrupts the biorhythm and leads to health damage. "For example, workers face an increased risk of, among other things, cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep problems." The inspectorate's research shows that more than half of the night workers spoken to sometimes or regularly feel tired and/or less alert during night work. In 12 percent of cases this has led to a safety risk on the work floor. Economic reasons Tijssen also sees that employers do not think enough about organising work differently. "We do not ask ourselves enough whether night work is always necessary." For example, fewer than half of the employers questioned by the Labour Inspectorate state that night work is necessary, for instance because the work must be done immediately or because installations cannot be shut down. Even so, nearly nine in ten employers see no possibilities to further reduce night work, because it is part of their business structure. For 46 percent of employers, mainly economic reasons play a role. "Of course you want the ambulance to come in the middle of the night, but in other sectors employers really need to think carefully about whether the work is necessary at night and if so, what measures they must take to keep it safe", said Tijssen of the Labour Inspectorate. Still, the Labour Inspectorate believes that reducing night work is not solely the responsibility of individual employers. Clients, employers' and employees' organisations and the government must also play a role in this.

title: British singer Steve Ellis (76) of eternal hit 'Everlasting Love' has died
lead: In two takes, at the end of the 1960s, he managed to sing a classic that still gets hundreds of thousands of streams per month: Steve Ellis, singer of the British band Love Affair. Last Friday the musician died at the age of 76, as relatives of his have announced. He had been suffering from lung problems for some time. At 17 years old, Ellis sang the world-famous version of Everlasting Love in 1967, a song that singer Robert Knight had had success with in the US shortly before. The first recording with the members of Love Affair did not go down well with the record company. On the second version, only Ellis can be heard, with hired musicians. "Two takes and done", Ellis said at the beginning of this year about the recordings. Whether or not it was a deliberate publicity stunt, the song got the wind in its sails. The teenage boys stood for a photo session at Piccadilly Circus in London in November 1967, shivering in the cold. Ellis, out of mischief, climbed into a fountain, could not get back down, and needed help from the fire brigade. Fine: 12 British pounds. Result: the band made the front pages of British newspapers. When the press later got wind that not the whole band could be heard on the hit single, the band members themselves shrugged their shoulders a little. Because the newspapers were full of it, the commotion did nothing to diminish the band's popularity in and outside the UK. Hits such as Rainbow Valley and A Day Without Love followed shortly after. Those singles made Love Affair famous in a short time. In 1968 the band was the best-selling group in the United Kingdom after The Beatles. With Everlasting Love they even managed to knock Hello, Goodbye by The Beatles off the British number 1 spot. In the Netherlands the single reached position 12 in the Top 40. A hit every decade Over the years the song about eternal love has also proven to be an eternal hit, with a whole host of artists covering it. The most success was had by Carl Carlton, the duo Rex Smith and Rachel Sweet, and Gloria Estefan, and in Europe the German singer Sandra scored a hit with it at the end of the 1980s. Jamie Cullum and U2 also recorded popular versions. Because of all those versions released, the song has a special distinction: Everlasting Love is the only song in the UK that has had a chart hit in the 1960s, 70s, 80s, 90s and 00s. Reconciled After the short-lived success of Love Affair, Ellis never managed to reach the wider public again. He left the band at the end of 1969, done with that one big hit, and turned his back on the music industry for a while. In those years he worked, among other things, in a harbour and a supermarket. But the music kept calling, and with various bands he eventually toured the UK for decades, until his health no longer allowed it. Because of lung problems he stopped performing last year. Reluctantly. "It's a bit like being a carpenter and losing your arm", he said at the beginning of this year in conversation with music site The Strange Brew. Ellis gradually came to terms with the inevitable Everlasting Love, he said in that same conversation. "I can't find fault with that record. It was a great song, a great arrangement, a great producer. Everything. I was lucky to be allowed to sing it."

title: Revenue model of news media under pressure from AI results of search engines and chatbots
lead: AI summaries by Google are in some cases in breach of the copyright of newspapers and news sites. That is what Advocate General Maciej Szpunar says in an opinion to the Court of Justice of the EU in a case brought by a Hungarian media company against Alphabet, the parent company of Google. AI chatbot Gemini is used by Google to create AI summaries, which Google presents when a user has entered a search term. The "AI Overview", as Google calls it, has Gemini compile it from various sources on the internet. This scraping causes dissatisfaction among news media, because they see the number of visitors who come to them via Google shrinking. This is because users who look up news information rarely click on the source Google shows with the summary, a Reuters study showed this year. Scraping information As a result, news organisations see less traffic on their websites, which leads to fewer subscribers and less advertising revenue. And as a result, the newspaper or media company has less money to spend on journalism. Hester van Santen, ombudsman at NRC, voiced her concerns about this development this weekend. In her column in the newspaper, she described how the work of the newspaper's editors is used by the Google chatbot to generate brief summaries in response to search queries. And the NRC ombudsman is not the only one who is upset about this. Unrest has long been growing within journalism about AI chatbots that scrape information. For example, the Amsterdam Court of Appeal ruled last week that the commercial use of short fragments of news articles is an infringement of publishers' rights. The court made that ruling in a case brought by DPG Media (which owns, among others, the Volkskrant and AD) and Mediahuis (De Telegraaf and NRC) against the now defunct HowardsHome. According to the court, that company infringed copyright by unlawfully collecting articles and photos and then profiting from them. Stealing information Nienke Venema, director of the Stichting Democratie en Media, said last year on radio programme De Rode Draad that newspapers and news sites invest a lot of money in producing news reports and stories, but that at Google this news is turned into an AI overview in no time. She called that "the theft of information by AI chatbots". Under copyright law, it is permitted to use the facts that a newspaper writes about, for example, but AI must then use different words, Advocate General Maciej Szpunar now states. He also says that when the language model takes a publication from a website, reformulates it and then presents it to the user, copyright is in some cases infringed. In addition, it is not permitted to bypass a paywall to obtain the information or text that the chatbot uses for the AI answer, the opinion states. That last point seems to happen from time to time, says NRC editor-in-chief Patricia Veldhuis to the NOS. The newspaper has at times experienced days when the NRC website suddenly became very slow. "That turned out to be a swarm of bots that was stripping our website bare", she says. Veldhuis calls it "unpunished pilfering by tech giants". "It's as if you were a baker on a high street whose bread is stolen from the display window, and that bread is then sold further down on the market square", she explains. "They steal the product we make, and give nothing back for it." She hopes that politicians will take action and that there will be a sense of urgency that policy needs to be developed around the AI summaries of chatbots. "Because the current model is hollowing out journalism", Veldhuis says.

title: Binance: hackers got in via fake job application
lead: The hackers who broke into cryptoplatform Binance last week did so through a forged application procedure. The company posted an update on X about last week's hack at the cryptoplatform. In a short time, more than 6 billion dollars was taken from the platform. Binance itself speaks of a sophisticated operation consisting of several phases. One of the developers working at Binance was approached by someone who wanted to recruit him for a new job. The software developer had a live video call with that recruiter. According to Binance, the scammer shared information from his social media to build trust. In a second conversation, the employee had to download an assignment. It contained modified code, which according to Binance "set in motion a series of unauthorized activities". Access points closed: Among other things, a real development tool in Binance's system was replaced with a malicious version. That ended up on the software developer's laptop. Through it, the hackers made a connection remotely. Various cryptocurrencies were then moved from their digital wallet to accounts of the hackers. The world's largest crypto platform has previously said it will compensate all damage. The company also says that all systems involved have been adjusted: "The access points that have been determined to have been used in the attack have been closed." The US security service FBI says North Korea is behind the hack. The country itself denies that accusation.

title: Poland sends extra police to Russian border after 'provocation'
lead: Poland is increasing the police presence in the border area with Russia, says Polish Prime Minister Tusk. It concerns the area near the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, after a possible Russian "provocation" was thwarted overnight. Tusk reportedly was informed shortly after midnight that people with flashlights had been seen in the border area. "We have managed to prevent attempts at provocation, if provocation was the intention", said Tusk. He did not say what the people intended or whether they had been on Polish soil. According to the Polish prime minister, it will not stop at extra police, as anti-terror units are also being deployed. This was chosen because 'concrete' intelligence reportedly indicates that sabotage actions are to be expected early this month, including a possible incursion into Poland by "armed persons". "We have for some time been receiving information from our own services and those of our allies that sabotage actions or more serious provocations may take place at the border with Russia, possibly even directed by hostile intelligence services", said Tusk. Polish Prime Minister Tusk has long warned of "a real risk" that Russia will fire drones or other projectiles at the eastern flank of NATO territory in Europe. Such "hybrid" attacks would be carried out against countries that support Ukraine, he said last month in the Polish parliament.
