NOS correspondent Christiaan Paauwe earlier this year spoke in Peciszewo, Poland, at the border with Russia, about the Polish defence line:

title: Public Prosecution Service (OM) demands 12 years in prison for suspect in 'freezer murder' of father
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) demands a prison sentence of twelve years for a 33-year-old man from Heerhugowaard. According to the OM, it has been proven that in January 2021 he killed his father and kept the remains at home for years in chest freezers. 'Irreversible' According to the OM, this constitutes manslaughter and not murder, because it cannot be proven that V. acted with premeditation. "The suspect has committed one of the most serious criminal offences," said the public prosecutor. "He killed his own father. A violent act, irreversible, with lasting grief for many people." Justice holds the suspect heavily accountable for having disposed of the remains. "The suspect treated the body in a gruesome, utterly disrespectful and degrading manner and seriously damaged it. Nobody deserves such an end." Fled abroad The 66-year-old victim was reported missing by a friend in October 2021, after he had not been seen for months. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> thought the man had committed suicide or fled abroad due to financial problems. The latter was also suggested by the suspect, his son Thomas V. From spring 2023 the police nevertheless started a criminal investigation. Various scenarios were examined: natural death, accident, suicide or a crime. More than 200 pieces Despite some tips, it remained quiet for a long time. Until November 2024, when the police searched V.'s home. The body of his missing father was found there in chest freezers. The body had been cut into more than 200 pieces. The victim was presumably murdered in that house in January 2021. He lived there with his son. There had been conflict between the two over that housing for some time, according to the OM. Self-defence Investigation shows that they got into a fight and the victim was struck on the head several times with a hard object. Experts also reported strangulation and/or smothering. The son has always said he acted in self-defence, reports regional broadcaster NH. The father, with whom he had a poor relationship, allegedly tried to poison him with rat poison. When he confronted his father about it, his father attacked him with a knife, the lawyer said. During a struggle that followed, the son struck his father several times, until he noticed he was no longer breathing, according to the defence. In panic and horror, the son reportedly sawed his father's body into pieces. Afterwards he suppressed the event. According to the lawyer, V. had a difficult youth due to his father's violent behaviour and addictions. Woman suspected A 31-year-old woman from Purmerend is a co-suspect in the case. She is suspected of disposing of the victim's body. The nature of the relationship between her and V. is not known. They may be former lovers. The case against her will be heard at a later date.

title: King Charles calls slavery a 'shameful chapter', but offers no apology
lead: The British role in slavery is a "shameful chapter from history, which fills me with horror and causes me deep sorrow". With these words King Charles said today more than ever, but they are not quite an apology for the British role in the slave trade. However, behind the scenes work is reportedly underway on an official apology from the British government. Prime Minister Burnham is reportedly discussing the wording with former British colonies. That is a shift from where the British have stood until now. In recent years there has been talk of sorrow (deep grief) over this dark history, but not of 'sorry'. Because the fear is that with 'sorry' you acknowledge responsibility and open the door to talks about reparations. Brutal conditions Reparations, that is something we are not going to do, the prime minister emphasised this weekend. Because why should the current inhabitants of the UK, the tax-paying citizens, now pay the bill for something that happened hundreds of years ago, the prime minister asks. Slavery, however terrible, took place in another era and the current British citizens had no role in it at all, according to Burnham. However, his government is reportedly working on a package of investments in former colonies. All of this is taking place during a royal state visit to the Caribbean, where King Charles addresses the Commonwealth today. Charles is, besides king of the United Kingdom, head of state of fourteen other countries, including host country Antigua and Barbuda. He is also the symbolic head of the Commonwealth, which consists of 56 countries. It is a charged gathering today, because it takes place in the Caribbean, which played a crucial role in the trans-Atlantic slave trade. Between 1624 and 1807 an estimated 2 million enslaved Africans were brought to the British colonies in the Caribbean. Countries lining up for reparations When it comes to historical injustice, many more countries will undoubtedly point to the crimes that English history is full of. If you look, for example, at the number of countries Great Britain has invaded over the centuries, and include brief military incursions, you arrive at impressive numbers. Historian Stuart Laycock arrives at 171 countries, almost 90 percent of all countries in the world. The scale of the British colonial past, with a history of slavery, plunder, oppression and exploitation, makes the discussion about apologies and reparations very complex. According to most experts, that enormous scale makes the British government and the British royal family more reticent than, for example, the Dutch <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity>. Various researchers are studying archives that expose the ties between former British monarchs and the slave trade. Findings regularly surface showing that the role of the monarchy was not passive. For example, in 1564 Elizabeth I deployed Royal Navy ships for a voyage by trader John Hawkins. Shortly before, he had become the first Englishman to sell 300 enslaved people and had discovered how lucrative that trade was. Old registers also show that King Charles II and his successor James II were tied to the RAC (Royal African Company), a trading company that shipped hundreds of thousands of enslaved people. Ideas vary widely. Another point that makes the question of financial compensation complex is that when slavery was abolished, Great Britain compensated not the enslaved but the slaveholders. The British taxpayer ultimately paid 20 million pounds for this; the final instalments were only paid in 2015. Ideas on reparations vary widely. For some, apologies are enough, while others think that billions should be paid to the regions where slavery lasted for centuries. Another proposal is to set up a fund into which money is put for development aid, education and other social goals in former colonies. The words King Charles spoke today were also an attempt to take the conversation a step further. "We cannot choose our history, nor can we change it", the king said. He spoke of how much potential the 56 Commonwealth countries have to work together on climate, education and poverty reduction. "We cannot change the past together", the king concluded, "but we can change the future".

title: Traffic controller in hospital, man arrested for aggravated assault
lead: In Haarlem a traffic controller was assaulted by a motorist, reports regional broadcaster NH. It happened during roadworks in the Haarlemse Waarderpolder. A 29-year-old man from IJmuiden has been arrested on suspicion of aggravated assault. The traffic controller was first treated on the spot by ambulance staff and then taken to hospital with unknown injuries. What the precise cause was has not been disclosed. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> it concerns a traffic conflict, NH reports.

title: Stream, blog, map: here's how to follow the results from America at NOS
lead: Results of the congressional elections in the United States can be followed live at NOS tonight. At 01:00 the polling stations closed in the first states. During the night, more and more states will be added and a first picture of the results will emerge. We are tracking all developments in a liveblog on NOS.nl and in the NOS app. From 03:00 we are there with a livestream for no less than 6.5 hours. There is also plenty of attention on TV and radio for the midterms . An overview: Curious what is at stake in the congressional elections? Our correspondent explains it in the video:

title: Indonesia arrests three senior police officers on suspicion of wiretapping president
lead: In Indonesia three senior police officials have been arrested on suspicion of illegally wiretapping President Prabowo and many other prominent Indonesians. The possible motive of the three has not yet been disclosed. According to the government, there are so far no indications of treason. The police investigation focuses on illegally intercepting communications. That reportedly happened by tapping phones in violation of the rules, "including those of the president, government officials, politicians, media figures, community leaders, activists of NGOs and businesspeople", according to the head of the national criminal investigation service. Illegally on the wiretap list That unauthorized wiretapping reportedly took place this year and last year, after Prabowo took office. The three suspects reportedly gave orders for wiretapping without following the applicable procedures. For example, all kinds of phone numbers suddenly appeared on a list of numbers the police are allowed to tap. Recently the three suspects ordered that communications they had collected via that list be deleted, the national criminal investigation service reported today. The police suspect they did this to conceal evidence and erase traces of the wiretapping operation. Meanwhile eleven phones, a tablet and four USB sticks have been seized. The authorities do not yet want to say anything about the purpose or motive of the wiretapping operation. Justice Minister Mahendra did indicate that investigators have no indications that the three wanted to or did endanger Indonesia's security. That could be the case if they passed on obtained state secrets to other parties. Multiple charges The three senior police officials are now held in the detention centre at the headquarters of the <entity id="org:politie">nationale politie</entity>. There the authorities also gave their press conference on the case. The suspects are the president's chief of staff, the head of the legal department, and an instructor at the training institute of the national police. Minister Mahendra said the three are being charged on multiple grounds. The highest maximum sentence is for unlawfully intercepting non-public electronic communications. That carries up to 10 years in prison. Two other offences, including deleting data, carry a maximum of 6 years in prison.

title: Dutch industry to receive compensation for expensive electricity
lead: Industry will receive 150 million euros extra next year from <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to compensate for high electricity prices. That is stated in a letter to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. Money that was already agreed in the coalition agreement will also become available earlier. From 2028 that is 345 million euros and from 2029 it is 495 million per year. Companies that want to receive this compensation must, however, spend half of it on sustainability, such as saving more energy in the company or generating sustainable electricity. Competitors Also a comparison by the cabinet shows again that Dutch companies pay much more for electricity and network costs than competitors in Belgium, Germany, France and the United Kingdom. The cabinet would therefore prefer to compensate industry directly, but that is not allowed under the European state aid rules. That is why it must now go through a kind of sustainability fund. The trade association for energy companies in our country, Energie-Nederland, says in a response that it views the cabinet's support positively. "But for companies that want to invest, this is not sufficient. They need long-term and predictable policy, so that they can invest with confidence." According to the association, more money is needed to help industry. The amount should moreover also be structurally available in a fund, they argue.

title: Farmers' organisations critical of nitrogen law: 'Not good enough yet'
lead: Farmers' organisations are critical of the detailed nitrogen plans presented by <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. They find that the nitrogen law presented today is an improvement on a number of points, but that it is still far from good enough. Environmental organisations are pleased that work can now begin on nature restoration. The law, which was already presented in outline before the summer, is intended to ensure that emissions are drastically reduced by 2035 compared with 2019. For example, in zones around vulnerable nature, farmers may in the long term keep no more than 1.5 cows per hectare of land. LTO chair Ger Koopmans finds the nitrogen package "less bad on important points than the earlier outline letter", but says that "a number of fundamental objections have not yet been, or have not been sufficiently, removed". He finds that the uncertainty in which farmers have lived in recent months has not been removed and that the cabinet must change this quickly. "Without certainty there is also no prospect." "Steps have been taken on zoning, land-based farming, financial support and permit granting", says Koopmans. He predicts "still very tough and intensive talks with the cabinet". The largest agricultural organisation finds it unacceptable that the cabinet still cannot make clear how much in total must be reduced and how much reduction has already been achieved since 2019. As a result, "farmers still do not know how much nitrogen emission they must reduce where". Implementation is important The Dutch Agricultural Young People's Contact (NAJK) is also critical of the nitrogen package. The young farmers find that there are "fundamental improvements", but that "the implementation must show whether the measures are feasible, affordable and practicable in practice". "It remains an enormously far-reaching package that places a huge task on young farmers and growers," says NAJK chair Gerben Boom. "The cabinet must now show that its commitments are actually being fulfilled." He wants young farmers and growers to be offered prospects. Housing and roads The law is also of great importance for housebuilding. Chair Arno Visser of Bouwend Nederland considers it good news that projects can go ahead again. The cabinet wants to bring forward the increase in the computational lower limit, making it easier to grant permits. "If this package is implemented, there will again be room to build homes and roads," says Visser. He does point out the right order, however. "Permits can only be granted once emissions fall and nature recovers. In some areas this can happen faster than in others. There are a few regions where the nitrogen problem is greater. We have been at a standstill for six years and we will be working on this for a few more years." Absolute minimum Environmental organisations call the nitrogen package the absolute minimum needed to get the Netherlands out of the nitrogen crisis. Natuur & Milieu is pleased that there is now more clarity, which reduces pressure on nature, allows work on nature restoration to begin, and also gives farmers prospects. "Unless nature recovers, no permits can be granted either," says director Marjolein Demmers. "If we do not do this, the Netherlands will remain stuck. That is not good for nature, but also not for the economy or for people." Important step Natuurmonumenten also speaks of an important step in solving the nitrogen problem. " Zoning around nature areas is the basis for restoring nature. It is the backbone of the package. Close to nature, nitrogen, pollution and drying out must be tackled most directly," says director Leonard Geluk in an initial reaction. Greenpeace calls it an important improvement that a rapid approach to peak polluters is being examined. But not all concerns have been removed, says agricultural campaigner Hilde-Anna de Vries. "We are concerned about the latest adjustments made under pressure from the agricultural lobby, which cause further delay, while the concerns of green farmers have not been removed. It remains unacceptable that this cabinet is ignoring the Greenpeace ruling, tearing the KDW out of the law and speeding up the increase of the computational lower limit."

title: Duitse supermarkten ook getroffen door hack
lead: Ook supermarkten in Duitsland zijn slachtoffer geworden van een aanval op hun koel- en vriesinstallaties. Supermarktketens Edeka, CAP en REWE melden dat hun koelsystemen door hackers waren overgenomen. Gisteren werden supermarkten in onder andere Zweden, België en Italië getroffen. Ook in Nederland werden bedrijven getroffen: de temperatuur van de vries- en koelsystemen van ten minste zeventien bedrijven werd verhoogd. In Frankrijk was drie weken geleden een soortgelijke cyberaanval op supermarkten. De temperatuur van de installaties liep op door een hack op de kastjes die ervoor zorgen dat een vriezer of koelvak met het internet verbonden is. Zo kan de installateur bijvoorbeeld op afstand zien dat er een storing is. In de meeste gevallen ging het om koelinstallaties van Danfoss en Copeland. De bedrijven adviseerden supermarkten om hun koel- en vriessystemen los te koppelen van internet en alleen via een beveiligd netwerk verbinding te maken. Spoedoverleg In Italië heeft <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> spoedoverleg gehad met de inlichtingendiensten en cyberexperts na de hack van gisteren. De directeur van het Nationaal Agentschap voor Cyberbeveiliging noemt tijdige informatie-uitwisseling essentieel om de cyberaanvallen te voorkomen en erop te reageren. Ook EU-agentschappen hebben spoedoverleg gehad om te bepalen hoe het beste op de aanvallen kan worden gereageerd. EU-landbouwcommissaris Hansen sprak over een "opzettelijke poging om onze voedselketen te onderbreken en het consumentenvertrouwen daarin te ondermijnen". Het is nog altijd onduidelijk wie er achter de aanvallen zit. Omdat er geen financiële eisen zijn gesteld, vermoeden experts sabotage.

title: Spaanse minister van Transport stapt alsnog op na treinramp
lead: De Spaanse minister van Transport Puente treedt af na de dodelijke treinramp van vorige week in Urda . Daar kwamen 69 mensen om het leven toen een hogesnelheidstrein op een stilstaande regionale trein inreed. Het was de tweede dodelijke treinbotsing dit jaar met tientallen doden, waardoor Puentes positie als minister van Transport onder druk kwam te staan. "Een minister van Transport in een land als Spanje kan niet aanblijven na twee ongelukken in minder dan een jaar tijd", verklaarde de minister. Hij zei dat hij dat besluit al had genomen direct na het ongeluk in Urda, maar dat hij in functie was gebleven om de gevolgen aan te pakken en maatregelen te treffen om dergelijke ongelukken in de toekomst te voorkomen. Vorige week zei hij op een persconferentie nog dat hij geen gehoor gaf aan de oproep van oppositiepartijen en een vakbond om op te stappen. Veiligheidsmaatregelen Voordat hij zijn aftreden bekendmaakte kondigde Puente een nieuw pakket veiligheidsmaatregelen aan, waaronder nieuwe technieken in de twintig verkeersleidingcentra, aanpassing van de veiligheidsprotocollen en betere arbeidsomstandigheden voor het personeel in de verkeersleidingscentra. Ook zei hij dat "het spoorwegsysteem in Spanje herzien moet worden". Zo ging het vorige week mis bij de treinramp:

title: Death toll after attack in Zaporizhzhia region rises, UN condemns attack on civilians
lead: The death toll from yesterday's Russian attack on a former school building in Ukraine has risen to more than 30, and at least 50 people are missing. Rescue workers are still searching for survivors. At least nine bombs were dropped on the building in Komysjoevacha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, where humanitarian aid was being distributed. The building also served as a shelter. The village lies close to the front. The local authorities had announced that relief goods would be handed out in the building. That is why a long queue of people was waiting. Attack condemned. The UN mission monitoring compliance with human rights in Ukraine, HRMMU, says the attack appears to violate the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law. "Either the Russian army knew that relief goods were being distributed, or it did not inform itself beforehand about what was going on in the village it wanted to attack," the UN mission says. The attack shows the devastating impact of glide bombs on densely populated areas, the UN mission says. Glide bombs or gliding bombs can, through their wings, make a long glide flight and, with the help of navigation, hit a very precise target. They can carry hundreds of kilos of explosives.

title: Drenthe residents want stricter approach to wolf: 'Children no longer dare to cycle'
lead: Residents of <entity id="org:provincie-drenthe">Drenthe</entity> are very worried about the wolf in the province. Mayors of ten municipalities sent an open letter about this to State Secretary <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Silvio Erkens</entity> (Agriculture). Today he came to Drenthe for a discussion. The discussion focused mainly on the damage wolves cause in the countryside. Not only because they take horses, cows and sheep, but also because people then become afraid. Some attendees were moved to tears, RTV Drenthe reported. "Children no longer dare to cycle towards <entity id="org:gemeente-hoogeveen">Hoogeveen</entity>," said one of them. Mayors <entity id="person:jan-zwiers">Jan Zwiers</entity> (<entity id="org:gemeente-midden-drenthe">Midden-Drenthe</entity>) and <entity id="person:jouke-spoelstra">Jouke Spoelstra</entity> (<entity id="org:gemeente-westerveld">Westerveld</entity>) joined the round-table discussion, as co-signatories of the open letter. Wolves must become wary, State Secretary Erkens concluded. He wants to ensure that wolves that are not (and cause too much nuisance) can be shot more quickly. For example by introducing a maximum number of wolves, and shooting the most problematic packs. This is also done in Germany. "It is necessary to ensure that attacks on livestock and incidents involving people do not increase," said Erkens. It also became clear that the state secretary considers "active management" of the wolf necessary. When and how quickly this can be arranged remains unclear. In the open letter, ten of the twelve Drenthe mayors further call for a protected habitat for the wolf. The animal would then live only in designated nature areas, as is also the case for wild boar, for example. Growing population Currently four wolf packs live in Drenthe. So far this year at least 13 pups have been born in the province. "We increasingly hear stories about wolf damage, concerns about safety and changes in daily life," said the ten mayors. In a few places in the province more wolves are found than elsewhere. Beilen is such a hotspot. According to Mayor Zwiers the animals are increasingly seen there within built-up areas. "Especially parents and grandparents are asking how safe it is when children play outside or cycle to school alone in the dark." Only the mayors of <entity id="org:gemeente-tynaarlo">Tynaarlo</entity> and Hoogeveen did not sign the letter. So far this year 49 reports of damage by a wolf have been made in Drenthe. For 13 of these it has been confirmed that the animal is indeed responsible for the damage. The other reports are still being investigated. "This affects animal keepers and farmers who lose their animals, but also residents who are worried about their living environment or who avoid certain nature areas and walking routes," said the mayors. Financial compensation for wolf damage is important, they say, but it does not take away the fear, the grief and the uncertainty about the next night. The mayors are not asking the state secretary to implement measures immediately, but to seriously and thoroughly investigate the possibility of "active management of the wolf". "The debate about the wolf is ultimately about how we want to organise nature, agriculture, housing and recreation side by side in a densely populated country," they write. "Doing nothing is not an option for us."

title: Thousands of Czechs take to the streets again against reform of public broadcaster
lead: In the Czech Republic, thousands of people have once again taken to the streets in solidarity with the public broadcaster. Radio and television staff went on strike today in protest against the government's reform plans for the public broadcaster and marched through the centre of Prague dressed in black. They warn that these plans undermine the broadcaster's independence. The government of populist Prime Minister Babis, which relies on the support of two right-wing parties, accuses public and private media of partisanship and now wants to scrap the broadcasting fee. The money would then have to come from the general budget, so that the government gets more control over it. The coalition also plans to allocate 15 percent less for this than the budget the broadcaster currently has to spend. Babis points out that the public will pay less as a result. The government saw the bill passed in a first vote last month after limiting the debate time to a minimum. With further discussion in parliament on the way, opponents are fuelling the protest. Last Monday there was a demonstration, today the strike followed, and next Sunday another protest is planned. Orbán and Vucic Opposition groups draw a link with the reforms that Prime Minister Orbán in Hungary, who was voted out this spring, carried out, and with those of his former colleague Vucic in Serbia, who has also since lost his majority. They succeeded in building a network of government-friendly media. Dissenting voices have thereby receded into the background. "If this proposal is adopted, the governing coalition will gain instruments to influence the content of public media for political purposes", said Jan Molácek, a reporter at Czech television and a member of the strike committee, to news agency Reuters. Research shows that the public broadcaster is among the most watched and most trusted news sources in the country. Restricting the free press in the Czech Republic evokes memories of the communist past and the violent end of the Prague Spring in 1968, with Soviet Union attacks on Radio Prague. These are chapters of history that many Czechs thought the country had left completely behind. This resistance to anti-democratic developments partly explains the high turnout at the many demonstrations. Since the return of populist Babis as prime minister, just over a year ago, squares and parks in the Czech Republic regularly fill with citizens who express concern about what they see as the government's anti-democratic course. The largest demonstration took place in March, with an estimated 200,000 people. Thousands to tens of thousands of people have attended other demonstrations by the action group 'One Million Votes for Democracy' in recent months.

title: NOS podcast De Dag named best daily podcast
lead: The NOS podcast De Dag has been named best daily podcast at the Dutch Podcast Awards. According to the jury, the series makes complex topics easy for listeners to follow. "As a result, after the episodes on various topics, listeners can join the conversation at a layered level", is the verdict. In De Dag, each daily episode of about twenty minutes goes deeper into a topic from the news. The regular presenters are Elisabeth Steinz and Marco Geijtenbeek. De Dag started on 1 February 2018, and more than 2300 episodes have since been made. The jury speaks of a "richly filled podcast", in which "there is a balance between information and calm, so that De Dag never overwhelms. That reflects strong editorial work". Also want to listen? You can listen to all episodes of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. The Dutch Podcast Awards, an initiative of BNR Nieuwsradio, present prizes every year in various categories. A jury of 37 people decided this year who would take home the prizes. The main prize, for 'best podcast of the Netherlands', went to De Rolverdeling by broadcaster NTR. Journalist Sara de Monchy spent a year following children from a group 8 class at a primary school in Rotterdam for that. Last year the NOS podcast Mino's Imperium , about football agent Mino Raiola, won. Roxanne and André Hazes took home the audience prize. In their podcast ADHAZES, the brother and sister discuss a range of topics, from their youth to everyday worries. An overview of all winners:

title: Government was unreliable for farmers, says National Ombudsman
lead: The government was unreliable for farmers over the past ten years. That is the finding of the National Ombudsman, based among other things on conversations with 32 farmers. Shifting rules, contradictory policy and unclear decisions caused uncertainty. According to ombudsman <entity id="person:reinier-van-zutphen">Reinier van Zutphen</entity>, this affected not only the farmers' businesses but also their families. New agricultural policy is not enough to win back the trust of the sector, warns Van Zutphen, the day after <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> presented a new nitrogen law . "Farmers have suffered under the actions of the government and the uncertainty about the future. They can only go on if the government acknowledges what has gone wrong and what consequences that has had." Caught in a bind Farmers paid the price, according to Van Zutphen, for changing rules on nitrogen, manure, nature, water and animal welfare. "As a result, investments were postponed and plans for sustainability and innovation came under pressure." According to the ombudsman, the government took too little control, was insufficiently reliable and transparent, and listened too little to farmers. The effects of the uncertainty carry over within families, Van Zutphen heard. In farming families, work and private life often run together. "Different views on continuing, stopping or adapting can put relationships under pressure." The way governments communicate can also breed distrust. Several farmers said that important decisions are often announced on a Friday or just before a holiday. They then cannot reach officials with questions or criticism, and they think this is done deliberately in the hope that the anger will have subsided by the time they return from holiday. Experiences are central Notably, the ombudsman did not take the actual conduct of governments as the main starting point. The conversations held with farmers since 2019 are central to the investigation. The ombudsman's team spoke with 32 farmers from across the country, from different sectors, both organic and conventional. The ombudsman distilled common threads from their unverified stories. The ombudsman also spoke with farmers' interest organisations, Natuurmonumenten, scientists and other experts, including from Rabobank. Those conversations took place between November 2025 and May 2026, before agriculture minister Van Essen presented his nitrogen plans. In the report, the ombudsman writes that farmers themselves also contribute to the uncertainty they face. "On the one hand, they are confronted daily with changeable policy and laws and regulations. On the other hand, the sector actively lobbies politics. As a result, farmers sometimes contribute to the changeability themselves, while that same changeability does not make the day-to-day running of their farm any easier." Recommendations "Set goals for the long term and stick to them", advises the National Ombudsman based on what he heard in the conversations. Van Zutphen also believes that the minister of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> should take more control and ensure that the rules and plans of different governments align better with one another. Finally, Van Zutphen believes that "common sense among farmers has been ignored too often in recent years." Governments should make better use of the knowledge and experience of farmers in the decisions they make.

title: Light flares fired into stadium from outside De Kuip, two arrests
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in Rotterdam has arrested two people for setting off fireworks outside the Feyenoord stadium, the police tell news agency ANP. The flares landed on the pitch and the roof of De Kuip. The incident occurred during the second half of the Champions League match between Feyenoord and Internazionale. The match was then briefly halted. Nothing is yet known about the identity of the two people arrested. It is clear, however, that they were arrested outside the stadium. Feyenoord lost the match 0-3, by the way. According to AD, the fireworks caused a hole in the stadium roof. Nothing is yet known about the extent of the damage. Not the first time Coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst was annoyed after the match about the fireworks. "That of course should not happen and will probably result in another fine," he said. "I was glad it was not in the crowd, but this is of course something you do not want to see." The Rotterdam club still has a conditional penalty pending with the European football association UEFA following earlier disturbances. This season Feyenoord already received a fine from UEFA for several incidents with supporters at the away match against FC Barcelona. In the Netherlands, there was a sanction after fireworks at the away match against SC Cambuur in Leeuwarden.

title: University of Maastricht cancels Jewish gathering for safety reasons
lead: The University of Maastricht cancelled a gathering of a Jewish student association last night. The educational institution says safety could not be guaranteed due to online calls from both supporters and opponents. A room in a university building had been made available for a gathering of student association IJAR and the pro-Israel organisation StandWithUs. University lecturer Eli Sapir was to give a lecture there on the theme 'Three years after 7 October', referring to the terrorist attacks by Hamas in 2023. Unacceptable manner The University of Maastricht writes in a statement that several pro-Palestinian groups had announced they wanted to prevent the gathering. "Information about the lecturer involved was also shared online in an unacceptable manner." StandWithUs then called on people to come to Maastricht. "We will not be silenced" was written in the call on social media. Taken together, this led according to the university to "too great uncertainty about the safety of the gathering", after which the decision to cancel was taken. "An accumulation of risks", the university writes. "First by the announcement by others that they wanted to prevent the gathering and thereby curtail academic freedom, and then the counter-reaction and the call to come to Maastricht." Intimidation According to the organisers of the gathering, the university informed them less than an hour before the start that the lecture could not go ahead. In a statement on Instagram, IJAR and StandWithUs write that the educational institution "gives in to intimidation". According to the organisers, it is also the third time the University of Maastricht has cancelled an event of Jewish students, which amounts to "a systematic suppression of Jewish student life on campus". The University of Maastricht says it was also proposed to hold an online gathering, but the student association declined.

title: Suspected instigator of Starlink sabotage in Poland arrested
lead: German police believe they have arrested the instigator of an arson attack at the end of September at a Starlink station in Poland. The Turkish man was arrested in Reutlingen, south of Stuttgart. Last month, two other Turkish men were already arrested in the same area. They are suspected of carrying out the sabotage. The two were arrested at Poland's request and are still in custody. The Polish government previously said it assumed the Russians were behind the incident. Prime Minister Tusk spoke of an "act of hybrid warfare". Starlink is crucial for the Ukrainian army, which uses the network to control drones and for communication on the battlefield. Eight mobile phones The man who has now been arrested is suspected of preparing a terrorist offence. Eight mobile phones and ammunition were seized during his arrest. According to prosecutors, he directed the two perpetrators from Germany. He also reportedly arranged for another suspect to take the two men to Poland. The two perpetrators reportedly went to Poland on the night of 23 September to commit the arson. Last month, attempts were also made to set fire to Starlink installations in Bulgaria and Lithuania. Two Germans were arrested in Duisburg for the sabotage in Bulgaria. They are in custody pending their extradition to Bulgaria.

title: Huge win for Democrats in midterms, Republicans lose House and Senate
lead: President Trump and his policies have been punished in the midterm elections in the United States. The results are still coming in, but it is clear that the Republicans are not only losing their majority in the House of Representatives, as expected, but also in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. That means a gigantic victory for the Democrats and makes governing a lot more difficult for the president. Live blog and -stream Follow the latest developments in our live blog or via our livestream . All results can be viewed on our results map . A blue wave was mentioned beforehand as a possibility, but American media now even speak of a blue tsunami. At least six seats in the Senate are going from a Republican to a Democrat: Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, North Carolina and South Carolina. That means that from January, when the winners take their seats, there will be a Democratic majority in the Senate. Especially in the red states Texas and Kansas, the Democrats' win is a big surprise. It is the first time since 1990 that the Democrats have elected a senator in Texas. For a blue Kansas we have to go much further back: 94 years. Not yet certain In a number of states it is not yet certain who will win a Senate seat, for example in Maine, Michigan and Alaska. Counting is still ongoing there. According to CNN and NBC News, Maine too, in the far northeast of the US, is going to the Democrats. That would also be a big surprise, because Republican Susan Collins has been a senator there since 1997, and the Democrats saw their dream candidate Graham Platner drop out due to allegations of sexual abuse. After Platner's fall, Troy Jackson was hastily put forward, and according to several media this turns out to be a success. That would mean a seventh Republican state goes to the Democrats. Blue wave visible early The Democrats' victory in the House of Representatives became apparent early in the night through surprises in Florida. Several constituencies that had been redrawn by the Republicans in their favour nevertheless turned blue. In addition, in various rural districts in other states, the Democrats did much better than expected. That things went the wrong way for the Republicans specifically in rural areas is largely due to the rising cost of living and high fuel prices, as a result of Trump's war in Iran. Farmers among others have been hit hard by the sometimes nearly doubled prices of diesel, which they need for their agricultural vehicles. Trump: willing to accept results In a first reaction to the poor results for his Republican party, President Trump says he hopes to be able to work with the Democratic politicians in the House and Senate. "I think they want to work with me," he told broadcaster <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity>. "Otherwise I will just veto everything and they don't want that." Beforehand there was fear that he would not accept a bad result, as he still does not accept his own defeat in 2020. But he cautiously reached out: "We will work with the Democrats, we look forward to working with them. We can surely arrange something." Incidentally, shortly after that message he posted an image prominently featuring the word 'VETO' on social media, so it remains to be seen what he will make of his offer. The midterms often turn into a referendum on the policy of the sitting president, and his party regularly loses Congress seats. That was not different today. Not all results are in. View them all here on our interactive map:

title: Tax plan meets opposition from both left and right in the Senate
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has difficulty finding sufficient support for the tax plan in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, but in the Senate the political puzzle becomes even more complicated. The minority cabinet needs support from opposition parties on the left or right, but both Pro and BBB show little willingness to help the plan get a majority, according to Nieuwsuur. "It means quite a lot to vote down a tax plan," admits Paul Rosenmöller, parliamentary leader of Pro in the Senate. But in his view, passing a bad tax plan also has consequences. The cabinet has adjusted the plans on several points to gain support, but that does not mean the objections have disappeared. BBB parliamentary leader Ilona Lagas is also very worried about the way the cabinet operates. She calls the current state of affairs "far beyond an experiment" and even speaks of a "disaster scenario". 'Buckshot' The cabinet has tried to accommodate several opposition parties. For example, the VAT increase on ornamental plant products, also known as the flower tax, has been shelved for now. Other adjustments have also been made in other areas. SGP parliamentary leader Peter Schalk sees in this mainly an attempt to gather support on all fronts. "There have been a number of gestures made in all directions. It's a kind of buckshot, in the hope that everyone says: okay, just leave the other things be." Pro leader Jesse Klaver is also critical of the cabinet's approach. He calls it an "enormous gamble" and believes the cabinet is taking a major risk with the stability of the Netherlands. According to Klaver, this shows a "complete lack of leadership". Pro says it has been willing to compromise several times, but according to Klaver it gets stuck on the VVD. That party does not want an increase in the tax on wealth, which according to Klaver makes cooperation impossible. Still, he does not want to give up yet. "In the debate we will really make one final attempt to reach an agreement anyway." For Volt, the cabinet, for example, set aside extra money for new AI policy. But that does not remove the party's objections. Parliamentary leader Gaby Perin calls the cabinet's approach "downright irresponsible". According to her, Jetten should have talked with Volt to secure a reliable majority. "The responsibility for whether the plan gets through or not really lies with the cabinet," says Perin. Lagas is also not impressed by the concessions. She considers it insufficient that the VAT increase on flowers and plants has been postponed by a year. "If we are only supposed to be satisfied with a postponement of the flower tax, I don't know how you would feel about that. We even feel a bit insulted by it." 50Plus and ChristenUnie open to it Still, there is also support in the Senate for the tax plan. The cabinet has at least secured that from 50Plus. Parliamentary leader Martin van Rooijen says his party is constructively involved in the process. "I really don't like talking about votes against at all. Assume that we support the tax plan." ChristenUnie parliamentary leader Mirjam Bikker in the House of Representatives is glad that the cabinet has listened to her party. She had been urging since May that working people and families should not have to pay for the cabinet's extra spending and that the sick should stay out of the first round of cuts. "Finally, that has been listened to. I think that is good news for these people and therefore also a step towards a more sensible tax plan," she says. JA21 meanwhile is not showing its hand. Political commentator Arjan Noorlander "The cabinet is no longer in charge now, but the Senate and the House of Representatives are. It has actually long stopped being about meaningful plans for the future of the Netherlands. It is about the survival of this cabinet, about stumbling over coincidental majorities in the Senate and House, so that the cabinet can last another year and then they can try again. Then, if they are still in office, perhaps something will come of all those grand ambitions." In the House of Representatives, the cabinet seems able to get sufficient support, with backing from, among others, ChristenUnie, 50Plus and Groep Markuszower. In the Senate that is more complicated. There the cabinet has no fixed majority and depends on opposition parties that have not all declared their positions yet. Rosenmöller hopes that sufficient support will eventually come for the tax plan and the budgets. He does not want new elections: "No one is waiting for that at all."

title: Morning briefing 4/11: US results come in • Lawsuit over Tarwekamp explosion
lead: Good morning! In The Hague, the trial of the four suspects in the 2024 attack on a bridal fashion shop begins, and the quintessentially Dutch department store chain HEMA turns exactly one hundred years old. First, the weather: this morning there is a mix of clouds and sunshine. During the afternoon it will gradually clear up further. It will be 9 or 10 degrees, with a strong north-easterly wind. The coming days bring fresh autumn weather with plenty of sun and quite cold nights. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? The elections in the United States have resulted in a huge defeat for the Republicans and a win for the Democrats. Exactly how large that victory will be will become clearer during the course of today. What is already clear is that the Democrats have obtained a majority in both the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. The first was widely expected, the second was much more uncertain beforehand. Follow the results in our liveblog or in our stream . And here you can find all the results on our interactive map . Other news from overnight: And finally, one more thing: not only on earth, but also in space, people voted. On the International Space Station ISS, the three American astronauts cast their votes. Astronaut Anil Menon posted a video of the event on X. "Yes! You can even vote from space", he wrote. Have a good day!

title: Inflation rises further to 3.7 percent in October, groceries slightly cheaper
lead: Prices rose more in October than in the month before. Inflation was 3.7 percent, in September it was 3.4 percent. That is according to the preliminary estimate of the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity>. The inflation figure means that prices in October were 3.7 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier. The final figure comes on 10 November, when it can still be adjusted. In the first estimate, price changes were calculated for a number of product groups. This showed that groceries became slightly cheaper, but energy, including motor fuels, became more expensive. Month on month: When comparing month on month instead of year on year, prices in October were 0.7 percent higher than in September. On average over the past ten years, prices in October were 0.5 percent higher than in September. The CBS notes that when comparing two consecutive months, seasonal influences must be taken into account. For example, clothing is cheaper during the sales. Prices are then temporarily lower, but this is not a structural price decline.

title: ING opens its doors on Saba and Sint-Eustatius at the end of this month
lead: Residents of Saba and Sint-Eustatius can bank with a Dutch bank again from the end of this month. ING opens an office on Sint-Eustatius on 24 November. Two days later the doors open of an ING branch on Saba. With the opening of the offices, residents of the Caribbean Netherlands can open an account with a Dutch bank again for the first time in years. One and a half years ago ING unveiled plans to return to the Dutch islands in the Caribbean. This would happen with "the same service as on Texel", the bank promised. A lot still had to be arranged for this. The islands are so-called special Dutch municipalities, but do not fall under the European Economic Area. Payments are made in US dollars. That makes it legally challenging for a Dutch bank to offer accounts and cash. Away from the islands. Partly for that reason ING pulled the plug on Netherlands Caribbean Bank in 2009. Internet banking with ABN Amro is still possible, but this bank no longer accepts new customers from the islands. Rabobank does so only if someone has a "clear economic link" with the Netherlands. For a bank account, residents had to go to foreign banks, which is also cumbersome. ING says it has now complied with all laws and regulations to resume services on the islands. Initially, residents and entrepreneurs of Sint-Eustatius and Saba can open a payment account with ING, apply for a debit card and bank digitally. The online and telephone customer service will go through ING's regular services. Cash can be obtained from new ATMs that <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity> (DNB) has placed. ING calls the first two offices on Sint-Eustatius and Saba a "first step in the further development of services on the islands". About 3200 people live on Sint-Eustatius, just over 2000 on Saba. ING says it wants to contribute to the economic development of the islands with the bank offices.

title: Trump accepts election defeat, but also immediately threatens vetoes
lead: President Trump says he will accept the results of yesterday's Congressional elections. His Republican party achieved even worse results than expected, but Trump said he hopes he can work with the Democrats in the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. "I am absolutely willing to accept those results", he said in an interview with The New York Times. "We will work with the Democrats; we look forward to getting started with them. We will probably manage", he told the newspaper. Liveblog Follow the latest developments in our liveblog . Beforehand there was fear that Trump would not accept a poor result, as he never recognised his defeat in the 2020 presidential elections. Now, in his first reactions, he chose a conciliatory tone. Perhaps he is looking for ways to reach a compromise with the Democrats, who from January will gain more power in both chambers of parliament and have a majority. Vetoing everything "I think they do want to work with me", he told broadcaster <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity>. "Otherwise I will simply veto everything, and they don't want that." On Fox News Trump gave a first, telephone reaction to the election results. There he said he was surprised: Still, the question is how much Trump's outreach is worth. On his platform Truth Social he struck a sharper tone in new posts. For example, he shared an image of a red cap with the word 'VETO' prominently on it. 'No attack on me' He also repeatedly tried to place the blame for the Republican defeat on the candidates. He feels that some "fought against him". For instance, he lashed out at Texas governor Greg Abbott, who according to him lost because he behaved like a "RINO" ("Republican In Name Only"). In another post Trump claimed that the Republicans would have won by a large margin if his name had been on the ballot. "I was not on the ballot, and if I had been, we would have won overwhelmingly." Trump therefore does not believe he is partly responsible for the loss. "I don't see it as an attack on me", he said by phone to Fox News. "We have just come through the best two years in the history of the presidency, in terms of the economy and everything we have achieved", he claimed. 'Iran was part of it' Yet Trump acknowledged to The Wall Street Journal that the war in Iran has something to do with his loss. "Iran was part of that", he stated in a telephone interview with the newspaper. But he specifically expressed his support for Defence Secretary Hegseth, one of the driving forces behind the war: "I actually think he is fantastic". Trump was sporting enough to congratulate the winners: "Well, I'll say this: congratulations to the Democrats", Trump said. "They did a good job. They have been looking for this for eleven years, and now they have finally pulled it off." See all the results on our interactive map:

title: Dozens of golden hearts for war children stolen from path in Utrecht
lead: The Hearts Path in Wilhelminapark in Utrecht, a war memorial consisting of 150 golden hearts for war children who were rescued, has become a lot shorter. Recently at least sixty hearts have been stolen, the initiator tells RTV Utrecht . Each golden heart stands for a child who was rescued during the Second World War by resistance women Trui van Lier and Jet Berdenis van Berlekom. Jewish children were taken in at Van Lier's day nursery in Utrecht so that they would not be deported. From there they went on to other hiding addresses. 150 children survived the war this way. The Hearts Path, together with a plaque in the park, tells that story. The theft hits initiator Michèle van Lier hard: "I find it deeply sad that we cannot leave such a beautiful monument there." Not worth money Van Lier is a second cousin of the resistance woman, who died in 2002. Shortly after the path was laid in 2024, 22 hearts were also stolen. Almost no spare hearts are left. "I have only six left", says Van Lier. She does not understand why someone takes the hearts: "Perhaps people think it is worth money, but it is simply a mix of two types of metal." There is no real gold in the hearts. Historical researcher Jim Terlingen wrote a biography of Trui van Lier and is very upset about the thefts. Most of the hearts are not linked to specific children, with the exception of two. These symbolise the Amsterdam twins Deetje and Joeki, who did not go to a hiding address but stayed at the day nursery for almost the entire war. Terlingen is still in contact with one of them. "That affects me in particular", says Terlingen. "Those two hearts lay next to each other. That they are gone does something to me." The playground at the end of the Hearts Path is named after Trui van Lier: Michèle van Lier is in talks with the municipality about a possible solution. Whether the missing hearts will be placed again is still uncertain. "Honestly, I don't think it makes sense to keep putting new hearts back when they keep disappearing." She says she still has to come to terms with the recent theft. "The Hearts Path was very popular. I saw children and adults follow that path so often. Now it is ruined." Newsletter World War II Interested in World War II? Subscribe to our newsletter here.

title: Ahold Delhaize sees damage of tens of millions from cyberattack
lead: The cyberattack last month costs Ahold Delhaize 200 to 250 million euros in revenue. As a result, the final profit will be between 75 and 100 million euros lower. The international supermarket company says this today when presenting the figures for the third quarter. The cyberattack caused major disruptions at Albert Heijn stores and other retail chains of the group. A number of systems were taken offline to limit the consequences of the attack. Distribution centres came to a standstill, leaving stores with empty shelves. Websites and apps were unreachable for days. Hit again Subsidiary Delhaize was hit again by a hack this week, as were other European supermarket chains. Digital intruders turned up the temperature of refrigerators. Ahold Delhaize has slightly adjusted its profit forecast for the full year. It went from "around 4 percent" to "approaching 4 percent". Third quarter In the third quarter Ahold Delhaize earned 976 million euros from its operating activities. The company has just over 9,000 supermarkets in 9 countries worldwide. "Although most of the disruption was under control within two weeks, we are still working on fully restoring our normal business operations", says CEO Frans Muller in a statement on the results. Earnings per share are expected to grow this year by "low single-digit" percentages. Ahold Delhaize previously expected growth of mid to high single-digit percentages. In the past quarter the group achieved revenue of 23.1 billion euros, 1.9 percent more than in the same period last year. Without unfavourable exchange rates, this would have been an increase of 2.6 percent. The operating profit of Ahold Delhaize, which is based in Zaandam, rose by just over 7 percent in the third quarter to 976 million euros.

title: History is being made in the US midterms, these are the firsts
lead: The Kansas Senate seat that has gone to the Democrats for the first time in 94 years, and the state of Georgia that has elected its first Black female governor ever. In the US midterm elections, which result in a so-called blue wave for the Democratic party, history is being written. We list a number of firsts: In his victory speech in New Hampshire, Pappas thanked his husband: Also on 3 January, the Democrats can once again make history. That is when the new Congress will be sworn in. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries could then become the first Black speaker of the House of Representatives. He is expected to be nominated and elected as the so-called Speaker of the House.

title: Digital crook Tony must help farmers say no to real criminals
lead: Farmers can recently practise conversations with the criminal Tony. Tony is not a real criminal, but an AI version that tries to persuade farmers to rent out their barn for illegal activities. By practising the conversations, entrepreneurs, trade organisations, municipalities and the judiciary hope that farmers will learn to say no better. Dutch farmers have for years been approached by criminals to rent barns, stables or sheds. Criminals are willing to pay thousands or even tens of thousands of euros per month to grow weed or start a drug lab, for example. About 1 in 10 to 1 in 5 farmers in the Netherlands is approached now and then, research by farmers' organisation LTO shows. The proposals are often simple but tempting, says Pedro Bogerd of Platform Veilig Ondernemen (PVO) Midden-Nederland at Omroep <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity> . "Literally notes through the door or ringing the bell with: 'We want to rent space from you, we want to put plants there. Don't worry, because we've been doing this for years. And you earn 30,000 to 40,000 euros per month'." Practising conversation techniques The AI criminal is a creation of PVO, a partnership of entrepreneurs, municipalities, <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, judiciary and trade organisations. According to Bogerd, the goal is clear: "Ideally you make sure that person leaves calmly and never comes back. With your conversation techniques you can make that happen." This is how the AI criminal works: The entrepreneurs can talk to the digital criminal in two ways: through an organic conversation in which AI listens to the answers and responds, or a version with multiple-choice questions in which different scenarios are run through. Afterwards a report follows on how the conversation went. Bogerd also tried it out and there turned out to be enough room for improvement. "I stayed very friendly, but in the end I gave away quite a lot of information," he says. "The worst thing you can do is make direct promises. I did make some. I have a score of 37 percent and that is not good," he says. Lively The reactions from agricultural entrepreneurs are positive, says Bogerd. "This morning I spoke to someone who had a conversation with Tony. She is a woman who can stand her ground well, but even she got tips. She had handled it calmly, but still gave a number of details that she should not have mentioned." That the farmers know beforehand that they are talking to a fake criminal does not make much difference, according to Bogerd. "They are already alert, but it's a nice gimmick to get the conversation going. Most people have some idea how this works, only this makes the situation lively."

title: The Netherlands nominates Klaas Knot for president of the European Central Bank
lead: The Netherlands is nominating Klaas Knot as a candidate to become the new president of the European Central Bank (ECB). The post is becoming vacant because the current president Christine Lagarde is leaving earlier. Knot was president of <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity> (DNB) from 2011 to 2025. The <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">ministerie van Financiën</entity> has announced that, as far as the Netherlands is concerned, he is the best successor to Lagarde. Member states of the European Union have until and including Friday to nominate candidates. Next Monday, at a meeting of the European finance ministers, it will be considered who has been nominated. It is expected that a decision will be made in mid-December on who becomes the new president. That person must in any case gain the support of 16 of the 21 EU countries where the euro is used. Those must together represent at least 65 percent of the population of the eurozone. Rare royal honour Klaas Knot has a long career at DNB behind him. Before becoming president there, he worked there as an economist and strategist. When he left De Nederlandsche Bank last year, he received a rare, high royal honour: he is grand officer in the Order of Orange-Nassau. Since leaving DNB he has been mentioned as a possible successor at the ECB. He is seen as an important candidate, who has the most competition to fear from the former president of the Spanish central bank Pablo Hernández de Cos. Christine Lagarde announced last week that she will leave the ECB on 7 February. Her term actually runs until the end of October 2027. Lagarde is reportedly a candidate for chair of the World Economic Forum. The Netherlands has previously had a president of the European Central Bank. That was Wim Duisenberg. He was the first to hold the post from 1998 until the end of 2003 and played an important role in introducing the euro.

title: Climate finance for vulnerable countries keeps falling short, while the problem grows
lead: Money flows meant to make poor countries less vulnerable to climate change keep falling short by many billions. And this while the chance that global warming stays below 1.5 degrees Celsius is for now out of the question . That is stated in a new report from the United Nations Environment Programme. The shortfall in financing again promises to be a point of contention at the climate summit in Turkey next week. "The world is not ready to adapt to the current climate, let alone to the consequences that overshooting 1.5 degrees is going to bring," says director Inger Andersen of the UN Environment Programme. She calls on countries to increase their contributions at the climate summit, in order to prevent damage and victims. In 2024, the most recent year for which data is available, the contribution of rich countries to developing countries rose to around 30 billion dollars. An important financing target that countries agreed earlier, 40 billion dollars in 2025, appears unattainable. Three times as much Year after year, this report concludes that the implementation of the plans is lagging far behind, which stands in the way of the climate ambitions of poorer countries. "As long as no more financing comes, it will become very difficult for these countries to realise their ambitions, let alone increase them. Then everything is at a standstill," says climate finance expert Pieter Pauw of the TU Eindhoven, who, like in previous years, is contributing to the report. This time, the researchers examined, among other things, a grand plan that was proposed at the climate summit last year: countries must pay three times as much to developing countries by 2035 to protect themselves against the consequences of climate change. That would mean that between 85 and 120 billion dollars a year would flow from rich to poorer countries. Although that is considerably more than the current amount, it is still far too little for the high costs that poor countries will incur by then. The researchers point out that the amount needed, corrected for inflation, will rise to 420 billion dollars by then. Frustration The gap between the required financing and the amount actually available is a growing source of frustration for poorer countries, which historically have contributed far less than rich countries to global warming. They want the richer industrialised countries, which built up their economies by emitting large amounts of greenhouse gases, to pay their share to make their countries less vulnerable. Rich countries endorse this in theory, but in practice they open their purses too little, the UN Environment Programme warns again and again. The dissatisfaction of developing countries over the lack of financing often returns at the climate summits. In recent years, the tone has become harsh. "Just as the need for adaptation is growing faster than ever, financing is stagnating," responds Barbara Rosen Jacobson of the aid organisation Prosper Global. As a result, she says, the gap between what is needed and what is available continues to widen, while vulnerable countries particularly need more support to adapt to a changing climate. More financing The fact that the cabinet-Jetten is increasing climate finance again after the cuts by the cabinet-Schoof is seen by financing expert Pauw as a favourable development for the poorer countries. "But other countries have actually lowered it again. Germany, for example, and the United Kingdom." Another positive development that the scientist sees is the amount of money that appears to flow from developing countries to other developing countries. According to the UN report, this rose from 3.8 billion to 9.6 billion dollars between 2019 and 2024. This larger share is mainly the result of a different accounting method, but it does show that these countries also contribute considerably. "It is more than I thought. I was pleasantly surprised by that," says Pauw, who considers this an important insight. "This could open up the discussion a little more about how that financing should work in the future. After all, it cannot be the case that a few industrialised countries have to pay for everything."

title: Policyholders of De Goudse also to receive compensation for woekerpolis policies
lead: Customers of De Goudse with a woekerpolis can now definitively count on financial compensation. The insurer is setting aside about 12.5 million euros for this. As early as January 2025, De Goudse reached an agreement on the compensation with the Consumentenbond and the claim foundations ConsumentenClaim, Stichting Woekerpolisproces, Vereniging Woekerpolis.nl and Wakkerpolis. However, for this settlement to succeed, 90 percent of the aggrieved parties had to accept their personal settlement offer. That is now the case. As a result, De Goudse must pay 12.5 million euros. The insurer De Goudse does not want to say how many aggrieved policyholders the amount must be divided among. What are woekerpolissen? Woekerpolissen are insurance policies in which the paid premiums are invested. They were sold from the early 1990s until 2008. Customers were lured in with high possible returns. What insurers usually did not tell, or did not make clear, was that they deducted (high) costs from the premium to be invested, so that the promised return was far from achieved. In total, an estimated seven million woekerpolissen were sold in the Netherlands, with a total value of 100 billion euros. According to the <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-autoriteit-financiele-markten">Autoriteit Financiële Markten</entity> (AFM), there were probably still about 2 million ongoing woekerpolissen in 2018. Payout can take months. "We are glad that the participants are satisfied with their personal offers. For these consumers, a long-running case finally comes to an end," says Sandra Molenaar, director of the Consumentenbond. As the implementing organisation, ConsumentenClaim can now begin with the payouts. "The process is not going to be finished tomorrow. It can still take three to six months before everything has been processed," says director Stef Smit. The Consumentenbond advises consumers who have not yet accepted their offer, and who now still want to do so, to do this as soon as possible so the process can be completed quickly. This way, they can be included in the payout process without delay. End of the woekerpolis case? Interest groups such as the Consumentenbond have been fighting for compensation for years. Earlier, they reached settlements with Allianz, ASR/Aegon, Nationale Nederlanden, Achmea and Reaal. As a result, settlements have now been reached with the largest Dutch insurers. The end is in sight, although the interest groups are still focusing on smaller insurers. For example, the Consumentenbond emphasises that consumers who have or had an investment insurance with ERGO Insurance, KBC Group, Legal &General/Scildon, Onderlinge 's-Gravenhage and Waard verzekeringen can still report to them.

title: Marco Borsato hints at a comeback and wants 431.000 euro back from the state
lead: Marco Borsato demands more than 431.000 euro back from the state, mainly for legal fees. That became clear in the court in Utrecht. The singer was acquitted last year of sexual misconduct with a minor girl. The singer incurred these costs by engaging the lawyer couple Geert-Jan and Carry Knoops, hiring various experts, and using a private security company for his trips to the courtroom. The 59-year-old singer, who was personally present in the courtroom this morning, was acquitted at the end of 2025, after a legal process that lasted four years, of indecently touching a girl in her bedroom. Her mother was the chair of Borsato's fan club. The judge ruled that there was insufficient corroborating evidence to substantiate the accusations against the singer. It was already known that the singer wanted his lawyers' costs back, around 389.000 euro. On top of that, he now also claims the costs of hired experts, around 35.000 euro, and the costs he incurred for hiring security guards, about 7000 euro. The total amount thus comes to 431.000 euro, including VAT. Not unique, but a lot of attention. That someone who has been acquitted claims back the costs of his defence is not unique, but that there is so much attention for it is. Often a case to recover legal costs incurred is settled in writing. Whether the money that is claimed is actually paid out must be assessed by the court. In the courtroom, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) questions whether all the amounts claimed by Borsato qualify for reimbursement. The OM points out that the opinion of an expert did not make it into the judgment. Justice also doubts whether everything invoiced by the lawyer couple Knoops must be reimbursed. Some of it must, the OM acknowledges, but the costs of refuting rumours in the media, for example, do not, the OM says. The court also asks whether it was necessary for Borsato to hire lawyers before a complaint had actually been filed. According to the singer, he had to do so because he is a public figure and rumours about him could be "disastrous" for his career. Carry Knoops also points to the enormous drop in Borsato's income as a singer from the moment the accusations came out. She asks what an acquittal is worth if he himself has to pay for the costs incurred. 'I want to carry on with my life' Before Borsato entered the courtroom, he told various media that reclaiming his defence costs was "a matter of principle". "This is part of the system, and for me that is no different than for anyone else." He also said he was "a bit done" with everything surrounding the criminal case against him and that he is now thinking about a comeback as a singer. "I want to carry on with my life, I want to carry on with what I am good at, and that is practising my profession." Borsato said he is taking singing lessons and that they were going "remarkably well". "I am very cautiously looking ahead to next year, but first this has to be behind me." The ruling on the costs Borsato is claiming back is expected on 27 November.

title: First of nine hearing days: main suspect heard over explosion at Tarwekamp
lead: Today in the court in The Hague the first of nine hearing days began in the criminal case over the explosion at Tarwekamp in The Hague. Four men are suspected of organising and carrying out the devastating explosion in a flat in the Mariahoeve neighbourhood. In the attack on a bridal fashion shop on the ground floor of the building on 7 December 2024, part of the building collapsed and six people lost their lives. Around 100 residents of the affected flat are sitting in the courtroom or in video rooms set up for them. There is also a special room for the relatives of the victims who died. Commissioning party Moshtag B. Moshtag B. is the main suspect in the case. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> suspects him of giving the order for the attack. He is also suspected of stalking, threatening and assaulting his then girlfriend. According to the Openbaar Ministerie, the 35-year-old wanted revenge on his ex-girlfriend, the owner of the bridal fashion shop. She had ended the relationship shortly before the explosion. A reconstruction by the NOS had already shown that Mosthtag B. felt his honour was damaged and that he "wanted to make her pay for it". B. was questioned by the judge this morning about the period leading up to the devastating explosion, when he was still in a relationship. That questioning reveals a picture of a relationship in which his girlfriend initially felt pampered, because Moshtag B. took her out to eat, bought her gifts and gave her a monthly allowance. Stalking and threats The relationship later changed: he became possessive and jealous. For example, he regularly hung around her home and her bridal fashion shop. After he saw messages come in on her phone, he cloned her phone so that he could read along on her WhatsApp as well as social media such as Facebook and Instagram. For months he read along with her messages. By his own account, he wanted to see his suspicions that she was cheating confirmed. He is also said to have threatened her. "I wouldn't do anything to you, but I would to the people who are dear to you", his ex-girlfriend stated about those threats. She was afraid to end the relationship. She is said to have told family members that "if something happens to me, you know who did it". Moshtag B. denies this. "They are lying", he stated this morning. It also emerged that the suspect had given his ex-girlfriend thousands of euros, or lent it to her. Because he feared he would lose the money if he ended the relationship, he, by his own account, kept her "on a leash". From 'destroying her' to explosion To "destroy her financially", as he had stated, he then took more drastic measures. Where he had first planned to rob her bridal shop empty and smash it up, the plan for arson at the shop later arose. Moshtag B. contacted others to do it for him. They caused the eventual explosion. These three men are also on trial. Two of them are suspected of the murder of six people and the attempted murder of eight people in homes on Tarwekamp. The third was not present at the explosion. Because of his role in the preliminary stage, the OM holds him jointly responsible for the fire in the bridal shop.

title: 'Underground banker' from Rotterdam suspected of laundering millions to Turkey
lead: During an action by Europol against an international money laundering network, German and Dutch investigators arrested five suspects, including a 55-year-old man from Rotterdam. He is suspected of involvement in receiving and sending cash worth about 60 million euros. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the suspect is presumably an illegal financial intermediary, colloquially also called an underground banker. He is suspected of ties to a mainly Turkish-German criminal organisation. The 55-year-old man from Rotterdam was arrested in Eindhoven. Smelted gold and silver bars The Rotterdam Seaport Police searched two properties for this case, in Eindhoven and Rotterdam. About 10,000 euros in cash, a vehicle and real estate were seized. In Sliedrecht and Zwijndrecht, properties were also searched by the German police. In addition, about forty locations spread over several German states were raided. Four men aged between 43 and 59 were arrested. The German police seized real estate worth at least 2 million euros, nineteen vehicles, about 100,000 euros in cash and a large quantity of smelted gold and silver bars. About 500 Dutch and German police officers were deployed for the large-scale operation on 7 October. Years of investigation preceded it. The trigger was a routine check two years earlier, when German traffic police on a motorway found a modified vehicle. Several kilos of gold and nearly half a million euros in cash were hidden in it. The money and gold, with a total value of 4 million euros, have been seized. Follow-up investigation showed that the criminal organisation possibly offers money laundering services to third parties. Investigators suspect that tens of millions of euros of criminal money a year, presumably from drug trafficking, has been funnelled to Turkey. From scrap gold to jewellery The criminal organisation would have laundered the money by buying old gold and scrap gold through friendly jewellers. That gold was then melted down into gold bars and smuggled to Turkey via modified vehicles or air routes. There, jewellery was made from the gold to pay clients, or the gold was illegally sent back to Germany to compensate the jewellers. Police estimate that over six years, between 1 and 4 tonnes of gold were smuggled to Turkey this way, with a total value of 55 to 210 million euros.

title: Amsterdam mayor closes party venue after new violent incidents
lead: <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Burgemeester Halsema</entity> has closed a party venue in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>-Sloterdijk for three months. That decision was made because serious violence has occurred several times in a short period. On 6 September there was a shooting and on 24 October an assault.
