Opponents did not want the king to go to the World Cup because of the human rights situation in the country. The king said at the time that personal feelings would play a role in the decision to go. If Oranje had reached the final, a government delegation would have travelled to Qatar. The Dutch team was knocked out in the quarter-finals. Tightened travel advice Because of the war between the US and Iran and the rising tensions in the region, the travel advice for Qatar was tightened to orange earlier this year. In response to American attacks, Iran attacked US allies in the Middle East. The travel advice is now yellow. That means travel to the country is possible, but there are still security risks.

title: Brother of former Prime Minister Orbán arrested in Hungary on suspicion of human trafficking
lead: The brother of the former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, Áron Orbán, has been arrested on suspicion of human trafficking. The current Prime Minister Magyar reports this on Facebook, based on press releases. The National Investigation Bureau (NNI) and the anti-corruption service NVVH are conducting the investigation. Arrests and house searches have taken place at several locations in the capital Budapest. Former Prime Minister Orbán writes on Facebook that the authorities are playing a "dirty game" and only want to eliminate political opponents. "I am the target; my younger brother is merely an instrument", he writes. In response, Prime Minister Magyar says that Orbán is "as usual" pointing at others. According to Euronews, Áron Orbán's company may have made it easier for Vietnamese citizens to obtain a Hungarian visa, and therefore a Schengen visa. This possibly happened for payment. The company reportedly did this by enrolling them in a two-day course at the University of Pécs, in southern Hungary. Tackling corruption In April, Magyar won the Hungarian elections. This ended Orbán's rule after sixteen years. Magyar has said that he wants to tackle corruption in Hungary and to hold the circle around the former Prime Minister to account. In June, the director of the Hungarian anti-corruption watchdog was himself charged with corruption. And in October, the former head of the Hungarian central bank was arrested on suspicion of financial fraud. The anti-corruption organisation NVVH has been given more powers under Magyar. This is one of the agreements the new Prime Minister made with the European Union in order to gain access to billions of euros in frozen assets for the country.

title: More than 10 years in prison for British comedian Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault
lead: British comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault. The 51-year-old Brand was already found guilty last week. It concerns one rape and three cases of sexual assault. In one of the incidents, he unsolicited pushed his face, nose and mouth into one victim's crotch. The offences took place between 2004 and 2009. Brand has always said he is innocent. The judge called Brand a "sexual predator" and stood up for the victims: "Whatever women wear, wherever they are and however much they drink. They retain the right to say 'no'". 'Trauma that I carry with me every day' During the hearing on sentencing, the four victims sat behind screens to remain anonymous. One of the victims of a sexual assault said the event had a major impact on her life. "For years I was in shock. I was extremely upset and traumatised and had no respect left for myself." The other victims had a statement read out by the prosecutor. The woman who was raped by Russell Brand in 2009 wrote in her statement that after the attack she could no longer work and moved back in with her parents. "It is a trauma that I carry with me every day and it feels like it never ends." Brand's fame made it extra difficult for the women to process the events. "It was impossible not to see him in the media", said one of the victims. "Every time I saw or heard him somewhere, I was startled", said another woman. According to BBC journalists, Brand showed no emotion when hearing the victims' statements. He did, however, close his eyes several times. While the judge read out the verdict, he stared straight ahead. Brand faced seven charges. In addition to the rape and the three cases of sexual assault for which he has been convicted, he was acquitted of two other rapes and one attempted sexual assault. The incidents were said to have taken place between 1999 and 2009. During that period, Brand was at the height of his career. "Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually abuse women", the police wrote in a statement. Since his conviction last week, Brand has been in prison. According to the BBC, he will be closely monitored there, because due to the nature of his offences, his wealth and his fame, he is at risk. Other prisoners might want to harm him. More allegations Brand is known, among other things, for his roles in films such as Forgetting Sarah Marshall (2008), Despicable Me and Get Him to the Greek (2010). He also presented various programmes on British radio and television. As a comedian, Brand is known for his controversial stand-up comedy. He also made podcasts and YouTube videos, and gained fame through his marriage to pop star Katy Perry between 2010 and 2012. "I hope this conviction sends a clear signal that nobody is above the law, however famous or powerful he or she may be", said the police. More victims of Brand are expected to now feel brave enough to come forward. In the United Kingdom, Brand is currently still being investigated in connection with new allegations of rape made by two women. In the United States, a civil lawsuit is pending against him. He is alleged to have raped an extra during the filming of the movie Arthur.

title: Rachel Hazes sells music rights to folk singer André Hazes after 40 years
lead: Rachel Hazes has sold the music rights of André Hazes to investment fund Pythagoras Music Fund (PMF). The company reports this in a statement following coverage by De Telegraaf. It is not known how much was paid for this. The rights were bought by taking over the shares of Melvin Produkties, Rachel Hazes' production company, PMF says in the statement. According to PMF, Rachel Hazes will keep a watchful eye in the background and advise where needed. The widow of the folk singer says in the statement that she wants to step back and take more rest. "After almost forty years in which I have dedicated myself and carried the responsibility to protect André's legacy as well as possible, I want to be able to take a bit more rest in the years ahead of me." The 56-year-old Rachel Hazes says it is especially important to her "that the name André Hazes, his music, his rights and everything he has left behind is treated with respect, remains protected and is also preserved for the generations to come, and so is kept in honour". Name and image PMF says it is grateful that Rachel is entrusting André Hazes' musical legacy to the company. "Together we want, on the one hand, to continue building on André's musical legacy and, on the other hand, we want to protect and cherish his name and image for future generations." PMF was founded in 2021 by, among others, composer John Ewbank and buys music rights. The investment fund holds, among other things, the rights to bands such as Golden Earring and Shocking Blue, and to songs such as Come Fly With Me by Frank Sinatra and Ain't that A Kick In The Head by Dean Martin. André Hazes is known for songs such as Kleine Jongen, Zij Gelooft in Mij and Bloed, zweet en tranen . On 23 September 2004, the Amsterdam folk singer died at the age of 53 from the effects of two heart attacks and a cardiac arrest.

title: Does tear gas disrupt menstruation? Women in France want it investigated
lead: Severe cramps, unbearable pain or an early period. Thousands of women in France say their menstrual cycle has been seriously disrupted after being exposed to tear gas at recent protests. A link between serious menstrual complaints and tear gas has not been scientifically established, but the call to stop using the agent is growing louder. French police have frequently used tear gas at the large-scale protests against the state of education and rising living costs. On 17 October as many as 22,000 tear gas grenades were deployed against demonstrators, says <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Minister Nunez. Police also used tear gas at protests last week. Complaints collected After Eva Luna Tholance heard stories from women who experienced abnormal menstrual complaints after exposure to tear gas, she founded the collective Lacrymos de sang (Blood tear gas) on 8 October. More than 10,000 women from all over France have since reported their experiences. Tholance says she is shocked that so many women say they have the same complaints. "Women experience anything from mild pain to the worst cramps of their lives. But also severe blood loss, so that some have to go to hospital." Sometimes the complaints appear within 48 hours, says Tholance. "We don't know what the long-term consequences are. That has not been investigated." Lacrymo de sang also says it has received many reports from women with complaints who did not take part in a protest. For example, they were walking their dog or had opened a window. "Tear gas doesn't discriminate, it affects everyone", says Tholance. 'Unbearable pain' French women are also telling their stories on social media. "On 17 October I was at a demonstration where tear gas was used", says a young woman in a video on TikTok. She says she came into brief contact with tear gas, and that it was enough to get watery eyes and a burning throat. "I went home and the next evening, about 28 hours after the exposure, I got very severe cramps. I have never in my life experienced such pain." Another woman says on Instagram that she unexpectedly got her period a day after a protest this month. Despite pain medication, which she calls "unbearable", she could not get out of bed. She reported her complaints to the platform Lacrymos de sang. Professor of clinical and forensic toxicology Eric Franssen is surprised by the reports and calls them serious. Still, he is cautious about drawing a direct link between tear gas and menstrual complaints, because too little research has been done. "Tear gas is essentially a powder that is dispersed into small particles that irritate the nerves and mucous membranes. That is why you get tears in your eyes and itching. In some cases blisters also form on the skin and the agent can cause an allergic reaction." There are different types of tear gas. In the Netherlands mainly CS gas is used, says Franssen, who is affiliated with the University of Amsterdam. This type of tear gas is also used in France. Voluntary sign-ups In 2020 a Scottish university researched the effects of tear gas on women who took part in yellow vest demonstrations in France. The study suggested there is a link between exposure to tear gas and menstrual complaints. In the United States a doctor decided a year later to conduct research, after several American women reported changes in their menstrual cycle. They were exposed to tear gas at Black Lives Matter protests in Portland, in the state of Oregon, in 2020. Just over 54 percent of the 1,650 respondents said they had problems with their periods. Most complaints concerned increased menstrual cramps and heavy bleeding. According to the study, the symptoms occurred mainly among women who had been exposed to tear gas on several days. In another American study, from 2023, 83 percent of the 1,276 respondents say they have complaints such as cramps, sensitive breasts and an early period after police used tear gas at protests. However, the participants in the studies signed up voluntarily and filled in questionnaires themselves. The women therefore did not undergo medical examinations to establish menstrual complaints or a possible link with tear gas. Stress Although all three studies suggest a link, they also point to other factors that may play a major role in the disruptions, says Franssen, such as stress. "You are being chased by the police during a demonstration. That adrenaline rush and stress can also lead to a disrupted menstrual cycle", says the professor. "It is an interplay in the body in which all those things can have an effect. That makes it difficult to draw firm conclusions." According to Franssen there is a knowledge gap. He therefore calls for more research. "It does say something that there is little knowledge about this issue." It has long been known that healthcare for women lags behind that for men. In recent years more attention has been paid to women-specific health problems in research and treatment. Falling on deaf ears Tholance of Lacrymos de sang also calls for more research. But she does not believe stress is the main cause. Her collective wants the French government to stop using tear gas until more is known about its effects. But that demand is for now falling on deaf ears. Minister Nunez of the Interior defended the use of tear gas last week after questions in parliament about the consequences of tear gas for women. According to him, officers must "be able to defend themselves when they are attacked at demonstrations". Nunez also said he was "not aware of the harmful nature of tear gas". According to him, the effects of tear gas are short-lived. "That is why I will not suspend the use of tear gas."

title: Nvidia shares drop sharply on American stock exchange after CEO spy affair
lead: Nvidia takes a heavy hit on the American Nasdaq stock exchange after the affair of CEO Jensen Huang was made public. At the opening of the exchange, the share dropped by about 8 percent. That would mean more than 350 billion dollars in market value has been lost. The share later recovered somewhat, but is still well in the red. Nvidia makes chips that are used, among other things, for AI data centres. In recent years these have been installed worldwide at a high pace, and this led to large profits for companies such as Nvidia. On the stock market, the company's value this spring was more than 5 trillion dollars . That made it the most valuable company in the world. Spy affair The shares of Nvidia fell because of an affair by Huang. He had an intimate relationship with a Chinese spy, suspected by American intelligence services. The woman named Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is said to have been recruited by the Chinese secret service for espionage. She worked for a company that had a customer relationship with Nvidia. Nvidia is starting an independent investigation into the CEO's intimate relationship. The fear is that Chinese companies had access during that period to the chips that, due to sanctions, were not supposed to end up in China. The board of directors states in a statement that there is no reason to assume that American national security or the company's secrets have been endangered. Setbacks in tech shares Other tech shares also took a beating recently. After the Democrats' gains in the United States in the midterm elections, investors are wondering whether the growth of artificial intelligence will slow down more than expected. Nvidia's shares also fell last week to their lowest point in six months. That wiped out nearly 400 billion dollars in value. On top of that comes this price drop caused by the CEO. Investors wonder how long and whether Huang can remain as CEO. Meanwhile, the shares of most tech companies have recovered.

title: French government raises minimum wage after protests, union speaks of crumbs
lead: After weeks of social unrest, the French government has announced it will raise the minimum wage by 1.6 percent from next month. This is partly a correction for inflation. The commitment followed talks in a hotel in Paris with trade unions and employers' organisations in Paris. This social conference, as the government had dubbed the talks, was meant to end the social unrest. In France, there have been several large nationwide protest days in recent weeks, with demonstrators demanding improvements in education and complaining about the high cost of living. 'Alms' Trade unions, however, are not impressed by the higher minimum wage and speak of "crumbs" and "alms". "The anger will not disappear, because the government is going to announce an increase of a few euros in the minimum wage", says Sophie Binet, chair of the CGT, one of the largest trade unions in France. Prime Minister Lecornu disputes that view and points out that it is "the second-largest increase in the minimum wage in twenty years". "I don't think that should be scorned." Taken together, this year's increase amounts to 5.3 percent, Minister of Employment Farandou added. With this last "push", the net minimum monthly wage would come to just over 1,500 euros. Approaching Christmas period At the press conference after the 'polder consultation' in Paris, Lecornu called for a "return to calm, especially in city centres", also with an eye on the approaching Christmas period. The prime minister said he did not want to discourage demonstrations, but hopes chaos and violence can be prevented. Escalations in French cities are putting shopkeepers in a difficult position and "undermining competitiveness", he said. What began as a small-scale protest at a secondary school outside Paris has in recent weeks grown into a national popular movement: For now, trade unions are not impressed by the announced increase in the minimum wage. They have announced new demonstrations and strikes. A group of secondary schools, student and teacher organisations is calling on people to take to the streets again tomorrow. In addition, a coalition of trade unions is calling on its members to make their voices heard again on 17 November. Full agenda At the same time, Lecornu is filling his agenda this week with talks with all kinds of representatives of the people taking to the streets, such as trade unions, employers' organisations, pupils and students. The prime minister is also speaking this afternoon with the committee that wants to reform the outdated system for applications to higher education. The big question is whether these talks can calm the unrest in the country.

title: Death toll of capsized migrant boat off Senegal rises to 39
lead: The death toll after a boat carrying migrants capsized off the coast of Senegal has risen to 39. Senegal's emergency services today, a day after the tragic accident, have recovered several bodies from the water. Earlier, the death toll stood at 34. It is not known exactly how many people were on board the small boat. One survivor has been found. The boat was heading from northern Senegal to the Canary Islands, a popular migration route for thousands of young Senegalese and other West Africans. Deadliest route Migrants often make the crossing on fragile wooden fishing boats. With these boats, thousands of migrants each year try to survive a journey of 1300 kilometers across the Atlantic Ocean to the Spanish island group. The popular migration route is at the same time the deadliest migration route in the world. European Union deal Two years ago, the European Union promised financial support to Mauritania, which lies north of Senegal, to curb migration. An amount of 210 million was involved. Tightened border surveillance and interceptions are meant to discourage migrants from travelling through the African country to the EU. Although the measures Mauritania is taking against migration appear to be having an effect, human rights organisations have criticism of the policy.

title: Eight years in prison for rape and attempted rape in a forest in Zeist
lead: The court in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> has sentenced a 47-year-old Georgian with no fixed abode or residence to eight years in prison for a violent rape and an attempted rape, both in Zeist. He has also been convicted of an attempted sexual assault in <entity id="org:gemeente-bunschoten">Bunschoten</entity>-Spakenburg. In addition, he has been issued a contact ban with his victims and a location ban for both municipalities. He must also pay his victims thousands of euros in damages. Rape The man on 15 August last year approached a woman in a forest in Zeist, struck her in the face out of nowhere and grabbed her by the throat with both hands. He repeatedly shouted "I kill you", dragged her into the bushes and raped her. The man says he cannot remember the rape, but according to the court it is established that it was him, also because his DNA was found on the woman. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> tracked him down with help from images recorded by a security camera of a house in the area. These were shared, which yielded usable tips. Attempted rape The investigation further revealed that an hour and a half earlier, in the same area, he tried to rape a woman who was cycling past. He grabbed her by the upper arm, held her bicycle and pointed in the direction of the forest. The woman began to scream for help and kept doing so, even when the man put his hand over her mouth. Eventually he let her go and fled, leaving DNA evidence on the bicycle's luggage carrier. Attempted sexual assault The attempted sexual assault took place almost two weeks earlier in the outskirts of Bunschoten-Spakenburg. The man approached a woman who was walking there and took a selfie with her. When she wanted to keep walking, he became angry and kept following her. When she made contact with a group of birdwatchers, he cycled on. Half an hour to three quarters later she ran into him again. He told her he had a pistol on him, but that he did not use it against friends. When he put his hand on her shoulder, she made a defensive gesture, after which he turned around and cycled away.

title: VVD figures back Weekers, who wants a different course for the party
lead: It is not an attack on the party or the leadership, not at all. It is rather an offer of support, which he wants to give "from the back bench". That is what Frans Weekers said last night, when he surprised many VVD members by putting himself forward as a rival candidate for <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> in the programme Pauw, De Wit en Moggré. The board had already nominated former minister Adriaansens, but members of VVD branches in Limburg and Brabant will also nominate him soon. Weekers says he is worried about the party. Members are leaving. Some think the VVD sits too much on D66's luggage carrier, others think the VVD is a PVV-light. He wants the party to return to liberal ideas and stop excluding other parties. According to him, the VVD should never have done that in last year's election campaign, and it should not do so now either. Support for Remkes, Teeven, Zijlstra and De Krom This is criticism that VVD members active in local or provincial government have voiced more often. But Weekers' criticism and candidacy are now also openly supported by, among others, former minister Johan Remkes, former state secretary Fred Teeven, former minister Halbe Zijlstra and former state secretary Paul de Krom. Remkes and Teeven leave it at a statement of support, while De Krom and Zijlstra gave the NOS extensive interviews. They too want an end to excluding other parties and a debate about the course. Former parliamentary group leader and minister Zijlstra thinks Weekers' candidacy could be "a reset for the party". "Power and counterpower within a party are ultimately vital, and that has now slipped away too far," he thinks. Members should, according to Zijlstra, regain more influence. 'No attack on leadership' He calls anyone who starts on Yesilgöz's position "naive". The problem has existed for longer; in his view the VVD has strayed too far from its course. As for the timing of Weekers, in a week in which the minority cabinet is still looking for a way to agree on the tax plan, they see nothing strange. Candidates for the parliamentary group leadership can register until mid-December, and Weekers is "neatly following that route", according to Zijlstra and De Krom. 'Candidacy in itself already an attack' A former VVD minister who does not want to be named thinks Weekers' candidacy is in itself already an attack. Former minister Henk Kamp does not see it that way. According to him, Yesilgöz's party leadership is not up for discussion, not even because of this candidacy. "Dilan remains our leader for this term. The question of the lead candidacy only arises at new elections," says Kamp. A lead candidate election for the Senate fits the democratic process now, given the provincial elections next spring, he thinks. Kamp supports Adriaansens, who was nominated by the party board, but has no problem with Weekers putting himself forward now. On substance, Kamp does not agree with Weekers: the clarity Yesilgöz gave in the campaign about parties and plans the VVD wants nothing to do with, he saw as a clear course. That Weekers did not call Yesilgöz before sitting down in a TV programme is not strange, says De Krom. The board should have known, and he had informed it. On the NOS's questions to Yesilgöz herself, a spokesperson said today that she will not answer them.

title: Sinterklaasjournaal keeps things exciting, successor to De Walle still unclear
lead: In the first episode of Het Sinterklaasjournaal it has not yet become clear who will look after the Grote Boek from now on. Last September it became known that Stefan de Walle would hang up the red cape after fifteen years. Broadcaster NTR remained silent about his successor. That is still a mystery. In the first episode Hoofdpiet showed presenter Merel Westrik the steamboat, but Sinterklaas was nowhere to be seen. "We don't need to worry about Sinterklaas," said Hoofdpiet. "He's just hard at work in his study. He's sitting right here behind his desk. He can't be missed." But <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de kamer</entity> turned out to be empty. "I think I missed something," stammered Hoofdpiet. "I think so too," Westrik responded. "Sinterklaas is not on the steamboat," she said at the end of the episode. "Well, I never." On Saturday the Sint can at least be seen in all his glory. Then he and his helpers will set foot ashore in Grave, in the <entity id="org:gemeente-land-van-cuijk">gemeente Land van Cuijk</entity> in Brabant. According to <entity id="person:marieke-moorman">burgemeester Moorman</entity>, the historic city is ready for him. "We already have a lovely present for him," she said in Het Sinterklaasjournaal. "Tomorrow we are going to unveil it on the market." 'Hallootjes' The 61-year-old De Walle was responsible for the Grote Boek for fifteen years. "Dear Netherlands, with gratitude and with pain in my heart, after fifteen years my role as adviser to the national Sint is coming to an end," De Walle said in a statement in September. The actor called it an honour and a pleasure to have been Sinterklaas for many years. "Hallootjes" rang out every year as De Walle waved to the thousands of adults and children who had come along. His last national arrival was last year, when the steamboat docked in the harbour of Oudeschild on Texel. De Walle broke through to the general public in the 1990s with the role of Kees in the television series Flodder , about the antisocial Flodder family who move into the villa neighbourhood Zonnedael in the fictional city of Amstelhaeghe. Left voluntarily? It is not entirely clear whether De Walle's departure as Sinterklaas was voluntary. Just over a week ago, cabaret artist Karel de Rooij said to De Walle in his podcast Het bankje van Karel that it may be difficult to say goodbye to the role of Sinterklaas at some point. "Certainly," De Walle responded. "I will one day tell the full, detailed story of how all of that went and how this outcome came about," De Walle further said. The Instagram account SintTalk also discovered that De Walle will be seen as Sinterklaas again soon. On 2 December the actor performs two shows as Sint at Theater aan het Spui in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>. Rumours After the announcement that De Walle would stop, the rumour mill started up. For example, Matthijs Jansen of SintTalk reported that Daan Schuurmans would take on the role. The 54-year-old actor denied this report. He did say he knew who would be playing Sinterklaas, without giving further details. Although De Walle played the role of Sint Nicolaas for years, his predecessor, Bram van der Vlugt, was seen in the role for an even longer period: a quarter of a century. The actor, who died in 2020, was the Sint at the national arrivals and in Het Sinterklaasjournaal between 1986 and 2010. Sinterklaas on television through the years:

title: Political message at Kristallnight commemoration: 'Red Line protest is anti-Israel'
lead: In Amsterdam the Kristallnacht has been commemorated, 88 years ago today. The chairman of the Central Jewish Council (CJO), Chanan Hertzberger, chose a remarkably political message in his speech. He drew a direct link to yesterday's Red Line demonstration. Hertzberger thanked Jetten for not having gone into "the demands of the organisers of the anti-Israel demonstration". At his weekly press conference last week, the prime minister said that "the Netherlands is definitely taking a stand". According to him, it works better to put pressure on the Israeli government from Europe and with other international partners. At the Red Line demonstration against the Dutch government's Israel policy yesterday, according to the organisation at least 200,000 people took part. Demonstrators argue that violations of international law are being normalised and that this must stop. They demand, among other things, that military cooperation with Israel be halted. By wearing red, the demonstrators figuratively drew a red line. According to Hertzberger, the measures demanded "amount directly or indirectly to Israel being wiped off the map". 'Genocide lie' In his speech Hertzberger said that it "was to be expected that the extremes of the political spectrum would embrace the genocide lie". He is referring to the violence in Gaza. An independent UN investigative commission concluded last year that Israel is committing genocide in the Gaza Strip. According to Hertzberger, a judge determines whether there is genocide in Gaza. "Not demonstrators full of hate. Not politicians. Not journalists." According to the chairman, "Jews are collectively held responsible". "Who are being confronted in Arnhem, in Groningen, in Amsterdam about this so-called genocide? Us. The Jews. In our own city. On our street. In our children's class. We are being excluded and pushed to the margins of society," said the CJO chairman. In his speech Hertzberger draws parallels between history and now. "Ultimately the question is not how often antisemitism has been condemned, but what has actually been done to combat it," is his conclusion. Also, for the first time in ten years a Dutch prime minister gave a speech. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> spoke of anti-Jewish sentiments in the Netherlands. "Pogroms have occurred throughout history, and the lesson of history is that violence against Jews is never far away." The prime minister described antisemitism as "back, never having gone away". He described it as a smouldering peat fire, with flames of hatred flaring up again. "We see and hear it again in public debate and on social media, in antisemitic expressions that increasingly reach us unfiltered." Hertzberger stressed in his speech the importance of the presence of the prime minister, "especially now that Jewish life in the Netherlands is increasingly under pressure". What was Kristallnacht? In the night of 9 to 10 November 1938, Jews were attacked, arrested or murdered across Germany, Austria and parts of what was then Czechoslovakia. The violence spread as an organised pogrom by National Socialists. Hundreds of Jews were murdered, synagogues were set on fire, and shops and homes of Jews were looted and destroyed. Jewish schools and cemeteries were also targets. It is estimated that 30,000 arrested Jews were deported to concentration camps. Kristallnacht is also known as 'The Night of Broken Glass'. It was the prelude to the genocide of Jews in the Nazis' concentration camps and in large-scale executions in German-occupied territory. In the days after Kristallnacht in 1938, thousands of German Jews fled to the Netherlands. They sought a safe refuge, said Jetten. "The harsh truth is that most of them did so in vain." Resilient against antisemitism In his speech Jetten said that a few weeks ago he received a book from a young man, containing the story of his great-grandmother who survived the concentration camps. He quotes what the man wrote in it: "This is the story of my great-grandmother who survived the camps. Thanks to her willpower I am here. I hope my daughter has a future here in the Netherlands." Jetten said that it must never be the case that the man's daughter has no future in the Netherlands. According to him, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has earmarked funds for the protection of Jewish buildings and institutions. "But there is also a broader task, because combating antisemitism must be more than action and reaction. (...) As a society we must become more resilient against antisemitism. We must arm ourselves against it. Keep fighting it." Jetten said it is necessary for the Jewish community to remain visible in society. He says that he has hung a Delft blue mezuzah, a prayer scroll in a small case, by his front door. "To show that I want to be prime minister of a country in which Jewish life is visible."

title: France believes Iran was behind attack on supermarket cooling systems
lead: The French Public Prosecution Service has started an investigation into the leader of an Iranian group that allegedly sabotaged the cooling systems of about 700 French supermarkets in October. Major supermarket chains such as Intermarché and E.Leclerc had to throw away stock because hackers pushed the temperature in fridges and freezers up to 50 degrees. According to the French news channel BFM, the investigation is focused on the head of the hacker group Shahid Kaveh, which has ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the elite force of the Iranian state. French investigators conclude that this group was behind it from the "characteristic way of attacking", the use of the Persian language and IP addresses pointing to Iran. French Foreign Minister Barrot speaks on the news site France24 of an unprecedented act of aggression. "We will impose sanctions at European level on anyone responsible for this attack." He will also summon the Iranian ambassador in Paris. Also in the Netherlands Earlier this month, unknown persons attacked cooling systems of companies in the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden. In the Netherlands, large supermarkets were spared, but at least seventeen other companies were hit, including butchers and neighbourhood shops. In Belgium, the cooling in dozens of supermarkets was sabotaged, including those of Carrefour and Delhaize. In France, cooling systems at blood banks were attacked. This butcher in the Belgian town of Hove had damage of tens of thousands of euros:

title: Increasing electricity's share of energy use is a major task for the Netherlands
lead: This is one of the main items on the agenda of this year's climate summit: can the world use a larger share of its energy in the form of electricity? Electricity's share in the Netherlands is currently still 25 percent. Countries want to increase this worldwide to 35 percent within nine years. When done wisely, experts say this has several advantages. It saves energy, makes countries less dependent on energy imports, and reduces greenhouse gas emissions that warm the earth. 1200 degrees Celsius But it would be a major challenge for the Netherlands to reach this goal, especially given the problems with the overloaded electricity grid. Our country is switching to electricity, but should do so faster. "A lot really needs to happen for that," says Sanne de Boer, energy transition expert at RaboResearch. Especially in industry, transport and homes there are opportunities for electrification. De Boer expects industry's contribution to be limited in the coming years. Many factory processes take place at such high temperatures that they cannot (yet) run on electricity. Think of fertilizer production. In 'lighter' sectors such as paper and glass production more is possible, and this is already happening. At Isover in Etten-Leur, for example, they make insulation material from glass wool, made from a mixture of cullet, soda, sand and lime. This takes place in a furnace at 1200 degrees Celsius, and for two years now it no longer runs on gas alone. Industrial kettle The company built a furnace with electrodes that supply heat from electricity. "Like a kettle, but on an industrial scale," says factory director Jurgen Nooren. The furnace uses a quarter less energy and more than half less gas. "Still, industry is only electrifying sparingly," says Michèlle Prins, expert in industrial transformation at environmental organization Natuur & Milieu. In recent years expectations have been lowered. Many companies want to, but face numerous obstacles, such as the overloaded grid. Isover already made plans in 2020 to partly switch to electricity. The grid problems were less serious then, says factory director Nooren, and did not cause much delay. Companies are now on long waiting lists. Grid operators also keep charging higher and higher tariffs. And even if a company can electrify, that does not mean it is attractive. Isover received a subsidy from the European Union for the construction because it was an innovative project. But even now that it is running, the furnace is more expensive than a gas furnace, says Nooren, even with current gas prices. Here too, a subsidy narrows the difference. Struggling to survive Meanwhile European industry is having a hard time. The chemical industry in particular faces higher energy prices, an uneven playing field and fierce competition. "Where competition is fierce, companies are mainly busy surviving," says Prins. "So it is up to the government to step up sharp policy, such as scaling up offshore wind, expanding grids and a mandatory share of green electricity use." To still reach 35 percent, homes and transport would therefore have to electrify considerably. There are options for this: petrol cars can be replaced with electric cars, a home can be heated with a heat pump, and cooking can be done by induction. There are also fewer obstacles here than in industry, De Boer of RaboResearch explains. For example, the grid usually does not pose a problem. However, homes must be sufficiently insulated and have room for a heat pump. Furthermore, electrifying is often advantageous in the long term. People do have to make a considerable upfront investment. In new construction, heat pumps and induction cooking are already standard. Electricity is efficient Transport is also electrifying steadily. Hybrid and electric passenger cars are gaining ground. De Boer sees delivery vans and heavier transport increasingly switching to electricity too. That reaching 35 percent is still tough is, oddly enough, due to how efficient electricity use is. When a home switches to a heat pump, it needs only a third of the energy that was required to heat it with gas. So the share of electricity is increasing only slowly. If you want to reach 35 percent, you have to electrify far more than 35 percent of homes, De Boer explains. Say you have 100 homes heated with gas, you would need to install a heat pump in 60 homes. For passenger cars the difference is even larger. Especially if industry's contribution lags behind, the Netherlands can only come close to the goal with far-reaching electrification.

title: What to expect from the Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi?
lead: Tomorrow envoys from the US, Russia and Ukraine will meet in Abu Dhabi to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. European representatives have also travelled there. It is not yet certain whether they will sit at the table during the talks. The negotiations are led by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are the fourth round of talks under American leadership. Witkoff and President Trump's son-in-law Kushner want to reach agreements on de-escalation and security guarantees for after the war. According to Witkoff, the final goal is "a comprehensive, lasting peace agreement". Europe wants a say. Only this morning Europe announced that it too will travel to Abu Dhabi. There are concerns that the European voice is being heard too little, while the outcome of the talks could have major consequences for the security and future of the continent. Last week the US said that a 'new European security structure' may be discussed as part of an arrangement to end the war. That led to unrest in European capitals. A group has been hastily assembled to stand up for European and Ukrainian interests. It includes representatives of the EU, NATO, France, Germany and the United Kingdom. It is still unclear what role the delegation will have. It may only be involved on the sidelines of the talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia. Direct participation is not ruled out. Europe has not been directly involved in the talks since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russia wants to do business. As far as Russia is concerned, the talks in Abu Dhabi will not be limited to the situation in Ukraine. According to Russian media, the makeup of the Russian delegation shows that Moscow also wants to talk with the Americans about other international matters. On the talks about Ukraine, the Kremlin's approach is predictable: Russia categorically does not want a ceasefire and says fighting will continue during negotiations. Ukraine must accept 'the situation on the ground' and vacate the entire Donbas. Moscow also demands guarantees that Ukraine will never become a member of NATO. If Ukraine does not agree, Russian air strikes on Ukrainian cities will continue unabated and in full force. "Russia's strategy is aimed at the economic and humanitarian exhaustion of Ukraine, which leaves the regime in Kyiv no choice but to accept the Russian conditions for a ceasefire", said Russian political commentator and TV presenter Dmitri Suslov to the NOS team in Moscow. Ukraine does not expect a breakthrough. In Ukraine, too, the new round is not expected to lead to a breakthrough. Little suggests that President Putin seriously wants to engage in dialogue, they think in Kyiv. This is shown by the delegation Moscow is sending. In the meantime, air strikes on Ukrainian cities continue day and night, and they are claiming more and more civilian lives. A ray of hope was the recent ceasefire around Olешky and the evacuations of civilians from the town. It showed that the two countries can reach agreements and that if Russia stops fighting, the war can end. Ukrainians long for that, but not at any price. They are convinced that Russia still wants to subjugate all of Ukraine. In addition, there are concerns that the US will soon again put pressure on Ukraine to give up the part of the Donbas that is not occupied, which Ukraine does not want. The hope is that progress can be made on sub-issues, for example through the exchange of prisoners of war or an agreement on the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Kyiv continues to look for a way out of this war, but wants to prevent a ceasefire from merely paving the way for a next Russian invasion. Talks weigh heavily on Trump. For President Trump the talks weigh heavily after the defeat in last week's midterm elections. From January he will have less room to manoeuvre. A Democratic majority in Congress could, for example, push for stricter sanctions or more support for Ukraine. In addition, Trump wants to show results at his meeting with Chinese President Xi, later this month in Shenzhen. That could become a three-way meeting in which Putin also takes part. American analysts expect little from the talks in Abu Dhabi. The Institute for the Study of War notes that Russia is sending a delegation with officials who have previously stalled negotiations. "This suggests that the Kremlin is not interested in negotiating in good faith." John Herbst, former US ambassador to Ukraine, also writes that expectations should be "very modest". The previous round under American leadership took place in February in Geneva and produced little. Last month negotiator Witkoff revived the talks during a visit to Putin. Shortly before that, the US had suspended sanctions on the sale of Russian diesel.

title: Lots of criticism of new box 3 proposal, House wants absent minister Heinen to speak
lead: In <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> there is a lot of criticism of the new cabinet proposal to introduce a tax on realised capital gains in box 3 as quickly as possible. Opposition parties in particular feel the proposal is being rushed through parliament and that the funding is shaky. "An uncovered, blank cheque of 17 billion euros for the wealthy," said Pro-Kamerlid Stultiens in tonight's debate. The coalition parties CDA and D66 also have questions about how the minority cabinet intends to make up for the lower tax revenue. "We find this exciting too," said CDA-Kamerlid Van Dijk. But in the end CDA and D66 are willing to support the proposal. D66'er Oosterhuis called the funding by minister Heinen of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> "a rather creative interpretation of the budget rules". But the largest government party also sees no reason to block the proposal. In its view, clarity needs to come quickly "for households, entrepreneurs and the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">belastingdienst</entity>" about box 3. "If it is reasonably responsible, we are willing to jump in," said CDA'er Van Dijk. The House was supposed to discuss the whole proposal today, but a majority of the Kamerleden present want to make the decision only once they have also been able to speak with Heinen. He is in Brussels for a meeting with his EU colleagues, so <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> had sent only <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (Fiscaliteit) as its representative. But it was Heinen who decided at the end of February that the plans for box 3, which after years of work were awaiting treatment in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>, had to be overhauled again. The opposition mainly wants to question him about how the proposed changes are to be financially covered. Billion-euro gap after 2031. In Heinen's proposal we move to a tax on actually realised gains, which is only levied at the moment shares or property are sold. According to estimates, that system will bring the state 22 billion euros less revenue up to 2040 compared with earlier plans. The appendix to the proposal shows that the minority cabinet has largely covered this loss of revenue until 2031. But after that, once this government term is over, a gap arises that could grow to 17.6 billion euros. "The rule always applies here: how are you going to pay for it? Except for Eelco Heinen," argued Stultiens of Pro. He called it "expensive bungling". The only reason this proposal is on the table now, he said, is that minister Heinen and the VVD want it. Stultiens pointed out that the cabinet has meanwhile left room to postpone the introduction, from 2028 to 2029 at the latest. "So there is no reason to be in a hurry." Kamerlid Grinwis of the ChristenUnie agreed with him. He called it "undesirable and careless" that the proposal must be dealt with within a week. Grinwis feels the plan is being "forced down the House's throat". Heinen's own party, the VVD, considers the proposal sufficiently funded despite the billion-euro gap. Kamerlid Van Eijk urged quick introduction, because in her view there must be calm and clarity for the people who pay tax in box 3. The PVV is also in favour, but Kamerlid Vlottes called the financial underpinning a "phantom funding". The PVV member did not yet want to say how his party will vote next Thursday, when the vote on the proposal is scheduled. "But if this cabinet wants to make itself dependent on the PVV, then they could well come home from a cold fair," said Vlottes. Eerste Kamer. Despite all the criticism, the minority cabinet does see a majority in the Tweede Kamer on the horizon, with the support of the right-wing opposition parties JA21 and SGP. It is still unclear how the proposal will be received in the Eerste Kamer. The Senate traditionally looks at the quality of legislation and its feasibility. Last week the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> was scathing about the cabinet's haste. The Belastingdienst and the banks, which must supply data on their customers to the tax authorities, also indicate that rapid introduction will be difficult.

title: Four dead, including three children, after sandbank collapse in Gaza
lead: Four people were killed when a sandbank collapsed in Gaza. They were a woman and her two children, aged 8 and 6. A third child, aged 4, also did not survive. Six others were injured. The sandbank collapsed last night due to heavy rainfall in a camp for displaced families, near Deir al-Balah in southern Gaza. The displaced Palestinians had pitched their tents next to the sandbanks, believing they would protect them, local authorities report. According to a witness, the collapse sounded like an explosion. "We saw that three tents were completely buried after the sandbank fell on top of them", says Sohaib Abu Darbali. "People were lying under the rubble and we could not see them." Rainy season The rainy season has begun in Gaza. According to local authorities in Gaza, some areas are about 1.5 metres under water. At least 70,000 tents were flooded when the heavy rain began on Saturday. The UN organisation OCHA reports that humanitarian organisations have received requests from more than 26,000 households reporting damage to their shelter or belongings as a result of the rainstorms. A further 600 families have also been displaced by them, the UN organisation says.

title: A black leather jacket and AI visionary: who is Nvidia boss Jensen Huang?
lead: "I have a lot of them, probably thirty or forty", Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said of his signature black jacket in an interview with CBS News. He wears the same thing every day so that, by his own account, he can focus on other things. Most of those jackets were given to him by his wife Lori. Yesterday Huang admitted that he had cheated on her, possibly with a Chinese spy. 'Stubborn entrepreneur' The CEO will continue to lead the chip company for the time being. He founded it himself in 1993. He did not do so in a garage, like the founders of Apple or Google, but with two colleagues in the American restaurant chain Denny's. It became one of the most valuable companies in the world. In the biography The Thinking Machine, author Stephen Witt describes it as the story of a "stubborn entrepreneur" who pushed through his vision and in doing so became one of the richest men in the world. Huang ranks 10th on the Bloomberg Billionare Index, with an estimated fortune of 155 billion dollars. From Taiwan to Silicon Valley Jen-Hsun Huang, later anglicised to Jensen, was born in 1963 in Taiwan. His parents sold many of their possessions so they could send him to family in the United States at a young age. There he studied electrical engineering and went to work in Silicon Valley, a region in the state of California known for technological inventions and developments. Huang has been with his wife since a young age: in 1985 he married Lori, who also graduated in electrical engineering. At the age of 30 he resigned from his job and founded Nvidia, a chip company that did not make processors for a computer, but rather a graphics card. These were mainly used in gaming computers. Besides Huang, another founder, Chris Malachowsky, still works at Nvidia. The third founder, Curtis Priem, left the company in 2003 and sold his shares years ago. At the end of the 1990s, Huang had beaten most of his competitors in the market, biographer Witt says in a podcast. But Huang was not satisfied with merely supplying components for gaming computers. In 2014 he took steps to fully embrace AI. Nvidia made a move toward mobile computing power: computers that are not only programmed to do the same thing every time, but also to learn. That technology is now used by companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. "He paints a clear picture of 2026, while the rest of us are playing Flappy Bird on our phones", Witt says of Huang's 2014 vision. Where millions guided a little bird between obstacles on their mobile phones, Huang foresaw the flight that AI would take. Share price In the first years after 2010, Nvidia was known as a bad investment on the stock market; the company's share price, led by Jensen Huang, collapsed twice. Today the share price is worth a lot more, despite today's drop caused by the news about Huang's affair. Huang's idea of investing in AI and using chips in a different way initially met with much resistance. In those years such an investment seemed unprofitable, and Nvidia made good profits from selling gaming chips. Only when Google placed an order in 2014 for chips worth 130 million dollars did the market take Huang's ideas more seriously. In the years that followed, Nvidia would receive orders worth many billions of dollars. Future as CEO Besides a large fortune, Huang also has political connections. He has close contact with Donald Trump, and Huang sits on a council that gives technology advice to the president. In addition, Nvidia makes specialised chips that the US does not allow to be exported to China. The CEO seems to have been partly chosen for spying for that reason. Nvidia has started an investigation into Huang's affair. It is not certain whether he will ultimately have to step down as CEO, says Leen Paape, a corporate governance expert. "If I were in leadership, I would say: this is unacceptable. I am strict myself: you cannot simply let this pass. Certainly not at a company like this", he says about market leader Nvidia, where the outspoken founder Huang has been at the helm for decades. "But nothing is ruled out: precisely because it is such a special company, he may get away with it."

title: NASA is looking for new astronauts who want to live and work on the moon
lead: The American space agency NASA is looking for astronauts who want to live and work on the moon. NASA announces this on the website . "The people we select could walk on the moon, live and work at the moon base, and help develop the systems and procedures that will ultimately bring crews to Mars", says NASA director Jared Isaacman. Currently 32 active astronauts work at NASA. The selected astronauts will join them and prepare for a new Artemis mission. Artemis II Last April NASA astronauts flew to the moon on Artemis II. It was the first time since 1972 that people went towards the moon again. The aim of Artemis was to fly along the far side of the moon and test systems for future moon landing missions. The mission was successful and the four astronauts returned to Earth. The flight set a distance record. Never before had humans gone so far into space: 406.773 kilometres from Earth. Next year a new Artemis mission is planned: Artemis III will fly in an orbit around Earth, where several challenging tests will be carried out. For the first time the crew includes a European, the Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano. At the earliest in 2028, Artemis IV has the mission to put astronauts back on the moon. No Dutch people Applying for the astronaut corps is possible until Thursday 3 December. NASA expects to make the selection for the next group of astronaut candidates at the end of 2027. Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the selection committee, calls it a "chance to be part of a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of science and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity's future in space". In 2024 there was last an open vacancy at NASA. Ten astronaut candidates were then selected from over 8000 applications. They are currently following training of almost two years. For Dutch people who would like to join NASA there is bad news: the vacancy is only open to American citizens.

title: Mega drug case against 46 suspects in Belgium, main suspect denies murder attempts
lead: In Belgium the mega trial against 46 suspects started today. According to the Public Prosecution Service, they were part of a drug gang from the Brussels neighbourhood of Peterbos. They are suspected of being responsible for large-scale international drug trafficking and six attempted murders. The central figure in this case is 30-year-old Imad B., better known in the circuit as 'Mara'. He allegedly was the leader of the criminal network that from Brussels also has branches to the southern French port city of Marseille and Panama in Central America. In 2022 he was already sentenced to eight years in prison for drug trafficking. Mistaken murder in 2023 The suspicion is that after this conviction he continued his criminal activities from prison and remained in a leading position. The PPS supports this with wiretapped phone calls from prison and messages B. sent via the secure chat app Signal. In them he allegedly ordered murder six times, one of which in 2023 had a fatal outcome. This later turned out to be a mistaken murder. He also allegedly ensured that the drug trade from Peterbos kept flourishing. For this he remained in contact with international drug cartels. Calling with 6-year-old daughter B., who was present in the courtroom, denied all the accusations. According to him, he did not use Signal, nicknames used in the conversations are wrongly attributed to him, and he no longer has any ties to the drug trade in the Peterbos neighbourhood. The wiretapped phone calls are, according to him, "exaggerated". He said: "Detainees talk and tell all sorts of stories. In prison everyone wants to appear more important than he or she really is." That he had a phone smuggled into prison he did not deny. He says he did so to be able to call his family and his 6-year-old daughter. That he no longer earned income from Peterbos, according to him, was evident from the fact that his family financially supported him. B. and the 45 other suspects are also on trial for illegal weapons possession, intentional arson and money laundering. Lucrative trade The Peterbos neighbourhood in Brussels has for years been known for drug trafficking. Belgian media write that B. was born and raised there, but as a twentysomething he left for Marseille, where he came into contact with leading figures in the drug scene. After spending several years in Marseille, he returned to his home country in 2020. There he set up a lucrative drug trade, through which, between 2020 and his conviction in 2022, he earned more than 11 million euros according to the PPS.

lead: The search for the new Sinterklaas began two months ago. On 9 November he or she was then supposed to finally present themselves to the Dutch people, according to the rumour mill.

lead: A wave of student and secondary school protests is sweeping through part of Europe. In countries such as France, Germany, Switzerland, Portugal, Albania and England, these demonstrations are being hijacked by troublemakers and criminals. lead: It began with a cargo bike loaded with green beans and cauliflower. Now, more than a hundred years later, the sixth generation is poised to lead supermarket chain and family business Poiesz.

lead: New-build homes are becoming less and less attractive. High mortgage rates are curbing demand, because prices remain stubbornly high. That is what research by ING shows. Estate agents have long been concerned: "New-build prices are quite rigid."

title: Wall Street awaits midterm results as tech companies disappoint
lead: The election outcome could determine policy changes that affect important markets, such as pharmaceuticals, the housing market and AI.

lead: The online chess revolution is bringing hundreds of millions of people to the chessboard worldwide. On the computer screen, that is, where you inevitably run into YouTuber Levy Rozman. lead: After years of preparation, the municipality of Terneuzen is granting a permit for an asylum seekers' centre in a former Neckermann building in the Zeeland city. lead: During a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky, Russian troops have, according to Ukrainian soldiers, strengthened their positions and brought in additional equipment. Now that the fighting has resumed, evacuated residents are deeply worried about the people who stayed behind in the city.

lead: Rens Kroes has given birth to her second child. The cookbook author and entrepreneur says the little boy is named Loïc. "You could choose any day, but now you share your birthday with your big sister," she writes.

title: RDI warning: digital infrastructure not always available as a matter of course
lead: In the Netherlands we are used to critical infrastructure working. Availability and accessibility are normally almost 100 percent (>99.98%). But due to the strong increase in hybrid threats, the RDI doubts whether this will also be the case in the future, as described in the annual trend radar.

lead: With Ukraine being bombarded almost every day by Russian drones and missiles, the Netherlands is coming to its aid with additional drones and air defence weapons. During a surprise visit to The Hague, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Wednesday that the support helps with 'saving lives'. "We need it to get through this winter."

lead: An earthquake with a magnitude of 5.7 in central Japan injured at least 24 people on Sunday, local media report. The quake caused damage to buildings and disruption to train traffic. No deaths have been reported.

lead: The French utilities group wants to divest assets worth €2 billion to reduce its debts. What will happen to the company's other Dutch activities is unclear.

lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity>-Rutte I deliberately and knowingly steered towards a dubious interpretation of European temp agency rules. As a result, millions of temp workers missed out on many billions of euros in income, while the temp agency sector enjoyed golden times.

lead: Lionel Messi has become the first footballer ever to be top scorer in the American football league MLS for a second year in a row. The Argentine received the American version of the Golden Boot for it. The 39-year-old star scored 26 goals in 34 matches for Inter Miami. lead: Rich countries made €31.7 billion available in 2024 so that developing countries can adapt to climate change. That is far from enough, the UN concludes.

lead: 'We need to move from plans to concrete homes, and foreign money is needed to make that happen', says Amsterdam alderman Scholtes. Together with four colleagues, he visited the real estate fair Expo Real in Munich.

lead: The RTL Nieuws investigative team found more than 200 online fake pharmacies where you can still buy medicines used to lose weight, without a prescription. Yet these drugs are not meant for that purpose. Most of the webshops went online this year. We speak to a user who fell ill. We also ordered a package ourselves, and hospital pharmacist Corine Bethlehem of Erasmus MC explains how dangerous this illegal trade is.

lead: Het kabinet hervat deze week de gesprekken met zeven oppositiepartijen terwijl het probeert de stemmen te verkrijgen die het nodig heeft...

Fry up boiled potatoes: 'Even with mayo still healthier than eating boiled potatoes straight away'
lead: This morning <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> officially opened the new laboratory of potato breeder Agrico. New potato varieties are developed in the lab and research is done into sustainable cultivation. We spoke with several experts about how things really stand with the potato. lead: What do politicians really do behind the scenes? And how can you learn that as a newly minted councillor too? In her book 'De magie van de achterkamertjes', political coach Kiki Bakker uses seventeen interviews with (former) politicians to describe how things go in the council and parliament, and explains how to develop political savvy. title: Judge temporarily blocks start of construction of Trump's 76-metre-high triumphal arch
lead: A national judge has temporarily blocked the start of construction of the 76-metre-high triumphal arch in the American capital Washington. And Donald Trump has declared the Oval Office, the presidential workroom in the White House, a national monument. He thus wants to prevent successors from being able to undo the changes he made to the office. Follow all developments in the United States via our liveblog.

title: Residents protest against electricity substation right in front of their door on Veerstraat: 'Surely nobody is waiting for that?'
National government wants to reduce digital dependencies through procurement
lead: The national government wants to use its purchasing power more emphatically for digital autonomy and the continuity of public services. Joint ICT procurement, more room for European providers and better exit arrangements should reduce dependence on a limited number of technology companies. At the same time, the procurement organisation must work more simply and cheaply.

title: Scoop: imperial eagle receives 3D-printed claw
lead: An imperial eagle in Greece has received an artificial leg with a 3D-printed claw. The bird of prey was found last year with a shattered right leg and is learning to walk again after three operations. If it recovers sufficiently, it will move to a reserve to breed.

title: Teachers are leaving education disillusioned, while the solutions are there for the taking
Green light for Nedersaksenlijn after all: despite billion shortfall, important rail link will go ahead

lead: No Mathieu van der Poel at a cyclo-cross championship in the Netherlands. The European cyclo-cross championships in Zeddam are therefore a test case for the discipline's popularity in our country. The weekend in the Achterhoek paints a hopeful picture for the future despite a completely Belgian podium.

title: Suzan & Freek attend the outstanding achievers' lunch hosted by Willem-Alexander and Máxima
lead: Suzan and Freek Rikkerink were guests at the outstanding achievers' lunch of King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima on Tuesday. The singing duo was invited as the winner of the Popprijs 2025 and the 3FM Awards in the Best Live Moment category.

title: North Holland has already killed over 100,000 geese this year, more than in other years
lead: In the province of North Holland, a total of 100,291 geese were killed between February and the end of September, the Faunabeheereenheid (FBE) reports. That is considerably more than in previous years, says director Patty Laan. The province had already announced that the culling had to be doubled in order to significantly reduce the large goose population.

title: US space telescope Swift burns up in the atmosphere after 22 years and a failed rescue attempt
lead: The American space telescope Swift burned up in the atmosphere on Wednesday. The telescope spent 22 years researching explosions in the universe, while the mission was originally only supposed to last 2 years.

title: OM: statements by PVV MP Marjolein Faber about Amsterdam neighbourhood police officer not punishable

lead: PostNL is again asking the cabinet for a contribution of millions of euros for the delivery of letters and small parcels, mainly to private individuals.

title: American voter causes political earthquake: what now?
lead: The dust is slowly settling after the overwhelming victory of the Democrats in the American midterm elections. The big question: what now? Three questions about the (consequences of the) rebuke for President Donald Trump.

title: Herman Bröring looks back on settling Groningen damages: 'Those with the greatest needs are in the most difficult position'
lead: For years, professor Herman Bröring has been providing explanation on gas extraction in Groningen. Now that he is retiring, he cannot let the subject go. 'The next time I visit the Eerste or <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity>, I will explain what a law is and how legislation works.'

title: Confidence in politics low after chaotic week in The Hague: 'They only think about themselves'
lead: Confidence in national politics is exceptionally low after a week of squabbling in The Hague over the tax plan. Only 13 percent of Dutch people have confidence, according to research by the RTL Nieuwspanel. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity>-Jetten fares no better, at 12 percent. title: Democrats score big win with majority in Senate and likely also in House of Representatives
lead: The Democrats are likely to also gain the upper hand in the House of Representatives, following <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. That is what American media predict after the midterms. The victories in Texas, North Carolina and Ohio in particular stand out for the Democrats.

lead: Differences in staff shortages between sectors hardly lead to differences in collective agreement wage growth. Only when the labour market as a whole becomes very tight do collective agreement wages rise noticeably faster.

title: Children of missing Ratelband get stuck with authorities and landlord: 'We don't know what to do anymore'
lead: Rolls and Minou Ratelband, two of the older children of missing Emile Ratelband, are getting stuck with the authorities in their search for their father. The contact that <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> says it had with their father 'dates from the summer of 2025'. Meanwhile, the situation surrounding Ratelband's properties in Arnhem is becoming increasingly strange.

title: Misty and wet morning, it clears up this afternoon
lead: The day begins with locally dense fog and here and there some rain, but this afternoon the sun also shows itself now and then. The next two days are calm and mostly dry. The chance of dense fog at night and in the morning remains.

lead: Twenty years after the first edition of DocLab, immersive media art has come of age, says founder Caspar Sonnen. "We do not sit at home all day with a VR headset from Meta on our heads, as Mark Zuckerberg hoped."

lead: Lewis Hamilton takes back nothing of his harsh words about Charles Leclerc after the Mexico Grand Prix. The tensions at Ferrari have not yet been resolved. Team boss Fred Vasseur wants to sit down with his drivers on Friday.

title: Caribbean football associations back FIFA president Infantino
lead: Gianni Infantino can also count on the support of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) for the FIFA presidential election next March. The organisation unanimously backs the Swiss head of the world football federation. That emerged after a meeting on the island of Saint Lucia.

lead: Henri Bontenbal of coalition party CDA also delivers harsh criticism of the lack of an agreement: 'I am not one for casino politics.'

title: Surrogacy is a deliberate choice: 'Giving up the child was not difficult'
lead: Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> announced on Monday that he is expecting a child via a surrogate. In the Netherlands, around thirty to fifty children are born each year with the help of a surrogate. NU.nl spoke with surrogates about their experiences: "She has two fathers and one mother."

title: Six years ago Petra from Goes was still in a wheelchair, now she shines among the best bodybuilders in the world
lead: No parties, going to bed very early every evening and a strict diet schedule. And of course training. Training very hard. When bodybuilder Petra Behage (43) from Goes does something, she does it well. This month she shines in Las Vegas, at the biggest tournament in the world. title: At the ChristenUnie, 'compassion remains important', but 'clear limits and clear agreements' on asylum take priority
lead: On Tuesday <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> debates two asylum measures that the ChristenUnie parliamentary group in the House of Representatives voted for before the summer. title: Mystery surrounding man who stayed for weeks at Naples airport solved
lead: The search for the family of a man who had been staying at Naples airport for weeks has finally succeeded. The man, who calls himself Daniel, said he had lost his memory and been robbed of his identity documents. As of today the authorities know who he is and where he comes from.

title: KNMI issues code yellow, orange and red more locally: this changes for weather warnings
lead: From Monday 2 November, the KNMI will issue weather warnings in a different way. Code yellow, orange or red per province is a thing of the past. The KNMI now issues targeted and local warnings. This is what the KNMI is changing from 2 November.

title: Breakthrough in unsolved murder of Sjef thanks to commercial DNA databases
lead: More than twenty years after the murder of Sjef Leukel, a breakthrough may have been reached. Investigators found relatives of the suspected perpetrator using commercial DNA databases. lead: Americans go to the polls today for the midterm elections, better known as the midterms. To a large extent, these determine how the last two years of President Donald Trump's term will unfold.

lead: The number of reports of labor exploitation in the Netherlands increased by 13 percent over the past year. title: White privilege is so self-evident that no one sees it
lead: Racism is rife. A colour in an expensive BMW or a black teenager on a fatbike is quickly pulled aside by uncle cop. lead: Zoos that do not keep up with new insights on animal welfare will soon be easier to take harder action against. In the most extreme case, withdrawing their licence could even be considered. Now they are also releasing an album together. "I could not be with someone who does not understand what I hear in music."

title: Water board tax up again by tens of euros
lead: The water board tax will again rise by a few tens of euros next year for households with an owner-occupied home. For tenants, the tax also rises by an average of 7 percent, and for farmers and nature managers by 7.5 percent. The Association of Water Boards expects this based on the proposals on the table in the 21 water boards. They are setting their rates for 2027 in these weeks.

title: Is there hope for the cabinet? There are reasons why the tax plan may still pass
lead: Once again the cabinet is reworking its tax plans, hoping to still win support from opposition parties. They are grumbling, but note that they are not closing the door completely either. Three reasons why the cabinet could still succeed.

title: Videoland may take over streamer Viaplay, including Formula 1 and darts
lead: Streaming service Viaplay will become property of DPG Media, and will be merged with Videoland. The <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">Autoriteit Consument en Markt</entity> (ACM) has approved this.

lead: In a container in Papua New Guinea, an object was found last week that looks strikingly like a grenade. Four Chinese nationals are in custody. According to the Chinese embassy, it is all a misunderstanding. It is said to be a wine bottle.

title: Annika makes people's dreams come true and reaches hundreds of thousands of viewers: 'It's about deep longings'
lead: In a world where negativity and polarisation sometimes run rampant, the Delft resident Annika Hopstaken (36) brings people closer together. With Annika's Dromenbox she makes people's dreams come true, and sometimes even draws a million viewers. "It's about a sense of freedom and happiness."

title: Queen Máxima was set to listen to a pro-Palestinian band on 7 October, and then the visit was called off
lead: A working visit by <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima is rarely cancelled at the last minute. Yet it happened earlier this month: Máxima was due to visit Poppodium 013 on, of all days, 7 October, with the pro-Palestinian band Droom Dit on the programme. Behind the scenes it is now said that this date was not a good choice for the visit.

title: School bus crashes into tree in France, two dead and several injured
lead: Two people have died in an accident involving a school bus in eastern France. They are a child and a young adult. Sixteen people were injured, three of them seriously.

title: Marco Borsato could easily fill a stadium, but: 'He steps onto the stage with a huge backpack full'
lead: Now that Marco Borsato wants to get back to work as a singer after a serious court case in 2027, three considerable hurdles await him after years of silence and inactivity: directing his comeback, building up a rock-solid condition and retraining his voice. Three experts sketch the route map to the stage.

title: Imam used WhatsApp not to call for riots, yet police came to his door
lead: Imam Azzedine Karrat had police at his door because he allegedly called for riots. That was based on a misunderstanding. According to the imam, it feels to people with a certain background and religion as if they are "under a magnifying glass". Police Rotterdam says it "deeply regrets" the incident.
